en.titol: What Girona’s town council websites look like in 2026
en.resum: Data on 208 Girona town council websites in 2026, by county and town size, and what is missing most.
en.descripcio: We analysed 208 of the 221 town council websites in Girona. Only 30 pass all six basics and 141 have no meta description. Data by county and town size.

dataset.nom: Girona town council websites 2026, aggregates by county and by population band
dataset.descripcio: Counts by county and by population band for 208 town council websites in the province of Girona analysed on 30 and 31 October 2026, with no data on individual councils.
dataset.ambit: Province of Girona

seccions.titol: Only 30 of 208 town council websites pass all six basics at once
seccions.text:
The technical groundwork is done and what shows up in Google results is missing. Forced HTTPS, 200 of 207 sites (96.6%). Mobile viewport, 206 of 208 (99.0%). On the other hand, only 67 of 208 (32.2%) have a meta description, and 47 of 208 (22.6%) do not link to the accessibility statement from the home page.
141 of the 208 sites (67.8%) use the same WordPress theme, the one from the municipal websites platform of the Diputació de Girona, the provincial council. All 141 have a single H1 and structured data, 139 of 141 (98.6%) have an accessibility link and only 20 of 141 (14.2%) have a meta description.

seccions.titol: How we measured and what we could not measure
seccions.text:
A program of ours downloaded the home page of each official website on 30 and 31 October 2026 and read its HTML, without running JavaScript. The list of the 221 municipalities, with county, population on 1 January 2025 and official website, comes from the Generalitat’s open data (Municat), checked against Wikidata. It identifies itself as crida studio, respects robots.txt and makes at most one request per second to each server.
13 sites were left out, 4 with a domain that does not resolve, 3 with a 403 error, 3 with a 404 error, 2 that disallow robots in robots.txt and 1 that leads to a generic listing. None were forced. On 30 October the provincial council’s shared server, home to 143 of the 221 sites, stopped answering us after a burst of about three requests per second. The next day, at two seconds between requests, nothing was rejected.
This is not an audit. We only look at the home page HTML, so anything a site adds with JavaScript is invisible to us. We did not open any accessibility statement and we did not measure whether robots.txt blocks AI crawlers. The six-basics index is for comparing groups and is not a quality score. Groups with fewer than 8 sites are not compared.

seccions.titol: What happens in each county
seccions.text:
On the basics index the counties look alike. Among those that can be compared, with 8 or more sites analysed, the average runs from 5.2 in the Garrotxa to 4.7 in the Baix Empordà. Indicator by indicator there is more difference, and it depends mostly on how many sites in each county use the provincial council theme.
The Selva is the county where the fewest sites use that theme, 8 of 23 (34.8%), and the one with the most meta descriptions, 17 of 23 (73.9%). The Garrotxa, with 20 of 21 sites on the theme, is the only county where every site analysed links to accessibility from the home page.

seccions.titol: Small villages have more accessibility links and fewer meta descriptions
seccions.text:
In small villages almost every site is on the provincial council platform. Up to 500 residents, 75 of 79 sites (94.9%) use that theme, 75 of 79 (94.9%) have the accessibility link and only 9 of 79 (11.4%) have a meta description. Between 5,001 and 20,000 residents, where only 2 of 23 sites (8.7%) use the theme, it flips, a meta description in 16 of 23 (69.6%) and an accessibility link in 9 of 23 (39.1%).
In towns with over 20,000 residents none of the 10 sites uses the provincial council theme and only 1 of 10 is WordPress. They are the most likely to have a meta description, 8 of 10 (80.0%), but only 5 of 10 (50.0%) have a single H1.

seccions.titol: 47 sites do not link to the accessibility statement from the home page
seccions.text:
161 of the 208 sites analysed (77.4%) have a link on the home page with the word accessibility. The other 47 of 208 (22.6%) do not. Spain’s Royal Decree 1112/2018, in article 15.1, says the statement must be reachable from every page through a link labelled “Accessibility” and must be updated at least once a year.
If the link is not on the home page, it is not on every page. Among the 141 sites on the provincial council theme, 139 (98.6%) have the link. Among the other 67 sites, only 22 (32.8%) do. We did not open any statement, so we do not know whether it exists, whether it is up to date or whether the site is actually accessible.

seccions.titol: What a town council can do with this data
seccions.text:
Many of the missing items can be fixed from the content management system, without changing the website. The list lets you review your council’s home page with the same criteria as the study. If the site is on the provincial council platform, first check what the editor lets you change.
The aggregates by county and by population band can be downloaded as CSV from the links below, with no data on individual councils. If you work for the council and want to know how your site did, ask us through the contact form.

en.titol: What Girona’s accommodation websites look like in 2026
en.resum: Data on 675 accommodation websites in Girona in 2026, by type, county and category, with direct booking and languages.
en.descripcio: We analysed 675 Girona hotel, campsite and rural house websites. 487 have a booking engine or button, 515 two or more languages and 103 lodging schema.

dataset.nom: Girona accommodation websites 2026, aggregates by county, type, category, population band and tourist brand
dataset.descripcio: Counts and shares by county, type of accommodation, category, municipality population band and tourist brand for 675 accommodation websites in the province of Girona analysed on 31 October and 1 November 2026, with no data on individual establishments.
dataset.ambit: Province of Girona

seccions.titol: What the figures from 675 Girona accommodation websites say
seccions.text:
Most sites analysed invite visitors to book without going through a portal. 487 of 675 (72.1%) have a booking engine or a booking button on the home page, and 73 (10.8%) link to a booking portal such as Booking or Tripadvisor. 515 (76.3%) offer two or more languages. Meanwhile, 103 (15.3%) tell Google through structured data that they are a hotel, a campsite or a rural house.
The basics do not go together. 584 of 675 (86.5%) redirect on their own to HTTPS and 617 (91.4%) adapt to mobile, but 364 (53.9%) have exactly one H1 and 33 (4.9%) pass all six basics at once. The six-basics index, the same one used in the town council website study, averages 4.01.

seccions.titol: How we measured and what we could not measure
seccions.text:
We start from two official sources. The Catalonia Tourism Register, open data from the Generalitat, lists 2,160 accommodation establishments in the province of Girona, not counting tourist-use homes, but has no website field. We took each website from the establishment’s listing on catalunya.com, the Catalan Tourist Board’s website, which covers 1,943 of them (90.0%). 1,301 listings carry their own website, adding up to 1,037 distinct sites because 147 are shared.
A program of ours downloaded the home page of each site on 31 October and 1 November 2026 and read its HTML without running JavaScript, with the same method as the town council study. It analysed 675 of 1,037 (65.1%). Of the other 362, 194 have a domain that does not resolve, 46 answer 403, 39 disallow robots and the other 83 are empty or parked, lead to another platform, do not respond or return an error.
This is neither a census nor an audit. A property may have a website even if its catalunya.com listing shows none, and domains that do not resolve reflect the listing, not the establishment. Whatever a site adds with JavaScript, such as many booking engines and language switchers, is invisible to us, so these figures are minimums. The two indexes are our own criteria for comparing groups, not quality scores. Groups with fewer than 8 sites are not compared.

seccions.titol: How bookings work on Girona accommodation websites
seccions.text:
487 of 675 sites (72.1%) have a booking engine or a direct booking button on the home page. On 196 (29.0%) we identified the engine by name, such as Mirai, Avirato, SiteMinder, Thelis or WitBooking, and on 291 (43.1%) there is an identified engine or a booking subdomain. The other 196 (29.0%) only have a booking button or link, which may lead to an engine loaded with JavaScript or to a contact form.
Booking portals rarely appear on home pages. 73 of 675 (10.8%) link to an OTA, 62 (9.2%) to Tripadvisor and 16 (2.4%) to Booking.com. 13 sites (1.9%) link to a portal and have no engine or button of their own. 379 (56.1%) have WhatsApp or a clickable phone number, and 210 (31.1%) show prices or a date search.
The direct sales index, our own criterion from 0 to 4, gives one point each for a booking engine or button, two or more languages, WhatsApp or a clickable phone number, and prices or a date search. The average is 2.36 and 123 of 675 sites (18.2%) score all four points. By type, over the sites analysed in each, a booking engine or button ranges from 83.2% of campsites to 54.8% of guesthouses.

seccions.titol: Which languages the sites offer and which they are written in
seccions.text:
515 of 675 sites (76.3%) offer two or more languages, counting the language switcher and hreflang tags. Spanish is on 501 (74.2%), English on 479 (71.0%), Catalan on 459 (68.0%), French on 418 (61.9%), German on 161 (23.9%) and Dutch on 90 (13.3%). 415 (61.5%) have hreflang, the tag that tells Google the version for each language.
The home page is declared in Catalan on 315 of 675 sites (46.7%) and in Spanish on 220 (32.6%), and 73 (10.8%) declare no language. On the Costa Brava, 402 of 503 sites (79.9%) offer two or more languages, and in the Pyrenees brand (Pirineus) 110 of 164 (67.1%). By county, that figure runs from 83.2% in the Selva to 63.8% in the Garrotxa, leaving aside Osona, which has only 8 sites.

seccions.titol: The technical basics and what Google can read
seccions.text:
33 of 675 sites (4.9%) pass all six basics at once, forced HTTPS, viewport, meta description, a single H1, declared language and accessibility link, and 272 (40.3%) pass five or six. The least common indicator is the accessibility link, 42 of 675 (6.2%), followed by the single H1, 192 sites (28.4%) have none and 119 (17.6%) have more than one.
386 of 675 (57.2%) carry structured data (JSON-LD). 103 (15.3% of the 675) use it to say they are a lodging, with a type such as Hotel (63 sites), LodgingBusiness (24) or Campground (21). The most common types are Organization (248), WebSite (243) and BreadcrumbList (196), which describe the website rather than the kind of business.
Compared with the 208 Girona town council websites we analysed in October 2026 with the same method, accommodation sites have more meta descriptions (73.6% against 32.2%) and far more hreflang (61.5% against 3.4%), and fewer accessibility links (6.2% against 77.4%) and fewer six-basics passes (4.9% against 14.4%). The accessibility obligations of a town council and a private company are not the same, and the link is counted only for comparison.

seccions.titol: What an accommodation business can do with this data
seccions.text:
The list lets you review your property’s home page with the study’s criteria. Almost everything can be checked by opening the site on a phone and, if needed, the page source, and many items can be fixed from the content management system or from the booking engine. Our guide on rural tourism websites explains how to make direct booking easier.
The aggregates by county, type of accommodation, category, population band (on 1 January 2025, from Municat) and tourist brand can be downloaded as CSV from the links below, with no data on individual establishments, in case you want to compare your group or redo the sums.

seccions.titol: A direct booking example
seccions.text: Can Junqué, a rural holiday home in Ullà, sells its stays on its own website. Visitors pick their dates, see which units are free and book and pay without leaving the site, and the calendar is synced with Airbnb and Booking so no night is sold twice.

en.titol: What European bioprocess equipment makers’ websites look like in 2026
en.resum: Data on 66 European bioprocess manufacturer websites in 2026, covering languages, contact, datasheets and AI readiness.
en.descripcio: We analysed 66 websites of European bioprocess equipment makers. 62 offer English, 10 a quote or demo button and 11 an llms.txt file.

dataset.nom: European bioprocess equipment manufacturer websites 2026, aggregates by country group and segment
dataset.descripcio: Counts and shares by country group and segment for 66 websites of European bioprocess equipment manufacturers analysed on 1 November 2026, with no data on individual companies.
dataset.ambit: Europe

seccions.titol: What the numbers say about 66 bioprocess manufacturer websites
seccions.text:
European bioprocess equipment makers have the technical basics and English covered, and fall short when it comes to selling. 61 of 63 (96.8%) redirect to HTTPS on their own, 62 of 66 (93.9%) offer English and 52 (78.8%) have a meta description. By contrast, only 10 (15.2%) have a quote or demo button and none has all five sales elements we looked for.
The sample is 79 Europe-based makers of bioreactors, filtration, single-use systems, chromatography, sensors and process plants. We could read the home page of 66 (83.5%). 45 of the 79 are headquartered in Germany, Austria or Switzerland, which weighs on the overall figures.

seccions.titol: How we chose the companies and how we measured
seccions.text:
There is no census of European bioprocess equipment makers, so we cross-checked the public exhibitor lists of BioProcess International in Europe and the United States from 2023 to 2026, ACHEMA 2027 and analytica 2026, plus the bionity.com and AseBio directories. We kept own-brand manufacturers headquartered in Europe and left out distributors, CDMOs, software firms and subsidiaries of non-European groups.
Our own program read the home page, robots.txt and llms.txt of each site on 1 November 2026, without running JavaScript, one request at a time and with pauses. It identifies itself as crida studio and respects robots.txt. Of the 13 sites we could not read, 9 sit behind bot protection, which we did not try to get around.
This is neither a census nor an audit. Anything loaded with JavaScript is invisible to us, so the figures are minimums. The sales index is our own yardstick. We give no results by company size because no public source covers enough firms. The sample includes one crida studio client and the company where its founder used to work. Like the rest, they are not named.

seccions.titol: How many languages they offer and where the gaps are
seccions.text:
English is almost universal, but most sites stop there or shortly after. 62 of 66 (93.9%) offer English and 38 (57.6%) two or more languages. 28 (42.4%) show a single language, nearly always English, and 36 (54.5%) use hreflang, the tag that tells Google which version is meant for each language.
Companies headquartered in Germany, Austria and Switzerland offer more languages. 26 of 38 of their sites (68.4%) have two or more, against 5 of 10 (50.0%) in Spain and Portugal and 7 of 18 (38.9%) in the rest of Europe. For a maker selling across several countries, speaking the buyer’s language can still set it apart.

seccions.titol: How they invite quote requests and what buyers can download
seccions.text:
Nearly every home page has a contact link, 65 of 66 (98.5%), but few go further. Only 10 (15.2%) have a button or link in the HTML to request a quote, an offer or a demo, or to talk to an expert, and 20 (30.3%) have a form on the home page. For a buyer who knows what they need, a plain contact link is too generic.
49 of 66 (74.2%) link to LinkedIn and 31 (47.0%) to a PDF or to datasheets, a catalogue or downloads. Our sales index runs from 0 to 5 and gives one point each for English, a quote or demo button, LinkedIn, datasheets and company or product structured data. The average is 2.8, 19 sites score four and none scores five.

seccions.titol: What Google and AI assistants can read
seccions.text:
Structured data is there, but it often says little. 44 of 66 (66.7%) include JSON-LD, often what the content management system adds by default, and 33 (50.0%) state who they are with the Organization type. Only 1 (1.5%) describes a product with the Product type, which is what helps a search engine or an AI understand what the company makes.
11 sites (16.7%) already have an llms.txt, the file that summarises a website for language models. Only 4 (6.1%) block at least one of GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended or CCBot, and none blocks all five. However, 9 of the 79 sites (11.4%) would not let our clearly identified robot read their home page.

seccions.titol: What an equipment maker can check on its own website
seccions.text:
Use this list to go through your home page against the study criteria. Almost everything can be checked by opening the site and its source code, and fixed from the content management system. Our guide to bioprocess equipment manufacturer websites covers each element in more detail.
The aggregates by country group and segment can be downloaded as CSV files from the links below. They contain no data on individual companies and let you compare your own group or simply rerun the numbers.

en.titol: Cell and gene therapy clinical trials in Spain in 2026
en.resum: Our own count of 81 cell and gene therapy trials in Spain, by sponsor, phase and city.
en.descripcio: We counted 81 active cell and gene therapy trials with a site in Spain. Who sponsors them, what phase they are in and what that means for marketing.

dataset.nom: Cell and gene therapy trials with a site in Spain, by phase and city
dataset.descripcio: crida studio count of the 81 active cell and gene therapy trials with at least one site in Spain, from the ClinicalTrials.gov download of 1 November 2026. Trials by phase and by city, and the list of NCT identifiers.
dataset.ambit: Spain

seccions.titol: Who sponsors advanced therapy trials in Spain
seccions.text:
Most cell and gene therapy trials active in Spain are sponsored by industry. Of the 81 we counted, 62 (76.5%) have a lead sponsor in the registry’s industry class. 18 are led by hospitals, research institutes and foundations or individual investigators, and 1 is in the network class. There are 32 different industry sponsors.
The count covers CAR-T, other cell therapies, mesenchymal cells and gene therapies using AAV or lentiviral vectors. Every trial has at least one Spanish site and is recruiting, not yet recruiting, active but not recruiting, or enrolling by invitation. We count trials, not patients or purchasing volume.

seccions.titol: Which phase the trials are in
seccions.text:
Almost half of the trials are in early phases. 36 of the 81 (44.4%) are early phase 1, phase 1 or phase 1/2, while 26 (32.1%) have already reached phase 3. The rest are 16 in phase 2, 2 in phase 2/3 and 1 in phase 4.
Phase 3 belongs almost entirely to industry, with 25 of the 26 trials. Non-industry sponsors cluster at the start. They hold both early phase 1 trials, 4 of the 10 phase 1 trials, 7 of the 24 phase 1/2 trials counting the one in the network class, and 5 of the 16 phase 2 trials.

seccions.titol: Which Spanish cities host the most trials
seccions.text:
Barcelona and Madrid host the most trials. Barcelona has a site in 62 of the 81 trials and Madrid in 46. Next come Salamanca with 23, Valencia with 21, and Pamplona and Seville with 19 each. Santander has 12, Córdoba 10, Badalona 8 and Málaga 7.
Each trial counts once per city, even if it uses more than one hospital there. Cities are taken as written in the registry, which is why Badalona appears separately from Barcelona. For a supplier based in Girona or elsewhere in Catalonia, a large share of this activity is close to home.

seccions.titol: Trials run by hospitals and foundations themselves
seccions.text:
Trials with sites only in Spain are mostly academic. There are 20 of them out of 81, and 17 have a non-industry sponsor. Put another way, 17 of the 19 non-industry trials run only in Spain, while just 3 of the 62 industry trials are Spain-only.
The registry shows clear examples. Fundació Clínic per a la Recerca Biomèdica is listed as lead sponsor of the CAR-T trials ARI0002h, in phase 2, and ARI0003, in early phase 1. Hospital Infantil Universitario Niño Jesús in Madrid sponsors AloCELYVIR, in phase 1/2. Here the sponsor is the hospital or foundation itself, which makes it a potential buyer or partner.

seccions.titol: How to use this data in your marketing
seccions.text:
Read from a marketing angle, the data points to two audiences. In an industry trial, the hospital is where the trial runs, but decisions on equipment and consumables may sit at the sponsor’s headquarters or its CDMO, which may be outside Spain. In an academic trial, the hospital or foundation may be the buyer or the partner.
So it pays to split your accounts. Most of the 32 industry sponsors are global accounts, reached at headquarters and often in English. Hospitals and foundations running their own trials, mainly in Barcelona and Madrid, are local accounts where direct contact and site visits make sense.

seccions.titol: How we counted and what the data does not say
seccions.text:
We used the ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, downloaded on 1 November 2026, with registry data up to 30 October. We filtered by site in Spain and by status (recruiting, not yet recruiting, active not recruiting or enrolling by invitation) and searched interventions for CAR-T, CAR T, chimeric antigen receptor, gene therapy, cell therapy, AAV, lentiviral and mesenchymal.
The query returned 147 records. We kept interventional studies where one of those terms, or certain product names ending in -leucel or -vec, appears in the intervention name, description or other names. That leaves 81. We have kept the list of NCT identifiers, and the count can be repeated with the same query.
There are limits. ClinicalTrials.gov does not cover every trial authorised in Spain, and the Spanish Clinical Studies Registry run by AEMPS is a separate registry. The term-based classification is ours and may miss or include a borderline case. The sponsor class is the registry’s own. These are trial counts, not market size, and a multinational trial counts the same as a Spain-only one.

en.titol: Bioprocess Market Watch. January 2026 edition for European suppliers
en.resum: December 2025 approvals, biologics trials and EU imports from open data, read for European bioprocess suppliers.
en.descripcio: 17 industry biologics trials started in Europe in December 2025. EMA and FDA approvals, trials and EU imports, read from open data for suppliers.

dataset.nom: Bioprocess Market Watch, data for the January 2026 edition
dataset.descripcio: Monthly 2025 counts of EMA and FDA approvals, industry biologics trials by territory, FDA CGMP warning letters and ANVISA registrations, plus imports of subheading 8419.89 into EU member states and PMDA approvals by fiscal year.
dataset.ambit: Europe, United States, Asia and Latin America

seccions.titol: What the December 2025 data say
seccions.text:
In December 2025, 17 industry biologics trials started in Europe, 9 more than in November, and 62 worldwide. Spain had 13, more than any other European country we track. The EMA authorised 1 medicine and the FDA approved 10.
FDA CGMP warning letters came to 13, and imports of subheading 8419.89 stayed almost level with November. The table compares each indicator with the previous month, and its figures are counts of official records, not equipment demand.

seccions.titol: EMA authorisations and FDA approvals, July to December
seccions.text:
In December 2025 the EMA authorised 1 human medicine and the FDA approved 10, made up of 7 novel drugs from CDER and 3 biologics licenses from CBER. In November each agency had approved 14. From July to December, the EMA ranged between 1 and 14 authorisations a month and the FDA between 2 and 14.
The EMA authorises in batches, so a month with 1 authorisation does not mean the sector has stalled. In November, 9 of the 14 medicines authorised were biosimilars, and in December none. The EMA table flags biosimilars but does not single out other biologics. CBER approves vaccines, blood products, gene therapies and some diagnostic reagents.
Each authorisation is a product that can now be sold and will need manufacturing with qualified consumables, equipment and services. This edition only counts authorisations, and the individual products are listed in the EMA and FDA sources.

seccions.titol: Where biologics trials started in December
seccions.text:
In December 2025, 17 industry biologics trials started with sites in Europe, 31 in the United States, 32 in Asia and 9 in Latin America. Worldwide the figure was 62. The territories add up to more than the total because a trial with sites in several countries counts in each one.
Within Europe, Spain had 13, Italy 9 and Germany 8. France, the United Kingdom and Poland had 7 each, Belgium 6, the Netherlands 3 and Switzerland none. These are small numbers, and in November Spain had only 3. One month does not make a trend, and December may still rise because many studies are registered late.
A new trial means clinical batches that someone has to make, often a CDMO or a pilot plant. The site country tells you where patients are treated, not where the medicine is made. It shows where the activity is and which sponsors to follow.

seccions.titol: Imports under subheading 8419.89, which includes reactors and fermenters
seccions.text:
In December 2025, the latest month of the edition's period with data for all 27 states, EU member states imported goods under subheading 8419.89 worth 207,864 thousand euros, according to Eurostat. November stood at 207,414 thousand, 450 less, a change of 0.2%. Germany imported 41,479 thousand, the Netherlands 24,585, France 22,691 and Belgium 22,453.
Spain ranked sixth with 10,420 thousand euros, behind Austria with 12,451. Read this with care. The subheading includes other heat treatment apparatus that are neither reactors nor fermenters, and it counts purchases from any country, including within the EU.
The data files include the monthly 2025 series for the 27 states combined. The lowest month was August, at 152,702,945 euros, and the highest was December, at 207,864,244 euros. With such a broad subheading, there is no way to tell how much of it is bioreactors.

seccions.titol: What open data can tell you about Asia and Latin America
seccions.text:
In Asia, which here means Japan, China, India and South Korea, 32 industry biologics trials started in December 2025. China had 24, Japan 9, South Korea 7 and India 2. Latin America had 9, with 4 in Brazil, 4 in Chile, 3 in Argentina, 1 in Mexico and none in Colombia.
In Brazil, ANVISA completed 4 biologics registrations in December and none in November, by the date the process closed. In Japan, the PMDA gives 135 entries for fiscal year 2024, from April 2024 to March 2025. Fiscal year 2025 has 104 up to December and is still partial. These entries also include new indications and doses.
Many countries run their own trial registries, and not everything appears on ClinicalTrials.gov. ANVISA and the PMDA count different things from the EMA and the FDA and cannot be compared with each other. They show whether a country is moving.

seccions.titol: What this means for a European bioprocess supplier
seccions.text:
For the coming quarter, these data show where clinical and regulatory work is happening. Germany, Spain, France, Italy, Poland and the United Kingdom had industry biologics trials starting in every month of 2025. That makes a good list for checking whether your CRM covers the sponsors and CDMOs in those countries.
The message depends on who is buying. In November, 9 of the 14 medicines the EMA authorised were biosimilars, a field where cost per batch and capacity weigh heavily. Among the licenses CBER approves are gene therapies, made in small batches with tight traceability. English works across the sector, but buyers in Germany, Spain, Italy or France appreciate their own language.
Before the quarter starts, it pays to prepare a page for each type of customer, datasheets to download in English and in each country's language, a kit for distributors and a trade show calendar with the cost per contact. At crida studio we do marketing for bioprocess equipment makers and life science companies, and the studio's founder ran marketing at a European manufacturer for three and a half years.

seccions.titol: What changed since November and how to read the series
seccions.text:
As this is the first edition, the comparison is with the previous month, November 2025. Trial starts rose in every territory, up 9 in Europe, 18 in the United States, 14 in Asia and 7 in Latin America. Approvals fell, down 13 at the EMA and 4 at the FDA, and CGMP warning letters went from 8 to 13.
The chart shows trials started worldwide in each month of 2025, between 37 in January and 65 in June, with 62 in December. Each point is a count of records, and the latest months can rise with late registrations. A real change shows up when it repeats over several months.

seccions.titol: Method, sources and limits of this edition

seccions.titol: January 2026 in numbers
seccions.text:
Europe saw 6 new industry biologics trials in January 2026, 11 fewer than in December. Worldwide, 57 trials started, and Asia, with 27, had more than any other territory. The EMA authorised 11 medicines and the FDA approved 1, the reverse of December.
FDA CGMP warning letters fell from 13 to 5, and imports under subheading 8419.89 into the 27 EU member states went from 207,864 to 159,894 thousand euros. These are counts of official records and Eurostat trade statistics, and with counts this small a single month does not make a trend.

seccions.titol: The EMA authorised 11 medicines in January and the FDA approved 1
seccions.text:
The EMA authorised 11 human medicines through the centralised procedure in January 2026, 2 of them biosimilars. The FDA approved 1, a novel drug from CDER, and CBER approved no new biologics license. December had been the other way round, with 1 EMA authorisation and 10 FDA approvals, 7 from CDER and 3 from CBER.
EMA authorisations come in batches. A month with just 1, such as October or December 2025, does not mean anything has slowed down. The EMA table flags biosimilars but does not separate other biologics from small-molecule medicines, and it includes generics. CBER licenses vaccines, blood products, gene therapies and some diagnostic reagents. Neither count says where each product is made.

seccions.titol: How many biologics trials started in each territory
seccions.text:
In January 2026, 57 industry trials with at least one biological intervention started. Of these, 27 had a site in Asia, 18 in the United States, 6 in Europe and 6 in Latin America. A trial with sites in several territories counts in each one, and some countries fall outside the four territories, so these figures should not be added together.
In Europe, 5 of the 6 trials had a site in Spain, and 4 each in Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom. France and Poland had 3 each, the Netherlands and Belgium 1 each, and Switzerland none. Several trials run in more than one country, which is why the countries add up to more than the total.
The registry shows where patients are treated, not where the product is made or on what equipment. For a supplier of pilot plant or single-use equipment, it points to where clinical work is happening, which you then need to check with customers and distributors. Many antibodies are also registered as drugs rather than biologics, so the count falls short.

seccions.titol: Which EU member states imported most under subheading 8419.89
seccions.text:
January 2026 is the latest month with data for all 27 member states within this edition's period. That month, the 27 together imported 159,894 thousand euros under subheading 8419.89. Germany imported the most, at 33,924 thousand euros, followed by the Netherlands at 25,844 and France at 14,348. Spain came sixth, at 8,601.
Read this with care. Subheading 8419.89 covers other equipment for treating materials through a change of temperature, and much of it is neither a bioreactor nor a fermenter. It also counts trade between EU states. In the twelve-month series for the 27 combined, December 2025 is the highest month and August the lowest. January is 23.1% below December, and Eurostat may still revise these figures.

seccions.titol: What open data can tell you about Asia and Latin America
seccions.text:
In Asia, 21 of the 27 trials started in January 2026 had a site in China, 5 in South Korea, 4 in Japan and 2 in India. China has been the Asian country with the most trials every month, between 13 and 25 over the twelve months of the series. This edition reads only ClinicalTrials.gov, not the national trial registries of each Asian country.
In Latin America, all 6 January trials had a site in Brazil, 3 in Argentina and 1 each in Mexico, Colombia and Chile. ANVISA registered 1 medicine in the biological category in January and 4 in December, going by the process completion date. Over the series, ANVISA ranges from 0 to 10 registrations a month.
In Japan, PMDA approvals are counted by fiscal year, April to March. Between FY2020 and FY2024 they ranged from 123 to 146 entries a year. FY2025 is still partial, with 104 entries from April 2025 to January 2026, so it cannot be compared with complete years. The list also counts new indications and doses, not only new active ingredients.

seccions.titol: What it means for a European bioprocess supplier
seccions.text:
For the coming quarter, one month is no reason to move budget, but it is a reason to check where you are looking. Germany had sites in 4 of the 6 European trials in January and was the top importer under subheading 8419.89, while Spain appeared in 5 of the 6. Before deciding, open your country's records on ClinicalTrials.gov and see which companies sponsor them.
In your messaging, English is the base, because several trials run in more than one country at once. For Germany, datasheets and pages in German are worth having, and for Brazil, in Portuguese. The message that fits these figures is the step from the lab to clinical manufacturing, backed by IQ, OQ and PQ qualification documents and local service.
It is worth preparing a website with downloadable datasheets in each language, a kit for distributors in Asia and Brazil, and a trade show plan built on numbers, for example with the trade show cost calculator. At crida studio we do marketing for bioprocess equipment makers and life science companies, and the studio's founder ran marketing at a European manufacturer for three and a half years.

seccions.titol: What has changed since the January edition
seccions.text:
Compared with the previous edition, which ran to December 2025, almost every January count is down. Europe goes from 17 to 6 trials, the United States from 31 to 18, Asia from 32 to 27 and Latin America from 9 to 6. Spain falls from 13 to 5. Worldwide the drop is smaller, from 62 to 57, down 8.1%.
EMA authorisations rise from 1 to 11, and authorised biosimilars from 0 to 2. FDA approvals fall from 10 to 1, CGMP warning letters from 13 to 5, ANVISA biologics registrations from 4 to 1, and imports under subheading 8419.89 from 207,864 to 159,894 thousand euros.
The line shows the worldwide total each month, from a low of 38 trials in February 2025 to a high of 65 in June, with January 2026 at 57. December 2025 was the busiest month for Europe in the whole series, with 17 trials, which is why the January drop looks so steep.

seccions.titol: What the open data say for February 2026
seccions.text:
In February 2026, 55 industry biologics trials started worldwide, and 13 had at least one site in Europe. The United States also had 13, Asia 26 and Latin America 4. The EMA authorised 7 medicines, 2 of them biosimilars, while the FDA approved 4 and issued 6 CGMP warning letters.
According to Eurostat, the 27 EU member states imported 158,349 thousand euros under subheading 8419.89 that month, with Germany accounting for 38,846 thousand. Trials and approvals are small counts of official records, not equipment demand, and a single month does not make a trend.

seccions.titol: How many medicines did the EMA and the FDA approve?
seccions.text:
In February 2026 the EMA authorised 7 human medicines through the centralised procedure, 2 of them biosimilars. The FDA approved 4, all novel drugs from CDER, and CBER granted no new biologics license. The chart compares both agencies over the last six months.
The EMA authorises in batches. It authorised 1 medicine in October 2025 and 1 in December 2025, but 14 in November. So one weak month does not make a trend. For a supplier, each authorisation is a product that can now be sold in the EU and that someone will have to make. The EMA table flags biosimilars but does not single out other biologics.

seccions.titol: Where did February's biologics trials start?
seccions.text:
In February 2026, Europe and the United States had 13 trials each, Asia 26 and Latin America 4. These are interventional studies sponsored by companies, with at least one biological intervention, counted by start month on ClinicalTrials.gov. Each one needs clinical batches made under GMP.
By European country, France and Spain had 6 each, Italy 5 and the United Kingdom 3. Germany, Belgium and Poland had 2 each, the Netherlands 1 and Switzerland none. A study with sites in several countries counts in each one, which is why the countries add up to more than the European total.
This count does not tell you where manufacturing will happen. A trial's country is where the sites and patients are, and the clinical batch may be made elsewhere. For a supplier, the figure shows where there is clinical activity with biologics and where it makes sense to look for contacts, but not how much equipment will be bought.

seccions.titol: Which member states imported most under subheading 8419.89?
seccions.text:
February 2026 is the latest month with data for all 27 member states in Eurostat within this edition's period. That month the 27 imported 158,349 thousand euros under subheading 8419.89. Germany imported 38,846 thousand, followed by the Netherlands with 16,114, Sweden with 14,998 and France with 13,540. Spain imported 8,269 thousand.
Subheading 8419.89 covers other machinery, plant and laboratory equipment for treating materials through a change of temperature. It includes bioreactors and fermenters, but also plenty of equipment that is neither. It also counts goods arriving from other EU states. Over the last twelve months, the lowest month was August 2025, with 152,702,945 euros, and the highest was December 2025, with 207,864,244 euros.

seccions.titol: What can open data tell us about Asia and Latin America?
seccions.text:
In Asia, 26 biologics trials started in February 2026. Of these, 21 had a site in China, 4 in Japan, 4 in South Korea and none in India. China had more trials than each of the other three countries in every month of the series. Japan and South Korea see few trials a month, so a change from one month to the next says little.
In Latin America, 4 trials started in February 2026, 2 of them with sites in Brazil. That month the Brazilian agency ANVISA registered no biologics, after 1 in January. Over the last twelve months, the peak was 10 registrations, in March 2025. The ANVISA open file has no registration date, so the count uses the date the process was completed.
In Japan we count PMDA approvals by fiscal year, from April to March. Between FY2020 and FY2024 there were between 123 and 146 a year. FY2025 has 119 from April 2025 to February 2026, a partial figure. These entries include new indications and doses, not only new active ingredients, so they are context rather than a monthly gauge.

seccions.titol: What does this month mean for a European supplier?
seccions.text:
For the April to June 2026 quarter, February offers two leads in Europe. Of the European countries broken out here, France, Spain and Italy had the most trial starts. Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden imported the most under subheading 8419.89. France had both 6 trials and 13,540 thousand euros of imports. Before moving budget, check the twelve-month series in the CSV, because one month is not a trend.
If you sell to teams making clinical batches, talk about scale-up from lab to pilot plant, single-use and GMP documentation such as URS, FAT, SAT, IQ, OQ and PQ. Do it in English for the whole of Europe and add French, German, Italian or Spanish where you really want to win business. If you are looking at Asia, where China had 21 trials in February, prepare English material built for distributors.
Get your website ready with language versions and hreflang, downloadable datasheets and a kit for distributors in each country. If you are weighing up a trade show, work out the cost per contact first. At crida studio we do marketing for bioprocess equipment makers and life science companies, and the studio's founder ran marketing at a European manufacturer for three and a half years.

seccions.text:
Compared with the February edition, which covered January 2026, trials in Europe went from 6 to 13 and in Spain from 5 to 6. FDA approvals rose from 1 to 4, all from CDER. CGMP warning letters went from 5 to 6. EMA biosimilars stayed at 2 and CBER licenses at 0.
In the United States, trials fell from 18 to 13, and in Latin America from 6 to 4. Worldwide they went from 57 to 55 and in Asia from 27 to 26. EMA authorisations went from 11 to 7 and ANVISA registrations from 1 to 0. Imports under subheading 8419.89 fell from 159,894 to 158,349 thousand euros, down 1.0%.
The chart shows biologics trials started worldwide each month from March 2025 to February 2026. The low was 42 in November 2025 and the high 65 in June 2025. February had 55. With numbers this small, no one-month move is a trend.

seccions.titol: How many medicines the EMA and the FDA approved in March 2026
seccions.text:
The EMA authorised 6 human medicines in March 2026 and the FDA approved 7, made up of 5 CDER novel drugs and 2 CBER biologics licenses. The two figures do not measure the same thing. The EMA count includes generics and biosimilars, while the FDA count only covers CDER novel drugs and new CBER licenses.
The chart shows that the EMA authorises in batches. It authorised 14 in November 2025, 1 in December and 11 in January 2026, so a month with a single authorisation means little on its own. The FDA also swings widely, from 14 approvals in November 2025 to 1 in January 2026.
For a supplier, each authorisation is a product that can now be sold and that someone has to make at commercial scale. The EMA table does not say which ones are biologics and only flags biosimilars, none in March and 2 in February. CBER covers vaccines, blood products and gene therapies, but also some diagnostic reagents.

seccions.titol: Where biologics trials started in March 2026
seccions.text:
Asia was the territory with the most industry biologics trials started in March 2026, with 45. The United States had 11, Europe 8 and Latin America 4. The world total of 74 also counts countries not broken out here.
Within Europe, Spain led the nine countries we break out, with 4. Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom had 3 each, France and Poland 2, Switzerland 1, and the Netherlands and Belgium none. A trial with sites in several countries counts in each one, which is why the countries add up to more than Europe's 8.
A new trial usually means clinical batches that someone has to make, often in a pilot plant or at a CDMO. The count does not say where they are made or on what equipment, though. Many antibodies are also registered as drugs rather than biologics, so the figure falls short.

seccions.titol: Which EU states imported the most under subheading 8419.89
seccions.text:
Germany was the member state that imported the most under subheading 8419.89 in March 2026, with 45,827 thousand euros. France followed with 17,787 and the Netherlands with 17,370, while Spain came seventh with 9,053. March 2026 is the latest month with data for all 27 states within this edition's period.
In total, the 27 states imported 182,468 thousand euros in March, 24,119 more than in February, a rise of 15.2%. Over the twelve-month series, the total ranges from a low of 152,702,945 euros in August 2025 to a high of 207,864,244 euros in December 2025.
Subheading 8419.89 includes bioreactors and fermenters, but also other apparatus for treating materials through a change of temperature. These are imports from any country, other EU states included, in current euros. The data show which countries import most of this kind of equipment, but not how many bioreactors are sold.

seccions.titol: What open data can tell you about Asia and Latin America
seccions.text:
In Asia, China had 45 trials started in March 2026, as many as the whole territory, up from 21 in February. Japan had 4, South Korea 3 and India none. This is a one-month jump, and ClinicalTrials.gov does not capture every trial in the region, so it is too early to call it a trend.
In Latin America, 4 trials started, the same number as in February. Brazil had 3, Chile 2, and Mexico, Argentina and Colombia 1 each. In Brazil, ANVISA has 6 biologic medicine registrations with the process completed in March and none in February. The file has no registration date, so we use the process completion date.
For Japan, we count PMDA approvals by fiscal year, which runs from April to March. There were 135 in FY2024 and 119 in FY2025, which is partial because the list runs to February 2026. These entries include new indications and doses, not only new drugs, and serve as context.

seccions.titol: What this means if you sell bioprocess equipment or services
seccions.text:
To decide where to put your sales effort next quarter, look at the twelve-month series rather than March alone. Asia has had more trials than Europe every month, and more than the United States every month since August 2025. If you already have a distributor there, it may be worth giving them more support. If not, take the time to study it before entering.
What to say depends on who buys. Trials point to clinical manufacturing, and authorisations to commercial production. If you sell pilot or single-use equipment, talk about scale-up and clinical batches. If you sell to plants already in production, talk about GMP, validation and service. Do it in English and in the language of each key country, such as German for Germany, which led imports this month.
Before the next trade show, check that your website has technical datasheets in English, that distributors have the same material and that trade show contacts reach your CRM. At crida studio we do marketing for bioprocess equipment manufacturers and life science companies, and the studio's founder ran marketing at a European manufacturer for three and a half years.

seccions.titol: What went up and what went down since the last edition
seccions.text:
Compared with the previous edition, which covered February 2026, trials rose worldwide, from 55 to 74 (+34.5%), and in Asia, from 26 to 45. FDA approvals also rose, from 4 to 7, as did CGMP warning letters, from 6 to 9, and ANVISA biologics registrations, from 0 to 6. EU27 imports rose by 15.2%.
Trials fell in Europe, from 13 to 8, in the United States, from 13 to 11, and in Spain, from 6 to 4. EMA authorisations went from 7 to 6 and biosimilars from 2 to 0. Latin America stayed at 4. These are small numbers, and none of these one-month moves makes a trend.
The line chart puts March in context. Over twelve months, trials started worldwide range from 42 in November 2025 to 74 in March 2026, and before this month the peak was 65, in June 2025. Bear in mind that the last month in the series can rise as late registrations come in.

seccions.titol: EMA authorisations and FDA approvals over six months
seccions.text:
In May 2026 the EMA authorised 6 human medicines, including 1 biosimilar. The FDA approved 8, all from CDER, which approves novel drugs and therapeutic biologics. CBER, which licenses vaccines, blood products and gene therapies, approved none. April had been the other way round, with 12 at the EMA and 3 at the FDA.
EMA authorisations arrive in batches. The single one in December 2025 does not mean the EMA slowed down, since January brought 11. The FDA went the opposite way, with 10 in December and 1 in January. The EMA table flags biosimilars but does not single out other biologics, so we cannot say how many are antibodies or vaccines.

seccions.titol: Where biologics trials started in May 2026
seccions.text:
In May 2026, 26 industry biologics trials started in Asia, 14 in the United States, 10 in Europe and 4 in Latin America. These are interventional trials with at least one biological intervention, counted by the country of their sites. A trial with sites in several territories counts in each one, so the territory figures cannot be added together.
Within Europe, France had 6 and Germany, Spain, Italy and the United Kingdom 5 each. Poland had 3, the Netherlands and Belgium 2 and Switzerland none. The numbers are so small that one trial more or less reshuffles the order from month to month, so the series is what counts.
Every new trial means clinical batches that someone has to make, often in a pilot plant or at a CDMO. The count does not say where they are made, but it does show in which countries biologics trials are starting and how steadily.

seccions.titol: EU imports under subheading 8419.89 in May 2026
seccions.text:
In May 2026 the 27 EU member states imported goods worth 184,970 thousand euros under subheading 8419.89, which includes reactors and fermenters. In April the figure was 204,612. Germany comes first with 38,827 thousand euros, followed by Sweden and the Netherlands. Spain is tenth with 7,129,758 euros. May is the latest month in the edition period with data for all 27 states.
These figures are not the size of any market. The subheading also covers other machinery that treats materials through a change of temperature, and many of these machines are not bioreactors. These are imports from any country, including other EU states, in current euros. Over twelve months the EU27 total ranged from 152,702,945 euros in August 2025 to 207,864,244 euros in December.

seccions.titol: What open data says about Asia and Latin America
seccions.text:
In Asia, 26 industry biologics trials started in May 2026, 9 more than in April. China had 21, Japan 7, South Korea 3 and India 1. March brought 45, the highest of the twelve months, and that level has not been reached since.
In Latin America 4 started, with 3 in Brazil, 2 in Argentina, 2 in Chile, 1 in Colombia and none in Mexico. ANVISA, Brazil's regulator, lists 12 biologics registrations dated May and 20 dated April, the highest of the twelve months. They are counted by the date the process was completed.
In Japan, the PMDA list is counted by fiscal year, April to March. FY2024 has 135 entries and FY2025, still partial, 119 up to February 2026. It includes new indications and doses, so it is context only. The trial counts also miss studies that appear only in national registries and not on ClinicalTrials.gov.

seccions.titol: What this month means for a European supplier
seccions.text:
Where should sales effort go next quarter? These figures give no reason to change plans. Europe moves between 6 and 17 trials a month, and in May France, Germany, Spain, Italy and the United Kingdom had 5 or 6 each. If you already have customers or distributors there, that is where it pays to keep pushing. Asia has more, mostly because of China, but open data says little beyond that.
What to say depends on who buys. Teams making clinical batches need equipment that is fit for GMP and scales from the lab to the pilot plant, and that is what your website and datasheets need to show with data. English works across Europe. German and French are worth adding if you sell in Germany or France, two of the countries with most trials in May.
What should you prepare? Your website and datasheets in English, an up-to-date kit for distributors and a trade show calendar that reflects where most trials start. At crida studio we do marketing for bioprocess equipment makers and life science companies, and the studio's founder ran marketing at a European manufacturer for three and a half years.

seccions.titol: What has gone up and down since the previous edition
seccions.text:
Compared with the previous edition, which ran to April, biologics trials fell in Europe from 11 to 10, worldwide from 54 to 49 and in the United States from 17 to 14. They rose in Asia from 17 to 26 and in Latin America from 2 to 4. Spain went from 6 to 5. None of these moves is a trend.
EMA authorisations went from 12 to 6 and biosimilars from 5 to 1. FDA approvals rose from 3 to 8, with CDER up from 2 to 8 and CBER down from 1 to 0. CGMP warning letters fell from 12 to 10, ANVISA biologics registrations from 20 to 12 and imports under subheading 8419.89 from 204,612 to 184,970 thousand euros.
The line shows biologics trials started worldwide over twelve months. They range from 42 in November 2025 to 74 in March 2026, and May stands at 49. That figure may still rise as late registrations for May come in.

seccions.text: Edition prepared in November 2026 with the data for its period. The figures run to 31 May 2026 and were downloaded on 1 November 2026 from eight public sources. They are counts and values from official records, with no estimates. The latest month may fall short because some registries fill in late, and EMA authorisations arrive in batches. The list gives each source's exact query and limits.

seccions.titol: What the open data says about June 2026
seccions.text:
In June 2026 industry sponsors started 10 biologics trials with sites in Europe, the same as in May. Worldwide they started 59 and in the United States 23, more than the month before. The EMA authorised 5 medicines and the FDA approved 4, across CDER and CBER.
The FDA also issued 15 CGMP warning letters to drug and biologics manufacturers, and Eurostat puts EU imports under subheading 8419.89 at 213,482 thousand euros. Trials and approvals are counts of official records, not equipment demand, and with numbers this small one month up or down is not a trend.

seccions.titol: How many medicines the EMA and the FDA approved up to June
seccions.text:
In June 2026 the EMA authorised 5 medicines through the centralised procedure, and 1 of them was a biosimilar. The FDA approved 4, made up of 3 novel drugs from CDER and 1 biologics license from CBER. Over the six months in the chart, the EMA peaks in April with 12 and the FDA in May with 8.
The EMA authorises in batches, so the series jumps a lot. Across the twelve months of data there are months with a single authorisation, such as October and December 2025, and one month with 14, November. A low month means nothing on its own. The EMA table includes generics and flags biosimilars, but does not single out other biologics.
For a supplier, each approval is a product moving into commercial manufacturing. CDER approvals are new molecular entities and new therapeutic biologics, while CBER approvals are licenses for products such as vaccines, blood products and gene therapies, plus some diagnostic reagents. These counts do not say who makes each product or where.

seccions.titol: Where industry biologics trials started in June 2026
seccions.text:
In June 2026 industry sponsors started 25 biologics trials with sites in Asia, 23 in the United States, 10 in Europe and 4 in Latin America. These are interventional studies with at least one biological intervention, counted by start month. One study can count in more than one territory, so the territories cannot be added up.
Of the nine European countries we track, Spain had the most trial starts in June, with 7. Italy and Poland follow with 6, and Germany, France and the United Kingdom with 5. Belgium has 2, the Netherlands 1 and Switzerland none. Because one study can have sites in several countries, the countries add up to more than the European total of 10.
A biologics trial needs batches of the product, made in the sponsor's own plant or at a CDMO. The site country does not say where those batches are made, but it does show where sponsors with products in trials are active. For a supplier of pilot-scale equipment or consumables, it is a pointer to potential customers, bearing in mind how small the numbers are.

seccions.titol: Which EU states import the most under subheading 8419.89
seccions.text:
In June 2026, the latest month with data for all 27 member states, EU imports under subheading 8419.89 came to 213,482 thousand euros. Germany imported 42,653 thousand euros and the Netherlands 34,871. France, Italy, Belgium and Sweden follow, between 15,616 and 12,284. Spain ranks ninth, with 8,804,245 euros.
Subheading 8419.89 covers other equipment for treating materials through a change of temperature, and includes much equipment that is neither a bioreactor nor a fermenter. These are imports from any country, including other EU states, in current euros. The figure shows where this family of equipment is bought, not how many bioreactors are sold.
In the twelve-month series of the EU27 total, June 2026 is the highest month and August 2025 the lowest. A rise over a single month is not a trend, and Eurostat may revise these figures in later releases.

seccions.titol: What open data can tell you about Asia and Latin America
seccions.text:
In Asia industry sponsors started 25 biologics trials in June 2026. China has 18, Japan 9, South Korea 4 and India 1. ClinicalTrials.gov is a US registry, and trials registered only in the national registries of these countries do not appear in it. That is why the Asian count falls short.
In Latin America 4 trials started, 3 with sites in Brazil, 2 in Argentina and 1 in Chile. Mexico and Colombia had none. The open data file of ANVISA, the Brazilian regulator, shows 14 biologics registrations with the process completed in June, 12 in May and 20 in April. The file has no registration date, so each registration is counted by the date its process was completed.
In Japan, the PMDA lists approved drugs by fiscal year, from April to March. FY2024 has 135 entries and FY2023 had 123. FY2025 only has data up to February 2026, with 119 entries, so it is partial. Each entry can be a new drug or a new indication. It is context and is not compared month by month.

seccions.titol: What a European bioprocess supplier can do with this data
seccions.text:
Where should sales effort go next quarter? In June, Germany and the Netherlands lead imports under subheading 8419.89, and Spain, Italy and Poland have the most trial starts of the nine European countries we track. One month is not enough to decide. Before moving budget, check whether the pattern holds across the twelve-month series.
What should you say, and in which language? A multinational sponsor may make purchasing decisions at headquarters or through its CDMO, and English is the way in. For a plant or a distributor in Germany, Italy or Poland, a datasheet and a page in the local language help. The message needs to be concrete, covering scale-up, GMP documentation and after-sales service.
What should you prepare? A website in the languages of the markets you choose, downloadable datasheets, a distributor kit and a trade show calendar that fits those countries. At crida studio we do marketing for bioprocess equipment manufacturers and life science companies, and the studio's founder ran marketing at a European manufacturer for three and a half years.

seccions.titol: What has changed since the previous edition
seccions.text:
Compared with the previous edition, with May 2026 data, Europe holds at 10 trials and Latin America at 4. Trials started worldwide rise from 49 to 59, in the United States from 14 to 23 and in Spain from 5 to 7. Asia goes from 26 to 25. The EMA goes from 6 to 5 authorisations and the FDA from 8 to 4.
CGMP warning letters from the FDA also rise, from 10 to 15, as do ANVISA biologics registrations, from 12 to 14, and imports under subheading 8419.89, from 184,970 to 213,482 thousand euros. In the chart, trials started worldwide move between 42 and 74 a month, with the high in March 2026. No single-month change is a trend.

seccions.titol: EMA authorisations and FDA approvals over six months
seccions.text:
The EMA authorised 8 human medicines in July 2026, 1 of them a biosimilar. The FDA approved 8, made up of 6 novel drugs from CDER and 2 biologics licences from CBER. The two agencies do not count the same thing. The EMA includes generics and biosimilars, while the FDA counts only novel drugs and new licences. To see which products they are and who holds the authorisation, look each one up on each agency's website.
Over the six months in the chart, the EMA ranges from 5 to 12 authorisations a month and the FDA from 3 to 8. EMA authorisations come in batches. The twelve-month series has months with 1, such as October and December 2025, and months with 13 or 14, so a quiet month is not a trend. The EMA table also flags biosimilars only and does not single out other biologics.

seccions.titol: Where biologics trials started in July
seccions.text:
Of the 7 biologics trials that industry sponsors started in Europe in July 2026, 4 have sites in Spain. Germany, France, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Belgium have 1 each, and Italy, Poland and Switzerland none. A study with sites in several countries counts in each of them, so the country figures add up to more than the European total.
Outside Europe, 14 started in the United States, 12 in Asia and none in Latin America. Every trial needs clinical batches made under GMP, but the country of the sites does not say where they are made or on what equipment. The count shows where industry is running clinical work.

seccions.titol: Which EU states import most under subheading 8419.89
seccions.text:
In July 2026, the member states imported 192,247 thousand euros under subheading 8419.89, 9.9% less than in June. It is the latest month in the period with data for all 27 states. Germany imported 54,060 thousand, well ahead of the Netherlands with 23,288. Spain is third with 14,961, just ahead of France with 14,659.
Subheading 8419.89 includes bioreactors and fermenters, but also other machinery, plant and laboratory equipment for treating materials through a change of temperature. These are imports from any country, including other EU states, and Eurostat may revise them. June 2026, at 213,482 thousand euros, is the highest of the twelve months in the series, and August 2025 the lowest.

seccions.titol: What open data shows for Asia and Latin America
seccions.text:
In Asia, industry sponsors started 12 biologics trials in July 2026, 13 fewer than in June. Of these, 8 have sites in China, 3 in South Korea, 1 in Japan and none in India. China has more than Japan, India and South Korea in every month of the series. Trials listed only in national registries are left out, so the count may fall short.
No trial started in Latin America in July, after 4 in June. ANVISA, Brazil's regulator, registered 10 biological medicines in July and 14 in June. Since April 2026 every month has had 10 or more, while from November 2025 to March 2026 no month went above 6. The date used is the process completion date, not a registration date.
In Japan, the PMDA counts approvals by fiscal year, from April to March. FY2024 had 135 and the four years before it between 123 and 146. The count includes new indications and doses, not only new active ingredients. FY2025 is partial, with 119 entries from April 2025 to February 2026, and cannot be compared yet.

seccions.titol: What this means for a European supplier
seccions.text:
Where should sales effort go next quarter? One month does not change a plan, but the twelve-month series gives some pointers. Spain, Germany, France and the United Kingdom have new trials every month, and Spain reached 13 in December 2025. The United States has between 11 and 31 a month. It is worth checking which sponsors run trials in these countries and which CDMOs they work with.
What to say, and in which language? This data cannot tell you whether the sector is growing or slowing, so do not use it to claim either. Explain which stage each piece of equipment serves, from pilot plants for trials to production of an approved product. English is the base. Spanish covers Spain and Latin America, Portuguese covers Brazil and German covers Germany, July's top importer under 8419.89.
What to prepare? A page per market with datasheets, GMP documentation and a local contact, a kit for distributors in Asia and Latin America, and a trade show calendar chosen by cost per contact. At crida studio we do marketing for bioprocess equipment makers and life science companies, and the studio's founder ran marketing at a European manufacturer for three and a half years.

seccions.titol: What has changed since the previous edition
seccions.text:
Compared with the previous edition, which had June data, trials fell in every territory, while EMA authorisations rose from 5 to 8 and FDA approvals from 4 to 8. Outside the table, Spain went from 7 trials to 4, Latin America from 4 to 0, ANVISA registrations from 14 to 10 and imports under 8419.89 from 213,482 to 192,247 thousand euros.
The line shows biologics trials started worldwide each month since August 2025. They range from 39 in July 2026 to 74 in March 2026. July is the lowest month in the series, but it is also the latest, and late registrations may still be added. It would take several months in a row moving the same way before calling it a trend.

seccions.titol: Method and limits of this edition
seccions.text:
Edition prepared in November 2026 with the data for its period, which runs to 31 July 2026. All sources were downloaded on 1 November 2026, and the figures are counts of official records, not sales or equipment demand.
The latest month usually comes in low, because many trials are registered weeks after they start and the FDA posts warning letters late. Many antibodies are also registered as drugs rather than biologics. Below is each source with its exact query, download date and limits.

In Asia, 16 biologics trials started in September 2026. China had 9, Japan 6, South Korea 5 and India none. In Latin America, 3 started, with 2 in Mexico, 1 in Brazil, 1 in Argentina and none in Colombia or Chile. As in Europe, a study with sites in several countries counts in each one.
In Brazil, ANVISA registered 6 biological medicines in September, the same as in August. The highest of the twelve months was April 2026, with 20. In Japan, the PMDA recorded 135 new drug entries in FY2024, from April 2024 to March 2025. FY2025 is still partial, with 119 entries from April 2025 to February 2026.
These figures have three limits. Only studies registered on ClinicalTrials.gov count, not those that appear only in a national registry. The ANVISA file has no registration date, so the process completion date is used. PMDA entries include new indications and doses, and they serve as context, not for month-by-month comparison.

seccions.titol: What a European bioprocess supplier can do with these figures
seccions.text:
For the coming quarter, put your effort where new trials appear month after month, not where there is a one-off spike. In September, the United Kingdom and France were the European countries with the most new trials, and the United States was the territory with the most. Before moving budget, look at each country's twelve months in this edition's CSV file and compare them with your current customers and distributors.
A trial count is a good reason to talk to clinical development teams and CDMOs. If you are targeting the United Kingdom or the United States, your content needs to be in English and speak to clinical manufacturing and scale-up. For France, Germany or Italy, a page in the local language and a local contact help.
To prepare, make sure your website and datasheets answer the usual questions on GMP and scale-up, and that your distributors have the same material. If you are heading to a trade show, bring these figures to open conversations. crida studio does marketing for bioprocess equipment makers and life science companies, and its founder ran marketing at a European manufacturer for three and a half years.

seccions.titol: What went up and what went down compared with August 2026
seccions.text:
Compared with August, most September counts are higher. Biologics trials rose from 46 to 62 worldwide (+34.8%), from 18 to 24 in the United States (+33.3%), from 12 to 16 in Asia (+33.3%), from 6 to 10 in Europe and from 1 to 3 in Latin America. Spain stays at 2.
The EMA goes from 4 to 7 authorisations and the FDA holds at 10, with CDER up from 7 to 9 and CBER down from 3 to 1. CGMP warning letters rise from 11 to 13 (+18.2%) and imports under subheading 8419.89 fall 9.9% from June to July. No one-month change is a trend, and in the chart worldwide trials range from 39 to 74 a month.

seccions.titol: Where the figures come from and what they cannot tell you
seccions.text: Edition prepared in November 2026 with the data for its period. All sources were downloaded on 1 November 2026 and the data run to 30 September 2026, except Eurostat, which runs to July, and the PMDA, to February. These are counts of official records, not equipment sales, and recent months may still rise. The list below gives the exact query, download date and limits for each source.

en.titol: EMA-approved biosimilars list. Which molecules and which years
en.resum: Our own count of the 153 biosimilars authorised by the EMA, by year, molecule and holder.
en.descripcio: We counted the biosimilars authorised by the EMA. There are 153 across 27 molecules, and 44 date from 2025. What supplier marketing teams can do with it.

dataset.nom: Biosimilars authorised by the EMA, by year and molecule
dataset.descripcio: crida studio count of the 153 biosimilars for human use authorised in the public EMA file of 22 November 2026. Biosimilars by year of authorisation and by molecule.
dataset.ambit: European Union

seccions.titol: How many biosimilars the EMA has authorised and who holds them
seccions.text:
The EMA's public medicines file shows 153 biosimilars for human use with the status authorised. They cover 27 different active substances and 41 marketing authorisation holders. In the EMA's words, a biosimilar is a biological medicine highly similar to another one already approved in the EU, known as the reference medicine.
The file also keeps the ones that left or never made it. There are 22 withdrawn biosimilars, 14 withdrawn applications, 2 refused and 1 lapsed. Another 6 have the status opinion, meaning the EMA's scientific committee has given an opinion but they are not yet listed as authorised.
For a supplier, every holder is a potential account. Behind each authorisation is a biological medicine made from living cells or organisms, in the holder's own plant or at a CDMO. The holder is not always the manufacturer, but it is the first name to look at.

seccions.titol: How many biosimilars were authorised each year
seccions.text:
2025 is the year with the most biosimilars still authorised today. There were 44, more than double the 17 from 2024. 2026 already has 14 up to 22 November. Adding up the three years, 75 of the 153 have an authorisation date from 2024 onwards.
Before that, the peak came in 2017 and 2018, with 11 and 14. Between 2019 and 2023 there are 4 to 8 a year. Only medicines that are authorised today count here. Withdrawn ones are left out, so the older years look smaller than what was actually approved.

seccions.titol: Which molecules have the most authorised biosimilars
seccions.text:
Denosumab is the molecule with the most authorised biosimilars, with 30. Next come aflibercept and pegfilgrastim with 12 each, ustekinumab with 11 and adalimumab with 10. Trastuzumab, bevacizumab and ranibizumab have 8 each. The other 19 molecules have 7 or fewer.
The 2025 jump has clear names behind it. Of the 44 biosimilars authorised that year, 26 are denosumab and 8 are aflibercept. For denosumab, 26 of its 30 authorised biosimilars date from 2025. In this molecule, most competitors arrived in the same year.
Of the 6 files with the status opinion, 2 are insulin aspart and there is 1 each for ranibizumab, filgrastim, omalizumab and pertuzumab. Omalizumab and pertuzumab have only 1 authorised biosimilar each today. For these two molecules, only a few companies have reached this stage.

seccions.titol: Why biosimilars arrive in waves
seccions.text:
Authorisations follow the timeline of the reference medicine. The EMA explains that a biosimilar can only be authorised once the data exclusivity period of the reference medicine has expired. In general, the reference medicine must have been authorised for at least eight years before another company can apply for approval of a biosimilar.
For marketing, that buys you time. Before authorisation, the EMA requires comparative quality, non-clinical and clinical studies. We have no data on when each company buys. But those studies need a working production process, so our reading is that much of the process buying happens earlier. If you wait for the approval news, you may be late.
So it pays to watch two things. Holders that already have authorised biosimilars know the route and can run it again with another molecule. Files with the status opinion show which biosimilars are about to arrive, and for which molecules.

seccions.titol: How to use this list in your marketing
seccions.text:
The EMA list is public, free and easy to filter in a spreadsheet. With the filters in this guide, your marketing team gets an account base sorted by molecule and date that it can share with sales.
This is where we work with suppliers in the sector. We help turn public data like this into account lists, messaging and web content for each type of buyer, without promising results that depend on each market.

seccions.titol: How we counted and what the data does not say
seccions.text:
We downloaded the file Medicines output, medicines report from the EMA's Download medicine data page. The EMA generated it on 22 November 2026 at 6 pm and we downloaded it the same day. We kept the rows with category Human and Biosimilar Yes. That gives 198 rows, and 153 have the status Authorised.
We counted holders without regard to upper or lower case. For the yearly count we used the marketing authorisation date. Two authorised medicines, Pavblu and Nylaspeg, have no such date in the file and are left out of the yearly count, which therefore adds up to 151.
There are limits. The EMA itself says it evaluates the majority of biosimilar applications in the EU, not all of them. We count authorisations, not sales or production volume. One molecule can have several brand names from the same holder.
