seccions.titol: Quants medicaments hi ha al programa PRIME i de quin tipus són
seccions.text:
La llista de l'EMA té 98 medicaments al programa PRIME. Són medicaments encara en desenvolupament als quals l'agència dona suport perquè poden cobrir una necessitat mèdica no resolta. Per a cadascun, la llista diu el tipus, l'àrea, la indicació, la data d'entrada i el tipus de sol·licitant, però no el nom de l'empresa. 43 són de pimes, 52 d'altres empreses i 3 del món acadèmic.
45 dels 98 són medicaments de teràpia avançada, o ATMP, el 46 %. Després venen 26 biològics i 24 químics, i hi ha 2 immunològics i 1 radiofàrmac. Als noms de les teràpies avançades hi surten vectors virals adenoassociats i lentivirals, cèl·lules T amb receptors quimèrics, les CAR-T, i cèl·lules mare modificades.
Les teràpies avançades són medicaments basats en gens, cèl·lules o teixits, i a la UE tenen unes normes GMP pròpies, a la part IV de l'EudraLex volum 4. Per a qui ven equips, consumibles o serveis de procés, és el grup que més pesa a la llista. La nostra guia de les teràpies avançades autoritzades a la UE explica quantes n'hi ha al mercat.

seccions.titol: A quines malalties apunten els medicaments PRIME
seccions.text:
L'oncologia va al davant, amb 15 medicaments. La segueixen l'àrea d'endocrinologia, ginecologia, fertilitat i metabolisme, amb 14, i l'oftalmologia, amb 12. Després venen la neurologia, amb 9, i les malalties cardiovasculars i les vacunes, amb 7 cada una. Entre totes, aquestes sis àrees sumen 64 dels 98 medicaments.
El pes de les teràpies avançades canvia molt d'una àrea a l'altra. A l'oftalmologia són 9 de 12 i a l'oncologia, 10 de 15. A les malalties cardiovasculars en són 5 de 7. A les vacunes i a les malalties infeccioses no n'hi ha cap, i a la neurologia només 3 de 9.

seccions.titol: Quants medicaments entren al PRIME cada any
seccions.text:
Del 2016 al 2025, cada any van entrar al PRIME entre 13 i 20 medicaments. En total, l'EMA ha concedit 179 designacions. Les 98 de la llista actual i les 81 de la pestanya dels que ja n'han sortit sumen exactament la xifra acumulada que publica la mateixa agència.
El 2026 ja en porta 20, fins a la reunió del comitè d'octubre, tantes com el 2020, l'any amb més entrades fins ara. 11 de les 20 són teràpies avançades, la xifra més alta de la sèrie. El 2025 en van ser 6 de 16, i el 2019, que tenia el rècord anterior, 10 de 16.
La llista actual és jove. 65 dels 98 medicaments hi han entrat des del 2023, perquè els més antics ja n'han sortit, amb una autorització o sense. Només 12 hi són des d'abans del 2020.

seccions.titol: Quantes peticions accepta el comitè de l'EMA
seccions.text:
El 2026, el comitè de l'EMA accepta una de cada tres peticions d'entrada. Fins a la reunió d'octubre, el CHMP, el comitè de medicaments d'ús humà, n'ha decidit 59. N'ha acceptat 20, el 34 %, i n'ha rebutjat 39. És una mica més que el 28 % del conjunt des del 2016.
Les teràpies avançades són el grup amb més peticions i també el que en té més d'acceptades, 11 de 29, el 38 %. Dels químics en passen 5 de 19, el 26 %. Per tipus de sol·licitant, les pimes en passen 7 de 24, el 29 %, i la resta d'empreses, 13 de 34, el 38 %.
Des del 2016, l'EMA ha acceptat 179 peticions i n'ha rebutjat 458, sense comptar-ne 26 que quedaven fora d'abast i 17 que es van retirar. Les pimes en presenten més de la meitat però en passen menys, 76 de 339, el 22 %, contra 100 de 288 de la resta d'empreses, el 35 %.

seccions.titol: Què passa amb els medicaments quan surten del PRIME
seccions.text:
De les 81 entrades de la pestanya dels que ja han sortit del PRIME, 45 van acabar amb una autorització de comercialització a la UE, encara que unes quantes l'han perduda després. 31 van perdre la designació abans d'arribar-hi, 3 estan en avaluació i 2 van retirar la sol·licitud o la van tenir denegada. Les 81 entrades són 80 medicaments, perquè un hi surt amb dues indicacions.
Les teràpies avançades són les que més designacions perden. Són 37 de les 81 entrades que han sortit, però 17 de les 31 retirades. 18 sí que van arribar a l'autorització. La llista no diu el motiu de cada retirada, i l'EMA explica que pot ser a petició de l'empresa o perquè les dades noves ja no compleixen els criteris.
El fitxer de medicaments de l'EMA del 24 de novembre de 2026 marca 46 medicaments com a PRIME, i 38 consten avui com a autoritzats. 43 tenen data d'autorització, del 2018 al 2026. D'aquests 43, 17 són teràpies avançades, 26 són medicaments orfes i 14 van rebre una autorització condicional. El 2025, segons l'EMA, 6 dels medicaments que va recomanar venien del PRIME.

seccions.titol: Què vol dir el PRIME per a la fabricació i per als proveïdors
seccions.text:
El PRIME vol accelerar el desenvolupament i l'avaluació, i això també escurça el temps per tenir la fabricació a punt. Segons l'EMA, el medicament té un ponent del comitè un mes després d'entrar-hi, una reunió d'inici amb experts al cap de tres o quatre mesos i assessorament científic a cada fita. Quan l'empresa demana l'autorització, pot optar a l'avaluació accelerada, que es fa en 150 dies com a màxim en lloc de 210.
Aquest calendari no sempre es compleix. L'anàlisi de l'EMA dels cinc primers anys del programa diu que passar de l'avaluació accelerada al calendari normal va ser freqüent, en un 56 % dels casos, i que en les teràpies avançades les objeccions de qualitat n'eren sovint un dels motius. En aquells cinc anys, dels 16 medicaments PRIME que van començar l'avaluació amb el calendari accelerat, només 7 el van mantenir fins al final.
La fabricació és un dels punts delicats. L'EMA i l'FDA van escriure el desembre de 2023 que generar la informació de qualitat i fabricació, el CMC, amb uns terminis tan curts pot ser un repte per a les empreses, i que aquests programes poden tenir menys lots abans del llançament. Tot i així, el producte per llançar s'ha de fer amb un procés validat del tot i, en general, a la planta comercial prevista.
La nostra lectura per a un proveïdor és que la llista PRIME assenyala empreses que necessiten tenir el procés, l'escalat i la documentació GMP a punt abans del normal. 43 de les 98 són pimes, que segons l'EMA solen tenir menys experiència reguladora. El nostre recompte d'assajos de teràpia cel·lular i gènica a Espanya ajuda a veure qui hi treballa aquí.

seccions.titol: Com fer servir la llista PRIME a màrqueting i vendes
seccions.text:
La llista és gratuïta, l'EMA l'actualitza després de les reunions del comitè i cap en un full de càlcul. Amb uns quants filtres es converteix en una llista de comptes, com qualsevol estudi de mercat amb dades públiques. Aquests són els passos, en l'ordre que els faríem.
A crida studio fem aquesta feina dins del màrqueting per a proveïdors de biotecnologia i bioprocés. Creuem la llista PRIME amb els registres d'assajos per fer una llista de comptes. Després preparem missatges diferents per a les pimes i per a la resta d'empreses, i continguts per a la web que vendes pot fer servir.

seccions.titol: Com hem comptat i què no diuen les dades
seccions.text:
Vam baixar de la web de l'EMA el 24 de novembre de 2026 la llista de medicaments del programa PRIME, el fitxer de recomanacions del 2026 i el fitxer de medicaments, que marca quins han passat pel PRIME. La pàgina diu que els dos primers es van actualitzar el 16 de novembre de 2026. Vam treure les files buides i les notes del peu, i vam unificar dues àrees escrites de dues maneres.
Per comptar per anys fem servir la data en què l'EMA va concedir la designació, i sumem els medicaments actuals i els que ja han sortit. El 2026 arriba fins a la reunió del CHMP d'octubre. Les xifres acumulades de peticions des del 2016 són les dels gràfics de la mateixa pàgina de l'EMA, i poden no quadrar d'una en una amb el fitxer de l'any.
Comptem designacions, no vendes ni comandes. La llista no diu qui fabrica cada medicament ni en quina fase clínica és. Dos dels medicaments del 2026 surten amb un nom diferent a cada fitxer, però el recompte quadra. Les xifres dels gràfics es poden baixar en aquesta pàgina, i guardem la llista de les 179 designacions.

en.titol: WordPress and custom web design and development
en.resum: Web design and development in Girona, with WordPress or custom code, from €1,200 and yours with full access.
en.descripcio: WordPress or custom websites for companies across Europe. Simple sites from €1,200, corporate sites from €3,000, with full access. Quote within five days.

seccions.titol: Three kinds of website and what each one costs
seccions.text:
A simple template website starts at €1,200. A custom WordPress business website starts at €3,000, and an online shop at €4,000. All prices exclude VAT.
If you need bookings, private areas or a connection to your ERP, custom development starts at €8,000. Before we start you get a fixed quote in writing, within five working days.

seccions.titol: Which website suits you
seccions.text:
The simple website works if you’re just starting out, in a hurry or want to test the waters before investing more. The custom website makes sense when it has to sell or bring in enquiries and you want it to show who you are.
The online shop is for businesses that already sell and want to sell online under the same brand. To decide, we look at what your business offers, who you’re talking to and what a visitor should be able to do on arrival.
According to Spain’s statistics office (INE), 82.9% of businesses with 10 or more employees and internet access had a website in the first quarter of 2026, compared with 36.2% of those with fewer than 10. If you don’t have one yet, the simple website is a good start.

seccions.titol: What the project includes
seccions.text:
Depending on the website, the work includes organising the content, designing the screens, building it in WordPress or custom code and integration with the tools the business needs, such as your CRM or bookings.
The custom website can grow to 10 to 20 pages in three languages, with a blog and copy written by us. We look after mobile, accessibility and speed throughout the project.
Google’s Web Vitals guidance, updated in 2024, treats a page as good when its main content appears within 2.5 seconds, it responds within 200 milliseconds and its elements barely move while loading (a CLS of 0.1 or less).
If the website sells to consumers, Spain’s Law 11/2023 has required accessibility for e-commerce services since 28 June 2025, except for microenterprises with fewer than 10 staff and up to €2 million in turnover or balance sheet.

seccions.titol: How we work and how long it takes
seccions.text:
We start with a thirty-minute call with no commitment. From what you tell us, we give you a fixed quote in writing within five working days, with the pages, the features and what’s left out.
Then we organise the structure, design the screens and build the website. You review and sign off each phase before we move on, and before launch we test every page and feature we agreed on.
A simple website is ready in three to four weeks. A custom website takes six to ten weeks from when we have the copy and images.
The first month after launch is included. After that, monthly maintenance is optional.

seccions.titol: The website is yours
seccions.text:
When we finish, the website is yours. The domain, hosting and logins are in your name, with no lock-in.
We show you how to edit it, so you can change copy and photos without depending on anyone. And the person you talk to is the one who designs and builds. When a project needs it, trusted collaborators join in.

seccions.titol: Web design in Girona, la Selva and the Costa Brava
seccions.text:
We’re in Caldes de Malavella and mostly work with businesses in Girona, la Selva, the Empordà and the Costa Brava. We meet in person when it’s needed and handle the rest remotely.
If your customers come from abroad, the website can be in several languages, each with its own page and address. Levinil’s is in Catalan, Spanish and English, and Can Junqué’s is also in German.
If you also want to be found on Google, local SEO starts at €450 a month, with your Google Business Profile included.

seccions.titol: Websites you can check
seccions.text:
Can Junqué is a rural holiday home in Ullà. We made its brand, photos and a website with direct booking and payment. Levinil, a signage company in Sils, now shows 48 projects on a website in three languages.
For Catherine Rusconi, a coach in Switzerland, we built two English websites, Breath Coaching and My Happy Retreats. And for the ERAM campaign, for a university arts school in Salt, we developed the interactive website with creative direction by Aire i Forma.

seccions.titol: What to tell us
seccions.text: You don’t need to arrive with everything decided. It helps more to know what you want to achieve, what’s holding you back and what material you have.

seccions.titol: From Girona, with companies across Spain
seccions.text: We work from Girona and run projects for companies across Spain. We agree on the starting point, the materials and who signs off each phase, and from there we work remotely without any trouble.

faqs.q: How much does a website cost in Girona?
faqs.a: A simple template website starts at €1,200 and a custom WordPress business website at €3,000. An online shop starts at €4,000. Prices exclude VAT, and we give you a fixed quote in writing within five working days.

faqs.q: What determines the cost of a web project?
faqs.a: The number of pages and languages, who writes the copy and what the site has to connect to. That’s why one five-page website can cost twice as much as another.

faqs.q: WordPress or bespoke development?
faqs.a: We build custom business websites with WordPress, with original design and no template, and you can edit them yourself afterwards. For bookings, private areas or ERP connections, custom development starts at €8,000.

faqs.q: Can you work with an existing brand or website?
faqs.a: Yes. First we look at what can be kept and what’s holding you back. Sometimes improving the website you have is enough, and sometimes it’s better to start again.

faqs.q: How long does it take to build a website?
faqs.a: A simple website, three to four weeks. A custom website, six to ten weeks from when we have the copy and images.

faqs.q: Who owns the website when it’s finished?
faqs.a: You do. The domain, hosting and logins are in your name, with no lock-in.

faqs.q: Can the project include SEO work?
faqs.a: Yes. The custom website already comes with basic SEO. If you want to work on search every month, monthly SEO starts at €450 a month, with your Google Business Profile and a monthly report.

faqs.q: Does a new website guarantee more bookings or enquiries?
faqs.a: No. A clear website helps people understand what you do and get in touch, but your offer, demand and being found all count too. To know whether it works you need data and time.

cta.titol: What should your website do?
cta.text: Tell us what you sell and what the website needs to do. We reply within 24 working hours, and within five working days you have a fixed quote in writing.

seccions.titol: What we do and what it costs
seccions.text:
We do the strategy and the work too, so your brand, website and lead generation all pull in the same direction. We give you a fixed quote in writing within five working days.
These are the starting prices for each service, all excluding VAT.

seccions.titol: We start with what’s holding you back
seccions.text:
A website that doesn’t explain the service well, ads that lead to a page that doesn’t convince, or a brand that says different things in each place can look like separate problems. First we look at how they connect and what’s holding you back.
It might be a business that already works or an offer that still needs presenting. The first job is to sort out what we know, what data is missing and what needs deciding before doing anything else.
If what you need is a new website or a rebuild of the one you have, we are also a web design agency in Girona. We build websites with WordPress or custom development, connected to the brand and the content, so people understand the service and get in touch.

seccions.titol: The marketing diagnosis
seccions.text:
If you don’t know where to start, the diagnosis is the first step. It starts at €2,500, excluding VAT. In three or four weeks we review your website, how people find you on Google and in AI answers, your ads, your sales materials and your competitors.
You come away with a twelve-month plan with a budget and the measures to tell whether it works, and we present it in a meeting with management. It’s for deciding before committing to anything else.

seccions.titol: What we decide with you
seccions.text:
Depending on the starting point, we review the offer, who you’re talking to, the messages, the path to getting in touch and the role of each channel. Every recommendation ends in a task with someone who can do it.
Having a website and social media is normal now. According to Idescat, in the first quarter of 2025, 88.9% of Catalan companies with 10 or more employees and internet access had a website and 75.2% used some form of social media. The question is whether they bring you customers.

seccions.titol: From diagnosis to a plan you can carry out
seccions.text:
A long list of ideas is not a work plan. We separate what can start now, what needs material or sign-off and what is best left for later. The time your team has counts too.
In the proposal we set out what we deliver, who approves each decision and whether the website, brand or campaigns are included or separate. That way you can compare what you pay with what you need.

seccions.titol: If you want us to run it
seccions.text:
If someone already does the work but nobody directs it, a fractional CMO starts at €2,100 a month. That’s two days a month, with quarterly priorities, the budget, coordination of your team and agencies, a meeting every two weeks and a monthly report.
If you have no marketing team, or a team of one, the outsourced marketing department starts at €5,000 a month. That’s forty hours a month, with direction, a quarterly plan and the work done by us. Both options have a six-month minimum term.

seccions.titol: How we start
seccions.text:
We start with a thirty-minute call with no commitment. It helps if you tell us what you sell, which website and channels you have, what enquiries come in and what worries you right now.
From there we see whether something specific is enough, like a website or a campaign, or whether more needs sorting out. Then we review decisions with data, without taking the first idea for granted.
Before comparing visits, check how they were measured, because the cookie guide from Spain’s data protection authority (AEPD), updated in May 2024, notes that analytics cookies need informed consent.

That change also reaches Google, whose Business Profile guidelines, current in 2026, ask businesses to be represented as they are recognised in the real world across signage, stationery and other branding.

If the brand will be used online, test its colours against WCAG 2.2, updated in 2024, which asks for a contrast of at least 4.5 to 1 for normal text and 3 to 1 for large text, with logos exempt.

For My Happy Retreats, Catherine Rusconi’s retreat brand, we refreshed the logo and built the website.
These are two examples. Not every business needs the same pieces or a complete change.

seccions.titol: How long it takes
seccions.text: A new brand takes five to eight weeks. Photos, names and copy that need preparing can make it longer.

en.descripcio: 3D renders and visualisations for property developers and estate agents. Interiors from €350 per image, packs from €2,000 and two review rounds.

seccions.titol: What’s included and what it costs
seccions.text:
A single-room interior starts at €350 per image and a pack of 3 to 5 images at €2,000, excluding VAT. Both include two review rounds. The price goes up with bespoke furniture or if the finishes haven’t been decided yet.
A development exterior has no starting price, because it adds the surroundings, with the neighbouring buildings, the street, the planting and the sky. A detached house is not the same as a block on a narrow street. A quotation from us is fixed and in writing.

seccions.titol: We start with what the development needs to explain
seccions.text:
Each image answers a different question. An exterior view places the building, an interior helps people understand a space and a shared area shows what goes unnoticed on a plan.
Before doing anything we decide which parts of the project need to be seen, based on the type of development, the unit types and the launch stage. That way no images are made that never get used.

seccions.titol: Which images a development usually needs
seccions.text: The number of images and their adaptations are agreed before starting. This table helps decide.

seccions.titol: What material we need
seccions.text:
We can start from the plans, dimensions, the model if there is one and material references. If modelling is needed or information is missing, we include it in the quote.
We need to know who signs off the architecture and finishes. A reference helps guide the work, but it doesn’t replace what has been approved in the project.

seccions.titol: Two review rounds
seccions.text:
In the first round we go over the cameras and volumes with you. In the second, the materials, light and finish. That way a change is made while it still costs little, not once it affects the whole series.
The quote sets out who reviews and which dates depend on each sign-off. A new unit type or a change to the project is assessed separately.

seccions.titol: The images have to match what is delivered
seccions.text: In housing, advertising has to match what will actually be delivered. So it pays to commission the final images once the specification is closed, and to mark as a proposal anything still being decided.

seccions.titol: How long it takes
seccions.text: A render takes one to two weeks per image, depending on the starting material. In a development the first images take longest, because they set the camera, light and finishes for all the others.

seccions.titol: For the website, the brochure and the campaign
seccions.text:
A landscape image for the website and a portrait one for a campaign need different framing. If we know the uses from the start, we prepare each image with the space it needs.
As well as the 3D, we can handle the development identity, the website and the campaigns to attract buyers, so everything tells the same story.

seccions.titol: From Girona, with developers across Spain
seccions.text: Plans, reviews and deliveries are handled remotely, so we work with developers and estate agents across Spain and abroad. At the start we agree what gets reviewed, which files you send us and who decides.

faqs.q: How much does a property render cost?
faqs.a: A single-room interior starts at €350 per image and a pack of 3 to 5 images at €2,000. All excluding VAT and with two review rounds.

faqs.q: How much does an exterior render of a development cost?
faqs.a: It has no starting price, because it depends on the surroundings. A building with its street, planting or an aerial view is quoted per project, with a fixed quote within five working days.

faqs.q: Is an architectural visualisation the same as a render?
faqs.a: Yes. In architecture, a 3D visualisation and a render are the same image and cost the same.

faqs.q: Can you work from plans if there is no 3D model yet?
faqs.a: Yes. First we look at what information the plans contain and what modelling is needed, and we include it in the quote.

faqs.q: Can we show finishes that are still being decided?
faqs.a: Yes, if they are marked as proposals and you agree who signs them off. Before an image is used to sell, it must be checked against what has been approved.

faqs.q: How long do the renders for a development take?
faqs.a: One to two weeks per image, depending on the starting material. The first images take longest.

faqs.q: Can the commission include the development website and marketing?
faqs.a: It can. We can handle the identity, 3D, website, SEO and campaigns, and the proposal sets out what each part covers and the ad spend, if any.

faqs.q: Do you work with developers outside Spain?
faqs.a: Yes. All the work is done remotely, so we work with developers and estate agents across Spain and abroad.

cta.titol: What does your development need to show?
cta.text: Send us the plans, the unit types and where you’ll use the images. We reply within 24 working hours, and within five working days you have a fixed quote in writing.

en.titol: Product renders for catalogues, brands and online sales
en.resum: 3D product renders for catalogues and online shops, from €250 per image with two review rounds.
en.descripcio: 3D product visualisation for catalogues, online shops and campaigns. crida studio connects imagery, brand and web for businesses throughout Spain.

seccions.titol: What’s included and what it costs
seccions.text:
A product render on a neutral background with a single view starts at €250 per image, excluding VAT, and a pack of 3 to 5 images at €2,000. The starting price includes two review rounds. It goes up if the model has to be built from scratch, if the materials are difficult or if more views are needed.
Scenes with a setting, colour or finish variants and product families have no starting price, because they depend on how many combinations need to be shown. We tell you in the quote, which is fixed and in writing.

seccions.titol: Renders of bioreactors and lab equipment
seccions.text:
We also make renders of bioreactors, skids, filtration systems and lab equipment. They start at €450 per image, excluding VAT, because the engineering CAD has to be cleaned up and every part has to be accurate, from the probes to the connections.
They show what a photo can't, such as the inside of a vessel, how a single-use bag is fitted, a skid that hasn't been built yet or a GMP suite that can't be photographed. A cutaway, a full GMP suite or an animation is quoted separately.

seccions.titol: We start by putting the catalogue in order
seccions.text:
Before making any image we go through the catalogue with you. How many references there are, which ones share a shape and what each image has to explain.
Every image in a collection needs the same camera, the same light and the same background. That way the products can be compared and, when a new reference arrives, you don’t start from scratch.

seccions.titol: One model and all its finishes
seccions.text:
Changing a colour or a finish reuses the model and the light, and only the material changes. Changing the dimensions or the parts is a different model.
If you sell on Google Shopping, Merchant Center asks for a different image for each variant, with the exact colour, finish and material. So it pays to decide from the start which combinations are really on sale, to avoid making images of options that don’t exist.
To prepare the quote we need to know four things.

seccions.titol: What material we need
seccions.text:
We can start from a 3D model, dimensioned drawings, photographs or finish samples. With what you have we see whether the product needs modelling or whether what already exists can be reused.
Before an image is used to sell, someone on your team who knows the product reviews it. A render has to show what the customer will receive.

seccions.titol: The same images for the shop, the catalogue and the campaign
seccions.text: Product pages in an online shop, a printed catalogue and a campaign call for different proportions and space. We agree the framing and resolution for each use before calling the images finished.

seccions.titol: Two review rounds
seccions.text:
Every render includes two review rounds. In the first we go over the shape and framing with you. In the second, the materials, colour and light, compared with the samples.
First we close one reference and, once you approve it, we apply the same to the rest of the family. The quote sets out what happens if the product changes midway through the job.

seccions.titol: How long it takes
seccions.text: A render takes one to two weeks per image, depending on the starting material. In a catalogue the first reference takes longest, because it sets the camera, light and background for all the others.

seccions.titol: Images, brand and website in one place
seccions.text:
As well as renders, we build brands, websites and online shops. If the images are going on a website we also look after, we prepare them with the catalogue or online shop experience in mind.
We work from Girona with companies across Spain and abroad. Reviews are done remotely, on the images themselves.

faqs.q: How much does a product render cost?
faqs.a: A product render on a neutral background with one view starts at €250 per image, and a pack of 3 to 5 images at €2,000. All excluding VAT and with two review rounds. Variants and scenes are quoted separately.

faqs.q: How much do the images for a whole catalogue cost?
faqs.a: It depends on how many references and finishes it has. For 12 models with one view each, the starting point is 12 times €250, that is, €3,000 excluding VAT. The other finishes of each model are quoted separately, because they reuse the model and the light and only the material changes.

faqs.q: Must the product already be manufactured to create a render?
faqs.a: No. If there is a model, dimensioned drawings or good references, it can be done before manufacturing. You need to be clear about what is approved and what is still a proposal, and review the image before using it to sell.

faqs.q: Does a render always replace product photography?
faqs.a: Not always. If the products already exist and there are few variants, a photo shoot can work out cheaper. With many variants, or if the product hasn’t been manufactured yet, a render fits better.

faqs.q: How many revisions are included?
faqs.a: Two review rounds on every render.

faqs.q: How long does a product render take?
faqs.a: One to two weeks per image, depending on the starting material you have.

faqs.q: Are models and working files included?
faqs.a: We agree it in the quote. Final images and working files are different things, and it says what is delivered of each.

faqs.q: Do you work with companies outside Spain?
faqs.a: Yes. We’re in Caldes de Malavella, in Girona, and work remotely with companies across Spain and abroad.

cta.titol: Which products do you need to show?
cta.text: Tell us how many references and finishes the catalogue has and what material you have. We reply within 24 working hours, and within five working days you have a fixed quote in writing.

en.titol: B2B marketing that reaches the people making the decision.
en.resum: B2B marketing for companies with long sales cycles and technical buyers, with a diagnosis from €2,500.
en.descripcio: B2B marketing for companies with long sales cycles and technical buyers. Diagnosis from €2,500, website, SEO and Google Ads, working with your sales team.

seccions.titol: What we do and what it costs
seccions.text: We can do one thing or handle everything, depending on what you need. These are the starting prices, excluding VAT. We give you the fixed quote in writing within five working days.

seccions.titol: In a company, no single person decides
seccions.text:
The person who finds a supplier is rarely the one who approves the purchase. Management, purchasing, the technical team and the people who will use the product have different doubts, and all of them need to be convinced.
So before choosing channels, we look with you at what you sell, who takes part in the decision and which questions hold a sale back. That tells us which pages and materials are worth preparing.

seccions.titol: The same argument on the website, in the campaign and in the meeting
seccions.text:
We put the services or products in order and work on positioning and brand architecture, so that the website, campaign pages and sales materials say the same thing. When it helps explain a solution, we make a video or 3D renders of the product.
SEO and Google Ads campaigns follow from that base. We measure the enquiries your team accepts as opportunities, as well as visits and form submissions.

seccions.titol: We work with the people who know the customer
seccions.text:
We can work with management and sales, or support an existing marketing team. On each project we agree who provides the information, who signs off and how what the sales team hears in meetings reaches us.
If what’s missing is someone to run marketing every month, we offer fractional direction and the full department, with a six-month minimum term.

seccions.titol: Work you can see
seccions.text: For Breath Coaching we did the strategy, the content architecture and the website for an offer aimed at both companies and individuals. The case is just below.

seccions.titol: Where we start and how long it takes
seccions.text:
We usually start with the diagnosis, which takes three or four weeks and can be commissioned on its own. If you already know what you need, we start with that project, with the scope, schedule and deliverables in writing before we produce anything.
A custom website takes six to ten weeks from when we have the copy and images. SEO needs three to six months to show, and with Google Ads enquiries can arrive from the first month.

seccions.titol: From Girona, with companies in Spain and abroad
seccions.text: We’re in Caldes de Malavella, in Girona, and work remotely with companies across Spain and abroad. We meet in person when it’s needed. We work in Catalan, Spanish and English.

faqs.q: How much does B2B marketing cost?
faqs.a: It depends on what you need. The diagnosis starts at €2,500, a custom corporate website at €3,000 and Google Ads management at €790 a month. Fractional marketing direction starts at €2,100 a month. All excluding VAT.

faqs.q: Do you work with manufacturers and industrial companies?
faqs.a: Yes. It’s the type of company we know best, because David Monje ran marketing at a bioreactor manufacturer for three and a half years.

faqs.q: Can one project include campaigns and web development?
faqs.a: It can. Before quoting we define what goes into brand, content, website and campaigns, and each part has its own deliverables.

faqs.q: Can you work with our marketing or sales team?
faqs.a: Yes. We can take on a specific project or work alongside your team. Before starting we agree who handles what and who signs off.

faqs.q: Do you only do the strategy, or the work as well?
faqs.a: Both. With the diagnosis you leave with a plan your team can carry out. If you want us to do it, we quote it per project or as an outsourced marketing department.

faqs.q: How do we assess whether an activity is working?
faqs.a: We agree what will be measured before starting. With your team we look at the quality of the enquiries and how many become opportunities, when we have that figure.

faqs.q: How long does it take to see results?
faqs.a: With Google Ads enquiries can arrive from the first month. SEO needs at least three to six months.

faqs.q: Do you work with companies outside Spain?
faqs.a: Yes. We work remotely with companies across Spain and abroad, in Catalan, Spanish and English.

cta.titol: What does your company sell, and to whom?
cta.text: Tell us what you offer, who you sell to and where sales get stuck. We reply within 24 working hours, and within five working days you have a fixed quote in writing.

en.titol: Campaigns and websites for institutions that need to communicate clearly.
en.resum: Accessible websites, campaigns and content for town councils, universities and public bodies across Spain.
en.descripcio: Campaigns, content and web development for institutions, universities and public bodies. crida studio works from Girona with defined objectives and approvals.

seccions.titol: What we do for town councils and universities
seccions.text:
We build websites, campaign pages and content for town councils, universities and public bodies across Spain. We can also handle just the development, working from the creative direction of another agency or your own team.
We start from what people need to understand and do, from a call for applications or a registration to an online procedure, and from who has to approve each part.

seccions.titol: Budget, tender and timing
seccions.text:
We don’t have a published rate for public bodies. If you have tender specifications, we study them and prepare a proposal with the deliverables, responsibilities and review criteria. If not, we give you a fixed quote in writing within five working days.
For reference, on our pricing page a simple website starts at €1,200 and a custom WordPress business website at €3,000, excluding VAT. A custom website takes six to ten weeks from when we have the copy and images.

seccions.titol: Every initiative has several audiences
seccions.text:
A university campaign, a public programme and a cultural initiative aren’t explained the same way. People need to understand what’s on offer, who it’s for, what they need to prepare and what the next step is.
Before designing anything we review the brief, the information available and what each audience needs to do. The website has to help people find the answer, and the campaign has to say the same as the website.

seccions.titol: Clear sign-offs before production
seccions.text:
We agree on the main contact, the review calendar and the criteria for signing off each part. If several departments are involved, we decide what each one approves and how changes are gathered.
We can handle the strategy, campaign identity, content and web development, or work as the development partner of an agency or creative team. The proposal makes clear who does what.

seccions.titol: Accessibility, required in the public sector
seccions.text:
In the Spanish public sector, Royal Decree 1112/2018 requires an accessibility statement that is linked from every page of the website and updated at least once a year.
In the July 2023 review by Spain’s Web Accessibility Observatory, only 2 of the 750 local government websites analysed, 0.27%, were estimated to be fully compliant with all of its checks.
That’s why we look after mobile, languages, readability and accessibility from the start. Before closing the scope we review hosting, integrations, documentation and maintenance.

seccions.titol: From Girona, for all of Spain
seccions.text:
We’re based in Caldes de Malavella, in Girona, and work with public bodies across Spain. Meetings, languages and delivery are agreed for each brief.
We meet in person when it’s needed, for example to present the proposal or review a phase, and handle the rest remotely.

seccions.titol: The ERAM case
seccions.text:
For the ERAM campaign, for a university arts school in Salt, Aire i Forma did the creative direction and we developed the interactive website, adapted to every screen.
The case shows the technical work and how we collaborate with another team. Each side signs its own part.

faqs.q: How much does a website for a town council cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the brief and the tender. For reference, a custom WordPress business website starts at €3,000 excluding VAT. We give you a fixed quote in writing within five working days.

faqs.q: What do you need to assess a project or tender brief?
faqs.a: The objective, audiences, available materials and timetable give us a starting point. Requirements and acceptance criteria let us assess feasibility, prepare questions and define a proposal.

faqs.q: Can you develop a website from an existing creative direction?
faqs.a: Yes. We can act as a development partner alongside the creative team or lead agency. We review design, content, interactions and requirements before defining the implementation and deliverables.

faqs.q: Will the website meet accessibility rules?
faqs.a: We work on it from the start with the WCAG guidelines and prepare the accessibility statement required by Royal Decree 1112/2018, linked from every page. Conformance has to be checked with an accessibility review before launch.

faqs.q: Do you maintain the website afterwards?
faqs.a: Yes, if it’s part of the brief. The first month after launch is included, and after that monthly maintenance is optional.

faqs.q: Do you work with universities and public bodies outside Girona?
faqs.a: The offer covers projects throughout Spain. Collaboration, languages, meetings and handover are agreed around the brief and its requirements.

faqs.q: Do you work in Catalan and Spanish?
faqs.a: Yes. We work in Catalan, Spanish and English, and the website can be in all three, each language with its own page.

faqs.q: Which public bodies have you worked with?
faqs.a: In Projects you can see the ERAM campaign, for a university arts school in Salt, with Aire i Forma. In 2026 we also published a study of the websites of Girona’s town councils.

cta.titol: Do you have an initiative to communicate?
cta.text: Tell us the goal, the audiences and the timeline. If you have tender specifications, they help us assess the scope. We reply within 24 working hours.

en.titol: Business process automation for small businesses
en.resum: Processes that run by themselves with n8n or Make, from €1,200 per process, with testing and documentation.
en.descripcio: Business process automation from €1,200 for small and mid-sized companies. We connect your tools with n8n or Make, with testing and documentation.

seccions.titol: What we do and what it costs
seccions.text: Automating a process means a task with clear rules gets done by itself. For example, an enquiry from your website reaches the CRM with all its details, an order alerts the warehouse, or every Monday your report is ready. These are our starting prices, excluding VAT.

seccions.titol: We start with a task, not with a tool
seccions.text:
You tell us what repeats in your company, who does it and with which tools. We pick one task, the one that takes the most time or causes the most mistakes, and agree what has to happen at the end for the work to count as done.
We use n8n or Make when they fit, and a custom integration when needed. The tool is chosen by the process you already have and by who will maintain it, not the other way round.

seccions.titol: Which tasks usually make sense
seccions.text:
The ones with clear rules that happen many times. Moving enquiries from the website or email into the CRM, preparing sales records, gathering data for a report, sending an alert when an order or booking comes in, or moving documents from one place to another.
If one part needs to understand a text, such as sorting an email or summarising an enquiry, that is where AI can come in. But many automations do not need it, and then we leave it out.

seccions.titol: We test it before it goes live
seccions.text:
We test the normal path and the odd cases too. What happens if a field is missing, if a tool does not respond or if something arrives that does not fit. In those cases the workflow stops and leaves a task for a person, instead of sending something incomplete.
If you prefer to go step by step, the first version can prepare the work, such as a draft or a record, and a person reviews it before it is sent.

seccions.titol: What you get at the end
seccions.text: The process working and the documentation your team needs to understand it. What each step does, what to do if a password or a field changes, and how to pause the workflow.

seccions.titol: Costs without surprises
seccions.text:
Some tools have their own monthly fee. We tell you in the estimate, before we start, separately from our work. That way you know what you pay once and what repeats every month.
The starting prices of all our services are on our pricing page. The timeline for each automation is written in the estimate, which you get within five working days.

seccions.titol: An example you can try
seccions.text: On our website, Ona welcomes visitors, asks the questions one by one when someone wants to start a project, and emails us the brief already organised. It is our own project, and it shows how information is collected and passed on without anyone having to copy it.

seccions.titol: From Girona, working with companies across Spain
seccions.text:
We are based in Caldes de Malavella, in Girona, and work remotely with companies across Spain and abroad. A video call to understand the task and access to the tools involved is all it takes, and the rest happens by email.
To get started, we only need an example of what comes in, what should come out and who checks it today. Please do not send passwords or sensitive data in the first email.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to automate a process?
faqs.a: From €1,200 excluding VAT, with two or three tools, testing and documentation. If a tool has a monthly fee, we tell you in the estimate.

faqs.q: Which tools do you use?
faqs.a: n8n or Make when they fit, and a custom integration when needed. We decide based on the tools you already use.

faqs.q: Can you connect an existing ERP or CRM?
faqs.a: First we check what access and permissions the system allows. With that we confirm what can be done and put it in the estimate.

faqs.q: Does every automation need AI?
faqs.a: No. Many tasks only need clear rules and connected tools. AI comes in when something needs interpreting and its output can be checked.

faqs.q: What happens if something fails?
faqs.a: The workflow stops and leaves a task for a person, instead of sending something incomplete. The documentation explains what to do and how to pause it.

faqs.q: Who maintains the workflow?
faqs.a: It is written in the estimate. It can be someone on your team using the documentation we leave, or us, and tool licences are separate.

faqs.q: How long does an automation take?
faqs.a: It depends on how many tools need connecting. The timeline is written in the estimate, which you get within five working days.

faqs.q: Do you work outside Girona?
faqs.a: Yes, we work remotely with companies across Spain and abroad.

cta.titol: Which task repeats every day in your company?
cta.text: Tell us about it with an example. We reply within 24 working hours, and within five working days you have a fixed written estimate.

en.titol: Motion graphics and explainer videos for businesses
en.resum: Explainer videos and motion graphics in Girona, with script, animation and voice-over, from €2,500.
en.descripcio: Animated explainer videos and motion graphics for companies across Europe. 60 to 90 seconds with script and voice-over, from €2,500. Quote in five days.

seccions.titol: What the video includes and what it costs
seccions.text:
A 60 to 90 second explainer video starts at €2,500, excluding VAT. It includes the script, 2D animation, voice-over in one language and the web version.
You can add 3D of the product or process, a version in three languages and versions for trade fairs and social media. Before we start you get a fixed quote in writing, within five working days.

seccions.titol: When an explainer video makes sense
seccions.text:
It makes sense when your sales team explains the same thing every week and wants a video to do it for them. Also when you need to show something that can’t be filmed, because it happens inside a machine or doesn’t exist yet.
Before we start, we agree on what viewers need to understand and what they should do next. A good video opens the conversation or helps explain an offer, but it doesn’t sell on its own.

seccions.titol: 2D animation, 3D or filmed footage
seccions.text:
2D animation works well for ideas, steps and data. 3D is for showing a product from the inside or a process you can’t see from outside. If you already have filmed footage, we combine it with the animation.
We choose the technique based on what needs showing and the material you have. We never present reference images as our own work, or show something as real when it’s still a design.

seccions.titol: How we make the video
seccions.text:
We start with a meeting to understand what you sell, who to and what people usually ask. Then we write the script. You review it, we change what’s needed and we don’t move on to animation until you’re happy with it.
Next we design the style and the first scenes with your brand. Once you sign them off, we animate the whole video, add the voice and review it with you before delivery.
At the end you get the files agreed in writing, in the right format for each place it will be shown. If the product changes often, we plan from the start which parts can be updated without redoing everything.

seccions.titol: Motion graphics and animated video production in Girona
seccions.text:
We’re in Caldes de Malavella, in la Selva. We mostly work with businesses in Girona, la Selva, the Empordà and the Costa Brava, and we meet in person when it’s needed, for example to see the product or the plant.
A 60 to 90 second motion graphics video, with script, 2D animation and voice-over in one language, starts at €2,500 excluding VAT. First we write the script, which you review and approve. Then we design the style and the first scenes with your brand, and finally we animate the video, add the voice and deliver it.
The rest we handle remotely, with companies across Spain too. We agree on the starting point, the material and who signs off each phase.
If you also need the website, 3D renders or SEO, we do that too, so everything comes out with the same brand.

seccions.titol: What changes the price of a video
seccions.text:
The price depends on the length, the scenes, whether there’s 3D or filming, the languages and the versions. A short video can cost more than a long one if it needs a lot of new material or detailed 3D.
To compare quotes, check which formats, versions, review rounds and usage rights each one includes. Voice, music and other licences should be listed separately, so you know what you’re paying for.

seccions.titol: What to tell us for the quote
seccions.text:
It helps to know who the video is for, the question the piece should answer, where it will be shown and what material you already have. Also your brand, a video you like and who has to approve the technical side.
With that and a thirty-minute call with no commitment, we give you a fixed quote in writing within five working days. It says what we’ll do, which versions are included and what’s left out.

faqs.q: How much does an explainer video cost?
faqs.a: A 60 to 90 second video with script, 2D animation, voice-over in one language and a web version starts at €2,500, excluding VAT. 3D, more languages and versions for trade fairs and social media are extra.

faqs.q: How long should an explainer video be?
faqs.a: The starting price is for a 60 to 90 second video, which is enough to explain a process or a piece of equipment. If you need it for trade fairs or social media, we prepare versions for each place.

faqs.q: What does an animated video production company do?
faqs.a: It turns an explanation into a video. It writes the script, designs the scenes, animates them and adds voice and music. We handle the whole process, from the first meeting to the final files.

faqs.q: Does every project need filming?
faqs.a: No. Many explanations work with 2D animation, graphics or 3D, with no camera. If you need to show the real product, we combine filmed footage with the animation.

faqs.q: Can you use our existing visual identity?
faqs.a: Yes. We start from your logo, colours and typefaces, and before designing we look at how you use them on your website and other materials.

faqs.q: Can you plan several languages?
faqs.a: Yes. The starting price includes voice-over in one language, and it can go up to three, for example Catalan, Spanish and English. Each version has its own text, voice and subtitles.

faqs.q: Can the same piece work on every channel?
faqs.a: Not as it is. Each place needs a different format, length and sound. That’s why we agree on the versions for trade fairs and social media before we start.

faqs.q: Where are you and who do you work with?
faqs.a: We’re in Caldes de Malavella, in Girona. We mostly work with businesses in Girona, la Selva, the Empordà and the Costa Brava, and remotely with companies across Spain.

cta.titol: What should your video explain?
cta.text: Tell us what you sell and who to. We reply within 24 working hours, and within five working days you have a fixed quote in writing.

en.titol: English-speaking web design and marketing on the Costa Brava
en.resum: Websites, SEO, Google Ads and Google Maps for businesses on the Costa Brava, in three languages, from €1,200.
en.descripcio: English-speaking web design and marketing studio near the Costa Brava. Websites, Google Maps, SEO and direct booking for businesses on the coast.

seccions.titol: What we do and what it costs
seccions.text:
We build websites and handle SEO, Google Ads and branding for businesses on the Costa Brava, in Catalan, Spanish and English. You get a fixed quote in writing within five working days, after a thirty-minute call with no commitment.
These are our starting prices, all excluding VAT.

seccions.titol: A studio in Caldes de Malavella, close to the coast
seccions.text:
We are based in Caldes de Malavella, in the Selva area, close to the southern Costa Brava. Our working area is the whole coast, from Blanes, Lloret de Mar and Tossa to Sant Feliu de Guíxols, Platja d’Aro, Palamós, Begur, L’Escala and Roses. We also work remotely with companies across Spain.
Meetings, proposals, website copy and campaigns can all be in English, Catalan or Spanish. That helps if you moved here from abroad and run a business on the coast, or if your customers come from other countries and need an English version written for them, using the words they actually search for.
The work can cover strategy, brand, web design on WordPress or as a custom build, SEO, Google Ads, AI assistants and automation. Every project starts with what the business sells, who buys it and which language they use when they search for it.

seccions.titol: Planning around high and low season
seccions.text:
On the Costa Brava, the calendar sets the pace. The Costa Brava Girona Tourist Board’s occupancy report for 2025 counts 246,321 bed places in total across hotels, campsites, apartments and rural tourism, extra beds included. Bed places on offer, which leave out establishments fully or partly closed for the season, came to 144,127. Many businesses open, close or change pace with the summer.
That is why it makes sense to plan the big changes for the quieter months. A new website, photos, copy in three languages or a review of your Google profile all need time from the owner, and in July that time does not exist. In high season the job is answering enquiries, keeping track of bookings and adjusting Google Ads campaigns to the season.

seccions.titol: Customers who search in several languages
seccions.text:
In 2025, more than half of the overnight stays in hotels, campsites, apartments and rural tourism on the Costa Brava were by guests from outside Spain. According to the Tourist Board, guests from Spain, Catalonia included, accounted for 41.9%. French guests made up 20%, Dutch guests 10.1%, German guests 7.2% and British guests 5.8%.
Each of them searches in their own language, on Google, on Maps or in an AI assistant. Residents from abroad do the same when they look for a restaurant, a builder or an estate agent. In the study we ran in 2026 on Girona accommodation websites, 402 of the 503 sites on the Costa Brava offered two or more languages.

seccions.titol: A website in three languages that Google can read
seccions.text:
Google recommends a separate URL for each language, hreflang tags that connect the versions and a single language per page, without side-by-side translations. It advises against redirecting visitors automatically based on their language and suggests links so people can switch to the version they want.
Each version should be written for the person reading it. The English page should name what someone from abroad searches for, the Catalan and Spanish pages speak to local customers, and all three should share the same prices, services and contact details. It is worth building the website so another language, such as French, can be added later.

seccions.titol: Direct bookings without leaving the platforms
seccions.text:
Booking platforms put you in front of a lot of people, but every booking through them pays a commission. In a factsheet from September 2026, the European Commission explains that businesses on Booking.com in the European Economic Area can now freely set their prices and conditions, including on their own website.
A website that sells directly needs a visible booking button on every page, an engine that works well on a phone, prices or a date search, and a quick way to ask questions, such as WhatsApp. The same applies to a restaurant table, a boat trip or a cooking class.
You do not need to leave the platforms. The aim is for your website to keep the bookings from people who already know you or come back every year, and to know which channel brings each booking. That way you know what each customer costs and where the effort pays off.

seccions.titol: Google Maps, where many customers find you first
seccions.text:
Google says local results are based mainly on relevance, distance and prominence. Verified profiles with complete details are more likely to appear, and more reviews and positive ratings can help a business rank locally. There is no way to pay for a better local position.
On the coast, a profile needs seasonal hours and special opening times, photos that show the place as it is, the right category and replies to reviews in the guest’s language. It is worth reviewing it alongside the website so both say the same thing.

seccions.titol: How long it takes
seccions.text:
A simple website is ready in three to four weeks, and a custom website takes six to ten weeks from when we have the copy and images. SEO is three to six months of work at the very least.
That’s why it pays to start in the low season and reach the summer with your website and profile ready. If you need bookings or enquiries now, Google Ads can bring them from day one.

seccions.titol: How we work and projects you can review
seccions.text:
We start with a conversation about the business, the customers and the season. Before any production starts, the proposal sets out the scope, budget and timing. Below you can see two international projects and a rural tourism project in the Baix Empordà.
For My Happy Retreats, a wellbeing brand for the Swiss market, we worked on the brand refresh, an accessible website, content architecture, SEO and SEM. My Happy Retreats and Breath Coaching, both run by Catherine Rusconi, and Can Junqué, a rural tourism business in the Baix Empordà, have their own case pages below.

faqs.q: How much does a website cost on the Costa Brava?
faqs.a: A simple template website starts at €1,200 and a custom WordPress business website at €3,000, excluding VAT. The final price depends on the pages, the languages, who writes the copy and what it has to connect to, such as a booking engine.

faqs.q: Can the project be run in English?
faqs.a: Yes. Meetings, proposals, documents, website copy and campaigns can all be in English, Catalan or Spanish. If part of your team prefers Catalan or Spanish, languages can be mixed within the same project.

faqs.q: Does our website really need three languages?
faqs.a: It depends on who buys from you. In 2025, more than half of tourist overnight stays on the Costa Brava were by guests from abroad, so English is usually needed, while Catalan and Spanish reach local customers. Each version should be complete and have its own URL, rather than a translated menu over a page in another language.

faqs.q: Should we stop selling through booking platforms?
faqs.a: Usually not. Platforms bring guests who would not find you otherwise. The aim is for your website to take the bookings it can, especially from returning guests and people who already know your name, with a clear booking engine and visible prices. Prices on each channel are your decision, based on your own figures.

faqs.q: How long does it take to get the website ready?
faqs.a: A simple website, three to four weeks. A custom website, six to ten weeks from when we have the copy and images. If you want to be ready for the high season, count back from the summer.

faqs.q: Do you also run Google Ads for the season?
faqs.a: Yes. Management starts at €790 a month, with search campaigns, lead tracking and a monthly report. Ad spend is on top, you pay it straight to Google, and it makes sense from €900 a month.

faqs.q: How do I choose a web design agency?
faqs.a: Ask for work you can check, a fixed quote in writing and who will actually do the work. With us you talk to the person who designs and builds, and the website is yours, with the domain, hosting and logins in your name.

faqs.q: Do you only work with tourism businesses?
faqs.a: No. Tourism weighs heavily on the coast, but the same approach works for shops, restaurants, clinics, estate agents and companies that sell to other businesses. We start with who your customers are, where they search and in which language, and then decide what the website and campaigns need.

cta.titol: Do you run a business on the coast?
cta.text: Tell us what you sell, who your customers are and which languages they speak. We reply within 24 working hours, and within five working days you have a fixed quote in writing.

en.titol: Hotel and holiday rental websites for Girona and the Costa Brava
en.resum: Websites for hotels, campsites, rural homes and apartments across Spain, with direct booking and languages, from €1,200.
en.descripcio: Websites for hotels, campsites, country houses and holiday apartments in Girona and the Costa Brava, with direct booking, languages, Google Maps and SEO.

seccions.titol: What goes into a website for a hotel, campsite or holiday rental
seccions.text:
An accommodation website has to show what a stay is like, let guests book without going through a booking portal and show up when someone looks for somewhere to stay in the area. That is why we plan design, copy, booking, languages and SEO together from the start.
Each type of accommodation has its own booking journey. A campsite sells pitches and bungalows, a hotel sells rooms and a country house is often rented out whole. A campsite on the Costa Brava needs a different website structure from a country house inland in the Selva.

seccions.titol: What it costs and how long it takes
seccions.text:
A simple template website starts at €1,200 and a custom WordPress business website at €3,000. The custom website can be connected to the booking engine you already use, and if you need your own booking system, custom development starts at €8,000. All excluding VAT.
A simple website is ready in three to four weeks, and a custom website takes six to ten weeks from when we have the copy and images. You get a fixed quote in writing within five working days.

seccions.titol: What we found on 675 Girona accommodation websites
seccions.text:
Our study analysed the home pages of 675 hotel, campsite, country house, guesthouse and apartment websites across the province of Girona on 31 October and 1 November 2026. Of these, 487 (72.1%) have a booking engine or button and 515 (76.3%) offer two or more languages. Yet only 103 (15.3%) use structured data to tell Google they are a lodging business.
These figures are minimums, because our program reads the HTML without running JavaScript and misses anything that loads later. Even so, they show where there is most room to improve. Most sites (617, or 91.4%) adapt to mobile screens, but fewer than a third tell Google what type of accommodation they are or show prices on the home page.

seccions.titol: Direct booking that works all the way through
seccions.text:
A booking button is not enough if it leads to a form or to a page the guest does not understand. In the study, 196 of the 675 sites (29.0%) only have a booking button or link, which may lead to an engine or to a contact form. That is why we test the whole journey, from the home page to the booking confirmation.
If you already use a booking engine, we first check what it allows and how it fits into the website. If bookings start with an enquiry, the website should say so clearly and ask only for what is needed, such as dates and number of guests.
It also helps to keep a clickable phone number or WhatsApp link and prices or a date search close at hand. In the study, 379 sites (56.1%) have WhatsApp or a clickable phone number, but only 210 (31.1%) show prices or a date search on the home page.

seccions.titol: Languages for guests from abroad
seccions.text:
If your guests come from France, the Netherlands or Germany, your website should speak their language. In the study, English appears on 71.0% of sites, French on 61.9%, German on 23.9% and Dutch on 13.3%. On the Costa Brava, 402 of 503 sites (79.9%) offer two or more languages.
Each language needs its own URL and hreflang tags, so Google knows which version to show to whom. Google explains that localised versions of a page are only treated as duplicates if the main content is left untranslated. That is why each version carries the full translated text, not just the menu, and links to all the others.

seccions.titol: Google Maps, SEO and data Google can understand
seccions.text:
When someone searches for a place to stay nearby, Google shows local results in Maps and Search. According to Google Business Profile Help, these results are mainly based on relevance, distance and prominence. Prominence also takes into account reviews and how many websites link to the business. Your website should show the same name, address and phone number as your listing.
For SEO, each room type, pitch or house is best given its own page, with a clear title, a meta description and a single H1. In the study, 73.6% of sites have a meta description and 53.9% a single H1. Structured data from schema.org tells Google what kind of accommodation you run. Types include Hotel, Campground, BedAndBreakfast and VacationRental.

seccions.titol: Marketing for hotels and holiday rentals
seccions.text:
We also run marketing for hotels, campsites and rural guesthouses on the Costa Brava and across Spain, with local SEO, the Google Business Profile, Google Ads and direct booking, so you depend less on Booking.
We start with the data you already have, where bookings come from, which ones pay commission and which searches bring guests, and decide together where the budget goes.

seccions.titol: Accommodation across Spain
seccions.text:
We’re based in Caldes de Malavella, in Girona, and work with accommodation businesses across Spain. We agree on the starting point, the materials and who signs off each phase, and from there we work remotely without any trouble.
The study data comes from Girona, but what it measures applies to any accommodation, on the coast, in the mountains or in a city. Before we start, we review your website against those same points.

seccions.titol: The Can Junqué project
seccions.text:
For Can Junqué, a rural hospitality project with direct booking, we worked on identity, photography, UX/UI, web development and integrations to build an independent booking channel. The project shows how presenting a place and booking it can be part of the same experience.
The case describes the work we did. A website alone does not guarantee higher occupancy, and a system that suits a country house may not be the best fit for a campsite or a hotel.

seccions.titol: How we work and what we need to get started
seccions.text: We start with how you receive bookings today, where your guests come from and which languages they speak. Then we review your current website against the study criteria, agree the structure and move on to design and development. Before going live, we test the booking flow on a phone in every language.

faqs.q: How much does a website for a hotel or holiday home cost?
faqs.a: A simple website starts at €1,200 and a custom WordPress business website at €3,000, excluding VAT. Connecting your booking engine is quoted separately, and your own booking system starts at €8,000.

faqs.q: How do I create a website for my hotel?
faqs.a: Start with what it has to do, which is show the accommodation, take bookings and show up on Google. We design and build it with WordPress or custom code, connected to your booking engine, and hand it over with all the logins in your name.

faqs.q: Can you connect the website to the booking engine I already use?
faqs.a: It depends on the engine. Some can be embedded in the page and others open their own booking page, often on a subdomain. We first check what options yours offers and how the journey looks on a phone. If anything limits the integration, we will tell you before design work starts.

faqs.q: How many languages should an accommodation website have?
faqs.a: The languages your guests speak. In our study of 675 accommodation websites in Girona, English appears on 71.0% and French on 61.9%. A few well-translated languages with hreflang work better than many half-finished ones. If you have booking data by country, it helps us decide where to start.

faqs.q: How do I get my accommodation to appear on Google Maps?
faqs.a: You appear on Google Maps through a Google Business Profile. Google says complete and accurate information helps a business show up in local search. On the website side, we check that the name, address and phone number match the listing and that the listing links to the right page.

faqs.q: Do you work with accommodation outside Girona?
faqs.a: Yes. We work with hotels, campsites, rural holiday homes and apartments across Spain, remotely and with the same phases. We meet in person when it’s needed.

faqs.q: Will a new website make me less dependent on Booking.com?
faqs.a: We cannot promise that. A website can make it easier for people who already know you to book directly, but bookings also depend on price, availability, reviews and day-to-day work. To see whether it is working, compare direct and portal bookings over time, across similar seasons.

faqs.q: How long does it take to build the website?
faqs.a: A simple website, three to four weeks. A custom website, six to ten weeks from when we have the copy and images. Before launch we test the booking on mobile in every language.

cta.titol: How would you like to receive bookings?
cta.text: Tell us what accommodation you have, how bookings reach you now and which languages you need. We reply within 24 working hours, and within five working days you have a fixed quote in writing.

en.titol: Marketing for biotech, bioprocess and pharma companies
en.resum: Marketing, websites, SEO, 3D renders, trade shows and international sales for biotech, bioprocess and pharma companies.
en.descripcio: Marketing, websites, SEO, Google Ads, 3D renders and trade shows for bioprocess and lab equipment makers, distributors, CDMOs, CROs and biotech startups.

seccions.titol: Who we help in biotech, bioprocess and pharma
seccions.text:
This service is for companies that sell technology or services to biotech and pharma. Each one has a different buyer and a different sales cycle, so the marketing has to fit the people who make the buying decision in each case.
In the end, they all sell to pharma and biotech companies that buy by committee, where engineering, production, quality and procurement look for different things on the website, from technical data to GMP documentation or after-sales service.
Since October 2026, crida studio has run the SEM strategy for PharmaBios Innova, which designs custom bioreactors and fermenters.

seccions.titol: Positioning and websites to compete with the big corporations
seccions.text:
A mid-sized equipment maker competes with corporations that have huge catalogues and sales teams in every country. So it needs to make clear where it is different, for example in direct access to engineering, in custom equipment or in how it supports scale-up from lab to pilot plant and production.
The website has to prove it, product line by product line. Each product needs its own page, with volumes, materials, single-use or stainless steel options, how FAT and SAT are run, which qualification documents are delivered and a clear button to request a quote.

seccions.titol: Branding and websites for science-led biotech startups
seccions.text:
We do branding and websites for science-led biotech startups that need to explain a complex technology to investors, partners and technical buyers.
It covers the name and identity, a website that explains the platform or pipeline without overpromising, mechanism figures and the deck template. A brand starts at €3,500, excluding VAT.

seccions.titol: New markets, distributors and AI-assisted sales
seccions.text:
Before entering a country, it pays to know who buys there, which competitors are active and whether to sell direct or through a distributor. We run that analysis with your sales team, then prepare the website in the local language, the campaigns and a distributor kit with datasheets, presentations, images and videos.
AI and automation help with long sales cycles. An assistant can answer questions from your technical documentation, your CRM can flag when a trade show contact comes back to the website, and sales visits can be better prepared. A person always checks the output.

seccions.titol: How a project with us starts
seccions.text: We start with a conversation about what you make or the service you offer, who you sell to and where you want to grow. It helps to have your current website, the countries where you sell and your planned trade shows at hand. If needed, we can sign a non-disclosure agreement before seeing drawings or client data. Then we propose scope, budget and timeline in writing. If you have no marketing team, we can also act as your outsourced marketing department.

faqs.q: Can you write about GMP and 21 CFR Part 11 on the website without overpromising?
faqs.a: Yes, with care. Section 11.10 of 21 CFR Part 11 requires anyone using closed systems to create, modify or maintain electronic records to apply controls such as system validation and audit trails. Equipment can help a customer comply, and the same goes for GMP, but compliance depends on the customer’s process. That is why someone from your engineering or quality team reviews these texts.

faqs.q: How do you tell a success story when the pharma client won’t let you use its name?
faqs.a: The case can be told without the name, with the type of company, the scale, the problem and what was done, always with the client’s permission and review. Public material also helps, such as application notes or trade show talks, along with a technician’s testimonial if the company approves it.

faqs.q: Can the project be run in English?
faqs.a: Yes. Meetings, proposals, website copy and campaigns can all be in English, Spanish or Catalan. In this sector English is usually the main language of the website. For markets such as Germany, each language needs its own complete version, reviewed by someone who knows the product.

faqs.q: How do you measure marketing when a sale takes months to close?
faqs.a: We look at what happens before the order. How many quote and demo requests arrive, from which channel, which come from companies and which from universities, and how many become an opportunity in the CRM. We review this with the sales team to decide where to put the effort.

faqs.q: How much does marketing for a bioprocess company cost?
faqs.a: It depends on what you need. A diagnosis with an audit and a twelve-month plan starts at €2,500, fractional marketing leadership at €2,100 a month, a new brand at €3,500 and a render of a bioreactor or lab instrument at €450 per image, all excluding VAT. You get a fixed written quote within five working days.

faqs.q: Do you work with companies outside Spain?
faqs.a: Yes. We work from Girona with manufacturers and biotech companies across Europe, in English, Spanish or Catalan. Work runs over video calls and email, and we can meet at trade shows such as ACHEMA or BPI Europe.

faqs.q: Which biotech and pharma companies have you worked with?
faqs.a: We run the Google Ads campaign for PharmaBios Innova, and the case study is public in our projects section, with what we did and how it is measured.

cta.titol: Tell us what you make and who you sell to
cta.text: Tell us which equipment or services you offer, which countries you sell in and what you want to improve. We will reply in English, Spanish or Catalan and suggest where we would start.

en.titol: Fractional marketing director for manufacturers and B2B companies.
en.resum: Part-time marketing leadership or a full outsourced marketing department, for companies that sell to technical buyers.
en.descripcio: A fractional marketing director or a full outsourced marketing department for B2B manufacturers. From €2,100 a month, with a six-month minimum term.

seccions.titol: Who an outsourced marketing department is for
seccions.text:
It is for companies of twenty to five hundred people that sell to other businesses and have no marketing team, or just one person. Often the managing director or the sales director runs marketing in their spare time, or agencies do things with nobody to direct them.
It is also for manufacturers launching a product, entering a new country or preparing a big trade show who need someone experienced for a few months, without hiring a full-time director.

seccions.titol: Two levels, a fractional CMO or the full department
seccions.text:
With the fractional CMO level, a senior lead sets the priorities for each quarter, manages the budget and coordinates your team and the agencies already working with you. It is two days a month, with a meeting every two weeks and a monthly report.
With the full department, we also do the work, from the website, SEO and Google Ads to LinkedIn, technical content and materials for trade shows and distributors. It is forty hours a month, and if you need more time we will talk about it.

seccions.titol: It starts with a diagnosis of your marketing
seccions.text:
Before we start, we spend three to four weeks reviewing your website, how you appear on Google and in AI answers, your ads, sales materials and competitors. The result is a twelve-month plan with a budget and the measures we will use.
The diagnosis can be booked on its own. If you then continue with the direction level or the department, the plan is the starting point and is not repeated.

seccions.titol: How much an outsourced marketing department costs
seccions.text:
The diagnosis starts at €2,500. The fractional CMO level starts at €2,100 a month and the full department at €5,000 a month. Prices exclude VAT and we give you a fixed quote in writing.
The service has a six-month minimum term and then continues month to month. Six months is the minimum time for a plan, a trade show or SEO to produce results that can be measured.

seccions.titol: How we work with your team
seccions.text:
We work with the tools you already use and with access to your CRM and website data, so decisions come from quote requests and not just from visits. Every month you know what has been done, what worked and what comes next.
We work with a limited number of companies at a time. If we already work with a manufacturer of the same type of equipment, we will tell you before we start.

faqs.q: What is an outsourced marketing department and how is it different from an agency?
