faqs.q: ¿Cuánto cuesta hacer una web para una empresa?
faqs.a: Una web sencilla con plantilla cuesta desde 1.200 € y una web corporativa a medida con WordPress, desde 3.000 €. Una tienda online parte de 4.000 €. Todos los precios son sin IVA, y el final depende de las páginas, los idiomas, quién escribe los textos y con qué se tiene que conectar.

faqs.q: ¿Cuánto cuesta el SEO al mes?
faqs.a: El SEO mensual parte de 450 € al mes, sin IVA. Incluye el SEO local en Girona y Cataluña, la ficha de Google, las páginas clave y un informe cada mes. Es un trabajo de tres a seis meses como mínimo. Si lo necesitas para mañana, lo tuyo es Google Ads.

faqs.q: ¿Cuánto cuesta gestionar Google Ads?
faqs.a: La gestión de Google Ads parte de 790 € al mes, sin IVA, e incluye campañas de búsqueda, la medición de contactos y un informe mensual. La inversión en anuncios va aparte y la pagas directamente a Google desde tu cuenta. Tiene sentido a partir de 900 € al mes de inversión, porque por debajo no hay datos suficientes para mejorar las campañas.

faqs.q: ¿Cuánto cuesta una marca o un logotipo?
faqs.a: Una marca nueva parte de 3.500 € sin IVA e incluye logotipo, colores, tipografía, un manual breve y las aplicaciones básicas. Una renovación parte de 4.000 €. Un logotipo solo no lo hacemos. Trabajamos la marca entera para que cuente lo que haces hoy.

faqs.q: ¿Cuánto cuesta un render 3D o un vídeo explicativo?
faqs.a: Un render de producto con fondo neutro parte de 250 € por imagen, y el interior de una estancia, de 350 €. Un pack de 3 a 5 imágenes parte de 2.000 €. Un vídeo explicativo de 60 a 90 segundos, con guion, animación 2D y locución, parte de 2.500 €. Todo sin IVA.

faqs.q: ¿Cuánto cuesta automatizar un proceso o tener un asistente de IA?
faqs.a: Automatizar un proceso con dos o tres herramientas parte de 1.200 € sin IVA, con pruebas y documentación. Ona, nuestra asistente de voz para la web, cuesta 149 € al mes con 12 meses de permanencia, o 350 € al mes sin ella, más 750 € de puesta en marcha. El mantenimiento está incluido y el consumo de IA va aparte, según el uso.

faqs.q: ¿Los precios llevan IVA?
faqs.a: No. Todos los precios de esta página son sin IVA y son precios de partida. El presupuesto cerrado te lo damos por escrito en cinco días laborables, después de una llamada de treinta minutos sin compromiso.

faqs.q: ¿Por qué no publicáis tarifas cerradas?
faqs.a: Porque dos webs de cinco páginas pueden costar una el doble que la otra según quién escribe los textos, cuántos idiomas llevan y con qué tienen que conectarse. Con el precio de partida sabes dónde empiezas, y con el presupuesto por escrito sabes la cifra.

faqs.q: ¿Qué pasa con una web de 2.000 € del Kit Digital?
faqs.a: El programa ya ha terminado. Por 2.000 € se hacía una plantilla con tus textos y un año de alojamiento. Si tienes una y te funciona, no la cambies. Si no te trae clientes, antes de rehacerla miramos qué le falta.

faqs.q: ¿Quién hace el trabajo?
faqs.a: David Monje. Cuando el proyecto lo pide entran colaboradores de confianza, pero la persona con la que hablas es la que diseña y construye.

faqs.q: ¿De quién es la web cuando se termina?
faqs.a: Tuya. El dominio, el alojamiento y los accesos van a tu nombre y no hay ninguna permanencia.

faqs.q: ¿Cuánto se tarda?
faqs.a: Una web sencilla, de tres a cuatro semanas. Una web a medida, de seis a diez semanas desde que tenemos los textos y las imágenes. Una marca nueva, de cinco a ocho semanas. Un render, de una a dos semanas por imagen.

faqs.q: ¿Qué pasa después del lanzamiento?
faqs.a: El primer mes está incluido. A partir de ahí puedes contratar el mantenimiento mensual o no.

faqs.q: Quant costa fer una web per a una empresa?
faqs.a: Una web senzilla amb plantilla costa des de 1.200 € i una web corporativa a mida amb WordPress, des de 3.000 €. Una botiga en línia parteix dels 4.000 €. Tots els preus són sense IVA, i el final depèn de les pàgines, els idiomes, qui escriu els textos i amb què s'ha de connectar.

faqs.q: Quant costa el SEO cada mes?
faqs.a: El SEO mensual parteix de 450 € al mes, sense IVA. Inclou el SEO local a Girona i Catalunya, la fitxa de Google, les pàgines clau i un informe cada mes. És una feina de tres a sis mesos com a mínim. Si ho necessites per a demà, el que toca és Google Ads.

faqs.q: Quant costa gestionar Google Ads?
faqs.a: La gestió de Google Ads parteix de 790 € al mes, sense IVA, i inclou campanyes de cerca, la mesura de contactes i un informe mensual. La inversió en anuncis va a part i la pagues directament a Google des del teu compte. Té sentit a partir de 900 € al mes d'inversió, perquè per sota no hi ha prou dades per millorar les campanyes.

faqs.q: Quant costa una marca o un logotip?
faqs.a: Una marca nova parteix de 3.500 € sense IVA i inclou logotip, colors, tipografia, un manual breu i les aplicacions bàsiques. Una renovació parteix dels 4.000 €. Un logotip sol no el fem. Treballem la marca sencera perquè expliqui el que fas avui.

faqs.q: Quant costa un render 3D o un vídeo explicatiu?
faqs.a: Un render de producte amb fons neutre parteix de 250 € per imatge, i l'interior d'una estança, de 350 €. Un pack de 3 a 5 imatges parteix de 2.000 €. Un vídeo explicatiu de 60 a 90 segons, amb guió, animació 2D i locució, parteix de 2.500 €. Tot sense IVA.

faqs.q: Quant costa automatitzar un procés o tenir un assistent d'IA?
faqs.a: Automatitzar un procés amb dues o tres eines parteix de 1.200 € sense IVA, amb proves i documentació. L'Ona, el nostre assistent de veu per a la web, costa 149 € al mes amb 12 mesos de permanència, o 350 € al mes sense, més 750 € de posada en marxa. El manteniment hi és inclòs i el consum d'IA va a part, segons l'ús.

faqs.q: Els preus porten IVA?
faqs.a: No. Tots els preus d'aquesta pàgina són sense IVA i són preus de sortida. El pressupost tancat te'l donem per escrit en cinc dies laborables, després d'una trucada de trenta minuts sense compromís.

faqs.q: Per què no publiqueu tarifes tancades?
faqs.a: Perquè dues webs de cinc pàgines poden costar el doble l'una de l'altra segons qui escriu els textos, quants idiomes porten i amb què s'han de connectar. Amb el preu de sortida saps on comences, i amb el pressupost per escrit saps la xifra.

faqs.q: Què passa amb una web de 2.000 € del Kit Digital?
faqs.a: El programa ja s'ha acabat. Per 2.000 € es feia una plantilla amb els teus textos i un any d'allotjament. Si en tens una i et funciona, no la canviïs. Si no et porta clients, abans de refer-la mirem què li falta.

faqs.q: Qui fa la feina?
faqs.a: En David Monje. Quan el projecte ho demana hi entren col·laboradors de confiança, però la persona amb qui parles és la que dissenya i construeix.

faqs.q: De qui és la web quan s'acaba?
faqs.a: Teva. El domini, l'allotjament i els accessos van al teu nom i no hi ha cap permanència.

faqs.q: Quant es triga?
faqs.a: Una web senzilla, de tres a quatre setmanes. Una web a mida, de sis a deu setmanes des que tenim els textos i les imatges. Una marca nova, de cinc a vuit setmanes. Un render, d'una a dues setmanes per imatge.

faqs.q: Què passa després del llançament?
faqs.a: El primer mes està inclòs. A partir d'aquí pots contractar el manteniment mensual o no.

en.titol: Can Junqué. Brand, photography and a direct-booking website for a rural holiday home in Ullà
en.resum: A new brand, photography and a website with direct booking and payment for a rural farmhouse in Ullà.
serveis: websites for hotels and holiday rentals
en.fet: Brand, photography and a website with direct booking and payment.

seccions.titol: How it started
seccions.text:
Can Junqué is a farmhouse in Ullà, below the Montgrí massif, with rural holiday apartments, a pool and gardens.
Their logo read “Can Junqué Restaurant”. They needed a clearer brand that worked online without losing the rural feel of the house, and a way of their own to take direct bookings and rely less on Airbnb and Booking.com.

seccions.titol: A clearer brand
seccions.text: The old logo was handwritten lettering over a photo of the pool, with the word “Restaurant”. The new one is cleaner, reads well at small sizes and looks the same in the website header, on phones and on the roadside sign.

seccions.titol: Photos first, then the website
seccions.text:
When you’re looking for somewhere to stay, you decide by how a place makes you feel before you get there. That’s why we took the photos before designing anything. The home page opens with the farmhouse and the pool at dusk, with the date search right below.
We took every photo of the house ourselves, from the farmhouse, pool and garden to the lounges, kitchens and bedrooms. We shot them by day, at dusk and at night, so whoever books can see what the house is like at every hour.

seccions.titol: Book and pay without leaving the website
seccions.text:
You open the website, choose your dates and how many of you there are, see what’s free, open the listing and confirm the booking by paying with a card. All without leaving canjunque.com.
Availability is synced with Airbnb and Booking, so Can Junqué can sell directly without losing control of the calendar.

seccions.titol: How is the Can Junqué website built?
seccions.text:
The website runs on WordPress with Elementor, a visual editor for changing text and photos without touching code. With WPML it’s multilingual, in Catalan, Spanish, English and German, so a visitor from abroad can read it in their own language.
Bookings are handled by MotoPress Hotel Booking, which shows the free dates and takes the booking on canjunque.com. Card payments go through WooCommerce and Redsys, the bank’s virtual card terminal. And the calendar is synced with Airbnb and Booking, so the same night can’t be booked twice.

seccions.titol: What else do we do besides the website?
seccions.text:
Beyond the website, we look after the Google Business Profile, SEO, Google Ads and the newsletter. We also made the roadside sign that points the way, 500 metres from the farmhouse.
The Google Business Profile is the listing that shows up on Google Maps and in search when someone looks for a rural holiday home in the Empordà. From there you can go to the website and book directly.
SEO for a rural holiday home means getting it to show up on Google when someone looks for a place to stay in the area. And unlike ads, you don’t pay for every visit.
Google Ads bring people straight to the website, where they book without going through Airbnb or Booking. And the newsletter keeps in touch with past guests, so they feel like coming back.
The sign reads “allotjament rural, casaments i esdeveniments”, Catalan for rural accommodation, weddings and events. It carries the same brand as the website, so drivers on that road recognise the house.

en.titol: Catherine Rusconi. Breath Coaching and My Happy Retreats websites for a Swiss coach
en.resum: Two English websites for a Swiss coach, one for companies and individuals and the other for retreats.
en.fet: Two English websites, with Breath Coaching later reworked.

seccions.titol: How it started
seccions.text:
Catherine runs breathwork and coaching sessions in Switzerland. With Breath Coaching she works with companies and individuals, and with My Happy Retreats she organises wellbeing retreats and holidays in several countries.
Each brand has its own website, in English, and we built both.

seccions.titol: A clearer brand for My Happy Retreats
seccions.text: The old logo had a sun, mixed typefaces and the line “feel good holidays”. The new one is simpler, carries the line “holidays with purpose” and is the one the website uses now.

seccions.titol: The retreats on the home page
seccions.text: The My Happy Retreats home page shows the retreats one by one, with the length, the place, the next dates and a link to find out more. Below that you see who runs them, what happens there and what past guests say.

seccions.titol: One path for companies and another for individuals
seccions.text:
The Breath Coaching website talks to two audiences at once. In the menu and on the home page, companies go in through “Companies” and people through “Individuals”, and each path has its own page.
Later we reworked this website, and we still keep making changes.

seccions.titol: How are the Breath Coaching and My Happy Retreats websites built?
seccions.text:
Both websites run on WordPress with BeTheme, a theme with ready-made layouts that adapts to the brand without coding every page. Both are in English only.
Breath Coaching uses Site Kit, Google’s plugin that connects the website to Search Console and Analytics, so we can see how people find it on Google and what they do there. It also uses SEOPress, which handles the titles, descriptions and the sitemap Google reads.
The cookie banner on Breath Coaching is from CookieYes, and in Europe Analytics uses no cookies until the visitor accepts them.
The newsletter sign-up form sits on the My Happy Retreats home page. It’s connected to Mailchimp, so anyone who signs up goes straight onto the list.

seccions.titol: What else do we do besides the websites?
seccions.text:
For Catherine we look after the Google Business Profile, SEO, Google Ads campaigns and the newsletter.
The Google Business Profile is the listing that shows on Google Maps when someone looks for a breathwork coach nearby. With SEO we get both websites ready to show up on Google when someone searches for breathwork coaching or wellbeing retreats.
Google Ads campaigns bring visits from day one, and you pay per click. The newsletter keeps in touch with everyone who has signed up to My Happy Retreats.

en.titol: Levinil. A three-language website for a signage and graphics company in Sils
en.resum: A website in Catalan, Spanish and English for a graphics and signage company in Sils, with a gallery of 48 projects.
en.fet: A new three-language website, built with Astro.

seccions.titol: How it started
seccions.text:
Levinil makes graphics for vehicles and fleets, brand spaces, signs and wayfinding, and works out of Sils.
They already had a website. What they wanted now was a fast one, made for them, where the quality of their work really showed.
For the gallery they sent us around 270 photos, almost all taken on a phone or sent over WhatsApp. Lots had vans in the background, boxes in the way or the yellowish light of a garage. Fair enough, that’s what photos look like when you take them on the job.

seccions.titol: The gallery comes first
seccions.text:
The home page opens with 48 Levinil projects full screen. Each photo says what kind of job it is, vehicles and fleets, brand spaces or wayfinding, and what the project is called. You can go forward, go back, pause it or view it full screen.
And to be clear, the projects are Levinil’s work. We did the website and the photos.

seccions.titol: Phone photos that look like a photographer’s
seccions.text:
Of the 48 gallery photos, at least 43 came from a phone or WhatsApp. Before putting them online we edited them so that, full screen, they’d look like a photographer took them. It was a big part of the job, and we think it’s what shows most.
In every photo we removed what got in the way and fixed the light and colour. Where needed, we straightened it or widened the frame so Levinil’s work sat right in the middle.

seccions.titol: Out with the distractions
seccions.text: In many photos the wrapped vehicle shared the frame with other cars, trucks or boxes. We took them out so your eye goes straight to Levinil’s graphics.

seccions.titol: Light and colour
seccions.text: Photos taken in garages, in warehouses or early in the morning had a yellowish or flat light. We corrected them so the whole gallery hangs together and the colours of the graphics look clean.

seccions.titol: The home page message
seccions.text: After the gallery, the website sums it up in one sentence, “Applied graphics for the real world”, and one line, “We design, produce and install graphics for vehicles, spaces and environments”. Next to it there’s just one button, “Tell us about your project”. We wanted it to be that simple.

seccions.titol: Three languages, each with its own address
seccions.text:
The website is in Catalan, Spanish and English. Each language has its own address, levinil.com, levinil.com/es and levinil.com/en, and the three versions link to each other so Google shows everyone the one in their language.
Under the hood, the code also says who Levinil is, with the name, email, phone number and logo, so Google understands it without having to guess.

seccions.titol: Contact details at the end of the home page
seccions.text: At the end of the home page, a blue block asks “Parlem?”, Catalan for “Shall we talk?”, and gives you the email, the phone number and where they are. Below come the languages, Instagram, LinkedIn and the legal pages.

seccions.titol: How is the Levinil website built?
seccions.text:
We built it with Astro, which gets the pages ready at the moment they’re published. Your browser receives them already made, with no database behind them, and that’s why they load fast.
Unlike a WordPress site, there are no plugins to keep updating. There’s less that can break, and it gives Levinil almost no work.
The photos are in WebP and come in several sizes, from 480 to 2,400 pixels wide. The browser picks the one that suits it, and a phone downloads the small one.
To give you an idea, the 44 original photos we could trace weighed 75.7 MB. On the website, at desktop size, they weigh 6.4 MB in total, about twelve times less, and at phone size, 1.6 MB.
When the page opens only the first photo loads. The other 47 arrive when the gallery needs them, and they all have their space reserved so the page doesn’t jump around.

seccions.titol: What else do we do besides the website?
seccions.text:
We look after Levinil’s Google Business Profile, so anyone searching for a signage company near Sils finds them on Google Maps.
And their SEO too, which starts with the website itself. The idea is for Google and AI assistants to understand clearly what Levinil does and where it works, so the website says it plainly.

en.titol: Do You Speak Djembe? A landing page, SEO and SEM to take a live show to the US
en.resum: A landing page, SEO and SEM to take a show where the audience plays the djembe to the US.
en.fet: A landing page for the US, with SEO and SEM.

seccions.titol: How it started
seccions.text:
Do You Speak Djembe? is a show created by Doug Manuel. The audience learns to play the djembe with the band, to songs everyone knows, from Otis Redding to Michael Jackson.
Doug wanted to offer it to US companies as an experience for conferences and teams. He needed an English landing page that explained it quickly and led people to book it.

seccions.titol: The home page message
seccions.text: The landing page starts with what a team gains, “Unlock Your Team’s Collaborative Potential”, and right below explains what the show is and where it has been. The “Book now” button appears twice, so nobody has to look for it.

seccions.titol: Booking the show from the landing page
seccions.text: “Book now” takes you to a booking page with Doug’s contact details and a short form. The company says what it wants, a keynote, a team-building session, information about the show or another enquiry.

seccions.titol: How is the landing page built?
seccions.text: The landing page runs on WordPress with Salient and WPBakery, a theme and a visual page builder. With the builder you change text, photos and blocks without touching code, so the page can be adjusted whenever the show changes audience or message.

seccions.titol: What else do we do besides the landing page?
seccions.text:
With the digital strategy we chose who the show was for in the US and what to tell them. The audience is companies looking for an activity for conferences and teams.
We also look after his SEO, Google Ads campaigns and newsletter. The ads bring visits to the page from day one. SEO takes months, but you don’t pay per click. And the newsletter keeps in touch with people who already know the show.
