marketing-plan.intro: Before choosing tools or channels, describe what needs to change in the business and what is preventing it. This preparation helps distinguish a messaging problem from a journey or acquisition problem. With that work done, the first conversation with a studio can focus on what to do first and with which resources.

seccions.titol: What objective should a digital strategy have?
seccions.text:
Selling more is a general direction. To start work, understand who should be reached, which offer makes sense to present and what step the person should take. A quote request, a booking and a commercial conversation need different journeys.
Write the objective as a sentence that can be checked. For example, receiving quote requests for home renovations in the Girona area, or getting bookings to come through the website. If it does not say who, what and which step, it still needs work.

seccions.titol: Bring information that helps decisions
seccions.text:
There is no need to collect reports without context. Customer questions, the reasons an enquiry goes no further and the material you already have can provide very specific information. Visitor and campaign data needs to be read with its limitations in mind.
Analytics data only captures part of your visits. The cookie guide published by the Spanish data protection agency (AEPD), updated in May 2024, states that analytics cookies are not exempt from the duty to obtain informed consent. The figures therefore depend on who accepts the banner. Read them as a trend.

seccions.titol: Choose what makes sense to do first
seccions.text:
If basic service information is unclear, attracting more visitors may leave the same difficulty in place. If the message is clear but the contact route is unsuitable, the priority may lie in the journey rather than in traffic.
Actions need to relate to a need and the practical capacity to carry them out. Separate what can be done now from what depends on other decisions, such as a price change, a new service line or a new hire.

seccions.titol: Define who will review the outcome
seccions.text:
A plan should identify who prepares material, who makes decisions and what information will be reviewed later. Without those responsibilities, a recommendation can remain a document with no follow-through. Naming people and a review point already changes a great deal.
Review is used to test hypotheses and adjust priorities. The commission can focus on one area if that is what the business needs first. A website, a campaign or a brand change can run in phases, with an owner for each phase.

seccions.titol: Five steps to organise before the first meeting
seccions.text: These steps can be done inside the business with the people who know the customers. No special tool is needed. A shared document with the answers is enough to prepare the conversation and to compare proposals using the same criteria.

seccions.titol: An example. A joinery in la Selva that wants more enquiries
seccions.text:
This example is made up. A family joinery in la Selva makes fitted kitchens and wardrobes and wants more presence online. Once the objective is pinned down, what it needs is quote requests from families renovating their homes around Girona.
Callers almost always ask the same things. Whether the workshop takes small jobs, how long it takes and how the process works. The website has only photographs and a phone number. The problem is messaging and journey. More visitors from ads would fill a page that does not answer those questions.
The priority is clear. First, explain the process and the services on the website, with a form that asks what kind of job it is. Then review the Google Business Profile. According to Google’s guidelines, its name should reflect the business’s real-world name, as customers know it. Ads can wait.

seccions.titol: How to decide where to start
seccions.text:
The decision can be made with four questions answered using what you have already collected. Each answer points to one part of the problem. If there is more than one, start with the one that blocks the others, which is often the message.
Having a website is the starting point. According to the Idescat survey on ICT use in companies, 88.9% of Catalan companies with 10 or more employees and internet access have one, and so do 36.0% of those with fewer than 10. What makes the difference is whether it answers what people ask.

faqs.q: Must I first decide whether I need SEO, brand work or a website?
faqs.a: It helps to explain the problem before choosing the discipline. Business information can then be used to assess which area needs attention and what depends on other changes. The answer often combines two things, such as the message and visibility, and then the order matters more than the label.

faqs.q: Do I need analytics data to start?
faqs.a: It is not essential. Customer questions and the reasons an enquiry goes no further already say a lot. If you have analytics, read it as a trend, because analytics cookies require consent and only capture part of your visits. If you do not, note down where enquiries come from.

faqs.q: What if the business has several objectives at once?
faqs.a: That is common. Choose one as the main objective for the first phase and write the others down for later. A main objective lets you organise the message, the journey and measurement around it. When objectives compete, it becomes hard to tell what worked.

brand-guide.intro: A brand may need a clearer explanation without changing all its elements. Before redesigning, understand what does not work and what still has value. This guide helps separate a messaging, application or identity problem before asking for proposals, and helps you decide what is worth keeping and what needs to change.

seccions.titol: When should a brand be redesigned?
seccions.text:
A redesign is worth considering when an identity no longer represents the offer, appears inconsistently or cannot support the applications the business needs. Before changing the logo, identify which of those problems needs solving, because each calls for different work.
Asking only whether someone likes a design can overlook the business problem. It is more useful to observe what they understand when they see the brand and what is missing. Try it with three or four customers and someone from outside.

seccions.titol: Recognise what should be retained
seccions.text: A name, visual features or a way of explaining the offer may have value because customers already recognise them. Assess that recognition before replacing them. Changing a name or a symbol means explaining who you are all over again to people who already knew.

seccions.titol: Test the identity where it will be used
seccions.text:
A visual proposal should be assessed using the applications the business needs. A homepage, service page and everyday document can test different requirements. A product label, a shop sign and a phone icon add other requirements.
At Can Junqué, identity, photography and the website are part of one project, from the sign to the web pages. The case helps show how these pieces relate without assuming every brand needs the same set of applications.
On screen, colour has to be readable. WCAG 2.2 from the W3C requires a minimum contrast of 4.5 to 1 between normal text and its background, and 3 to 1 for large text and interface elements, under criteria 1.4.3 and 1.4.11.

seccions.titol: Prepare a commission that can be compared
seccions.text:
Explain why change is being considered, who the brand addresses, which materials are needed, in which languages, and who will approve decisions. Proposals can only be compared properly when their scope is similar and their assumptions are stated.
The final question is what the brand should be better able to do after the work. That answer is more useful than a list of trends. If the answer is to look more modern, there is still work to do. If it is to explain a new service, work can begin.

seccions.titol: Four steps to review the brand before deciding
seccions.text: This review can be done in a few sessions with the people who deal with customers every day. The aim is to reach the decision with real examples in hand. Opinions about the logo can come later.

seccions.titol: An example. A Girona pastry shop opening a second store
seccions.text:
This example is made up. A long-established pastry shop in Girona opens a second store and starts taking orders online. The owner wants a new logo because hers looks old to her. Before drawing anything, it is worth looking at the brand everywhere it appears.
The review shows that everyone in the neighbourhood recognises the name and the shop sign. The symbol is unreadable at small sizes on a phone, boxes and bags carry different versions of the logo, and the website does not mention orders for celebrations.
The decision is to keep the name and the character of the sign, adjust the symbol so it works small, fix a single version for packaging and social media, and write the website so it explains the orders. Long-standing customers still recognise the shop.

seccions.titol: How to choose between adjusting, evolving or starting again
seccions.text:
The three options make sense in different situations. Deciding before asking for proposals avoids comparing a logo touch-up with a new identity as if they were the same commission. These criteria help place each case.
If the change affects the name, check first whether it can be registered. In Spain, ownership of a trademark is acquired by registration, under article 2 of Trade Marks Law 17/2001. The register is kept by the OEPM, under article 1, which offers a trademark locator for a first check.
In Catalonia, think about language as well. Article 128-1 of the Catalan Consumer Code gives consumers the right to receive fixed information, quotes and invoices in Catalan. Plan for this when you design the shop sign and the stationery.

faqs.q: Is evolving an identity always better than starting again?
faqs.a: It depends on the value of the existing elements and the kind of problem. Review recognition, applications and business direction before deciding. If everyone identifies the name and the sign, evolving is usually the way. If the identity confuses people, starting again may be more honest.

faqs.q: Do I have to change the name if I redesign the brand?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. The name is usually the element with the most recognition and the hardest to replace. Changing it only makes sense if it causes confusion, cannot be registered or the business has changed so much that it no longer fits.

faqs.q: How do I know whether the problem is the logo or the message?
faqs.a: Test it with someone who does not know the company. If they understand what you do but dislike how it looks, it is identity. If they do not understand what you do, it is messaging. If they understand it on the website but not on a label, it is application.

seo-sem.intro: SEO addresses how organic content is discovered and understood. Paid search uses ads to present an offer in paid results. They can complement each other, but are different services with different dependencies.

seccions.titol: What is the difference between SEO and paid search?
seccions.text:
For SEO, pages need to address real needs and be discoverable by search engines. Results depend on quality, search context and many other factors.
In a search campaign, advertising appears under the conditions of the platform and campaign. Ad spend does not buy better organic rankings.
Google confirms this in its guide to how Search works, updated in December 2025, which says it does not accept payment to rank a site higher or to crawl it more often.
In Google Ads, Ad Rank is calculated in each auction from factors such as the competition, the context of the person’s search and the ad quality at that moment, according to its help pages as of 2026.

seccions.titol: What both need in place
seccions.text: A clear offer and a suitable page matter in either approach. Establish who will handle enquiries and what qualifies as a useful contact.

seccions.titol: Decide according to the need
seccions.text:
If explanations of the services are missing, working on content and structure first may make sense. If there is a defined offer, a suitable destination and capacity to handle enquiries, a focused campaign can be assessed.
The decision also depends on resources, demand and the ability to learn from what happens. An investment split cannot be recommended on the sector name alone.

seccions.titol: Compare enquiries and learning
seccions.text:
To compare both approaches, Google Ads offers a paid and organic search report, which requires linking the account to Search Console, according to its help pages as of 2026.
Impressions, clicks and enquiries are different indicators. Review what has been measured and the quality of contacts before concluding that one approach works better.
A useful analysis distinguishes what can be observed from what is still a hypothesis. It also accounts for changes in the offer, season or page behaviour.

faqs.q: Can SEO and paid search run at the same time?
faqs.a: Yes, with defined objectives and resources. Distinguish the work and measurement for each approach while keeping the offer and destination pages consistent.

faqs.q: Is SEO free because it does not pay for each click?
faqs.a: There is no advertising charge for each organic click, but research, content production, development and monitoring require work and resources.

render-brief.intro: A render brief needs to explain what should be seen and what the image will be used for. References and starting material help define the work before talking about the final result. If you gather drawings, measurements, finishes and intended uses before asking for a quote, there will be fewer changes halfway through.

seccions.titol: What should be defined before commissioning a render?
seccions.text:
First, know where each image will go. A website cover, a presentation and a printed piece may need different proportions and sizes. A landscape image for the website and a portrait one for a banner do not come out the same.
Also say whether the image will sit with text, a brand background or other pieces that form a series. If a headline will go over the render, leave clean space for it from the start rather than cropping afterwards.

seccions.titol: Gather the available information
seccions.text: Do not assume a photograph, drawing and model contain the same information. Review what can be used and what will need preparing. A dimensioned drawing says far more than a catalogue photo and saves guesswork later.

seccions.titol: Which files and formats help most
seccions.text:
Send each item in a format that can be opened and measured. A drawing in DWG or DXF keeps its dimensions and can be imported into the 3D software. Autodesk describes DXF as an interchange format used to share drawing data between CAD programs.
For colours and finishes, a RAL code or a physical sample avoids arguments about which grey it is. RAL sets the colour standards for architecture, design, skilled trades and industry. If the model will go into a 3D viewer on the website, Khronos designed the glTF format for the efficient loading of 3D scenes.

seccions.titol: Agree what needs approval
seccions.text:
Review the composition first and the details afterwards. This reveals a difference in interpretation before it affects all the pieces. A white model view, without materials, is already enough to decide whether the framing and light work.
Define who will approve the material and which decisions need to be settled at each stage. A change in shape or framing means redoing more work than a small finishing adjustment. That is why it is decided first.

seccions.titol: A worked example with a developer in Girona
seccions.text:
Take a developer selling a small apartment building off-plan in Girona, a made-up example with no client data. It has the basic project in DWG, a facade elevation and a list of materials. It wants one exterior image for the hoarding and the website, and two interiors of a typical flat.
The brief settles that the exterior will be seen from the street at eye level, in afternoon light, with the real neighbouring buildings. Site photos and the mapping from Spain’s electronic cadastre office help place it. For the interiors, it sends the specification and the RAL codes for the joinery. The volume is approved first, then the materials.

seccions.titol: Make the deliverables clear
seccions.text:
The number of images, sizes, formats, variants and revisions should be written into the commission. If you need the working files, ask for them from the start. Say whether the images will go on social media, on hoardings or on a property portal.
With that information you can ask for comparable proposals and spot what is missing before starting. Two proposals with the same number of images, views and revisions can be compared. The same criteria help check that the result fits its intended use.

seccions.titol: Criteria for deciding and a final checklist
seccions.text: Think about the decision each image should prompt. If a view does not help sell, approve or explain anything, it is probably surplus. A render makes sense when what needs showing does not exist yet or cannot be photographed well. If the space is already built, a photo shoot may be more useful.

seccions.titol: 3D rendering brief template to copy
seccions.text:
Organise the image type, intended uses and available materials before requesting a proposal. The tool below creates a summary you can copy or save, and you decide later whether to share it with crida studio.
If you would rather do it by hand, copy this template into an email or a document and fill in each line with what you have. Any line left empty shows what still needs asking or deciding before you request a quote. The same template lets you compare two proposals on the same criteria.

faqs.q: Will one image work for every application?
faqs.a: It may be adaptable in some cases, but this should not be assumed. Proportion, dimensions, cropping and space for text may require different versions. An image composed for a landscape screen loses part of the scene on a portrait poster. So the formats should be known from the start.

faqs.q: Do I need a 3D model before commissioning a render?
faqs.a: No. Scaled drawings, measurements and reference photos are enough to model from. If a model from the architect or manufacturer already exists, it saves work, but check that it can be exported and that it was built for visualisation rather than only for construction calculations.

faqs.q: How many revision rounds are normal?
faqs.a: It depends on how approval is organised. If the volume and framing are approved first, then materials and light, most changes arrive while they are still easy to make. Agree how many rounds the commission includes and what counts as a change of brief.

faqs.q: Which format should I receive the final images in?
faqs.a: Ask for the final image at high quality for print and a light version for the web. Google explains that WebP offers lossless and lossy compression for web images. If it is going to a printer, ask them for the sizes and resolution they need.

ai-assistant.intro: A website assistant needs one clear job. Guiding someone to a service, explaining information and carrying out an action are different tasks, each with its own sources, permissions and checks. Before launch, decide which questions it will answer, where the answers come from and who takes over the conversation when it cannot help.

seccions.titol: When does a website AI assistant make sense?
seccions.text:
An assistant makes sense when it answers recurring questions or guides a visit using information the business can keep up to date. If the problem is that essential information is hard to find, first improve how the page explains it.
Pick the questions the business actually receives and define what a good answer or next step looks like in each case. A normal month of calls and emails is a good starting point for that list.

seccions.titol: Criteria for deciding whether you need one
seccions.text: Before commissioning an assistant, go through these points with your team. If two or more fail, it is probably better to fix the website or customer service first. An assistant amplifies what you already have, whether it is in order or not.

seccions.titol: Define what it can use to answer
seccions.text: Information needs a source and someone responsible for updating it. When the system does not have an answer, it should say so and offer another route. If the assistant gives old opening hours or conditions, check who is meant to review that information.

seccions.titol: A worked example with a clinic in Girona
seccions.text:
Take a physiotherapy clinic in Girona, a made-up example with no client data. The recurring questions are clear. Opening hours, how to book, which insurers are accepted, what to bring to the first appointment and how to get there. The assistant sticks to those answers and takes them from the pages the reception team maintains.
When someone describes pain or asks for advice about a treatment, the assistant does not assess it. It explains that the physiotherapist will do so at the first appointment and offers to book or to connect them with reception. It does not collect health data either. To book, it sends the person to the booking system, which asks for a name and phone number.

seccions.titol: Test the difficult questions too
seccions.text:
Do not test only the questions that already have a prepared answer. Try what happens when a fact is missing, when someone asks for something outside the scope or when they ask it to do a different job. OpenAI recommends testing an application with input designed to break it.
Review the journey as well as the content. People need to understand what happened, how to correct something and how to continue if the assistant did not help. OpenAI also recommends having a person review outputs wherever possible.

seccions.titol: Checklist before going live
seccions.text: Once the assistant answers the test questions well, the part usually left until last remains. Who monitors it, how errors are reported and when the sources are reviewed. Go through it with your team before switching the assistant on.

seccions.titol: Look at a demonstration critically
seccions.text:
Ona on the crida studio website is our own assistant demonstration. It shows one way of interacting and a tone of voice, but each business needs its own sources and use cases defined before copying anything.
Before launch, settle maintenance, usage costs, responsibilities and review criteria. Usefulness shows in specific tasks. Ask whoever gives the demonstration to try one of your real questions and one that has no answer on your website.

faqs.q: Can the assistant replace website content?
faqs.a: No. Services, limits and contact routes should be understandable without a conversation with the system. The page is what people who do not want to chat read, what Google indexes and what remains if the system fails. The assistant adds one more way to find it.

faqs.q: Does it have to say it is an AI?
faqs.a: Yes. Article 50 of the EU AI Act says people must be informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious, and that the information is given clearly and at the latest at the first interaction. A name that does not mislead and a notice in the chat window take care of it.

faqs.q: What data can the assistant ask for?
faqs.a: The minimum needed for the task. The Spanish data protection authority (AEPD) advises users to check that a chatbot offers a privacy policy identifying the data controller, clear data protection information and whether it keeps learning from conversations. Do not collect health or banking data in the chat.

faqs.q: How will we know it works once it is live?
faqs.a: By reading conversations. Set aside time each week to review a sample, note the unanswered questions and check that handovers reach the team. OpenAI recommends keeping human review and a way for users to report problems. Those notes decide what to update on the website.

web-leads.intro: When a website receives visits but few enquiries, first distinguish who arrives, what they find and where the journey stops. Changing the design or buying more traffic without reviewing these three things can leave the same problem unresolved.

seccions.titol: Are the people arriving able to hire you?
seccions.text:
Start with the source and purpose of visits. Reading an article, searching for the company name and clicking an advert to request a quotation do not express the same need.
For campaigns, review the queries triggering adverts and the areas the offer serves. For organic traffic, look at which pages appear and which searches show them. Visit numbers alone cannot tell you what needs redesigning.

seccions.titol: Is it clear what you sell and who it is for?
seccions.text:
Someone should be able to explain your offer after reading the page opening. Internal terminology, a list of techniques or a headline that could belong to any business makes this harder.
Check whether the content explains the situation you address, what the commission can cover and the next step. A new animation cannot provide missing answers.

seccions.titol: Is there enough information to make a decision?
seccions.text:
Identify questions that arise before hiring. Scope, process, responsibilities and real samples help someone assess a proposal without asking for everything by email.
Without a case study for a service yet, explain precisely how the work is approached and what is delivered. Figures, reviews and examples need support. Clear contact details and company identity also contribute to trust.

seccions.titol: Can someone actually get in touch on mobile?
seccions.text:
Follow the page as a first time visitor. Open the contact route, review fields, check the confirmation message and confirm with the team that an enquiry reaches its intended destination.
Distinguish a functional fault from uncertainty about the offer. A hidden button or broken form needs a different correction from a proposal that does not answer the search.

seccions.titol: What are you counting as a result?
seccions.text:
A contact click, a submitted form and a client contract are different steps. Understand what each tool records before comparing periods or campaigns.
With little activity, a few days may not be enough to evaluate a change. Record what changed alongside the offer, investment and response capacity. Review analytics permissions before treating data as complete.

seccions.titol: What should change first?
seccions.text:
Prioritise faults preventing contact and mismatches between the search and offer. Then organise missing content and design improvements that make it easier to understand.
At crida studio we can review web, brand, SEO and paid search in the same conversation. The commission can focus on the part needing work, with agreed responsibilities and review criteria.

faqs.q: Do I need more visits to receive more enquiries?
faqs.a: Only if current visits fit the offer and the journey already works. Increasing volume does not clarify a problem with unrelated visitors or a failing contact route.

faqs.q: Do I need to rebuild the whole website?
faqs.a: That cannot be decided from enquiry numbers alone. A review may identify specific message, structure, form or campaign changes. A full redesign makes sense when the base limits what the business needs.

faqs.q: How can I tell what has improved?
faqs.a: Define the change, action to observe and period that supports a contextual comparison. Relate enquiries to their quality and subsequent handling as well as visits and clicks.

property-launch.intro: Marketing a development requires images, web content, messaging and the sales response to explain the same project. Before commissioning separate pieces, establish what is approved, what will be offered and what someone requesting information needs to understand.

seccions.titol: Which information can be treated as confirmed?
seccions.text:
Collect the dwelling types, plans, finishes and approved development characteristics. Identify outstanding decisions and who must confirm each one before publication.
This starting document prevents an image showing one option while the page describes another. The responsible team should validate commercial information and the terms being communicated.

seccions.titol: What does the buyer need to recognise?
seccions.text:
The name, identity and message should help identify the development and its offer. Decide their relationship to the developer brand and the team answering enquiries.
A shared direction helps prepare websites, brochures, signage and adverts. Not every item needs producing at once, but know which will be required and which elements they should share.

seccions.titol: What should each render explain?
seccions.text:
Connect each image to something the buyer still needs to understand. Exteriors, interiors, terraces, shared spaces and layouts answer different questions. Several similar views do not necessarily cover them.
Before closing production, review where each image will be used. A website opening, vertical advert and brochure may need adaptations worth planning from the first camera choices.

seccions.titol: What should someone be able to do on the page?
seccions.text:
The page should help locate the project, understand the homes and find how to enquire. Availability, dwelling types and published documents need an owner responsible for updates.
Define what information contact requires and where it goes. With a CRM or sales tool, agree the integration and checks on the journey alongside screen design.

seccions.titol: Separate SEO, campaigns and sales follow up
seccions.text:
Organic content and advertising have different timescales and conditions. A campaign needs a destination prepared for its offer. SEO requires readable pages and content answering relevant searches.
Decide which enquiries matter and how their source will be recorded using available tools and permissions. The sales team should be able to distinguish information requests, arranged visits and opportunities progressing further.

seccions.titol: What should be validated before launch?
seccions.text:
Agree who confirms information, images, web content and messages. Check forms, contact details, documents and mobile use before sending traffic.
crida studio can connect strategy, identity, 3D, web development and SEO or paid search for a development. The scope is defined by phases and materials so every piece has a role in the launch.

faqs.q: Must the website and renders be commissioned at the same time?
faqs.a: Their schedules can differ. It is worth defining uses, messages and formats together so 3D production accounts for website and campaign needs.

faqs.q: Does one development need a complete website?
faqs.a: It depends on the information, dwelling types, languages and sales functions. A dedicated page may be sufficient in some cases and too limited in others.

faqs.q: How can the project be coordinated remotely?
faqs.a: With organised starting material, named approvers and agreed reviews. Plans, references and outstanding decisions need clear versions so the team works from the same base.

interior-render.intro: An interior render helps review the relationship between layout, materials and furniture before a renovation is built. To support a decision, it must be clear what the image represents, which information is validated and what remains a proposal.

seccions.titol: Which question should the image help resolve?
seccions.text:
Start with the outstanding decision. It may be comparing layouts, understanding a piece of furniture or reviewing how materials work together. This question helps choose the camera and level of detail.
A presentation image and one used to compare options need different finishes. Agreeing the purpose avoids spending production time on details likely to change.

seccions.titol: What is needed beyond photographs?
seccions.text:
Photographs help recognise the space but cannot explain all its dimensions and relationships. Plans, measurements and project references support a more precise base.
If information is insufficient, decide how it will be obtained and which preparation the commission covers. A render does not replace technical review or decisions belonging to the renovation professionals.

seccions.titol: How should finishes and furniture be reviewed?
seccions.text:
Identify approximate material references and confirmed selections. Review names, formats and proportions before final finishing to avoid confusing an atmosphere with a specification.
The screen, represented lighting and available references influence perceived colour. When a decision depends on the actual finish, compare it with samples used by the project team too.

seccions.titol: Which views do you actually need?
seccions.text:
One camera may explain an area and hide another. Review which spatial relationships need understanding and which objects could interfere with the view.
When comparing proposals, keep common framing and representation criteria. Changing the camera, furniture and light simultaneously makes it harder to identify the difference that matters.

seccions.titol: What should be approved before the final image?
seccions.text:
Review the layout, reference dimensions and cameras first. Then assess materials, furniture and lighting. This sequence deals with changes at a meaningful stage.
The commission should specify approvers, alternatives and included reviews. Introducing a new layout is different from correcting a finish within an approved proposal.

seccions.titol: How to prepare a commission for crida studio
seccions.text:
Tell us which space needs representing, what decision is outstanding and what material you have. We can assess the work with a professional team or someone preparing a project presentation.
At crida studio we connect 3D work with the communication needs of the commission. If images will also be used on a website, catalogue or property marketing material, include those uses from the beginning.

faqs.q: Can an interior render be produced from photos alone?
faqs.a: Photos can guide the work, but we need to assess whether they explain the space precisely enough. Additional measurements, plans or references may be needed.

faqs.q: Can I compare several layouts?
faqs.a: Alternatives can be defined within the scope. Agree their number, differences and review process before producing each finish.

faqs.q: Can a render show a renovation that does not exist yet?
faqs.a: Yes, as a representation of a proposal. Defined and indicative elements should be clear, especially when images are used to present or market the space.

product-visuals.intro: Choosing between rendering and photography depends on the product, existing material and what the image needs to explain. Combining them may make sense. Compare the same items, views and uses, rather than just the names of the techniques.

seccions.titol: Does the product exist and can it be photographed?
seccions.text:
With a finished, representative sample, photography can record its actual appearance. Consider session preparation and what the pieces need to be shown clearly.
For a product still in development, 3D work can represent a proposal when sufficient information exists. This requires reviewing what is defined and confirming that the final image matches what will be offered.

seccions.titol: How many items and combinations do you need?
seccions.text:
A family may share geometry and vary in finishes, or differ substantially between items. Review this structure before estimating production.
The decision is not just a count of colours. Consider which base can be reused, what needs new preparation and what checks will keep the range consistent.

seccions.titol: Which details must appear exactly as they are?
seccions.text:
Textures, fabrics, transparency, joints and small finishes may be decisive when assessing a product. Define which details need checking against samples and which references will be used.
An attractive image that simplifies a significant characteristic can create the wrong expectation. Someone who knows the item being sold should validate it, whether photographed or represented in 3D.

seccions.titol: Will the images appear in the same catalogue?
seccions.text:
Agree framing, proportions, backgrounds and scale criteria. The series should allow recognition and comparison as well as working in individual presentations.
When combining techniques, prepare a shared visual reference. The aim is continuity across the range without hiding differences a buyer needs to understand.

seccions.titol: What will the website and campaigns need?
seccions.text:
A product page may need a main view, detail and scale references. A campaign may require space for text. A printed catalogue adds its own delivery conditions.
Include these uses in the initial proposal. A set of large images does not automatically cover every adaptation or explain who will prepare later material.

seccions.titol: Decide using an equivalent scope
seccions.text:
Ask proposals to specify items, views, preparation, reviews, formats and subsequent use. You can then compare the actual work being delivered.
At crida studio we can consider 3D visualisation alongside brand and the digital catalogue. The first conversation should establish what material exists and what the person choosing the product needs to understand.

faqs.q: Is 3D work always less expensive?
faqs.a: The technique alone cannot tell you. Modelling, references, variants, finishing, reviews and uses all matter. Compare quotations for an equivalent scope.

faqs.q: Can I combine renders and photographs?
faqs.a: Yes, when they follow a common visual direction and each image has a clear purpose. Agree how scale, finish and range consistency will be reviewed.

faqs.q: Can I reuse a model for new colours?
faqs.a: It may be possible when the geometry remains valid and materials support the adaptation. Changes to finishes, parts or construction need reviewing before being treated as included.

seo-audit.intro: Publishing a website does not mean its services are easy to find. A review should separate technical access, content, identity and observable results. These layers help establish the work a business needs without rebuilding everything each time search changes.

seccions.titol: Can the pages be read and indexed?
seccions.text:
Check which addresses should appear and what each returns. Access errors, redirects and indexing restrictions can prevent a page from participating in search.
Search Console allows URL inspection, status review and testing the published version. A sitemap communicates which pages exist, but submitting one and obtaining a position are different events.

seccions.titol: Is there a clear answer for each service?
seccions.text:
List what someone can hire you to do and connect each need to a page. A list of terms on the homepage does not replace an explanation that helps assess the commission.
Distinguish a search for learning from one for hiring. A guide can explain how to decide and link to a service specifying the studio work, possible scope and proposal requirements.

seccions.titol: Is the company information consistent?
seccions.text:
Review names, contact details and links to genuine brand profiles. Pages should identify who offers the service and where to find information about their work.
Your own cases and precise explanations support the offer. Without a sample, explaining criteria and deliverables is more useful than presenting undocumented experience.

seccions.titol: What changes in AI answers?
seccions.text:
Google says its AI features use the usual SEO fundamentals and do not require a special file. A page should be eligible for search and provide information worth using.
A concise answer, explanation of its criteria and links to verifiable information help readability. Additional text formats may help some systems, but cannot require a brand citation or replace visible content.
In its 2026 guide to generative AI features, Google clarifies that creating llms.txt files will neither harm nor help visibility or rankings in its Search, because Google Search ignores them.

seccions.titol: Which searches are showing your pages?
seccions.text:
Observe queries alongside pages and dates. An impression means a page was shown. A click records a visit from that result. Neither independently establishes a new client.
Record published or revised content and retain the previous reference. Distinguish brand traffic, service searches and queries unrelated to the offer.
Since 31 August 2026, Search Console has offered every website a generative AI performance report showing its impressions in Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode.

seccions.titol: What is worth doing after the review?
seccions.text:
Correct access problems and pages that explain the offer poorly first. Then develop unanswered questions related to clients you can serve.
At crida studio we connect this review with brand, content, web, SEO and paid search. The outcome should define actions, approvers and observation methods as well as listing opportunities.

faqs.q: Do I need llms.txt to appear in Google AI search?
faqs.a: Google does not require it. It can serve as an additional reading format for other systems, but does not replace an accessible, indexable and useful page.

faqs.q: Can I know whether an AI system will recommend my business?
faqs.a: You can check accessibility, review mentions and observe specific results. You cannot assume that every system will use a source or repeat a recommendation.

faqs.q: Does producing more articles always help?
faqs.a: Only when they answer different needs connected to the real offer. If several pages repeat the same answer, review what each contributes and whether they should remain separate.

web-budget.intro: Two website quotations may have different prices because they cover different work. Before comparing them, check whether they start from the same pages, content, functions and responsibilities. A figure alone cannot show what the business still needs to publish and use the website.

seccions.titol: What should the project resolve?
seccions.text:
Explain your offer, audience and what someone should be able to do on the website. Include current limitations and any materials or systems that must remain.
Enquiry generation, a shop and a booking website have different journeys. A quotation should address this context as well as screen numbers.
If it is an online shop for consumers, ask whether the proposal covers Spain’s Law 11/2023, which has required accessibility for e-commerce services since 28 June 2025, except for microenterprises.

seccions.titol: Who prepares structure, copy and imagery?
seccions.text:
Check whether the work includes planning the structure and content, or whether design begins once the business supplies them. This changes the work and schedule dependencies.
Review languages, photographs, illustrations, 3D work and necessary adaptations. For outstanding material from other parties, identify who commissions it and who confirms it is ready.

seccions.titol: What does each included function mean?
seccions.text:
A form, catalogue or integration can have different scopes. Ask what a visitor will be able to do and what the team will be able to edit.
External tools, licences and accounts need a responsible owner. The proposal should explain the connection being implemented, how it is checked and its ongoing costs.
With WordPress, for example, WordPress.org states that only the most recent release in the current series, 7.1 in October 2026, is safe to use and actively maintained, so updates need a named owner.

seccions.titol: Use a table to review the same scope
seccions.text: Use the same criteria for the proposals you receive. Ask for missing answers before judging the price alone.

seccions.titol: What is meant by SEO and measurement?
seccions.text:
Distinguish technical website preparation, content production and ongoing review. SEO in a proposal may refer to only part of that work.
If measurement is included, define the events to be checked and their relationship with user permissions. Installing tools does not itself provide useful enquiry or sales data.
For example, the cookie guide from Spain’s data protection authority (AEPD), updated in May 2024, notes that analytics cookies are not exempt from the duty to obtain informed consent.

seccions.titol: Preparing a proposal with crida studio
seccions.text:
At crida studio we can connect strategy, identity, content, design, development and acquisition. The initial conversation helps establish project needs and worthwhile phases.
We work from Girona with businesses throughout Spain. The proposal defines pieces, responsibilities, approvals and continuity so the business can assess the complete commission.

seccions.titol: What a website costs with crida studio
seccions.text:
crida studio’s starting prices are public. A simple template website starts at €1,200, a custom corporate WordPress site at €3,000 and an online shop at €4,000. Prices exclude VAT.
The pricing page lists what each option includes and what can be added. We send a fixed quote in writing within five working days, using the same scope you used to compare.

faqs.q: Why can two website quotations differ so much?
faqs.a: They may cover different content, design, development, licences, testing or support. Comparing requires knowing what each includes and what the business must arrange separately.

faqs.q: Should maintenance be included?
faqs.a: It can be commissioned in different ways. What matters is clarity about responsibility for updates, incidents, hosting and changes, and the terms of that work.

faqs.q: Can I request a quotation before finishing the copy?
faqs.a: Yes. Explain what exists and what is missing. The proposal can then include structure and content work or identify it as a dependency before design and development progress.

automation-guide.intro: A small business should start with a repeatable task, understandable rules and a named owner. Before choosing n8n, Make or Zapier, define three things. What starts the work, what the finished result should be and when the workflow must stop so a person can review an exception.

seccions.titol: Which task is a good first candidate?
seccions.text:
Start with an operation you can describe from beginning to end. Moving an enquiry into a CRM, preparing a quotation draft or collecting reporting data may be candidates when they repeat and their inputs are recognisable. A frustrating task is not automatically ready for automation. You still need to understand the decisions inside it.
Over a representative period, record who does the work, what information they need, how long it takes and what goes wrong. Include difficult cases. If the team interprets each request differently, the first job is to agree the process. Connecting applications before resolving that difference usually moves the confusion between systems rather than removing its cause.

seccions.titol: What might this look like for a manufacturing business?
seccions.text:
Imagine a manufacturer in la Selva receiving catalogue requests through its website. This is an illustrative approach, not a crida studio project or a reported result. A workflow could check the fields, look for an existing company in the CRM and prepare a sales task containing the requested product and the language used by the enquirer.
If a product reference is missing or two contacts might match, the workflow should request a review. The initial goal can be to organise information without sending a quotation or promising availability. Separating preparation from sending makes the process easier to test with limited consequences. The sales owner first needs to agree what counts as a valid contact and who follows up.

seccions.titol: Does this workflow actually need AI?
seccions.text:
Not when the decision can be expressed through clear rules. Checking for a code, moving a file or flagging a missing field does not require language interpretation. A connection between systems may provide a simpler, more testable solution. Reserving AI for the part that needs interpretation avoids introducing uncertainty into the entire process.
AI may help classify a free-text enquiry or prepare a summary. That requires agreed sources, boundaries on the information it can use and a way to review the output. A convincing answer can still contain an error. Our approach at crida studio separates writing a proposal from authorising its delivery, even when both actions belong to the same commercial journey.

seccions.titol: What should you check in n8n, Make or Zapier?
seccions.text:
Compare the connection you actually need and who will maintain it. An extensive integration catalogue does not confirm that a connector supports your specific action, fields or permissions. Test a representative example, including incomplete data. Then review limits, execution records, responsibilities and the provider’s current terms before committing to a configuration.
n8n’s official documentation covers hosting on your own infrastructure and the associated management work. Make documents scenario error handling. Zapier provides human review steps that can pause a workflow. These differences help frame your evaluation. They do not make one tool universally better. The account access, plan and implementation still need to be checked for your situation.
Before choosing a tool, check which systems you already have, since according to Spain’s INE, 60.9% of businesses with 10 or more employees and internet access used an ERP and 33.9% a CRM in the first quarter of 2026.
Among businesses with 10 or more employees headquartered in Catalonia the share is higher, with 68.2% using an ERP and 41.0% a CRM, according to the same 2026 INE data.

seccions.titol: What happens when work fails or runs twice?
seccions.text:
The design should distinguish a new input from a repeated one and leave a clear signal when it cannot continue. Retrying without checking the current state can duplicate a record, a task or a message. Agree a reference that identifies work already completed and which actions are safe to repeat without creating another effect.
Test empty fields, duplicate contacts, an unavailable service and an interrupted execution. Write down the expected outcome for each situation. The owner should know where to look and how to recover unfinished work. A process that only its original builder understands will be difficult to operate when that person is unavailable or the team changes.

seccions.titol: How do you compare cost with work actually saved?
seccions.text:
Separate initial setup from software subscriptions, hosting, service usage and ongoing maintenance. The cost does not end when two applications connect. Reviewing changes, resolving incidents and checking that the information is still correct also take work. A platform name alone cannot establish the price of a business automation or its likely return.
Compare the same kinds of operation over equivalent periods. Measure the full effort, including reviews and corrections. Time spent preparing a system output is not automatically time saved by the business. Better follow-up or fewer missing details may also be useful outcomes, but decide how you will observe them before claiming that they have improved.

seccions.titol: What should be ready before you switch it on?
seccions.text:
Start with a limited scope and a way back to the manual process. Document account ownership, connections, rules, alerts and the person approving changes. Manage credentials through appropriate secure channels rather than a shared instruction document. Agree which test data should be removed and how the team will identify live work during the transition.
At crida studio, we consider automation alongside the sales journey and the systems a business already uses. The initial conversation can begin with a specific task and representative material that contains no sensitive data. From there, we can define a test, its limits and a proposal. A useful commitment is a verifiable acceptance criterion, not a promise that everything will run by itself.

faqs.q: Can we start without replacing our ERP or CRM?
faqs.a: Possibly, if the system provides the access the workflow needs. Check its connections, permissions and terms first. Having an API does not by itself resolve the implementation.

faqs.q: Can an automation send quotations directly?
faqs.a: A workflow can be designed that way, but preparation and approval should be separate decisions. Commercial conditions and exceptions need clear rules and an accountable owner.

faqs.q: Does every automation need an AI subscription?
faqs.a: No. Many tasks need rules and application connections. Add AI where interpretation has a defined purpose and its output can be reviewed.

faqs.q: Do you work with businesses outside Girona?
faqs.a: crida studio works from Caldes de Malavella with businesses across Girona, Catalunya and Spain, as well as remote clients. Meetings, test scope and maintenance are agreed for each project.

motion-guide.intro: An industrial explainer should help someone understand a product or process before requesting a meeting, specification or quotation. Make four decisions before production. Who the video is for, which question it answers, what it can show accurately and what the viewer should be able to do after watching.

seccions.titol: What should the viewer understand?
seccions.text:
Begin with a specific question from the person buying or using the product. They may need to understand how a machine fits into their process, what changes between configurations or what to prepare for a demonstration. If the brief starts with a list of visual effects, these questions often surface after important production decisions have already been made.
Separate audiences and moments. A technical buyer may need details that do not belong in an initial campaign video. A sales team might use one sequence in a meeting and send another afterwards. Define a main version and adaptations with a clear purpose. Do not assume the same edit will work equally well at an exhibition, on a website and as an operating explanation.

seccions.titol: Should you use filming, motion graphics or 3D?
seccions.text:
Choose according to what exists and what needs to be seen. Filming can show a real setting or action. Animated graphics can organise information, stages and relationships. 3D can represent components or viewpoints that are hard to photograph, provided the source information and review process allow the product to be represented accurately.
Combining techniques can help when each explains something different. A filmed exterior view can establish the product while a represented section explains its internal operation. Identify a representation where it could be mistaken for evidence of the finished product. The choice should improve understanding rather than create a more elaborate visual that still needs the same explanation beside it.

seccions.titol: What should be approved before animation starts?
seccions.text:
Review the information and the order of the explanation first. Then agree scenes, viewpoints, on-screen text and the relationship with narration. A storyboard lets the team discuss these decisions before producing every asset. Adobe describes this visual planning as a way to guide production from the script rather than leaving each shot open to interpretation.
At crida studio, we give each scene a job. It may establish the problem, show an operation, clarify a difference or support the next action. If it simply repeats a sentence without adding visual information, reconsider it. Identify who approves technical details and who reviews the brand language, so changes from different people do not pull the sequence in conflicting directions.

seccions.titol: How might you explain a machine with different configurations?
seccions.text:
Imagine a manufacturer offering one machine with several feeding systems. This is an illustrative approach, not a crida studio success story. A video might establish the shared function, compare the inputs and finish by explaining what information the sales team needs to recommend a configuration. The sequence follows a buyer’s decision rather than a tour of every component.
Compare options at the same scale, with consistent framing and recognisable names. There is no need to animate the entire machine if the buyer only needs to understand where configurations differ. The manufacturer should validate performance, dimensions and operating conditions. If these are undecided, record that in the production documentation rather than presenting a proposal as a final specification.

seccions.titol: What should you provide for a production proposal?
seccions.text:
Collect technical specifications, visual references, relevant dimensions and brand material. If a 3D model exists, its condition, format and permitted use need checking. Having a file does not establish that it is animation-ready. Internal components, materials and moving parts may require additional preparation before the model can support the sequence you want to show.
Include where the video will appear, its languages and the person reviewing its content. Clarify which photographs or footage the studio can use and who will obtain missing material. A video serving several channels needs defined deliverables. The proposal should specify versions, review stages and final files, as well as who retains source material for a later product update.

seccions.titol: How will it work without sound or in another language?
seccions.text:
Check that important information does not depend entirely on hearing narration. Consider on-screen text, captions and the relationship between visuals and sound while writing the script. W3C’s audiovisual accessibility guidance distinguishes resources including captions and transcripts. The appropriate provision depends on the information in the video and how that information is communicated.
An exhibition screen, a phone and a sales presentation create different reading conditions. Test text at its actual display size rather than loading every specification into one scene. For multiple languages, review terminology length and narration pace. Translating after an animation has been signed off can require reworking compositions that previously seemed complete, so agree the language plan before production.

seccions.titol: How can you tell whether it helps sales conversations?
seccions.text:
Define the intended action and how you will observe it before publishing. On a website, that might be continuing to a specification or enquiry. In a meeting, it might be understanding a difference without repeating the explanation. Views alone do not demonstrate increased sales or establish that the people making enquiries are suitable buyers.
Compare equivalent situations and collect the questions that still arise. A recurring question may indicate a missing scene or information needed on the accompanying page. At crida studio, we connect the video with the brand, catalogue and website experience. That gives the brief a concrete purpose and provides the same criterion for reviewing the finished piece after delivery.

faqs.q: How long should an industrial explainer be?
faqs.a: Long enough to answer its specific question without combining too many objectives. The script and viewing context help establish duration and useful versions.

faqs.q: Can it be produced without filming on site?
faqs.a: Sometimes, using graphics, existing material or 3D. Review whether the available information can represent the product accurately and distinguish a proposed design from something already made.

faqs.q: Can we reuse an existing 3D model?
faqs.a: Its format, structure, detail and permissions need checking. It may provide a starting point without being ready for the visual finish or animation required.

faqs.q: Can you plan Catalan, Spanish and English versions?
faqs.a: Yes, these languages can be included in the brief. Text, narration, captions and technical review for each version need to be agreed within the scope.

accessibilitat-web-empreses.intro: If you sell online to consumers or let customers book or sign up for a service on your website, Spain's Law 11/2023 has required that website to be accessible since 28 June 2025. Microenterprises that provide services are exempt, using the law's own definition. A website that only presents your business does not, on its face, fall under what the law calls e-commerce.

seccions.titol: Who the law covers, and since when
seccions.text:
Law 11/2023 brings the European Accessibility Act, Directive 2019/882, into Spanish law. Title I, the part that deals with products and services, has been in force since 28 June 2025 (eighteenth final provision). Article 2.2 lists the consumer services it covers. Among others, these run through a website or an app.
The law defines e-commerce services as services provided at a distance through websites or mobile apps, by electronic means and at the individual request of a consumer, with a view to concluding a contract with that consumer (annex VII, definition 32). As examples, an online shop in Girona, a Costa Brava campsite with online booking or a clinic that takes paid appointments online would fit that definition. A site that only describes the business, on its face, does not.

seccions.titol: Are you a microenterprise? What the exemption means
seccions.text:
Article 3.3 exempts microenterprises that provide services from the accessibility requirements for services and from any related obligation. The law defines a microenterprise as a business with fewer than 10 employees and an annual turnover or annual balance sheet total of no more than 2 million euros (annex VII, definition 16).
On those figures, that takes in many shops, restaurants, small clinics and holiday lets in Girona and la Selva. The exemption is for services, not for the products on the law's list, such as e-readers or payment terminals. And if you reach 10 employees, or exceed 2 million euros in both turnover and balance sheet total, you are no longer a microenterprise under that definition.

seccions.titol: What a website or online shop has to comply with
seccions.text:
Article 3.1 sends services to sections III and IV of annex I. Section III asks for information to reach people through more than one sensory channel, to be easy to understand, with an adequate font size and sufficient contrast, and for websites and apps to be perceivable, operable, understandable and robust.
For e-commerce, section IV adds that identification, security and payment functions must be accessible, and that the accessibility of the products on sale must be stated when the responsible operator provides that information. Article 13.2 asks service providers to explain in their general terms, or an equivalent document, how the service meets the requirements.
Which level? The third additional provision requires at least «the medium level of the generally recognised content accessibility criteria», with the Spanish standard UNE 139803 or its successor as the reference. In WCAG terms, that is read as level AA. EN 301 549 makes it concrete. Version 3.2.1 (2021) takes in WCAG 2.1 up to level AA, and version 4.1.1 (September 2026) moves to WCAG 2.2 and adds an annex for checking against Directive 2019/882.

seccions.titol: How to do a first check in an afternoon
seccions.text: You do not need special tools to find the most common problems. Take the home page, a product page and the form or the basket, and run these tests. Each one maps to a WCAG 2.1 success criterion.

seccions.titol: What can happen if you do not comply, and who checks
seccions.text:
Title I sets no fine of its own. Article 30 refers to the infringement and penalty regime of the relevant sector legislation and, where that makes no provision, to Title III of the consolidated General Law on the rights of persons with disabilities (Royal Legislative Decree 1/2013). Article 30 contains no amounts.
Supervision falls to the authorities each autonomous community designates, Catalonia included (article 27.3). They must check that services comply, follow up complaints and verify that problems have been fixed (article 24). Article 29.2 lets consumers, associations and disability organisations go to the administrative bodies and the courts to demand compliance. There are exceptions, such as disproportionate burden, but they must be justified, assessed and documented, and the results kept for five years (article 16).

seccions.titol: Fix the website or rebuild it. How to decide
seccions.text:
If the site runs on WordPress with a well-built theme, most of the points in the table can be fixed without a rebuild. Contrast, text alternatives, form labels and keyboard focus. If the theme or page builder makes the menu unusable with a keyboard, or the basket and checkout cannot be corrected, a rebuild is usually the better investment.
At crida studio we look before we quote. We check the site with these tests, separate what can be fixed from what needs rebuilding, and put it in writing so you can compare proposals. We do not sell certificates. The law asks that the service be designed and provided in line with the requirements (article 13.1).

faqs.q: My website only has information and a contact form. Does the law apply to me?
faqs.a: On its face, no. The law defines e-commerce as a distance service aimed at concluding a contract with a consumer (annex VII, definition 32). If nothing is bought or contracted on the site, it does not fit that definition. If you add bookings or payments, that changes. When in doubt, ask a lawyer.

faqs.q: We are 8 people with turnover under 2 million. Do we have to do anything?
faqs.a: If you provide services, article 3.3 exempts you from the requirements. Even so, everyone uses your website, and fixing contrast, text alternatives and forms is small work that serves more customers. If you sell products on the law's list, or grow past the figures in annex VII, look at it again.

faqs.q: Do I need to meet WCAG 2.1 or WCAG 2.2?
faqs.a: The law names no version. Article 17 presumes compliance if you follow a harmonised standard whose reference is published in the Official Journal of the EU. EN 301 549 3.2.1 takes in WCAG 2.1 AA and version 4.1.1 WCAG 2.2 AA. As of October 2026, version 4.1.1 is not yet cited there and 3.2.1 remains the reference. Secure 2.1 AA, and aim for 2.2 AA in new work.

faqs.q: Does this guide replace advice from a lawyer?
faqs.a: No. Here we explain what the text of Law 11/2023 says in the BOE and what the technical standards say, with article numbers. If your case is borderline or you have received a complaint, talk to a lawyer. At crida studio we do the technical part and work to the legal advice you are given.

declaracio-accessibilitat-ajuntament.intro: A council website’s accessibility statement has to say how far the site meets the standard, which content is not accessible and why, how to send a complaint and where to escalate it if nobody answers. It must be linked from every page under the word «Accessibility» and reviewed at least once a year. In Spain this is set by Royal Decree 1112/2018, which uses the EU model statement.

seccions.titol: What the accessibility statement has to say
seccions.text:
Article 15.1 of Royal Decree 1112/2018 asks for a «detailed, comprehensive and clear» statement on how the website complies with the decree. At a minimum (article 15.2) it must explain which parts are not accessible and why, with any alternatives, and link to the feedback mechanism and the complaints procedure.
The text follows the model in Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/1523, which public sector bodies in every Member State have to use (article 1 of the Decision). The model’s instructions say to edit or delete the text in italics and remove all the notes before publishing. The mandatory part has these blocks.

seccions.titol: Where it has to be linked and how to publish it
seccions.text:
The statement is published on the website itself and must be reachable from every page through a link called «Accesibilidad», or its equivalent in the language of the page (article 15.1). The usual place is the footer, next to the legal notice.
The EU model’s instructions add that it has to be easy to find, for example from a header or a static footer, and that it must be in an accessible format. If the council has a mobile app, the statement goes on the council’s website next to the download link, or with the information in the app store (article 15.1).

seccions.titol: How often to review it and the deadlines the decree sets
seccions.text:
The statement must be updated at least once a year, or every time an accessibility review is carried out (article 15.1). Reviews are a separate duty. Article 17 requires them at the design stage, before launch and periodically afterwards, especially when content or technology changes.
Each review must combine automated checks with expert manual review, and the result must be recorded in an accessibility review report (article 17.3), so an automated tool on its own is not enough. For websites, the first review had to be done within two years of entry into force on 20 September 2018, that is, before 20 September 2020 (article 17.6).

seccions.titol: How complaints and requests are handled
seccions.text:
Article 10 requires a feedback mechanism with two channels. One to report non-compliance or access difficulties, and another to file complaints and request excluded information. The first channel works by email or a form plus a phone line or an office (article 11). For complaints, the decree sets registration under Law 39/2015 and an answer within twenty working days (article 12).
The answer has to name the unit issuing it, the decision, the deadline for fixing the problem and where to appeal (article 12.5). If there is no agreement or no answer arrives, the person can appeal to the accessibility unit, which has two months to reply (article 13). The statement must link to the appeals procedure (article 15.2) and say which unit handles it.
One caveat. According to the BOE’s note on the consolidated text, Constitutional Court ruling 100/2019 found that the twenty working days, registration under Law 39/2015 and paragraphs 2 to 6 of article 13, including the two months, encroach on regional powers and are not basic legislation. For a Catalan council those deadlines are therefore a reference, not a national obligation. What binds is whatever Catalan rules set, if any.

seccions.titol: Who is responsible inside the council
seccions.text:
Every obliged body has to designate an accessibility unit, the Unidad responsable de accesibilidad. Local authorities designate it according to their own organisation (article 16.1). As an example, in a small council in the Gironès it may be the clerk’s office with the IT technician. In a comarcal council, the service that runs the website.
This unit coordinates the feedback mechanism, answers appeals and coordinates periodic reviews (article 16.3). Its designation is notified to the monitoring body (article 16.4), which according to the Web Accessibility Observatory is now the Ministry for Digital Transformation and the Civil Service.

seccions.titol: If the website runs on a shared platform, what is your part
seccions.text:
If the website runs on another administration’s platform, such as the municipal website platform the Diputació de Girona provides through its Oficina de Suport a l’Administració Electrònica, the template may already carry the «Accessibility» link. That does not settle it. The obligation sits with the body responsible for the website (article 15.1), even when a supplier builds it.
Check that the text names your council, that the preparation and last-review dates are real, that the contact and the responsible unit are yours and that the registry link works. If the electronic office (seu electrònica) sits on another domain, make sure the statement’s scope covers it.

seccions.titol: A checklist for the council’s technician
seccions.text: You can go through the statement in an afternoon with this list. The Web Accessibility Observatory offers public administration staff, through its Comunidad Accesibilidad, an online diagnosis service with an automated check of the website and the statement. Keep the result with its date for the annual update.

faqs.q: Our council website has no statement. Where do we start?
faqs.a: Start with an accessibility review, even a self-assessment, because the statement has to say what it is based on. Then fill in the EU model. Scope, compliance status, non-accessible content, contact details and appeals procedure. Link it from the footer of every page and review it within a year.

faqs.q: Can we say the website is partially compliant?
faqs.a: Yes, it is one of the three options in the model. You choose it when most of the requirements of the technical standard are met but with some exceptions, and you have to say which. If most are not met, the option is «not compliant». «Fully compliant» only when every requirement is met without exception.

faqs.q: Does this guide replace legal advice?
faqs.a: No. It summarises Royal Decree 1112/2018 and the EU model. The finer points are for the council clerk or the legal services. Constitutional Court ruling 100/2019 stripped paragraphs of articles 12, 13, 15, 16, 17 and 19 and the transitional provision of their basic character. Catalonia also has Law 13/2014 on accessibility. Article 33.4 asks public websites to state their accessibility level and the date of the last review.

ga4-baner-cookies.intro: GA4 shows fewer visits because, since the banner went up, it only measures the people who accept analytics cookies, and Spanish law requires that permission before the cookies are set. Anyone who declines, or closes the banner without answering, is missing from your reports. Your visits may be exactly the same and only the share you can see has dropped.

seccions.titol: Why does GA4 show fewer visits since the banner went up?
seccions.text: GA4 only records a visit when its tag loads and can set its cookie, and with the banner that happens after the person accepts analytics. Whoever declines, or leaves before deciding, is not there. If you see a drop, first check the day you switched the banner on and whether the drop starts right there.

seccions.titol: Basic or advanced consent mode. What each one measures
seccions.text:
Google’s consent mode is how your banner tells Google’s tags what the person has allowed. It has four signals. analytics_storage for analytics cookies, ad_storage for advertising cookies, and two more for ads, ad_user_data and ad_personalization. You will often see the four referred to as consent mode v2. For GA4, the first one is what matters.
You can set it up two ways. In basic mode, the tags do not load until the person answers, and if they decline nothing is sent to Google, not even the consent status. In advanced mode, the tags load from the start with everything denied and, while there is no permission, send the consent state and cookieless measurements, which Google uses to model the gap.
Behavioural modelling has thresholds. At least 1,000 events a day with analytics denied for 7 days, and 1,000 daily users with consent on 7 of the previous 28 days. Many small-business sites never get there, and below those numbers there is no modelling.

seccions.titol: What the law says. LSSI article 22.2 and the AEPD guide
seccions.text:
In Spain, article 22.2 of Law 34/2002 (the LSSI) says storage and data-retrieval devices may be used on a visitor’s device on condition that they have given consent after receiving clear and complete information about their use and the purposes of the processing. The only exception is technical access to transmit a communication, or what is strictly necessary for a service the person has expressly requested.
The AEPD’s Guía sobre el uso de las cookies (updated May 2024) says analytics cookies are not exempt from informed consent, although they are unlikely to pose a privacy risk when they are first-party, aggregated, strictly statistical, disclosed and refusable. Reject must be offered at the same level and with the same visibility as accept, and inactivity is never consent.

seccions.titol: How to read GA4 from now on. Trends instead of totals
seccions.text: Treat the day you switched the banner on as day zero and compare later months with each other, not with the months before. Look at proportions. The weight of each channel, landing pages, how many arrivals end up on the form. If you run a seasonal business on the Costa Brava, compare each summer with the previous one only when both come after the banner. If GA4 drops and calls and form submissions hold steady, the problem is the measurement.

seccions.titol: How to measure with fewer cookies, or none
seccions.text:
Some data never passes through the cookie banner, either because it stores nothing on the visitor’s device or because it comes from somewhere else. None of it replaces GA4 entirely, but together it tells you whether the business is going up or down.
The AEPD also has a guide on cookies for audience-measurement tools (Uso de cookies para herramientas de medición de audiencia, January 2024). It says measurement cookies could be exempt from consent if they only measure the site’s audience, on the publisher’s behalf alone, produce anonymous statistics, cross no other data, pass nothing to third parties and do not follow people across sites. It names no tool.

seccions.titol: What to check in your own cookie banner
seccions.text: Open your site in a private window and watch the browser’s network tab. In basic mode there should be no request to Google Analytics before the visitor decides. In GA4 Admin, under the consent settings, you can check whether the consent signals are arriving.

seccions.titol: How we do it at crida studio
seccions.text: At crida.studio we run our own banner with two categories, analytics and marketing. GA4 only loads if the person accepts analytics, and until then no Google tag loads and no analytics cookie is set. If someone withdraws permission, measurement stops and the _ga cookies are deleted. Since 31 October 2026 the Resources section carries the same banner, and one decision covers the whole site.

faqs.q: Can I use GA4 without a cookie banner in Spain?
faqs.a: According to the AEPD guide, analytics cookies are not exempt from informed consent, and GA4 works with first-party cookies such as _ga. The AEPD’s audience-measurement guide describes when a tool could be exempt, but it names none. Check it with whoever handles your legal side before removing the banner.

faqs.q: Have my visits really dropped, or does it just look that way?
faqs.a: Check three things. The day you switched the banner on and whether the drop starts right there. Your Search Console clicks, which do not depend on the banner. And the month’s real enquiries. If only GA4 drops, it is the measurement. If everything drops, you have a visibility or business problem.

faqs.q: Is it true GA4 will soon not need a banner?
