seccions.titol: Interviews with the people who buy and use the equipment
seccions.text: Public data tells you where the market is, and interviews tell you why people would buy. Talk to ten or fifteen people at potential customers, mixing process development, production, quality and procurement, because each values different things. A thirty-minute conversation with no sales pitch can tell you more than a long survey.

seccions.titol: A close look at competitors and what distributors say
seccions.text:
Take apart the offer of three or four competitors. Look at their datasheets, volume ranges, materials, the documentation they promise, their service network and how they talk on their website. Check where they rank on Google for searches about your type of equipment. That shows you which gaps your product can fill.
Distributors are an often forgotten source. They know which deals they lose and why, which equipment customers ask for that they cannot offer, and what prices their market will bear. A call with each current distributor, using a short script, can be worth as much as several interviews.

seccions.titol: How to size demand by modality and scale
seccions.text:
Bring it all together in a simple grid. Rows are the modalities your equipment can serve. Columns are the scales. In each cell, put the number of accounts you know, what interviews told you and what distributors think. The fullest cells are your initial market.
Finish with a one-page summary that says whether the equipment makes sense, for whom, with what core message and through which channels. That document is the basis for the launch, from the datasheet to the website and campaigns, and it stops each department from describing the equipment its own way.

faqs.q: Can I run the analysis without hiring a consultancy?
faqs.a: Yes, especially the first version. Public data is free, interviews can be run by someone from product or marketing with a script, and your distributors already work with you. An outside view helps you ask questions without defending the product and turn the conclusions into something the launch can use.

faqs.q: How many interviews do I need?
faqs.a: With ten or fifteen well chosen conversations you can usually see whether answers repeat. If everyone says something different, the segment is too broad or the problem is unclear, and you need to narrow it before going further. Mix roles and company sizes so you do not end up with a single point of view.

faqs.q: Are paid market reports worth it?
faqs.a: They can help with global figures, but they are often expensive and too broad for a specific piece of equipment. Start with public reports from associations such as AseBio and Biocat and with your own data. If you later need a global figure for investors or management, buy only the report that answers it.

faqs.q: How do I use the analysis in launch marketing?
faqs.a: Interviews give you the words customers use to describe the problem, and those words go into headlines, the datasheet and campaigns. The modality and scale grid tells you which segments to target first, and the competitor review tells you which arguments your website needs to answer.

bio-animacio-proces-bioproces.intro: To explain a bioprocess step in 90 seconds, pick one step, such as the seed train, perfusion or TFF concentration and diafiltration, and answer one buyer question. The script has four parts. The problem, what happens inside the equipment, what the system controls and what changes for the customer. Engineering reviews it before anything gets animated.

seccions.titol: A 90-second animation explains one step
seccions.text:
Ninety seconds is enough for one process step. Try to cover everything from the cell vial to the purified product and each stage gets a few seconds, so the buyer remembers none of them. Three short pieces work better than one long video that nobody watches to the end.
Choose the step from the questions that keep coming up in sales meetings. The person watching is often not a process engineer. It may be someone in procurement or finance, or the founder of a startup with a biology background. They need to understand what the equipment does and what it changes in their project. The membrane details can wait for the engineer.

seccions.titol: A four-part script, from problem to outcome
seccions.text: A script that works with non-specialist buyers usually has four parts. Each one answers a single question, and the timings below are a guide. Before anything is animated, read the script aloud with a stopwatch. If it runs past 90 seconds, cut sentences, because every extra second of animation is extra work too.

seccions.titol: Three bioprocess steps that animate well
seccions.text: Some steps are very hard to explain with photos and click straight away in animation. They are the ones that happen inside closed equipment or that change scale. These three come up again and again in conversations with biopharma customers, and each one fills a 90-second piece.

seccions.titol: Who should review the script before animation starts
seccions.text:
The process engineer reviews the script and the storyboard before any final frame is produced. An arrow pointing the wrong way or a sensor in the wrong place is easy to fix in a sketch. Once the animation is finished, every change goes back through modelling, animation and rendering.
Someone from quality or regulatory should read the text as well. Lines like GMP compliant or Part 11 ready depend on how the customer installs, validates and runs the equipment. If the system is built to order, the screen should say that it shows an example configuration.

seccions.titol: Plan captions and languages from day one
seccions.text:
A sales animation has to work with the sound off, because it is often watched at a trade show or in an open office. If it has a voiceover, the W3C says the audio needed to understand the video should be captioned. It also warns that automatic captions do not meet that need unless someone confirms they are accurate.
Words like diafiltration, perfusion or retentate are easy for automatic captions to get wrong. Keep on-screen text out of the animated layers and in a separate file. A German, Spanish or French version then means translating and checking text, with no new animation work.

faqs.q: Should we use 3D animation or film the real process?
faqs.a: It depends on what you need to show. What happens inside a closed bioreactor or a membrane cannot be filmed, and animation makes it visible. Filmed footage proves the equipment exists and shows how an operator uses it. A mix often works best, with animation to explain and real footage to build trust.

faqs.q: If the step takes hours, how do you show it in 90 seconds?
faqs.a: The animation compresses time and should say so. A small time-lapse label or a clock in the corner stops buyers thinking diafiltration takes a minute. What matters is the order of the stages and what the equipment does at each point, more than how long it really takes.

faqs.q: Can we reuse the 3D model from our product renders?
faqs.a: Yes, if there is a CAD model or the one built for the renders. It usually needs simplifying so the animation runs smoothly, plus additions a still render does not show, such as flows, bubbles or the impeller turning. Engineering should sign off those additions just like the script.

bio-assistent-ia-documentacio-tecnica.intro: Yes, as long as it only answers from the documents you give it and says where each answer comes from. An assistant built on datasheets, manuals and application notes handles questions on volumes, materials, connections or software well. Process, scale-up, GMP compliance and pricing questions should go to an application specialist. And since 2 August 2026 it has to tell people it is an AI.

seccions.titol: Questions whose answer is already written down
seccions.text:
An AI assistant works well when the answer already exists in a document. The working volume of a 50 litre bioreactor, which materials touch the product, which probes it carries, what connections the single-use bag has or how to change the filter on a TFF system. Today your sales reps and service engineers answer these, often by pasting the same email again.
It also helps with software and maintenance questions, provided there is a manual. How to export a batch, which user roles the control software has or how often a probe needs calibrating according to the manufacturer. If the assistant cites the page and version of the manual, the buyer does not wait a day and the engineer does not repeat the same work.

seccions.titol: Which documents to give it and which to keep out
seccions.text:
The assistant is only as good as what it reads. Before connecting anything, list the current documents with version and date, and remove the ones that no longer apply. An old manual that still describes a discontinued controller does real harm, because the assistant will quote it with the same confidence as the new one.
Keep customer URS documents, FAT and SAT reports, prices, quotes and anything under NDA out of it. If the assistant is public, anything it reads can end up in an answer. If it is an internal tool for your sales team, it can read more, but with permissions per person.

seccions.titol: When the assistant should hand over to a specialist
seccions.text:
The rule is simple. If the answer depends on the customer's process, the assistant should not give it. Cell line, media or moving from the lab to a pilot plant are questions for an application specialist, who will ask for data first. The same goes for anything that sounds like a commercial or compliance promise.
The handover has to be easy. The assistant summarises the question, asks for name, company and email, and sends it to the right person with the full conversation. The specialist does not start from scratch and the buyer does not explain the same thing three times.

seccions.titol: Every answer should show where it comes from
seccions.text:
In this industry a wrong figure can end up inside a URS. So the assistant must be able to say it does not know. Anthropic's guide to reducing hallucinations recommends letting the model admit it lacks information, having it pull word-for-word quotes from long documents before answering and asking it to back each claim with a quote and a source.
In practice every answer links to the document and page it comes from. If nothing relevant turns up, it says so and offers to put the buyer in touch with a person. Technical buyers can check the figure themselves, and your team can trace each mistake back to the document that needs fixing.

seccions.titol: Telling users it is an AI and what happens to their data
seccions.text:
Article 50 of the EU AI Act has applied since 2 August 2026. Paragraph 1 says systems meant to interact directly with people must be designed so that people know they are talking to an AI, unless that is obvious. Paragraph 5 adds that the notice must come at the latest at the first interaction, in a clear and accessible way.
When the assistant asks for contact details to pass the case on, the GDPR comes in too. Article 13(1) says that at the moment data is collected you must tell people who the controller is, what the data will be used for and the other points it lists. A short line in the chat with a link to the privacy policy covers it.

seccions.titol: How to test it before it goes on your website
seccions.text:
Start with real questions. Collect thirty or forty questions from sales and service emails, ask an application specialist to write the right answer and compare it with the assistant's. When it gets something wrong, the cause is often a missing document or an outdated one that slipped in.
We usually set it up first as an internal tool for the sales and service team. Once the answers hold up under engineering review, it moves to the website. Every time a new manual comes out or a product is discontinued, the documents need updating and the test questions need running again.

faqs.q: Can AI answer technician questions using our service manuals?
faqs.a: Yes, if it only answers from the current version of your manuals and says which document, page and version each answer comes from. When the manuals do not cover a question, it should say so and pass it to an application specialist. Start with an internal tool for your service team and test it with real questions first.

faqs.q: Can it answer in English or German if the manuals are in Spanish?
faqs.a: Current models can read a document in one language and answer in another, which helps if you sell into Germany or the Nordics. But technical terms have to match your official documentation in that language. If you have a translated manual, give it that version and have an engineer who speaks the language review a sample of answers.

faqs.q: Can it replace an application specialist?
faqs.a: No. It takes the repetitive questions off their desk and passes on the real cases with a summary of the conversation, which is already a lot. Process, scale-up and compliance decisions depend on customer data the assistant does not have and should not have in a public tool. The specialist still answers and signs off.

faqs.q: Should it go on the website or stay internal?
faqs.a: It depends on the problem you want to solve. If sales and service lose hours digging through manuals, start with an internal tool. If buyers cannot find technical data on your website, a public assistant makes sense. Starting internally and going public once the answers survive engineering review keeps the risk down.

bio-biospain-o-farmaforum.intro: BioSpain 2027 takes place from 28 to 30 September in Barcelona and Farmaforum 2027 on 22 and 23 September at IFEMA Madrid. BioSpain is AseBio's partnering event, built around one-to-one meetings, investors and biotechs. Farmaforum is the pharma industry forum, with an exhibition and congresses on production, laboratory and engineering. If you sell to biotechs or want partners, choose BioSpain. If you sell to pharma plants and labs, choose Farmaforum.

seccions.titol: The difference is who you will meet
seccions.text:
Both shows cover life sciences, but the audiences differ. BioSpain mainly draws biotechs, research centres, investors and the companies that serve them, and one-to-one meetings are at its core. Farmaforum, according to its organiser, draws professionals from the pharmaceutical, biotech, veterinary, cosmetics and laboratory technology industries.
For a bioprocess equipment maker, the question is where the customer is. A biotech scaling a process towards the clinic is still choosing platforms and partners. A plant already in production wants to improve lines, cleanrooms or its lab. Both may matter to you, but they need different messages and materials.

seccions.titol: What BioSpain is and how recent editions went
seccions.text:
AseBio has organised BioSpain since 2003 and describes it as the leading biotech event in Spain. The 2025 edition took place at Fira de Barcelona with Biocat and brought together more than 2,400 attendees from 1,065 organisations in 34 countries, 140 investors, 250 exhibitors and 4,500 meetings.
The 2026 edition was held in Bilbao from 29 September to 1 October and, according to AseBio, drew more than 1,900 professionals from 900 organisations and nearly 4,000 one-to-one meetings. The 2027 edition returns to Barcelona, from 28 to 30 September 2027.
For 2027, AseBio says details of the new edition will be published soon and that its members get special rates. If you are already a member, or were thinking of joining, factor that in when you compare costs. And since BioSpain falls the week after Farmaforum, book your Barcelona hotel early if you plan to attend both.

seccions.titol: What Farmaforum is and who you will meet
seccions.text:
Farmaforum is the forum for the pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical and laboratory technology industries, with dedicated areas for biotech and cosmetics too. It combines an exhibition, congresses, workshops and networking areas, with tracks such as Biotechforum, Labforum for lab instruments and equipment, and a pharma engineering forum covering process equipment, scale-up, cleanrooms and automation.
The 2026 edition, its twelfth, ran on 22 and 23 September in Hall 10 at IFEMA Madrid and, according to the organiser, drew more than 9,500 professionals. The next one is on 22 and 23 September 2027, again at IFEMA Madrid. During the year the organiser also runs technical days in other cities.
On the Farmaforum website, the 2027 exhibitor list and floor plan are still marked as coming soon, and stand options are requested from the organisers. If you want a good spot in the hall, ask for terms early. The organiser says it wants to add new specialist congresses, so check whether one covers your field.

seccions.titol: BioSpain and Farmaforum, criterion by criterion
seccions.text: The table sums up what to check before booking. The figures above are the ones each organiser publishes for its latest edition with data, and they are not directly comparable, because one show counts attendees and meetings while the other counts visiting professionals.

seccions.titol: Where Biocat fits if you are a Catalan company
seccions.text:
Biocat, the organisation that drives the BioRegion of Catalonia, plays a clear role here. It co-organised the 2025 edition in Barcelona, which drew 750 registrants from more than 300 Catalan companies, and for the Bilbao edition it offered BioRegion companies a 10 percent discount.
If you are a Catalan company, follow Biocat's events calendar, which lists BioSpain and other sector meetings, and get ready for 2027, when the show comes home. Farmaforum, by contrast, takes place at IFEMA Madrid, so build the trip into your budget.

seccions.titol: CPHI Spain, a third Spanish show in 2027
seccions.text:
In 2027 there is a third option in Spain. CPHI is launching CPHI Spain, on 1 and 2 June 2027 at Fira de Barcelona, on Montjuïc. The organiser expects more than 130 exhibitors and over 2,500 attendees, and presents it as a new event for growing your pharma business in Spain.
From what the organiser says, it targets the pharma industry rather than partnering with investors, so it compares more closely with Farmaforum than with BioSpain. As this is the first edition, there are no figures from a past show yet. If you sell to pharma plants, you can attend as a visitor first and decide later whether to exhibit.
The three shows fall in different months. CPHI Spain in June, Farmaforum on 22 and 23 September and BioSpain from 28 to 30 September. With a small team you can split the year between a production show and a partnering event, and reuse the same materials with different messages.
If you go, prepare it like the others. Request meetings in advance, through the organiser or by contacting people directly, bring datasheets in Spanish and English and decide who follows up each contact. As it is a new show, also check which companies sign up as exhibitors before you book anything.

faqs.q: When is BioSpain 2027?
faqs.a: According to AseBio, BioSpain 2027 will be held in Barcelona from 28 to 30 September 2027, after the 2026 edition in Bilbao. AseBio says more information about this edition will be published soon. Check its page before booking travel or committing budget, as details can still change.

faqs.q: When is Farmaforum 2027?
faqs.a: According to Farmaforum's official website, the 13th edition runs on 22 and 23 September 2027 at IFEMA Madrid. The organiser has already started planning it and says it wants to add new specialist congresses. If you want to exhibit, ask for terms early and book your space in good time.

faqs.q: Do we need a booth, or are meetings enough?
faqs.a: It depends on what you sell. At BioSpain the main value lies in one-to-one meetings with biotechs and investors, and a booth makes sense if you need to show product or build your brand. At Farmaforum, where visitors walk the exhibition looking for suppliers, a booth with equipment or a demo carries more weight.

faqs.q: Can we attend both?
faqs.a: Yes, and for many equipment makers it makes sense, because they reach different audiences. In 2026 they were held a week apart and in 2027 they fall in consecutive weeks again, so build one kit of materials and adapt the message. At BioSpain, talk about scale-up and development partners. At Farmaforum, talk about production, quality and service.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to exhibit at BioSpain or Farmaforum?
faqs.a: Neither show publishes rates on its website. AseBio says its members get special rates at BioSpain and that 2027 details are coming soon. Farmaforum refers you to the organisers for stand options. Ask for terms in writing and compare them using the same cost lines, from space and stand build to travel and follow-up.

bio-cas-exit-client-anonim.intro: An anonymous case study works when it tells buyers what they want to know. What kind of client it was, which process and scale, what the problem was, what was done and a result the client has approved. The name stays out, the technical detail stays in. And the text goes through the client's quality and legal teams before it is published.

seccions.titol: Start by reading what the confidentiality agreement allows
seccions.text:
Before writing anything, find out what the contract allows. A confidentiality agreement may rule out the client's name, but also process details, volumes, dates or price. The European Commission lists manufacturing processes, the price offered in a tender and information on whom a company buys from and sells to among the kinds of information a trade secret can cover.
The EU Trade Secrets Directive 2016/943 (Article 2), and Law 1/2019 in Spain (Article 1), protect that information when it is secret, has value because it is secret and its holder takes reasonable steps to keep it so. Article 4(3) of the directive treats disclosure without the holder's consent in breach of a confidentiality agreement as unlawful. So the first step is to talk to whoever owns the contract on your side.

seccions.titol: What you can say without naming the client
seccions.text: An anonymous case study persuades when it is specific about everything except the name. Buyers need to recognise a problem like their own. This is the information you can propose to the client, point by point, so they decide what can appear and how.

seccions.titol: How to get sign-off from quality and legal
seccions.text:
At a pharma company, a text about a project crosses more than one desk. The person who ran the project is usually supportive, but quality, legal and often communications will read it too. It helps a lot to send them a short draft that is already anonymised, rather than asking permission for an idea.
Prepare a table listing every fact in the text and how you have handled it. For example, scale as a range instead of the exact volume, or the year instead of the month. Get approval in writing and keep the approved version. If you later want to reuse the case in another piece, ask again.

seccions.titol: Formats that persuade without the client's name
seccions.text: A case study does not have to be a two-page PDF. Some formats work better when the name cannot appear, because they put the weight on the technical problem and on the way your team works.

seccions.titol: How to publish it so it helps your website too
seccions.text:
An anonymous case can make a strong page if it has real detail. Google asks whether content shows first-hand expertise and provides original information. A specific text about a process, a scale and a problem does that even without the client's name. A vague text full of brochure phrases adds nothing.
Give it its own page with a title that states the problem, such as scaling a perfusion process to pilot plant. Link to it from the equipment page and from your sector page. Put the name of the person on your team who ran the project on it, since they are the one who can answer questions.

faqs.q: Is an anonymous case study credible?
faqs.a: It is if it is specific. A well-explained process, scale and problem tell a sector buyer a great deal, even without a logo. What hurts credibility is generic phrasing and unexplained results. If the client agrees, you can also offer a private call with them to buyers who are close to a decision.

faqs.q: Can I name the client in a private meeting?
faqs.a: It depends on the confidentiality agreement. Some allow you to mention the client in private conversations and others rule it out completely. If it is unclear, ask in writing. When in doubt, present the case without the name and offer a direct reference only if the client agrees.

faqs.q: How long does pharma client approval take?
faqs.a: It depends on the company and there is no fixed timeline. What shortens it is arriving with a short, already anonymised draft and having one person on the client side coordinating reviews. What drags it out is sending a new version every week. That is why it pays to ask as the project closes, while everything is fresh.

bio-configurador-3d-interactiu.intro: A 3D configurator pays off when your range has options that combine, such as working volumes, ports, sensors or skid layout, and first meetings with customers keep circling the same questions. If you sell a few standard systems, or every project is fully bespoke, a good set of renders and drawings does the same job with far less upkeep.

seccions.titol: Renders, 3D viewer or configurator, three different tools
seccions.text:
Before deciding, separate three things. A render set is still images. A 3D viewer lets visitors rotate and zoom a model on the web, and sometimes place it in their own space with augmented reality. A configurator goes further and changes the model based on the options the customer picks, such as vessel volume or ports.
Each level takes more work than the one before. In a configurator, every option has to be modelled, validated by engineering and kept up to date when the product changes. If nobody owns that, the website ends up showing combinations you no longer build.

seccions.titol: When a configurator shortens URS conversations
seccions.text: The URS is the customer's document, and a configurator does not replace it. What it can do is help the customer arrive at the first meeting with a clearer idea of what they need. It makes most sense when some of these situations apply.

seccions.titol: When a good set of renders is enough
seccions.text:
If your range is a handful of standard models, a configurator adds little. A good render set, a clear product page and PDF drawings answer the same questions. It does not pay off either when every project is fully bespoke, because the options cannot be boxed into a menu and the conversation with engineering is unavoidable.
There is a third case. If your typical buyer is a technical team that wants documents for its evaluation, they would rather download datasheets and drawings than play with a model. Before commissioning anything, ask your sales engineers which tool they would genuinely use in meetings.

seccions.titol: What a good equipment configurator should do
seccions.text: A useful configurator is closer to a smart form than to a game. The rules come from engineering and the output goes to the sales team. These are the points it cannot miss if it is meant to help sell.

seccions.titol: A 3D model that does not slow down your site
seccions.text:
The usual format for 3D on the web is glTF. Khronos describes it as a royalty-free specification for transmitting and loading 3D models efficiently, and since 2022 it has also been the ISO/IEC 12113 standard. To display it there are open-source components such as Google's model-viewer, which runs in current browsers and also supports augmented reality.
Google's Core Web Vitals treat it as a good experience when the main content appears within 2.5 seconds and the page responds to input in 200 milliseconds or less. A heavy model can break both. Show an image first, load the 3D only when the visitor wants to use it and export a simplified version of the CAD.

faqs.q: Can we build the configurator from our engineering CAD?
faqs.a: Yes, but not as it is. The CAD model includes internal parts, fasteners and details that make the 3D file very heavy and also reveal how the equipment is designed. The usual approach is a simplified web version with the exterior, the ports and whatever the customer needs to see to decide.

faqs.q: Should the configurator show prices?
faqs.a: It can, but for process equipment the price depends on documentation, validation, consumables and service, and that is settled in the quote. A safer route is for the configurator to end in a quote request with the chosen configuration, which the sales engineer reviews before replying.

faqs.q: Does a configurator help the site rank on Google?
faqs.a: On its own, not much. What ranks is the page for each model, with a clear explanation, specifications and well-described images. The configurator mainly serves people who have already reached your site, helping them understand the system and request a quote with better information.

bio-embut-b2b-cicle-llarg.intro: A B2B funnel for long-cycle equipment sales should follow the milestones of the customer's project, from process development to capex approval. It needs a few stages you can verify, from the first visit to the URS and the quote, nurturing that matches each phase and tracking that runs from GA4 into the CRM. That way the sales engineer knows when to step in.

seccions.titol: Why the funnel should follow the customer's project milestones
seccions.text:
In bioprocess equipment sales, the customer moves forward when their project changes phase. A process development group looks for a benchtop bioreactor, a pilot plant needs to scale up and a tech transfer means repeating the process at another site. Each phase brings different questions and different people.
That is why an equipment manufacturer cannot copy the funnel of an online shop. The stages have to mirror what happens on the customer's side, such as a quote entering capex approval, QA asking for documentation or the project going on hold. If the CRM only separates leads from customers, sales cannot tell who is close to buying.

seccions.titol: The stages, from the first visit to the URS and the quote
seccions.text:
A useful funnel has few stages and each one is confirmed by a concrete event. When we set up the funnel for a maker of lab, pilot or GMP production equipment, we start from these six.
The URS is the clearest dividing line. Once a customer writes a user requirements specification, they usually have a funded project or are close to one. From there, marketing shifts to supporting the sales engineer with case studies, documentation and fast answers.

seccions.titol: Lead nurturing that follows the project, not the calendar
seccions.text:
Nurturing works better when each message matches a project phase. Someone who downloads a lab to pilot scale-up guide gets more from a tech transfer case study than from a generic newsletter. Someone asking about IQ and OQ documentation wants to see what the validation package looks like.
Timing is the hard part. Months can pass between the first download and the order, because the customer is waiting for a funding round, a research grant or annual capex approval. In the meantime, keep in touch rarely and with useful content, and restart the follow-up when a new signal appears, such as a demo request.

seccions.titol: Which emails you can send under Spain's LSSI
seccions.text:
In Spain, article 21.1 of the LSSI, the information society services law, bans promotional email that the recipient has not requested or expressly authorised beforehand. Article 21.2 makes an exception when there is a prior contractual relationship, the contact data was obtained lawfully and the email covers the company's own products or services similar to those the customer bought. The text refers to recipients in general, with no exception for business addresses.
The article adds that, in every case, recipients must be offered a simple, free way to object to the use of their data for promotional purposes, both when it is collected and in every message. In practice, the download form should have a clear checkbox for marketing emails. With trade show contacts, scanning a badge does not on its own record express consent, so it is safer to ask for it at the booth and log it.

seccions.titol: What to automate and when the sales engineer steps in
seccions.text:
Automation should handle repetitive work and alert sales at the right moment. Sending a requested datasheet, reminding someone about a webinar or routing a contact to the right territory are good jobs for a machine. Answering a question about pH control or scale-up should be left to someone who knows the process.
It works well to define two or three signals that create a CRM task, such as a demo request, repeated visits to the same product page or an attached URS. If the company sells through distributors, the automation should also pass the contact to the local distributor and log it, so the opportunity is not lost.

faqs.q: How long is the sales cycle for bioprocess equipment?
faqs.a: It depends on the project phase and on who pays. An academic lab depends on grants and public procurement, a startup often waits for a funding round and a pharma company goes through capex approval. That is why it makes more sense to measure how long each stage takes in your own CRM than to look for an industry average.

faqs.q: What CRM do we need for an equipment B2B funnel?
faqs.a: Any CRM that stores the lead source, the project stage, the scale, the process and the Google Ads click ID. If it also connects to the website form and your email tool, automation is straightforward. The brand matters less than the sales team actually updating it every week.

faqs.q: Can we email the contacts we meet at trade shows?
faqs.a: Under article 21 of the LSSI, yes, if they have expressly agreed to receive marketing emails or if they are existing customers and you write about products similar to those they bought. Ask for consent at the booth and log it in the CRM with the date and the show. If they only asked for specific information, send them that information and nothing more.

bio-estand-equip-gran.intro: Bring the benchtop or lab-scale unit, run it on the booth and show the pilot and production scales on screen. A life-size render, a cutaway animation of the inside and a single-use bag or sensor that people can pick up explain more than a catalogue photo. Design the booth around those three things.

seccions.titol: Bring the small unit and run it
seccions.text:
Shipping a 2,000-litre bioreactor to a show is costly and complicated, but a benchtop unit fits on any booth. Bring the smallest scale in your range and, if you can, have it running with the control software open on a screen. Visitors see how it is set up, how the data reads and how the bag is changed, which is what they want to understand before asking for a quote.
If the small unit uses the same software, sensors or consumables as the larger ones, say so on a clear sign. That way the unit in front of them also explains the ones you left at home. If it does not, do not imply it, because a process engineer will ask straight away.

seccions.titol: How to show the production scale on screen
seccions.text:
Large scales belong on a large screen, with life-size renders or a person standing next to the equipment so the size is clear. A cutaway animation that opens the vessel and shows the agitation, sensors and bag explains in seconds what a catalogue cannot. Make it silent with short captions, because the noise of the hall makes audio hard to hear.
A 3D configurator on a tablet lets visitors choose volume, options and connections while they talk to your sales engineer. Augmented reality can place the equipment at full size on the booth floor, but it is only worth it if it opens instantly and someone from your team runs it.

seccions.titol: What visitors should be able to handle
seccions.text: At a bioprocess show, people tend to want to handle the materials. A single-use bag, a sensor, a sterile connector or a sample of your stainless steel finish take up no space and start conversations. Put them at hand height, close to the aisle, rather than inside a locked display case.

seccions.titol: How to lay out a 12 to 25 square metre booth
seccions.text:
AUMA, the German trade fair industry association, recommends a stand with clear zones for consultation, product presentation and quieter conversations, with well-placed media technology. On a small booth, that means the unit at the front, the screen on the back wall and a meeting table set apart from the passing crowd.
At ACHEMA, the All-in-One Compact package covers stands from 12 to 25 square metres, with 2.50-metre walls, a 2.00 by 2.60-metre fabric graphic wall, a table, three chairs and a lockable counter. The Pro package, from 18 to 25 square metres, has 3-metre walls, a lockable 1-square-metre cabin and a 2.00 by 3.00-metre print on the rear wall.

seccions.titol: Booth material keeps working after the show
seccions.text: Renders, animation and a configurator are paid for once and can work all year. Commission them from the start in website and LinkedIn formats, landscape and portrait, and with text-free versions you can translate later. That way the material from the Frankfurt show also serves the Madrid one and your product page.

faqs.q: What booth size do I need for a benchtop unit?
faqs.a: At ACHEMA the minimum stand is 12 square metres, and the ready-built packages run from 12 to 25. For a benchtop unit, a screen and a meeting table, a small booth can be enough if the layout is right. Measure the unit with all its accessories and leave room for people to walk around it.

faqs.q: Is augmented reality worth it on a booth?
faqs.a: It can be, if it answers a specific question, such as how much floor space the production unit would take in the customer's cleanroom. It has to open instantly, on a tablet that stays on the booth, with someone from your team guiding it. If visitors have to download an app, keep it for the website instead.

faqs.q: Renders or photos to show large equipment?
faqs.a: If the equipment exists and you have an installation you can photograph without customer data in view, a photo builds trust. If you want to show the inside, different options or a unit that has not been built yet, renders are more flexible. Often the two are combined, with real plant photos and renders for the options.

bio-fira-retorn-inversio.intro: Add up the full cost, not just the floor space, and divide it by the useful meetings and the qualified opportunities the show produced. Then track those opportunities in your CRM across the whole sales cycle, which for bioprocess equipment can run for many months. Goals that are not about sales, such as finding distributors, hiring or watching competitors, are measured separately.

seccions.titol: Add up the full cost of the show
seccions.text:
Floor space is the line everyone looks at, but it is only one line. At ACHEMA 2027, the space fee ranges from 378 euros per square metre for a wall stand to 529.20 euros for a stand with two or more open sides. Working from these published fees, excluding VAT, a 25-square-metre wall stand comes to 9,450 euros in space, and the Compact build package at 198 euros per square metre adds another 4,950.
On top of that come the other charges and services listed in the conditions of participation, plus everything the organiser does not bill. Write the full list before you sign, because that is the figure you will divide later.

seccions.titol: Cost per meeting and per qualified opportunity
seccions.text:
Divide the full cost by the useful meetings and, above all, by the qualified opportunities. A qualified opportunity is a project with a stage, a scale, a timeline and someone who decides or influences the decision, not a business card. Define it before the show, because afterwards it is easy to count too generously.
That cost only means something when you compare it with other channels. AUMA, the German trade fair industry association, offers a tool called the Trade Fair Benefit Check that compares the cost of exhibiting with that of other marketing activities. You can do the same with what an opportunity costs you from Google Ads, LinkedIn or a sales visit.

seccions.titol: How to count the business that arrives months later
seccions.text:
In bioprocessing, a conversation on the booth can turn into an order many months later, after trials, URS and approvals. To see it, every show contact has to enter the CRM with its source tagged, for example ACHEMA 2027, and every new opportunity has to record whether that person or company visited the booth.
Review the data at three, six and twelve months. Count the opportunities that started at the show and the existing ones that moved forward there. QR codes and show links should carry campaign parameters so that website visits can be attributed as well. If you sell through distributors, ask them to tag the opportunities that come from the leads you pass on in the same way.

seccions.titol: Keep distributors, hiring and competitor watch separate
seccions.text:
A trade show is about more than selling. ACHEMA itself says it is a good place to recruit staff, and AUMA lists competitor analysis among the ways to measure a show. Finding a distributor for Scandinavia or seeing what competitors are showing has value, but it is not a sale.
Measure those goals separately, each with its own figure. How many distributor meetings, how many candidates, which competitor launches you saw. Mix them into sales and the show can look like a success with no business, or a failure that actually opened a market for you.

seccions.titol: What organiser surveys tell you and what they do not
seccions.text:
Organisers publish satisfaction figures. According to the official ACHEMA 2024 summary, 86.4% of exhibitors rated their success between very satisfying and solid, and 95.7% were considering rebooking for 2027. Those figures help you choose a show, but they say nothing about your own business.
Only you can answer whether the show paid off, using the full cost, the opportunities in your CRM and the length of your sales cycle. AUMA recommends closing every show with a report covering results, what can be improved and what you will change next time, and comparing all your shows against each other.

faqs.q: How do you calculate trade show ROI?
faqs.a: Add up the full cost, including space, stand, shipping, travel, staff time and materials. Divide it by the qualified opportunities the show produced and compare that with the cost of an opportunity from other channels. After six or twelve months, check which of those opportunities turned into orders and what they add up to.

faqs.q: How much does floor space cost at ACHEMA 2027?
faqs.a: The base fee is 378 euros per square metre for wall stands, with surcharges of 20% and 40% for aisle stands and stands with two or more open sides. Start-ups and academic research institutions pay 239 euros per square metre. All prices exclude VAT and the stand build, which is charged separately.

faqs.q: When can I tell whether the show paid off?
faqs.a: Meetings and opportunities can be counted the following week. Orders take longer, depending on your sales cycle. Do a first review at three months and a final one at twelve, and decide whether to exhibit again based on that data, before the cancellation deadlines for the next edition kick in.

bio-fires-biotec-farma-2027.intro: The key shows of 2027 are BPI Europe in Hamburg from 27 to 29 April, BIO in Philadelphia from 7 to 10 June, ACHEMA in Frankfurt from 14 to 18 June, Farmaforum in Madrid on 22 and 23 September, BioSpain in Barcelona from 28 to 30 September and CPHI Frankfurt from 9 to 11 November. Pick one or two to exhibit at based on who buys from you, and attend the rest as a visitor with meetings booked in advance.

seccions.titol: The official 2027 dates, show by show
seccions.text: These are the dates the organisers publish on their own websites, checked again on 11 November 2026. Before booking hotels or a stand, check them again on the official site, since organisers can change opening hours or halls. If a show has not published its 2027 date yet, it is better to wait than to trust an aggregator.

seccions.titol: BPI Europe and ACHEMA, for companies selling into bioprocess
seccions.text:
BPI Europe is the most bioprocess-focused of the lot. The organiser describes it as a meeting point for manufacturing professionals, from molecule to market, with strategies for mAbs, biologics and ATMPs. For a bioreactor or TFF system maker, it is the audience closest to the product, people who work in manufacturing and process development every day.
ACHEMA is much larger and broader. Its 2024 edition drew 106,001 participants from 141 countries, and for 52% of visitors it is the only trade show they attend. You will meet engineering firms, process plants and labs, but also many sectors that will never buy from you, so arrive with your meetings already requested.

seccions.titol: CPHI and Farmaforum, for selling to the pharma industry
seccions.text:
CPHI Frankfurt covers the whole pharma supply chain, with zones for APIs, bioproduction, contract manufacturing, CROs and machinery and equipment. For 2027 it announces new zones, including one for lab and analytical equipment. It suits CDMOs, service providers and manufacturers that sell to pharma plants.
Farmaforum is the Madrid forum for the pharma, biopharma and laboratory technology industry. The organiser says its 2026 edition brought together more than 9,500 professionals in hall 10 at IFEMA. For a manufacturer selling to pharma plants in Spain, it is a date in Madrid, with no need to travel to Germany.
In 2027 CPHI launches a show in Spain. CPHI Spain will take place on 1 and 2 June at Fira de Barcelona, on Montjuïc, and the organiser expects more than 130 exhibitors and over 2,500 attendees. It presents the event as a way to grow your pharma business in Spain. For suppliers selling to Spanish plants, it is an option that does not involve a trip to Germany.

seccions.titol: BIO and BioSpain, where the biotech companies meet
seccions.text:
BIO International Convention is an annual event that takes place at the Pennsylvania Convention Center in Philadelphia in 2027. On the exhibition floor there is a BioProcess Zone with a BioProcess International theatre for bioprocessing talks. It makes sense if you sell to North American biotech companies or are looking for partners there.
BioSpain is the event run by AseBio, the Spanish association of biotech companies. According to AseBio, the 2026 edition in Bilbao gathered more than 1,900 professionals from 900 organisations in 32 countries, more than 100 investors and nearly 4,000 one-to-one meetings. In 2027 it takes place in Barcelona, a good chance for start-ups, CDMOs and suppliers to get close to the sector.
If you are after partners or licensing deals rather than equipment sales, BIO-Europe Spring is another date to consider. It runs from 5 to 7 April 2027 at Eurexpo in Lyon, with digital partnering on 13 and 14 April. The organiser calls it Europe's largest springtime biotech partnering event, with more than 3,700 attendees from 51 countries.

seccions.titol: When to exhibit and when visiting is enough
seccions.text: Exhibit where your buyers are and where you can show something that does not come across on a video call. Visit where you are not yet sure there is business. Attending as a visitor with meetings booked tells you who exhibits, which booths work and whether it is worth coming back with a stand of your own.

seccions.titol: How to spread the year without wearing out the team
seccions.text:
Watch the weeks that run into each other. BIO and ACHEMA fall in consecutive weeks in June, and so do Farmaforum and BioSpain in September. If you want to attend both in each pair, prepare the materials and meetings for both at the same time and decide who on the team goes to which.
Materials can be used more than once. The renders, process animation and demo video you prepare for the big show also work for the others, for the website and for sales. What you cannot reuse is the message, because each show has a different audience and the booth headline has to reflect it.

seccions.titol: What it costs to exhibit and where to find the prices
seccions.text:
Of the shows on this list, ACHEMA publishes the most complete rate card. For 2027, space costs from €378 to €529.20 per square metre excluding VAT, depending on the open sides, and start-ups and academic research institutions pay €239. Stand build, services and the show's mandatory charges are billed separately.
The others do not list prices online. CPHI Frankfurt offers a Basic Package, a Modular Stand Design and a Shell Stand, and the price comes through its booking form. AseBio says its members get special rates at BioSpain and that 2027 stand sales would open in November 2026, but it does not yet publish prices on its website. On the Farmaforum site, the 2027 exhibitor list and floor plan are still marked as coming soon.
To compare shows under the same rules, add up space, stand build, travel, hotels and equipment shipping, then divide by the contacts and opportunities you expect. The trade show cost calculator does that sum with the ACHEMA 2027 fees already loaded, and with your own figures it works for any other show.

faqs.q: Can the 2027 dates still change?
faqs.a: They can. The dates in this guide are the ones organisers published as of 11 November 2026. AseBio, for example, announced on 10 November 2026 that BioSpain 2027 will be held at Fira de Barcelona Montjuïc from 28 to 30 September, that stand sales would open in November and that the official website for the edition will be available soon. Before booking hotels, travel or a stand, check each date on the show's official website and sign up for the organisers' newsletters.

faqs.q: Which bioprocess trade shows are there in Europe in 2027?
faqs.a: The two big ones are BPI Europe in Hamburg from 27 to 29 April and ACHEMA in Frankfurt from 14 to 18 June. CPHI Frankfurt, from 9 to 11 November, also has a bioproduction zone. If you also sell in the United States, BPI US West takes place in San Diego on 16 and 17 March.

faqs.q: Is it better to exhibit or just visit in the first year?
faqs.a: If you do not know a show, visiting first tells you who exhibits, which booths work and which customers attend. With that you can decide whether to exhibit in the next cycle, with what stand size and which equipment. A middle option is to share a stand with a distributor or partner who already goes.

faqs.q: Are there any new shows in 2027?
faqs.a: Yes. CPHI is launching CPHI Spain, on 1 and 2 June 2027 at Fira de Barcelona, with more than 130 exhibitors and over 2,500 attendees expected. At CPHI Frankfurt the organiser announces new zones for 2027, including one for lab and analytical equipment. As it is a first edition, check the official site before you book anything.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to exhibit at these shows?
faqs.a: Only ACHEMA publishes a full rate card, from €378 to €529.20 per square metre excluding VAT for 2027, without stand build or services. CPHI Frankfurt quotes through its booking form, and at BioSpain AseBio members get special rates. For the rest, ask the organiser for terms and compare every show using the same cost lines.

bio-fitxa-tecnica-web.intro: To turn an equipment datasheet into a product page that sells, every specification has to answer a buyer's question. Working volume tells them which scale it fits, the control software tells them how data is handled and material certificates tell them what they can validate. The page puts those answers in order, carries structured data and offers a PDF that says exactly the same.

seccions.titol: Why a datasheet on its own does not convince buyers
seccions.text:
A PDF datasheet says what the equipment is, but not whether it fits the customer's process. The engineer reading it wants to know whether it suits their scale, whether they can validate it and what it will cost to run. If the page only posts the table of values, they have to dig for those answers or ask for them.
Google also rewards pages that explain more than a list. Its guidance on helpful content asks whether a page gives a substantial, complete description of the topic and whether it shows first-hand expertise, for example from having actually used the product. A page written with the engineer who knows the equipment meets that naturally.

seccions.titol: How to turn each specification into an answer
seccions.text: The trick is to take each line of the datasheet and write next to it the question it answers. The page then explains the answer in plain words and keeps the exact value in the table. Nothing is lost, and readers who are not specialists still understand why it matters.

seccions.titol: In what order the information should appear
seccions.text: The top of the page should say what the equipment is, which process and scale it serves and the three or four facts that set it apart, with a button to request a quote. Below that, each block answers a different reader. Engineering, QA and procurement read different parts, so every block has to be easy to find.

seccions.titol: How to describe software and audit trails without overclaiming
seccions.text:
Control software is one of the things QA looks at most closely. Section 11.10 of the FDA's 21 CFR Part 11 requires, among other controls, secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails that record operator entries and actions that create, modify or delete electronic records. Explain how your software does this and show screenshots.
Be careful with phrases like Part 11 compliant equipment. The rule applies to the companies that use the systems, and it also requires procedures and training that depend on the customer. It is more accurate to say which software features help the customer comply.

seccions.titol: Structured data and a PDF that matches the website
seccions.text:
Google offers product structured data designed for pages where people cannot buy directly, which covers most bioprocess equipment. Mark up the name, brand, description and images, and if you sell several volumes of the same design, group them as variants.
The PDF is useful because people share and print it, but it has to say the same as the web page. The safest approach is to pull the data from a single source, give the PDF a version and date, and always link the latest one from the page. If the PDF duplicates the page, Google lets you use a rel canonical HTTP header to point to the page as the main version.

seccions.titol: Videos and visuals that show the equipment in use
seccions.text: A datasheet cannot show how people work with the equipment. A short operating video, a render with ports and sensors labelled or an animation of the flow path answers questions that text leaves open. For large units that are hard to photograph well, 3D renders explain more than a factory floor photo.

faqs.q: Should we ask for an email address before the datasheet download?
faqs.a: For the basic datasheet, better not. Buyers comparing suppliers want the data fast, and a form can send them to the next website. You can ask for details on more in-depth documents, such as a sample qualification package or an installation guide, which interest people who are already evaluating the equipment seriously.

faqs.q: Should we publish performance values such as kLa?
faqs.a: Yes, if you measured them with a method you can explain. A value without measurement conditions cannot be compared with another manufacturer's figure, and engineers know it. Publish the value with the medium, volume and test conditions, or leave it off the page and offer it in the technical meeting instead.

faqs.q: Do we need a separate page for every volume?
faqs.a: It depends on whether they share one design. If only the volume changes, a family page with a variant table is usually clearer and avoids near-duplicate pages. If each scale has a different design, software or options, each model deserves its own page, linked to the rest of the range.

faqs.q: Who should keep the product data up to date?
faqs.a: Technical data belongs to engineering or product management, and the way it is explained belongs to marketing. What works is one single source for specifications and one person who flags any change. Every update should reach the web page, the PDF and the sales deck at the same time.

bio-gamma-equips-escalat.intro: A bioprocess equipment range is easier to understand when its names and catalogue follow the same path as the customer, from the lab to the pilot plant to GMP production. If every model has a name unrelated to the others, buyers cannot see that they can grow with you. A scale-based architecture, with consistent names and well-linked pages, shows that path at a glance.

seccions.titol: Why a list of models hides the scale-up path
seccions.text:
People developing a process think in stages. They start with a benchtop bioreactor, move to a pilot plant and end up in production. If your catalogue mixes internal codes, legacy names and unrelated acronyms, that path disappears, and the customer may end up buying lab equipment from one supplier and production equipment from another.
Names are only part of the problem. When the range has no clear structure, the website shows it badly as well. Every model sits on an isolated page, links between scales are missing and the sales team has to explain in every meeting how the pieces fit. All of this can be sorted out before the catalogue is designed.

seccions.titol: A naming architecture that follows scale
seccions.text: The easiest architecture to read has three layers. First, the family, which tells you the technology. Then the scale level, which tells you where it fits in the process. Finally the variant, for example single-use or stainless steel. With those three pieces, any model can be read without opening the datasheet.

seccions.titol: What the range must share for the name to be credible
seccions.text: A shared name promises continuity, and buyers will check it. Before presenting a range as a scale-up path, review what the units at each level genuinely have in common. If the software, recipes or design criteria change completely between scales, the name makes a promise the datasheet cannot keep.

seccions.titol: How to reflect the range on your website and in Google
seccions.text:
On the website, each family needs a page that shows the full scale-up path, with links to every model and a comparison table. Each model gets its own page and links back to the family and to the neighbouring levels. That way customers and Google understand the same structure.
Google recommends marking up product variants with ProductGroup and the variesBy, hasVariant and productGroupID properties, and supports this on pages where people cannot buy directly. Schema.org defines a ProductGroup as products that vary only in well-described ways, such as size or material. Use it when models share one design in several volumes, not to bundle different machines together.

seccions.titol: Check and protect the names before printing the catalogue
seccions.text:
A range name ends up in catalogues, on trade show stands, on equipment nameplates and in validation documents. Changing it later is expensive. So check that it is free in the trademark databases of the markets you sell to before you invest in it.
If you export, WIPO's Madrid System lets you file a single international application and pay one set of fees to seek protection in the 133 countries it covers. You first need a national or regional mark that is registered or applied for. A trademark attorney can tell you which classes and countries make sense.

faqs.q: Should we rename equipment that already sells well?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. If a name is already known in the market, you can keep it and add the family or scale level next to it. The change can be gradual, first on the website and in new catalogues, then in the documentation. On the website, redirect old pages to the new ones so you do not lose visitors.

faqs.q: Should the volume be part of the product name?
faqs.a: Better next to it than inside it. Volume ranges change as the range grows, and a name with numbers dates quickly. Put the scale level in the name and the volume or membrane area range right beside it, on the website, in the catalogue and on the equipment nameplate.

faqs.q: Does the single-use line need a separate brand?
faqs.a: Usually a suffix or a word repeated across the range is enough. A new brand makes sense if the line sells to a very different audience or through another channel. Otherwise, splitting it off breaks the scale-up path you want to show and leaves you explaining two brands instead of one.

faqs.q: How do we show a range that goes up to 2,000 litres at a trade show?
faqs.a: Taking large units to a trade show is costly and complicated. What works is bringing the lab unit and showing the larger levels with 3D renders, animation or a wall graphic that lays out the whole range in order of scale. Visitors see the full path, touch what they can and leave with the idea that you can grow with their process.

bio-gmp-part11-web.intro: No piece of bioprocess equipment is GMP certified or Part 11 compliant on its own, because those rules bind the company that makes the medicine and uses the system. What a manufacturer can say is how the equipment is designed, what documentation it supplies for qualification and what the software does. Said precisely, that convinces buyers more and keeps the brand out of trouble.

seccions.titol: Why no equipment is GMP or Part 11 on its own
seccions.text:
GMP rules bind medicine manufacturers. The European Medicines Agency explains that authorities inspect manufacturing sites and then issue either a GMP certificate or a non-compliance statement. The certificate therefore belongs to the customer's site, not to the bioreactor or TFF system installed there.
Part 11 works the same way. Section 11.10 of the FDA rule is addressed to people who use systems to create, modify or maintain electronic records, and it asks them for controls such as validation, training of users and written policies. Some of those controls depend on the software, and others depend on the customer's own procedures.

seccions.titol: Risky phrases and better ways to say them
seccions.text: Some websites in this sector repeat short phrases that sound good but that a QA team will not accept. The risk goes beyond the legal side. An expert buyer reads them as a sign of shallow regulatory knowledge and starts doubting the rest of the page. The table lists the most common ones with a more precise alternative.

seccions.titol: How to describe IQ, OQ and PQ support
seccions.text:
Annex 15 of the EU GMP guidelines describes the qualification path, from the URS and design qualification through FAT, SAT, IQ, OQ and PQ. Point 2.6 says that when protocols come from a third party, site personnel must confirm they are suitable before approving them. The supplier supports and the customer decides.
On the website, explain what you deliver and who does what. For example, what the documentation package contains, whether you offer protocol templates for the customer to review and who runs the tests at FAT and on site. Also say which part stays with the customer, such as PQ, which under point 3.14 uses production materials or an equivalent substitute.

seccions.titol: How to talk about audit trails and software
seccions.text:
Describe concrete features. Sections 11.10 and 11.300 of Part 11 call for secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails, authority checks so only authorised people can use the system, and controls over user IDs and passwords. Point 9 of EU Annex 11 adds that the reason for any change or deletion of GMP data should be documented and that audit trails should be reviewed regularly.
In points 3.3 and 3.4, Annex 11 also says that regulated users should review the documentation supplied with commercial products, and that information on the supplier's quality system should be available to inspectors on request. A matrix that maps each requirement to a software feature or a customer procedure answers many questions before the audit even starts.

seccions.titol: What to say about Annex 1 if you make single-use equipment or consumables
seccions.text:
The revised Annex 1 on the manufacture of sterile medicinal products came into operation on 25 August 2023 and has been fully applicable since 25 August 2024. It asks each site for a contamination control strategy, and point 2.5 lists vendor approval among its elements, including suppliers of single-use systems. Point 8.134 states that assessing suppliers of disposable systems is critical to selecting them.
So what helps the customer is data. Points 8.134 to 8.137 of Annex 1 call for evaluating extractables and leachables profiles, system integrity during processing and evidence of sterilisation for each unit on receipt. If you can supply that information, say so and explain how it is delivered. It is far more useful than a general line about Annex 1.

seccions.titol: Who should review these claims before they go live
seccions.text:
Every regulatory claim on the website, in catalogues and in sales decks needs evidence behind it and a QA person who has reviewed it. A simple register with the claim, the evidence and the review date stops each document from saying something different.
Review that register whenever a standard or a product changes, and share it with distributors so they do not turn a careful sentence into a bolder one when translating it. Marketing writes and structures, while QA and regulatory affairs have the final say on what gets promised.

faqs.q: Can we call our software Part 11 ready?
faqs.a: If you do, explain what it means. A label like that without detail will not convince QA. Back it with a list of features, such as audit trail, user management and electronic signatures, and a matrix showing which requirements the software covers and which depend on the customer's procedures.

faqs.q: If a customer has qualified our equipment, can we say so?
faqs.a: Only with written permission, and precisely. The qualification belongs to the customer and their site, not to the equipment. You could say, for example, that the equipment runs in GMP plants for a given modality or country, as long as it is true and the customer agrees.

faqs.q: What if a competitor says GMP certified on their website?
faqs.a: Do not copy it. Customers' QA teams know the difference, and an overstated claim can make them doubt all your documentation. A precise explanation of what you deliver makes you look more expert, and that counts in a purchase where regulatory risk is the main concern.

faqs.q: Do we need a lawyer to review these claims?
faqs.a: For everyday wording, a QA or regulatory affairs person who knows the rules and the product is usually enough. Terms of sale, warranties and contracts should go through a lawyer. What matters most is that no claim goes live without someone qualified having seen the evidence behind it.

bio-google-ads-equips-laboratori.intro: Google Ads works for lab and bioprocess equipment when campaigns are built around application and scale, when you only bid on searches with intent to request a quote, and when budget is split by country. The last step is sending the leads your CRM marks as qualified back to Google Ads, so automated bidding learns from real projects.

seccions.titol: Why a single equipment campaign does not work
seccions.text:
Searches for lab and bioprocess equipment are few and mix very different audiences. A student may search for «bioreactor», and so may a researcher who wants a benchtop unit or a plant preparing a scale-up. If everything goes into one campaign with the same keywords and the same ad, it is hard to tell which part of the budget brings in buyers.
Google rates each keyword with a Quality Score from 1 to 10, based on expected clickthrough rate, ad relevance and landing page experience. It is a diagnostic tool and not an input in the auction, but it flags when the ad and the page do not match what the person is looking for.

seccions.titol: Campaigns by application and scale, each with its own page
seccions.text:
A structure that is easy to control is one campaign per application or per scale, with ad groups by equipment type. Each ad group leads to a page about the same application and scale as the search, with the data, the available documentation and a short quote request form.
Google offers three match types. Exact gives you the most control and reaches the fewest searches, phrase covers more, and broad reaches related searches even when they lack the exact meaning of the keyword. Google says broad match should be used with Smart Bidding. With only a few leads a month, starting with phrase and exact is the safer choice.

seccions.titol: Bid on searches that signal a quote request
seccions.text:
Buying signals are easy to spot. Price, quote, supplier, manufacturer or a specific scale in litres. Study signals are just as clear, such as «what is», «working principle», «types of» or «pdf». The first group goes into the campaigns with the larger budget and the second into a negative keyword list.
In between sit searches with no clear intent, such as the name of a process. They can make sense in a small campaign that leads to a downloadable application note. In that case, measure it by downloads and the contacts that follow, because it rarely turns into a quote request on the same day.

seccions.titol: One budget per country and language
seccions.text:
If you sell in several countries, split campaigns by country or group of countries, each in its own language. That way you decide how much goes to Germany, the Nordics or Spain, and one market does not eat the others' budget. Google recommends keeping language and location targeting consistent and writing the ads in that language.
For Search, Google recommends the «Presence or interest» option, which also reaches people who have shown interest in the area. It suggests «Presence» when you only want to reach people located there. If you sell through distributors by country, Presence keeps you from paying for clicks in markets someone else covers.

seccions.titol: Send CRM-qualified leads back to Google Ads
seccions.text:
A submitted form is a long way from an equipment order. If Google Ads only counts forms, automated bidding will chase more forms, including those from students or vendors. To avoid that, import what happens next in your CRM, such as a qualified lead, a quote sent or an order. Google calls this offline conversion import.
Google recommends starting with enhanced conversions for leads, an upgraded version of that import that uses hashed data the user provided, such as an email address. If your CRM uploads through the Google Ads API, since 15 June 2026 those uploads go through the Data Manager API and are blocked in the Google Ads API, so the integration is worth checking.

faqs.q: How much budget do we need to start Google Ads for lab equipment?
faqs.a: There is no figure that fits everyone, because it depends on the countries, the competition for each search and how many applications you want to cover. It is more useful to start with one application and one country, look at the cost per qualified lead after a few weeks and then decide whether to expand to other markets or scales.

faqs.q: Does the Google Ads healthcare policy affect equipment manufacturers?
faqs.a: The main Healthcare and medicines policy page does not mention lab or bioprocess equipment. Its section on pharmaceutical manufacturers does restrict suppliers of antibodies, peptides and compounds for commercial labs, who may only advertise in Canada and the United States. If your landing pages name prescription drugs, review that policy as well before you launch.

faqs.q: Do we need a landing page for every campaign?
faqs.a: Each ad group should lead to a page about the same application and scale as the search. Google considers landing page experience when it calculates Quality Score. You do not need a new website, but you do need application pages with data, documentation and a short form to request a quote.

bio-google-ads-estudiants.intro: Google Ads sends students when the words for your equipment are also the words of a lecture, such as «bioreactor», «tangential flow filtration» or «chromatography». You filter them with a negative keyword list for academic and definition searches, tighter match types, the odd audience exclusion and a form that asks about the project. The aim is to cut noise without losing volume.

seccions.titol: Why Google Ads sends you students
seccions.text:
Lab and bioprocess equipment shares its names with course topics. A biotech student and a process engineer can both type «bioreactor» on the same day. With broad match, Google can show your ad on related searches even when they lack the exact meaning of your keyword, and that is where definitions, lecture notes and final-year projects come in.
To see it, open the search terms report. It shows the actual searches that triggered your ads and which keyword matched them. Google lists searches used by a significant number of people, so some very low-volume terms will not appear. After a few weeks of data, the academic patterns are usually easy to spot.

seccions.titol: A negative keyword list for academic searches
seccions.text:
The foundation is an account-level negative keyword list, which applies to all your search campaigns. It should cover the words that signal studying in every language you advertise in. Negative keywords do not match close variants, so you need to add singulars, plurals and synonyms. Google also treats a word with and without an accent as two different negatives, such as «qué» and «que» in Spanish. In the PharmaBios case, a pharmaceutical equipment manufacturer, there were already more than 200 negative keywords by mid-November.
Watch out for words buyers use too. «PDF» blocks plenty of lecture notes, but also someone looking for an equipment datasheet. «Types of» can be a student or an engineer comparing options. In those cases, check the search terms report first and only add the combinations that bring no buyers. Google warns that too many negatives reduce your reach.

seccions.titol: Tighter match types where the noise is
seccions.text:
The most generic keywords, such as the name of a piece of equipment or a process, bring the most students. Exact match gives you the most control over who sees the ad, even though it reaches fewer searches. Phrase match lets the search include the meaning of your keyword alongside other words, and broad match reaches related searches.
A practical approach is to put generic keywords on exact match and those that already signal buying, such as a scale, an application or «supplier», on phrase match. If you use broad match, Google says to pair it with Smart Bidding. And for Smart Bidding to learn to avoid students, it needs qualified lead data, as we explain below.

seccions.titol: Audience exclusions, only as a complement
seccions.text:
Google Ads has detailed demographic segments, and college students is one of the examples it gives. It also lets you exclude demographic categories so ads do not show to certain groups. That can help, but Google warns that it cannot estimate demographic information for everyone, and the narrower your filters, the fewer people your ads reach.
Do not exclude by age. A young engineer may be the one preparing the equipment comparison for their manager. Do not exclude universities either, because research groups and core facilities buy equipment too. What you want to remove are searches for lecture notes and definitions.

seccions.titol: Form questions that filter without putting buyers off
seccions.text:
A good form separates students from buyers without scaring anyone away. Asking about the project helps more than adding mandatory fields. If a student does come through, it is worth pointing them to a resources page or an application note. That keeps them out of the sales inbox, and they may come back once they work in industry.
With these answers, your CRM can classify the lead before anyone has to read it. Keep the questions few and multiple choice, because a long form can also put off a buyer in a hurry.

seccions.titol: Measure lead quality, not just how many arrive
seccions.text:
If Google Ads counts every form as a conversion, automated bidding cannot tell a student from a pilot plant. That is why it pays to send the CRM outcome back to Google Ads, such as a qualified lead or a quote sent, and optimise for that conversion. Review the search terms report weekly at first and monthly after that.
When we review the SEM strategy of an account in this sector, the negative keyword list and what the CRM marks as a qualified lead are among the first things we look at, before touching bids or ads.

faqs.q: If we exclude «what is», do we lose engineers doing research?
faqs.a: Some engineers run these searches too, but at that point they are unlikely to ask for a quote. A good explanatory page that ranks organically, with links to your application pages, is a better way to reach them. That leaves ads for searches with buying intent and lets content handle the learning stage.

faqs.q: Should we exclude universities from our campaigns?
faqs.a: Not as a rule. University research groups and core facilities buy lab equipment and sometimes pilot plants. What you need to filter are study searches, such as lecture notes, definitions or coursework, and add a form question about the type of organisation and the project so you know who is who.

faqs.q: How often should we review search terms?
faqs.a: Weekly at the start, because that is when many of the academic searches you did not anticipate show up. Once the negative list settles, a monthly review is enough. Remember that the report only lists searches made by a significant number of people, so some very low-volume terms will not appear.

bio-google-ads-politica-salut.intro: A pharma or biotech company can advertise equipment, services and, with Google certification, over-the-counter medicines on Google Ads. Outside Canada, New Zealand and the United States it cannot advertise prescription drugs, and the policy also restricts antibodies and compounds for labs, cell and gene therapies and clinical trial recruitment. What you can run depends on what you sell, what your landing page says and the country.

seccions.titol: What the Healthcare and medicines policy covers
seccions.text:
Google explains that some healthcare content cannot be advertised at all, while other content can only run in certain locations and by advertisers it has approved. The policy is split into sections, such as prescription drug services, restricted drug terms, pharmaceutical manufacturers, unapproved substances, cell and gene therapies and clinical trial recruitment.
Two details are worth knowing. The English version is the official one used to enforce the policy, even though translations exist. And for most healthcare sections, when a campaign targets allowed locations and the domain is certified, the ad is labelled «Eligible (limited)» and only runs in those locations.
