For every country you target, you need to read its specific rules.

seccions.titol: Equipment makers and CDMOs, the risk is drug names
seccions.text:
The policy does not mention lab or bioprocess equipment, nor contract development and manufacturing services. The risk comes from elsewhere. Google restricts prescription drug terms in ads, landing pages and keywords. Outside Canada, New Zealand and the United States, you may not use them in ads or on landing pages.
For a CDMO, a case study that names a prescription drug or its active ingredient can get the ad pointing to it disapproved. It is safer to talk about the modality, such as monoclonal antibodies, vaccines or recombinant proteins, and keep drug names on pages that do not receive ad traffic. Google does allow non-promotional use, such as regulatory warnings, legal notices or academic publications.

seccions.titol: Who can advertise what, and in which countries
seccions.text:
Pharmaceutical manufacturers must be certified by Google to serve ads. They may only promote prescription drugs in Canada, New Zealand and the United States. Over-the-counter medicines can be promoted in a list of countries that includes Spain, Germany, France, Italy, Portugal, the Netherlands, Sweden and the United Kingdom, among others.
One section can affect many biotechs. Bulk drug manufacturers, medical professional suppliers and suppliers of antibodies, peptides and compounds for commercial labs may only advertise in Canada and the United States. If you sell these products to labs in Europe, this section does not allow you to advertise them in campaigns that run there.

seccions.titol: Cell and gene therapy, informational content only
seccions.text:
Google does not allow the promotion of speculative or experimental medical treatments, nor of cell or gene therapies. The only exception is in the United States, where it allows the promotion of FDA-licensed or approved cell or gene therapies by the entities that hold the licence or approval to market them.
It does allow ads for these therapies that are exclusively educational or informational, whatever their approval status. For a CDMO or a supplier working in this field, the cautious route is an ad and a landing page about the manufacturing service or the equipment, with no promise of any treatment effect in patients.

seccions.titol: Clinical trials and country changes in 2026
seccions.text:
Google does not allow clinical trial recruitment ads in most locations. Where it does, prescription drugs may not be promoted, ads may not create misleading expectations, and they may not imply that the product being tested is safe. The list includes Belgium, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom and the United States, but not Spain.
Country rules can change, and Google announces the changes in policy update notes. On 22 July 2026 it posted that, from August, telemedicine providers certified by LegitScript and by Google may promote prescription drug services in Spain. The current rules for Spain already include it, and ads and landing pages still cannot promote prescription drugs.

seccions.titol: What to check before a campaign goes live
seccions.text:
Before launching, check what you sell, which words appear in the ad and on the page, and which countries the campaign targets. If certification is needed, Google asks you to apply from the client account rather than the manager account, and an agency must send documentation of its relationship with the advertiser. In the PharmaBios case, a pharmaceutical equipment manufacturer, we reviewed the account they already had and put everything in a report before changing anything.
For sections such as pharmaceutical manufacturers or clinical trials, Google issues a warning at least seven days before suspending an account. Unauthorized pharmacies, on the other hand, are treated as an egregious violation and lead to account suspension.

seccions.titol: What Spanish law says about advertising medicines
seccions.text:
In Spain, the law also restricts advertising medicines to the public. Article 80 of the consolidated 2015 law on guarantees and rational use of medicines only allows it for medicines that are not publicly funded, that can be used without a doctor making the diagnosis, prescribing or monitoring the treatment, and that are not psychotropic or narcotic substances.
The same article requires the message to make clear that the product is a medicine, to give its name, to invite people to read the leaflet and ask a pharmacist, and to avoid promising a cure or using testimonials from well-known people or professionals. This advertising needs no prior authorisation, but health authorities monitor it. So in Spain, Google policy and the law point the same way.

seccions.titol: How to set up a Google Ads campaign in the pharma sector
seccions.text:
The structure that fits the policy best is one campaign per country, or per group of countries with the same rules, with ad groups by product or service. That way an ad that can only run in the United States never mixes with your European ones. If you sell equipment, our guide to Google Ads for lab equipment explains how to split applications and scales.
For locations, Google recommends «Presence or interest» by default, which also reaches people who have shown interest in your chosen places. The «Presence» option shows ads to people who are, or regularly are, in those places. In a sector with country-specific rules, we suggest «Presence», so the campaign targets people who are where the policy allows it.
Negative keywords, which Google describes as a way to exclude search terms from your campaigns, help keep out patient searches and drug names when you sell to businesses. Check the search terms report every week at first. When we run Google Ads campaigns for companies in this sector, these are among the first things we look at.

faqs.q: Can we advertise a bioreactor or a TFF system on Google Ads without certification?
faqs.a: The Healthcare and medicines policy does not mention this equipment, so in principle no healthcare certification is needed. The ad still has to meet the rest of the Google Ads policies, and the landing page should avoid prescription drug names, because outside Canada, New Zealand and the United States they cannot be used.

faqs.q: Can a CDMO say which drugs it manufactures?
faqs.a: On the website, yes, but take care with the pages that receive ad traffic. Outside Canada, New Zealand and the United States, Google does not allow prescription drug terms in ads or on landing pages. One option is to send ads to pages about capabilities and modalities, and keep case studies that name drugs in other sections.

faqs.q: What happens if Google disapproves an ad under this policy?
faqs.a: You can edit the ad or choose another landing page that complies, and Google reviews it again. If you think it is a mistake, you can appeal from the account. If you cannot fix it, Google advises removing it, because repeated policy violations can lead to account suspension.

faqs.q: Can a pharma company advertise OTC medicines on Google Ads in Spain?
faqs.a: Yes, if it holds Google certification as a pharmaceutical manufacturer, because Spain is on the list of countries where over-the-counter medicines can be promoted. Spanish law also only allows advertising to the public for medicines that are not publicly funded and do not need a doctor, and the message has to meet the requirements of Article 80.

bio-ia-preparar-visites-comercials.intro: AI can build a pharma account brief before a sales call if you give it reliable public sources and ask for a link behind every fact. What works is a one-page summary covering the pipeline, recent approvals, new facilities and job postings, checked by a person, with the data on meeting attendees handled in line with the GDPR.

seccions.titol: What an account brief should cover before the meeting
seccions.text:
A good account brief fits on one page and answers one question, why this company might need your equipment now. AI helps gather and summarise public information, but you decide the structure. If every sales rep asks for something different, every brief will look different and nobody can compare them.
These are the sections we suggest for a brief on a pharma company, a biotech or a CDMO. Every fact needs the link it comes from, and anything that cannot be verified becomes a question for the meeting.

seccions.titol: Where to get the facts without relying on what the AI says
seccions.text:
For a European pharma company, many of the most useful sources are public. The European Medicines Agency publishes a monthly list of medicines under evaluation by its human medicines committee. The list gives the international non-proprietary name of the substance and a short summary of the indication, and it is worth cross-checking against the company's press releases.
The EU clinical trials website has information on individual trials in the EU and the European Economic Area since 31 January 2022. A late-stage trial may mean the company is already thinking about scale-up and manufacturing. Annual reports, press releases about new sites and job postings fill in the rest of the picture.

seccions.titol: How to prompt the AI so it does not make up facts
seccions.text:
AI assistants can state false facts with great confidence, such as an approval that never happened or a plant in the wrong city. In front of a pharma customer, a mistake like that costs credibility straight away. So your prompt should force the tool to cite a link for every claim and to say clearly when it found nothing.
It helps to split the brief into two columns, sourced facts and the sales rep's hypotheses. Facts are checked by opening the link before the meeting, and anything without a source is removed or turned into a question. Someone on the team should review the brief before it is shared, especially figures and dates.

seccions.titol: From the brief to the questions you ask in the meeting
seccions.text:
The brief is mainly there to prepare good questions. If one of the company's antibodies reaches late-stage trials, it makes sense to ask how they plan scale-up or tech transfer. If they are hiring upstream specialists, they may be expanding cell culture capacity. These are hypotheses the customer has to confirm.
With a pharma buyer, showing that you understand their context opens the conversation, and reading the brief back to them closes it. Use the facts to ask specific questions and let the customer explain their project, their scale and their timeline.

seccions.titol: GDPR limits when you research people
seccions.text:
The GDPR does not cover data about companies as legal persons, as its recital 14 explains, but it does cover data about the people attending the meeting. If you store data in the CRM about someone who did not give it to you, article 14(3) says that, as a rule, you must inform them within a reasonable period and within one month at the latest, or at the first communication if you use it to contact them.
In practice, stick to job title, company and public professional profile, and leave private life out. If you use the data for direct marketing, article 21 gives the person the right to object at any time, and you must then stop using it for that purpose. Before pasting personal data into an AI tool, check what the provider does with it.

seccions.titol: How to roll it out across the sales team
seccions.text:
Start with a brief template and a fixed prompt for the AI assistant that the whole team uses the same way. Store each brief in the CRM under the account, so the next person who visits does not start from scratch. After the meeting, the sales rep adds what was confirmed and what was ruled out.
After a few meetings, compare the briefs with what actually happened. If the hypotheses were far from reality, adjust the sources or the prompt. When we set this up with a sales team, we start from the meetings already in their calendar and the sources they already use.

faqs.q: Which AI tool works well for preparing sales calls?
faqs.a: Any assistant that can search the web and cite the sources behind each answer. For a company, a business plan with clear data protection terms is the safer choice. The template and the prompt matter more than the tool, because they are what prevent invented answers and a different brief for every sales rep.

faqs.q: Can we look up the people who will attend the meeting?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. Job title, company and public professional profile help you prepare the conversation, and private life has no place in it. If you store that data in the CRM, article 14 of the GDPR generally requires you to inform the person within one month or at first contact, and article 21 lets them object.

faqs.q: How do we know whether a pipeline fact is correct?
faqs.a: Open the link that comes with it and check it against a primary source, such as the European Medicines Agency's list of medicines under evaluation, the EU clinical trials website or the company's own press releases. If there is no link, or the source says something different, the fact does not go into the brief.

bio-jornada-portes-obertes-planta.intro: A factory open house works when buyers see what a trade show cannot show them, namely how you build, who stands behind the product and the equipment running. Keep the agenda short with talks, small-group tours and live demos, invite selectively, set clear access rules for sensitive areas and film the day so it feeds your content for months.

seccions.titol: When it makes sense to open your plant to customers
seccions.text:
It makes sense when your product is hard to show on a booth. A production bioreactor, a TFF skid or a single-use consumables line is hard to bring to an exhibition hall, and buyers want to see where it is built, how quality is controlled and who will support them after the sale. At your own site all of that is within reach.
It also helps when the customer is close to a decision. A procurement, engineering and QA team from a pharma company or a CDMO understands a supplier far better after seeing the workshop, the test area and the applications lab before writing the URS or booking a FAT. If the decision is still far off, a trade show or a webinar gives more reach for less effort.

seccions.titol: An agenda with short talks, a tour and live demos
seccions.text: Leave room in the agenda for conversation. Two or three trend talks are enough, on topics customers deal with at work, such as scale-up from lab to pilot and production, single-use versus stainless steel, or contamination control under Annex 1. Then run the tour in small groups and the demos at separate stations.

seccions.titol: Who to invite and how to send the invitation
seccions.text:
Invite fewer people and choose them well. Start from your CRM, meaning open opportunities, customers who could expand, distributors who need to sell the equipment and an expert or two who give the talks weight. Ask for company, role, project stage and scale on the registration form so you know who needs a meeting and who is coming to learn.
Be careful with how invitations go out. In Spain, Article 21 of Law 34/2002 (LSSI) bans promotional email to people who have not asked for it or expressly agreed to it, unless there is a prior contractual relationship and the message is about your own products or services similar to what they bought. Article 13 of the GDPR also requires you to say, when collecting the data, who handles it, why and how long it is kept.

seccions.titol: Access rules for cleanrooms and GMP areas
seccions.text:
If your plant has a cleanroom or GMP areas, plan the route starting from where nobody can go. Point 2.13 of Chapter 2 of the EU GMP guide says visitors should preferably not be taken into production and quality control areas. If it cannot be avoided, they should be briefed in advance on hygiene and protective clothing and closely supervised.
Annex 1, written for sterile medicinal products, goes further. Point 7.2 asks for only the minimum number of personnel required in cleanrooms, and point 7.5 says unqualified personnel should not enter grade B cleanrooms or grade A in operation, except in exceptional cases under a written procedure. Even if you do not make medicines, many of your visitors know these rules and will notice if the tour ignores them.

seccions.titol: Reception, and what nobody should see
seccions.text:
Reception sets the tone for the day. Have badges ready, explain the route and the rules in a few minutes and make it clear where photos are not allowed. A simple map with stations and times keeps groups from mixing and stops anyone from wandering the workshop alone.
Check what will be in plain sight that day too. An equipment plant often has other customers' machines in assembly or in FAT, with drawings and screens showing project data. Move them off the route or cover them, scan the registration list for competitors and, if needed, ask for a confidentiality agreement at the door.

faqs.q: How far ahead should we plan a customer open house?
faqs.a: It depends on the size, but remember that visitors from abroad need to book travel and that industry calendars fill up around the big shows. Pick a date well away from weeks such as ACHEMA or CPHI, send a save the date early and follow with the full invitation and agenda later. Demos and talks are what take the most preparation.

faqs.q: Can we run a demo with live cells or microorganisms?
faqs.a: At an open event, better not. Water or a buffer is enough to show the control system, the software, a single-use bag change or how a TFF system runs. That avoids biosafety and cleaning risks and lets you repeat the demo as often as needed. If someone wants to see real culture data, show it on screen.

faqs.q: Can we film and photograph attendees?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as you tell them. Article 4(1) of the GDPR defines personal data as any information about an identifiable person, including through factors specific to their physical identity. Explain on the registration form that there will be photos and video, what they will be used for and how to opt out. On the day, mark who does not want to appear and check images before publishing.

faqs.q: Is an open house realistic for a small company?
faqs.a: Yes, and sometimes it makes more sense than a large booth. A small group of customers and distributors, one talk, the tour and two demos is enough. What you cannot skip is a clear agenda, one person leading each group, access rules worked out in advance and a plan to film the day and follow up.

bio-kit-distribuidor.intro: A lab or bioprocess equipment distributor needs a kit that lets them sell without improvising. Translated datasheets and application notes, renders and videos of the equipment, a price-free sales deck, use cases and clear brand rules for joint material. With a good kit, your brand looks the same in Germany, Scandinavia or Asia.

seccions.titol: Why distributors need a complete kit
seccions.text:
Without a kit, each distributor ends up making their own material. They translate datasheets as best they can, use old photos, change the colours and sometimes promise things the equipment does not do, such as GMP compliance that in fact depends on the customer. The result is a different brand in every country and a technical risk that the manufacturer ends up paying for.
A distributor carries many brands and has little time for each. If your material is translated, organised and ready to use, they are more likely to include you in visits and quotes. The kit is how you sell through others without losing control of what is said about your equipment.

seccions.titol: Datasheets and application notes in the distributor's language
seccions.text:
The core of the kit is translated technical documentation. Datasheets for each model and scale, application notes by modality, such as monoclonal antibodies, vaccines or microbial fermentation, and a document explaining what you deliver for qualification. Every PDF should carry a date and version number so nobody sends out an outdated datasheet.
Keep sales material separate from manuals. Article 10(7) of the EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230, which applies from 20 January 2027, says the manufacturer must provide instructions for use and safety information in a language easily understood by users, as determined by the Member State concerned. And the datasheets in the kit must say the same as the manuals.

seccions.titol: A sales deck without prices
seccions.text:
The deck in the kit should not include prices, because they change over time and vary by country. Price lists go through a private channel. Also, under Article 4(a) of Regulation (EU) 2022/720, agreements that restrict the distributor's freedom to set its own resale price lose the exemption. A recommended or maximum price is allowed, as long as in practice it does not become a fixed or minimum one.
Build an editable template in the distributor's language, with room for their contact details. A structure that works is the customer's problem, the equipment and range by scale, what sets it apart, documentation and service, two or three cases and the next step. Mark which slides must not be changed.

seccions.titol: Co-branding rules that keep one brand
seccions.text:
Co-branding rules set out how your brand and the distributor's sit together. Where each logo goes and at what size, which colours and typefaces to use, how product names are written and which line identifies the authorised distributor. Include right and wrong examples, because people grasp them faster than rules.
Before you hand over your logo, protect the brand in the countries where you sell. WIPO's Madrid System lets you apply for protection in up to 133 countries with a single international application, based on a national or regional registration or application. Each national office then decides whether to grant protection in its territory.
Agree too how they will use your brand in Google Ads. Google's trademark policy does not restrict using a trademark as a keyword. If the owner complains about ad text, Google does not restrict it when the landing page is mainly about selling those products, shows how to buy them with commercial details such as prices and makes clear it is a reseller. It does restrict confusing or misleading use.

seccions.titol: How to keep the kit up to date
seccions.text:
An outdated kit does more harm than having none. Give it an owner, keep it in one place, tell distributors when there is a new version and withdraw old material. Review it at least whenever you launch equipment, change a specification or enter a new market.
Ask distributors what they use and what is missing, and check which files get downloaded. They often ask for simple things, such as a shorter datasheet, a subtitled video or a case from their sector. Those small pieces are what get your equipment into their sales visits.

faqs.q: Who should handle translation, the manufacturer or the distributor?
faqs.a: The safest approach is for the manufacturer to commission the technical translation and the distributor to review it, since they know how customers in their country talk. That way you control what is said about the equipment and the distributor adds the local tone. Keep approved terms in a glossary to reuse in later translations.

faqs.q: Can I let distributors create their own material?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as they use your templates and brand rules and send you the important pieces for approval before publishing. Set a short review time so they do not feel held back. Local material, such as a case from a customer in their country, often works better than general material.

faqs.q: Do I need to register my trademark in every distributor country?
faqs.a: It is wise to have it protected wherever you sell. The Madrid System lets you apply for many countries with one international application, but each national office decides whether to grant protection. Do it before handing your logo to a distributor and get advice from a trademark attorney.

faqs.q: Can my distributor run Google Ads using my brand?
faqs.a: Google Ads policy does not stop anyone using a trademark as a keyword. In ad text, if the owner complains, Google still allows it when the landing page sells those products, shows commercial details and makes clear it is a reseller. The practical route is to agree it in the contract, with rules for ad copy and keywords, and to decide who runs campaigns in each country.

bio-landing-demo-equip.intro: A demo request landing page for lab or bioprocess equipment should say which demo formats you offer, what the customer will see and who will run it. Then it needs a short form that asks for scale, process and timeline without putting off an engineer, and a clear answer about what happens after they submit it. If it gets Google Ads traffic, it also has to load fast.

seccions.titol: What a demo landing page has to solve
seccions.text:
The person requesting a demo of a bioreactor or TFF system is usually a process scientist or an engineer who already has a project in mind. Before leaving their details, they want to know three things, whether the system fits their scale, what kind of demo they can get and how much work it will take on their side. If the page does not say, they leave without filling in the form.
That is why a demo landing page works differently from a generic contact page. It has a single goal, explains the process before asking for anything and removes doubts for a technical buyer. In return, the sales team receives requests with the information it needs to prepare a good demo.

seccions.titol: Demos at your site, at the customer's lab or online
seccions.text:
The landing page should state which demo formats you offer and what each one involves. Watching a system run at your facility is very different from testing it in the customer's lab or seeing the control software on a video call. Each format needs different preparation and appeals to different people.
If you offer all three formats, let visitors choose one in the form itself, so the sales engineer knows from the start what needs to be organised. If you only offer one or two, say so clearly on the page to avoid requests you cannot handle.

seccions.titol: What the landing page should show before the form
seccions.text:
The headline should say which system is being demonstrated and for which scale, whether lab, pilot or production. Then explain what the demo includes, who runs it and what the customer needs to bring or prepare. An application specialist with a name and job title builds more trust than an anonymous form.
A short video of the system helps an engineer understand what they will see before asking for it. An application note or an anonymised case study also fits here. All of this should sit above the form, because buyers decide whether to fill it in while they read.

seccions.titol: Form fields that qualify without scaring off an engineer
seccions.text:
The form should only ask for what sales will use to prepare the demo. The GDPR asks for this in article 5(1)(c), which says personal data must be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the purposes of the processing. On top of that, every extra field is another reason for an engineer to leave it for another day.
These are the fields we suggest for most equipment manufacturers. Dropdowns qualify faster than free text and take less effort to fill in. Phone number and budget can be left out or made optional, because the sales engineer can ask for them in the first conversation.

seccions.titol: What should happen after the form is submitted
seccions.text:
The thank-you page should say what happens next, who will contact the customer and how. For online demos, you can offer a calendar to book a slot straight away. A confirmation email summarising the request saves the customer from having to explain everything again.
Behind the scenes, the request should enter the CRM with its source and go to the right specialist or to the local distributor. The submission itself should be marked as a key event in Google Analytics 4, so you know which channels bring demo requests rather than just visits.

seccions.titol: If the page gets Google Ads traffic, it also needs to be fast
seccions.text:
Google Ads calculates Quality Score from three components, and one of them is landing page experience, meaning how relevant and useful the page is to people who click the ad. That is why it pays to have one landing page per equipment family or scale, using the same language as the ads and keywords.
Speed matters too, especially on mobile. Google recommends that the main content appears within 2.5 seconds, that the page responds to interactions in 200 milliseconds or less and that unexpected layout shifts stay at 0.1 or below. Videos and 3D viewers should load without slowing down the form.

faqs.q: Should we add a calendar so people can book the demo directly?
faqs.a: For online demos, yes, because it saves emails back and forth to find a time. For a demo at your site or at the customer's lab, a form followed by a call works better, since you need to discuss logistics, the sample process and who will attend. In those cases, say on the thank-you page when they will hear from you.

faqs.q: How many fields should a demo request form have?
faqs.a: There is no magic number. Every required field should help sales prepare a better demo, and the rest should be optional or removed. If nobody looks at a field when the request comes in, drop it. Scale, process and timeline usually give the most information for the least effort.

faqs.q: Do we need a separate landing page for each system?
faqs.a: If you run Google Ads campaigns by equipment family or scale, yes, because the page has to answer what the person who clicked was looking for. For organic traffic, a demo block on each product page that leads to a shared form with the system already selected may be enough.

bio-lead-scoring-universitat-farma.intro: To score academic, startup and pharma leads in one CRM, keep who the contact is apart from what they do. Fit tells you how much the account could be worth and how that type of customer buys. Intent tells you whether there is a live project right now. With signals from forms, content, demos and trade shows, sales knows whom to call first and whom to give time.

seccions.titol: Why an academic lead is not worth the same as a pharma lead
seccions.text:
A maker of lab and bioprocess equipment sells to customers who buy in very different ways. An academic group pays with research project funds, a startup spends money from a funding round and a pharma company or CDMO goes through capex approval and QA. Value, timing and the people who decide change in each case.
If they all enter the CRM with the same score, two things happen. Students downloading datasheets for a class project look like hot leads, and the pharma company that has read three pages of GMP documentation gets buried in the list. You need a model that takes into account who each contact is.

seccions.titol: Two scores, one for fit and another for intent
seccions.text:
It works better to run two separate scores. Fit measures whether the contact matches what you sell, and intent measures what they are doing right now. A very active postdoc can show high intent and low buying fit, while a head of MSAT can be the ideal fit and have visited only once.
These are the signals we usually propose, drawn from forms, content, demos and trade shows. The actual weights should be agreed with your sales team, looking at which contacts from recent years ended up placing an order.

seccions.titol: Universities and public research centres follow procurement rules
seccions.text:
At a Spanish public university, the price of the equipment weighs heavily on how it is bought. Article 118 of Law 9/2017 on public sector contracts treats supply contracts with an estimated value below 15,000 euros as minor contracts. Additional provision 54 raises that limit to 50,000 euros for public agents of the Spanish Science, Technology and Innovation System, such as public universities and public research bodies, when the contract is not for general services and infrastructure.
Above those amounts, the purchase goes through one of the other procedures set by the law, often with a published tender. For scoring, this means a researcher with an awarded grant and a benchtop system can buy soon, while a larger system may come back as a tender months later. Note it in the CRM and keep an eye on the procurement platforms.

seccions.titol: Startups and pharma companies run on different calendars
seccions.text:
At a biotech startup, funding sets the calendar. A lead with strong intent can stall until a round closes, then come back suddenly when the company announces the investment or posts job openings in process development. These public signals are worth as much as a download, and sales should be able to add them to the CRM.
At a pharma company or CDMO, each opportunity tends to be worth more and more people are involved. Engineering, QA, procurement and the project lead visit the website at different times. That is why it makes sense to score the account too, adding up the activity of everyone from the same company, not just each contact on their own.

seccions.titol: How to set it up in the CRM and in Google Ads
seccions.text:
Start with a few rules and a clear threshold for handing the lead to sales. Add decay so that old activity loses points over the months, and review the leads that crossed the threshold with sales every quarter. If the highest scores had no real project behind them, change the weights.
Scoring also helps your campaigns. Google Ads lets you import conversions from the CRM if you store the click ID for each contact. If you only import leads above the threshold as conversions, campaign optimisation is based on those contacts rather than on every download, including the ones from students.

seccions.titol: What the GDPR says about scoring contacts
seccions.text:
Article 4(4) of the GDPR defines profiling as automated processing of personal data to evaluate aspects of a person, such as their interests or behaviour. Automated lead scoring can fall under it. Recital 47 says processing for direct marketing purposes may be regarded as carried out for a legitimate interest.
Article 21(2) gives people the right to object at any time to that processing, including profiling related to it. Article 21(4) requires this right to be brought explicitly to their attention, clearly and separately from any other information, at the latest at the first communication.
Marketing emails have their own rule. In Spain, article 21 of the LSSI requires the recipient to have requested or expressly authorised them beforehand, unless they are already a customer and you write about products similar to those they bought. A high score does not replace that consent, and the CRM should record when and how it was given.

faqs.q: How do we filter out students without losing researchers?
faqs.a: Use a job title field on the form and a low fit score for students, without deleting them. Some will go on to work in a lab or at a company in the sector. Principal investigators and lab managers should earn more fit points, even if their activity on the website is lower.

faqs.q: How often should we review the scoring model?
faqs.a: At first, every quarter, comparing lead scores with the opportunities won or lost. Later you can space it out, but review it when you launch a new product line, enter a new market or when sales says the top-scored leads have no real project.

faqs.q: Do we need an expensive tool for lead scoring?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many CRMs include scoring features, and if yours does not, simple fields and rules will do. The hard part is agreeing the signals and weights with sales and keeping the data clean. A simple score the sales team understands is more useful than a complex model nobody looks at.

bio-linkedin-decisors-farma.intro: On LinkedIn, you reach pharma decision makers by combining an account list with specific roles, such as process development, MSAT, quality and procurement. Posts from founders and engineers about real problems help, with the company page providing context. And LinkedIn lead forms should feed straight into your CRM, so sales knows who responded and what they need.

seccions.titol: Who decides on equipment purchases at a pharma company
seccions.text:
At a pharma company or CDMO, buying process equipment involves several people. Process development defines the need, MSAT takes the process to the plant, engineering looks at the installation, quality and validation review the documentation, and procurement negotiates. Each looks for different things and holds a different job title on LinkedIn.
That is why a single ad for the whole company falls short. The head of process development wants performance and scale-up data. Quality wants IQ, OQ and PQ support and 21 CFR Part 11 compliance. Procurement wants lead times, service and total cost. Each group needs its own message.

seccions.titol: How to target by job title, function and skills
seccions.text:
LinkedIn lets you target by company, job experience, education, interests and your own lists. Job experience covers job title, job function, seniority, member skills and years of experience. LinkedIn maps job titles to functions with its own taxonomy, so function is broader. Job title is more precise, but people write theirs in many different ways.
Europe has limits. LinkedIn warns that reach for some attributes and audiences may be limited in the European Economic Area and Switzerland, and that Member Groups are not available for targeting there. Each ad set needs an audience of at least 300 members to run, a floor worth watching in niches this narrow.

seccions.titol: An account list instead of the whole industry
seccions.text:
Targeting the pharmaceutical industry across Europe reaches plenty of people who will never buy a bioreactor. An account list is more useful. LinkedIn lets you upload a list of companies or contacts, use it as an audience and then combine it with job titles and seniority. In the European Economic Area and Switzerland, only members who have opted in through their ad settings are matched.
The list comes from your CRM, from exhibitor lists at trade shows such as CPHI, ACHEMA or BioSpain, and from the plants your sales team already knows. With a few dozen well-chosen companies, the budget goes to people who can buy. If the list is very short, you may fall below the 300 members LinkedIn requires and need to add countries or roles.

seccions.titol: Founder and engineer profiles or the company page
seccions.text:
The company page provides context and is where people check who you are. In a technical sector, though, a founder explaining why they designed a piece of equipment, or an engineer describing how they solved a scale-up, opens conversations a generic ad rarely will. These are posts about real work, with names and faces.
LinkedIn lets you sponsor these posts through Thought Leader Ads, which promote content from your employees or other members. You need the author's permission, the profile must show their full name and the post must be public. Polls, celebrations, multi-image posts and reposts of someone else's content cannot be promoted.

seccions.titol: LinkedIn lead forms connected to your CRM
seccions.text:
LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms fill themselves in with profile data when someone clicks the ad. They support up to three custom questions and hidden fields that tell you which campaign each lead came from. You must link to your privacy policy, and members can delete the data they submitted.
What matters most is that leads reach the CRM with no manual steps. LinkedIn can integrate with platforms such as Salesforce or HubSpot through partners, and if your CRM is not supported you can download leads as a CSV file. Use the three questions to qualify, for example project stage, scale and purchase timeline.

seccions.titol: How not to waste budget on LinkedIn
seccions.text:
Start with a short account list and two or three roles, and expand once you know which messages get a response. Measure by meetings and quote requests in the CRM. Clicks and impressions say little in sales cycles this long, and an ad that reaches the person who signs off the purchase can be worth more than many clicks from an audience that is too broad.
LinkedIn also lets you retarget people who visited your website, watched a video or opened a lead form, and build predictive audiences from that data. Use them carefully. If the source data mixes students and vendors, the audience built from it will mix them too.

faqs.q: LinkedIn Ads or Google Ads to sell bioprocess equipment?
faqs.a: They do different jobs. Google Ads reaches people already searching for equipment or a supplier. LinkedIn reaches people who are not searching yet but hold the right role at the right company. In long sales cycles it makes sense to combine them, with LinkedIn opening conversations with target accounts and Google Ads capturing demand when it appears.

faqs.q: What is the minimum audience size on LinkedIn?
faqs.a: LinkedIn requires at least 300 members in the audience to run an ad set, and it warns you when targeting is too narrow. In niches such as MSAT or validation at pharma companies in a single country, it is easy to get close to that floor. If it happens, add countries, include similar job titles or combine the account list with broader functions.

faqs.q: Can we target skills such as GMP or cell culture?
faqs.a: Yes. Skills targeting uses the skills members list on their profile, those mentioned in the profile text and those LinkedIn derives from job title, employer or education. It helps narrow down a role, but combine it with job title or function so you do not reach students or consultants who only talk about the subject.

bio-marca-startup-spin-off.intro: Building a brand for a biotech startup or spin-off means choosing a name you can register, explaining the science in one sentence and having an identity that looks credible to investors, pharma partners and recruits. It can be done on a modest budget, as long as the trademark checks happen before you fall for a name and everything is consistent before the first funding round.

seccions.titol: What changes when a lab project becomes a company
seccions.text:
In the lab, a project often carries the name of a grant or an acronym only the group understands. Once it becomes a company, it has to make sense to investors, pharma partners, future employees and, later on, regulators. The brand should say which problem you solve and for whom, beyond the technique you use.
And you are not alone. According to Biocat, the BioRegion of Catalonia has 1,650 companies and 94 research institutions, and AseBio counted 1,119 biotech companies across Spain in 2025. A name and message that look like everyone else's get lost in front of a fund or in a partnering meeting.

seccions.titol: How to choose a name you can register and defend
seccions.text:
WIPO defines a trademark as a sign capable of distinguishing the goods or services of one company from those of others. That is why names that only describe the technique, or lean on the usual prefixes such as bio-, gen- or cell-, tend to distinguish little and are harder to defend. A short name that is easy to say in English and carries no odd meanings in key markets works better.
Run these checks before you fall in love with the name. WIPO's Global Brand Database pulls together registers from many countries, but WIPO itself advises also searching national and regional registers and consulting a trademark attorney.

seccions.titol: An identity that looks credible to investors, partners and recruits
seccions.text:
Credibility comes from clarity and consistency. One sentence that explains the science, a small colour palette, a typeface that reads well in charts and tables, and real images from your lab or your data. Stock DNA helices and blue molecules are used by everyone and say nothing about you.
Each audience meets the brand in a different format. Investors see it in the deck and on the website, pharma partners in a non-confidential presentation or a partnering meeting, and candidates on LinkedIn. Design those formats first, because they are the ones you will use every week.

seccions.titol: What a spin-off needs to settle with its university
seccions.text:
Showing your link to the university or research centre builds trust, especially early on. Before you put its name or logo on your website, ask the technology transfer office on what terms you can do so. The company brand has to stand on its own, because the relationship with the centre will change over time.
You also need to time the brand launch around your patents. Article 54 of the European Patent Convention treats everything made available to the public before the filing date, whether in writing, orally or by use, as part of the state of the art. An overly detailed website, poster or press release can cost the invention its novelty.

seccions.titol: What to have ready before your first funding round
seccions.text: Before you talk to investors, the brand has to be the same everywhere. An investor will usually look at the deck, the website and the founders' LinkedIn profiles, and will notice straight away if each one describes a different company. According to Biocat, investment in health startups and scaleups in Catalonia reached a record 517 million euros in 2025, and the number of companies grew 8.3% year on year.

seccions.titol: How to find a name for a biotech startup, step by step
seccions.text:
A good name comes out of a long list that you keep cutting down. Start with words for the problem you solve and the benefit, not the technique, and play with roots, sounds and combinations. Then run each candidate through these filters, quickest first, until you are left with two or three.
Health adds one more filter. The WHO asks that trademarks are not derived from international nonproprietary names for medicines and, above all, that they do not contain their common stems, such as -feron or -leukin. A company name is not a drug brand, but if you ever have a product, it helps if the company name does not clash with it.

seccions.titol: Which domain works best for a biotech company
seccions.text:
For Google, the domain extension gives no advantage. In a 2015 post, Google Search Central explains that it treats new generic top-level domains, such as .bio, like .com and .org, and that keywords in the extension neither help nor hurt in search.
So choose with people in mind. If a short .com is available, it is the easiest for investors and partners in any country to remember, and if it is not, a .bio or a country domain can work just as well. Before you buy it, check the name is not someone else's registered trademark, because owning the domain does not make you the trademark owner.

seccions.titol: What a branding service for a pharma or biotech startup should include and cost
seccions.text:
A branding service for a biotech or pharma startup should cover the name, the positioning sentence, the identity and the templates you will use every week. A trademark attorney confirms the clearance search, and the studio should say so plainly in its quote.
At crida studio, a new brand starts at €3,500 excluding VAT, covering logo, colours, typography, a short brand guide and basic applications, with positioning and full guidelines available as add-ons. A simple template website starts at €1,200 and a custom business website at €3,000. Prices were updated in November 2026.
Think ahead to the day the company grows or gets acquired. If you own the name, it is registered and the brand has a guide, rebranding after an acquisition is far simpler, whether the buyer keeps the brand or folds it into its own.

faqs.q: When should a biotech startup register its trademark?
faqs.a: As early as possible, and always before the name goes public on a website, in a press release or in a funding round. Protection is territorial. You apply to the office of each country or region, such as EUIPO for the European Union, or to several countries at once through WIPO's Madrid System.

faqs.q: Should we change the name we used in the lab?
faqs.a: If it is a project acronym, only describes the technique or is already used by another company, yes. The best time is before the first round, while there are few materials and few contacts who would have to relearn it. Later on, a change touches contracts, publications and all the communication done so far.

faqs.q: Do the name and website need to be in English?
faqs.a: The name has to work in English, because investors, pharma partners and conferences operate in that language. The website should have an English version at the very least. Catalan and Spanish help with the local ecosystem, such as Biocat, universities and public bodies, and when hiring talent nearby.

faqs.q: Does a startup without a product need a brand guide?
faqs.a: Yes, but a short one. The logo and its variants, colours, typography, tone of voice and a few templates are enough. That way the deck, website and posters stay consistent even when different people make them, and the brand can grow once the first product arrives.

faqs.q: Is a .bio domain better for a biotech company?
faqs.a: Not for Google. Google Search Central explains that it treats new generic top-level domains like .com and .org, and that keywords in the extension give no advantage. Pick a domain that is short, easy to say and easy to remember, and check first that the name is not someone else's registered trademark.

bio-mesurar-peticions-oferta.intro: To measure marketing at an equipment manufacturer, count qualified RFQs, booked demos and opportunities instead of visits. Each form should be a key event in GA4 and reach the CRM with its source attached. From the CRM, the stages that matter go back into Google Ads, so an order that arrives a year later, or through a distributor, still counts.

seccions.titol: Why website visits do not show whether marketing sells equipment
seccions.text:
A bioprocess equipment website can get plenty of visits from students, researchers and the curious, especially if it has strong technical content. Those visits help the brand, but few of them lead to a purchase. A single RFQ from a CDMO can be worth more than months of traffic.
If the monthly report talks about visits, sessions and time on page, management cannot tell whether marketing helps sell. You need to measure what happens before a sale, meaning who asks for a quote, who books a demo and how many of those conversations become real opportunities.

seccions.titol: The B2B marketing KPIs that actually explain sales
seccions.text: These are the metrics we suggest to a manufacturer or distributor of lab and bioprocess equipment. All of them can be counted in the CRM and split by channel, such as organic search, Google Ads, LinkedIn, trade shows or distributors.

seccions.titol: How to connect GA4 and the CRM so every request has a source
seccions.text:
The first step is to mark the forms that matter as key events in Google Analytics 4, such as quote requests, demo requests and documentation downloads. GA4 then shows which channels lead people to take those actions. The second step is for every form to send the source, the campaign and the Google Ads click ID to the CRM.
GA4 will not see every form. With consent mode, Google tags adapt to what each visitor has accepted, and people who reject cookies are not measured the same way. The CRM, on the other hand, receives every request. That is why the CRM should be the system that counts RFQs, while GA4 explains where they come from.

seccions.titol: What to do with deals that close a year later
seccions.text:
In Google Ads, the click-through conversion window is 30 days by default and can go up to 90. An order for a production bioreactor can come much later than that. If you only import the order, Google Ads will not link it to the click, and your campaigns will never learn what works.
The fix is to import intermediate stages from the CRM that happen sooner, such as the qualified opportunity or the quote sent. Google recommends starting with enhanced conversions for leads, which add data such as a hashed email address to the click ID. If you upload them through the API, since 15 June 2026 that has to be done with the Data Manager API.

seccions.titol: A monthly report that management understands
seccions.text:
The report should fit on one page. Qualified RFQs and demos by channel, new opportunities and pipeline value, cost per qualified RFQ and one line on what changed and why. Visits can appear as context, for example to explain a drop in requests.
Keep the same format every month so trends become visible. With long sales cycles, one bad month does not mean much, but three months in a row with fewer qualified requests from one channel is a signal to review the campaigns, the content or the website.

faqs.q: What is a good cost per RFQ?
faqs.a: There is no single figure that works for everyone. It depends on the value of the equipment, how many requests turn into quotes and how many quotes turn into orders. What does work is comparing cost per qualified RFQ across channels and over time, and always reading it next to the pipeline value each channel generates.

faqs.q: How do we know whether an RFQ is qualified?
faqs.a: You need to define it with sales. Usually the contact must be from an organisation that can buy, state the scale and the process and have a timeline, even a rough one. If the sales engineer rejects a request, log the reason in the CRM so you can keep adjusting forms and campaigns.

faqs.q: Should we stop looking at website traffic?
faqs.a: No. Traffic helps you diagnose SEO, content and the website, for example to see whether a product page has lost visits. What it should not do is take the place of business metrics. In the report for management, visits should come after RFQs and opportunities.

bio-missatge-comite-compra.intro: To reach engineering, QA and procurement at a pharma company at the same time, you need one core promise and a different proof for each role. Engineers want to know whether the equipment fits their URS, QA wants to know how much validation work it will create and procurement wants the total cost. A message map keeps the website, the sales deck and the sales team saying the same thing.

seccions.titol: Why one message for everyone falls flat
seccions.text:
Buying a bioreactor or a TFF system goes through many hands. Process development, engineering, QA, production, procurement and the site head all look at the same equipment, and each one is checking for a different risk. If your message only covers technical performance, QA and procurement find nothing for them and the project stalls.
Research by the Ehrenberg-Bass Institute for LinkedIn's B2B Institute points out that most of your customers are not in the market at any given time. So marketing's job is to make the brand come to mind in the buying situations that matter. In pharma, that means every role on the committee should know you before the specification is written.

seccions.titol: A message map for every role on the committee
seccions.text: A message map is a simple table. At the top sits the core promise, the same for everyone. Below it, each role gets its main question and the proof that answers it. You already have the arguments, because they come from technical meetings, quotes and customer questions. The map simply puts them in order.

seccions.titol: Engineering wants proof the equipment fits their URS
seccions.text:
For engineering, the document that rules is the user requirements specification, the URS. Points 3.2 and 3.3 of Annex 15 of the EU GMP guidelines say the URS should be the point of reference throughout the validation life cycle and that design qualification should verify its requirements. So your message has to speak that language.
A good approach is to offer a matrix that answers the client's URS point by point, and to show on the website which sizes, sensors, connections and software options can be configured. ISPE's Baseline Guide on commissioning and qualification covers best practices for the URS and for design review.

seccions.titol: QA and validation want to know how much work lands on them
seccions.text:
QA is mainly trying to reduce risk ahead of an inspection. Point 3.6 of Annex 15 allows, where appropriate and justified, some documentation review and testing to be done at the FAT, at the supplier's site. It then does not need repeating at IQ and OQ, provided it can be shown that transport and installation do not affect functionality.
That argument carries weight if you can back it up. Explain what documentation package you deliver, what your FAT and SAT protocols look like and how you support IQ and OQ. If the equipment runs software with electronic records, describe how the audit trail and access controls work, because QA will be thinking about the FDA's 21 CFR Part 11.

seccions.titol: Procurement and site heads look at total cost and risk
seccions.text:
Procurement compares quotes, but with bioprocess equipment the purchase price is only part of the story. There are single-use consumables, spare parts, service contracts, validation hours and production downtime. If you do not explain those costs, the buyer estimates them alone or sticks to the quote price, which is usually the worst comparison for a mid-sized manufacturer.
The site head adds one more question, which is what risk comes with choosing a smaller supplier. Local technical service, a response time you can actually keep, references you are allowed to show and a clear company profile all help here. All of it should be on the website and in the sales deck.

faqs.q: Do we need a separate page for each role?
faqs.a: Not always. A well-structured product page with blocks that answer each role, plus a few downloadable documents for QA and procurement, is often enough. What matters is that each block is easy to find, because the engineer and the buyer will not read the page in the same order or with the same questions in mind.

faqs.q: Who should write the message, marketing or engineering?
faqs.a: Both. Marketing structures and writes, and engineering and QA check that every claim is true and defensible. If one of your engineers would not say a sentence in front of a client, it should not be published. This review also stops you promising things the project team cannot deliver later on.

faqs.q: How do we know whether the message map is working?
faqs.a: Watch the conversations. If QA and procurement questions arrive earlier and are better framed, or if quotes get stuck less often at the review stage, the message is helping. You can also ask new customers what made them decide and compare their answers with what the map says.

faqs.q: What if we sell through distributors?
faqs.a: Then the map is even more useful. Distributors should receive the same arguments and proofs for each role, translated and adapted to their market. If every distributor explains the product their own way, the buying committee hears different messages depending on the country and the brand loses strength.

bio-newsletter-clients-laboratori.intro: A newsletter for lab and pharma customers works when every issue helps readers do their job. An application note, a scale-up data point, a product change that affects them or a question your team hears all the time. Split it by audience, send it only to people who opted in, tag every link and check in your CRM whether it leads to quote requests.

seccions.titol: What makes a lab customer open a newsletter
seccions.text:
Your readers are scientists, process engineers, quality people and buyers. They are short on time and get plenty of supplier email. They open what might save them work, such as a protocol, results from an application close to theirs, or a note that a datasheet has changed. They delete the weekly discount catalogue unread.
The test is simple. Before sending an issue, ask whether a lab manager would forward it to a colleague. If not, it is probably advertising dressed up as a newsletter. Sending the occasional one is fine, but if every issue is like that, the list goes quiet.

seccions.titol: One newsletter per type of reader
seccions.text: A scientist and a buyer do not want the same thing. If your sign-up form asks for role and application, and the CRM stores it, you can send each reader the version that fits from the same underlying work. Starting with two or three segments already makes a real difference compared with one email for everyone.

seccions.titol: What to cover each month without running out of topics
seccions.text:
Topics come from inside the company. Questions that sales and field service hear, application notes from the lab, a trade show you will attend, a product update or a real case a customer has agreed to share. With a running list of those sources, one issue a month is not hard to fill.
A structure that works is one main story, two or three short items and a single clear call to action at the end, such as booking a demo or registering for a webinar. One issue a month that keeps going for years beats a weekly one that stops after three months.

seccions.titol: Permission to send it, GDPR and Spain's LSSI
seccions.text:
If you send from Spain, Article 21 of the LSSI prohibits promotional emails the recipient has not previously requested or expressly authorised. The exception is existing customers, provided the contact details were obtained lawfully and the email covers your own products or services similar to those they bought.
In that case you must offer a simple, free way to object, both when you collect the data and in every message. Article 22 requires every email to include a valid electronic address for unsubscribing, and Article 20 says the message must be identifiable as commercial and show who is sending it. Article 21 of the GDPR also gives people the right to object to direct marketing at any time.
In practice, a business card collected at a trade show does not, on its own, show that the person wants your newsletter. The cleanest route is to ask at the booth, with a form or QR code that includes a consent checkbox, and to record in the CRM when and how permission was given.

seccions.titol: Getting into the inbox
seccions.text:
A great newsletter that lands in the spam folder is useless. Google requires everyone sending to personal Gmail accounts to authenticate their domain with SPF or DKIM and to keep the spam rate reported in Postmaster Tools below 0.3%. Senders of more than 5,000 messages a day to Gmail accounts must also support one-click unsubscribe in marketing email.
Many pharma customers use corporate email rather than Gmail, but the same habits help. Send from an authenticated domain with a sender name people recognise, remove addresses that bounce and unsubscribe anyone who asks straight away.

seccions.titol: How to tell whether the newsletter drives quote requests
seccions.text:
Open rates say little about what matters. Tag every link with UTM parameters, such as utm_source, utm_medium set to email and utm_campaign with the month's issue. Google Analytics suggests utm_content to tell apart two links in the same email. That shows which items send traffic to product pages and which end in a quote request.
The final answer sits in the CRM. Check how many newsletter recipients have asked for a quote or a demo, and whether open deals move forward when they read. We connect the email tool to the CRM so that, for example, a sales rep gets an alert when someone from a company with an open quote clicks a scale-up article.

faqs.q: How often should we send the newsletter?
faqs.a: As often as you can sustain with useful content. One issue a month is a good starting point, because you stay visible in the inbox and still have time to do it properly. If there are not enough topics for that, every two months or every quarter is better than sending empty issues.

faqs.q: Which language should we send it in?
faqs.a: The reader's own, if you have it. Store the language in the CRM from the sign-up form and prepare one version per language for the markets where you sell. If you cannot translate it into all of them yet, English works for international customers, but a German issue for a reader in Munich or a Spanish one for Madrid gets read with more interest.

faqs.q: Which email tool should we use?
faqs.a: One that connects cleanly to your CRM, supports segments by role and language, handles unsubscribes automatically and lets you add UTM parameters to links. Also check where it stores data and sign a data processing agreement. The brand of the tool matters less than keeping the list clean and the permissions on record.

bio-portal-distribuidors.intro: If you work with a handful of distributors and what you share is datasheets, brochures and price lists, a well-organised shared drive will do the job. Once the channel grows, distributors start bringing you deals and you need to know who owns each account. At that point you need a partner portal with deal registration connected to your CRM. The deciding factor is how much information has to flow both ways.

seccions.titol: What a bioprocess equipment distributor needs from you
seccions.text:
A distributor selling bioreactors or TFF systems needs three things from the manufacturer. Current sales material, clarity on which accounts and territories are theirs, and fast answers when a customer asks for a quote. In return, you want to know what is happening in their market. Which companies are evaluating equipment, which quotes are open and why deals are lost.
The most common problem is outdated material. An old datasheet with a working volume or temperature range that is no longer correct reaches a pharma customer and ends up inside a URS. So the first question is how you make sure everyone uses the latest version. Which tool makes that easier comes second.

seccions.titol: When a shared drive is enough
seccions.text:
A shared folder in Google Drive, OneDrive or SharePoint works when you have a few distributors, each with a clear territory, and material mostly flows one way. Deals are passed on by email or phone and the area sales manager tracks them in the CRM. It is cheap, everyone knows how to use it and nobody needs training.
What goes wrong is structure and permissions. Microsoft notes that external sharing is turned on by default in SharePoint and OneDrive, and suggests turning it off until you know exactly how you want to use it. And when a distributor stops working with you, you need to remove their permissions or delete the links they had.

seccions.titol: When you need a portal with deal registration
seccions.text:
A portal makes sense when distributors bring you deals and more than one of them can reach the same customer. It can happen, for example, with pharma groups or CDMOs running plants in several countries. Deal registration sorts it out. The distributor registers the opportunity with real details, you approve it and it stays protected for an agreed period.
A partner portal, or PRM software, also lets you route website enquiries by country and product, see which material each distributor actually uses and train partners before they sell a new piece of equipment. If you only need part of that, check first whether the CRM you already use includes a portal module.

seccions.titol: Shared drive or portal, point by point
seccions.text: The table sums up the differences that matter most in a distribution channel for lab and bioprocess equipment. You do not have to do everything on day one. You can start with a well-organised drive and add deal registration and the CRM connection when the channel calls for it.

seccions.titol: How to keep the portal and the CRM in sync
seccions.text:
A portal that does not talk to the CRM is just one more list that never matches. The rule is that every deal lives in one place. If the distributor registers it in the portal, it is created in the CRM with the distributor as owner. If your team changes its status, the distributor sees it in the portal without anyone sending an email.
This is where we use automation. We connect the website form, the CRM and the portal with simple rules your sales team understands and can change. For example, a quote request from Germany for a 50-litre bioreactor goes to the distributor for that region, and if nobody responds within a few days, the channel manager gets an alert.

seccions.titol: What the GDPR says when you pass contacts to distributors
seccions.text:
When you pass a contact's details to a distributor, that person needs to know. Article 13 of the GDPR requires you to tell people, when you collect their data, about the recipients or categories of recipients. In practice, your website form should say that the request may be handled by the local distributor, and your privacy policy should explain it.
The company hosting your portal or drive processes data on your behalf. Article 28 says you may only use a processor that provides sufficient guarantees, and that the relationship must be set out in a contract or other legal act. Check this with whoever handles data protection in your company before opening access to the channel.

faqs.q: Can the distributor portal live inside our website?
faqs.a: Yes. A private area on your website with a login works well for sales material, training and current datasheets. For deal registration and lead routing, though, it has to be connected to the CRM, or you use the CRM's own portal module. Otherwise you end up with two lists that never match. Keep the login area for material and training, and let the CRM own the deals.

faqs.q: How do we stop two distributors fighting over the same customer?
faqs.a: With written rules before the portal goes live. Who registers first with real details, how long a deal stays protected, what happens when it expires and what your own sales team does when it sells direct. These rules belong in the distribution agreement. The portal enforces them and keeps a record of who registered what and when.

faqs.q: What happens to our material when a distributor leaves?
faqs.a: Remove their access the same day. In a shared drive that means removing permissions and deleting the links they had, and in a portal, deactivating the user. Anything already downloaded cannot be recovered. That is why each datasheet should carry its revision date and customers should know where to find the current version.

bio-posicionament-fabricant-equips.intro: A mid-sized bioprocess equipment maker can compete with the global suppliers by picking two or three buying situations where it is the best choice and backing them with proof. Think of scaling a process from lab to production with the same control logic, or adapting ports, sensors and software to a specific process. Echoing the catalogue messaging of the big brands on a smaller budget only makes you easier to overlook.

seccions.titol: Why echoing the big brands makes you invisible
seccions.text:
The global life science suppliers sell breadth. They have a catalogue for the whole process, offices in many countries and a name the buyer already knows. When a mid-sized maker uses the same lines, such as end-to-end bioprocess solutions, the customer has no reason to remember it or to ask it for a quote.
Research by the Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, published by LinkedIn's B2B Institute, points the same way. It finds that the bigger problem for a B2B brand is that buyers do not know it, far more than buyers rejecting it. It also notes that most potential customers are not in the market at any given time. So you need to be remembered when the need comes up.

seccions.titol: Where a mid-sized bioprocess equipment maker can win
seccions.text:
A niche comes from specific buying situations. Ask your sales team which deals you tend to win and which ones you lose, and look for what they have in common. More often than not, the pattern is linked to one of these situations.
Pick two or three. A long list starts to look like a catalogue again, and then the buyer compares everything on price. The ones you choose have to be true today, because the customer will test them at the first technical meeting and on the factory visit.

seccions.titol: How to prove you are the best option in that niche
seccions.text:
Bioprocess buyers do not believe adjectives. They want data, documents and people who know what they are talking about. Every situation you choose needs at least one piece of proof you can show on the website, in a sales deck or on a trade show stand.
Good proof includes performance curves across scales, explained by an engineer. A sample of the qualification documents you deliver also helps, such as the FAT protocol or the IQ and OQ package, as does a 3D animation showing what changes as the equipment scales up. If confidentiality stops you naming a customer, describe the problem and the solution without saying who it was.

seccions.titol: One niche, explained to everyone involved in the decision
seccions.text: Several people take part in buying bioprocess equipment, and each of them looks for different proof. The niche stays the same while the argument changes. If the website and the sales team only speak to one profile, the deal stalls when the project moves on to the next person.

seccions.titol: Where to start with your brand positioning
seccions.text: Start by writing one sentence that says where you win and for whom. Then check whether your homepage, your LinkedIn page and your sales deck say exactly that. Quite often each channel describes a different company, and that is the first thing to fix.

faqs.q: Should a small company invest in brand or just in lead generation?
faqs.a: Both, with different weight depending on the moment. Lead generation answers people who are looking for equipment today. Brand makes sure you are considered when the need arrives, which in bioprocessing can be months or years later. If buyers already know you in a specific niche, your campaigns reach people who know who you are.

faqs.q: Do we need to compete on price with the global suppliers?
faqs.a: Competing on price alone pushes the buyer to compare everything on the final figure, and that is where a mid-sized maker has less room. It works better to defend what the customer gains with you, such as flexibility, speed or technical closeness, and to explain the total project cost, including service, spare parts and validation.

faqs.q: If we make both stainless steel and single-use equipment, should we pick one?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Offering both technologies can be your niche, as long as you help the customer decide. What matters is explaining when each one fits depending on batch size, product changeovers and cleaning, instead of presenting them as two separate catalogues with no guidance.

faqs.q: Does our website need to be in English?
faqs.a: If you sell outside Spain, yes. International buyers, technical publications and the sector's trade shows use English as their common language. Spanish and Catalan help with nearby customers and the local ecosystem, and German can make sense if Germany is one of your priority markets.

bio-preparar-fira-achema-cphi.intro: ACHEMA 2027 runs from 14 to 18 June in Frankfurt and CPHI Frankfurt from 9 to 11 November 2027. If you are a mid-sized equipment maker, start twelve months out with a goal you can count, a list of accounts you want to meet and a booth that says in one line what you do. What makes the difference is meetings booked before you arrive, the right demo and the follow-up.

seccions.titol: ACHEMA or CPHI, depending on who buys from you
seccions.text:
Pick the show by thinking about your buyer. ACHEMA presents itself as the leading show for the process and life science industries, with exhibition groups such as laboratory and analytical techniques or pharmaceutical, packaging and storage techniques. According to the official 2024 summary, more than two thirds of participants had a technical or scientific background.
CPHI Frankfurt covers the whole pharma supply chain, from APIs to CDMOs, CROs and machinery. It has bioproduction and machinery and equipment zones, and for 2027 it announces a new lab and analytical equipment zone. If your customer is a CDMO or a pharma company buying for production, CPHI may be the better fit.
Before choosing, check where each show falls in the year. BIO takes place in Philadelphia from 7 to 10 June 2027, the week before ACHEMA, and a small team will struggle to cover both. The calendar with the official 2027 trade show dates lists every event and who each one is for.
If your customers are in Spain, you may not need to travel to Germany at all. Farmaforum runs at IFEMA Madrid on 22 and 23 September 2027 and BioSpain in Barcelona from 28 to 30 September. The first reaches pharma plants and labs, the second biotechs and investors, so it is worth taking the time to compare BioSpain and Farmaforum before you decide.

seccions.titol: The twelve-month timeline before the show
seccions.text:
ACHEMA has no application deadline, but space is let on availability. The organiser sends stand offers based on when your application arrives, whether you have exhibited before and technical requirements. Location requests go in with the application itself, so it pays to know what you want from the start.
Watch the cancellation terms. Cancel between 1 September 2026 and 14 March 2027 and you pay 50% of the agreed fees. From 15 March, you pay 100% of the space. The online application is binding, so get the budget signed off by management before you send it.
Exhibitor passes are issued through the ACHEMA exhibitor portal from the end of November 2026, and each pass is personal. If someone on your team needs a visa for Germany, ACHEMA provides a personalised invitation letter for the business visa, so ask for it early.

seccions.titol: Who goes to ACHEMA and which days are busiest
seccions.text:
The official 2024 figures help with planning. ACHEMA drew 106,001 participants from 141 countries, 48.9% of them from outside Germany, who stayed 1.9 days on average. A third came from management, and half of that group were C-level. On top of that, the organiser reports that 52% of participants attend no other trade show.
Wednesday was the busiest day with 43,137 visitors, followed by Tuesday with 40,113. Friday had 18,470. Put your key meetings on Tuesday and Wednesday with the full team on the booth, and keep Friday for distributors, suppliers and a look at what competitors are showing.

seccions.titol: How to book meetings before you reach Frankfurt
seccions.text:
The meetings that matter are requested weeks ahead and with a concrete reason, such as seeing the scale the customer is evaluating in operation. The ACHEMA exhibition fee includes a digital logo with your hall and stand number and a social media kit. Use them in email signatures, on LinkedIn and on a web page with a link to book a slot.
A practical warning. ACHEMA states that only DECHEMA publishes the official exhibitor directory and app, and that other directories and fair guides are not authorised. When listing offers or invoices of that kind arrive, check them before anyone pays.

seccions.titol: What your booth should say and which demo to bring
seccions.text:
