Whether you hold the brand for the whole country or one region, whether demo units are available, how long a spare part takes, whether you handle installation and IQ and OQ documentation, and whether you can bid in a public tender for a university or a hospital.

seccions.titol: Brand pages that do not copy the manufacturer's text
seccions.text:
The easy route is to copy each product description from the manufacturer's website. It is often what other distributors of the same brand do too. Among its helpful content criteria, Google asks whether content that draws on other sources avoids simply copying or rewriting them and adds substantial value and originality. A copied datasheet adds none.
Each brand page should explain what you add. Which models you hold in stock or as demo units, which compatible consumables and accessories you supply, which engineer knows the instrument and what kinds of labs you have installed it in. Technical data can link to the manufacturer's official datasheet, which is the reference whenever something changes.

seccions.titol: Navigation by application alongside navigation by brand
seccions.text: Researchers tend to search for a way to get a task done, while purchasing and engineering search by brand and model. Your site has to serve both paths. An application menu leads to the instruments from each brand that fit, and a brand menu leads to the full catalogue. Both routes end on the same product page, with no duplicate pages.

seccions.titol: Stock, field service and qualification, what the manufacturer cannot say for you
seccions.text:
Service is often what sets one distributor apart from another selling the same brand. Show it with specific pages. Who your service engineers are and where they are based, which brands they can repair, whether you offer preventive maintenance and calibration contracts, and how to request a visit. If you keep spare parts or consumables in stock, say which ones and where.
For pharma customers and GMP production sites, qualification matters a great deal. If you handle installation and support IQ and OQ, or work with the manufacturer on FAT and SAT, explain what you do and what the manufacturer does. A buyer writing a URS wants to know who they will be dealing with at each step.

seccions.titol: How to rank next to the manufacturer's own website
seccions.text:
When someone searches for a model name, the manufacturer's site usually comes first, and that is fine. Distributors win the searches where location matters. A brand distributor in Spain, field service for a type of instrument in Barcelona or Madrid, spare parts or calibration nearby. Those pages need to state the territory, the brand and the service in the words your customers use.
A Google Business Profile helps here. Google says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity, and that links to your business and reviews count. For products, Google offers two types of structured data. Product snippets for pages where people cannot buy directly, and merchant listings for pages where they can.

seccions.titol: What the manufacturer can restrict on your website
seccions.text:
Distribution agreements usually set rules on the use of the brand, logos and photos, and sometimes on online advertising. Read yours before building the site. If the manufacturer has an image and copy library for distributors, ask for it and use it as a starting point, without letting it become the only content on the page.
EU law sets a limit here. Article 4(e) of Regulation (EU) 2022/720 on vertical agreements lists preventing the distributor or its customers from effectively using the internet to sell among the hardcore restrictions. The manufacturer can still impose other restrictions on online sales, and on online advertising as long as they do not aim to block an entire advertising channel. If in doubt, ask a competition lawyer.

faqs.q: Can we use the manufacturer's photos and datasheets on our website?
faqs.a: It depends on your distribution agreement and what the manufacturer allows. You can often use the official material they provide, but the whole page should not be made of it. Add your own photos of demo units or your service team, and copy that explains what you bring that the manufacturer does not.

faqs.q: Is an online shop worth it for a lab equipment distributor?
faqs.a: For consumables, spare parts and small instruments with fixed prices, yes, because lab customers reorder often and want it to be quick. For bioreactors, TFF systems or equipment configured from a URS, a page with a quote request makes more sense. Both can carry product structured data, each using the type that fits.

faqs.q: How do we stand out from other distributors of the same brand?
faqs.a: Through what happens after the sale and how well you know your customers' applications. Local field service, local stock, engineers trained by the brand and support with qualification. Show it on specific pages and, where a customer agrees, with a real case. The datasheet, on the other hand, is the same for everyone.

bio-web-fabricant-equips.intro: A bioprocess equipment manufacturer website has to answer the buyer's questions fast. Buyers want to know whether the system fits their scale, whether it suits their process and what documentation they will get to validate it. That is why it works best organised by scale and by application, with validation explained clearly and a straightforward path to a quote for every role involved in the purchase.

seccions.titol: What visitors look for on an equipment manufacturer website
seccions.text:
People who land on a bioreactor or TFF system manufacturer's website usually have a live project. It might be a process development scientist who needs to scale up, an engineer planning a pilot plant or a buyer comparing suppliers. None of them wants to start with the company history.
The home page should say in one sentence what you make, for which scales and for which processes. Then it should send each role to the right page. If finding a volume range takes three menus, the buyer goes back to Google and clicks on the next manufacturer.

seccions.titol: Application pages, from mAbs to cell and gene therapy
seccions.text:
Many buyers search by process rather than by product. They type cell culture for monoclonal antibodies, microbial fermentation or vaccine production. An application page explains the challenge of that process, which configuration fits and what proves it, such as an application note or a case study told without the customer's name.
Be careful with claims here. GMP applies to whoever manufactures the medicinal product, and they are responsible for qualifying the equipment at their site. A line like GMP validated equipment can make quality teams suspicious. It works better to explain how the system helps them comply and which documents come with it.

seccions.titol: Validation documents help you sell too
seccions.text:
Section 3 of Annex 15 of the EU GMP guidelines sets out the qualification stages for equipment. It starts with the user requirements specification (URS), moves through design qualification and factory and site acceptance testing (FAT and SAT), and goes on to IQ, OQ and PQ. Quality and validation teams will read all of it before they sign off.
Your website can get that work started with a page of its own. A sample table of contents for an IQ and OQ protocol says more than a paragraph of adjectives. These are the points validation teams ask about most.

seccions.titol: How Google and AI answers find you
seccions.text:
Google says its systems reward helpful, reliable content made for people. The questions it suggests for reviewing content include whether it shows first-hand expertise, whether it is clear who wrote it and whether it has easily verified factual errors. In bioprocessing, that means pages signed by engineers and specialists with a real name and role.
Product pages can also carry structured data. Google offers product markup for pages where people cannot buy directly, which covers most equipment sold on quotation. It helps the search engine understand what each system is, although Google does not guarantee it will show rich results.

faqs.q: Should a bioprocess equipment website show prices?
faqs.a: Usually not, because each system is configured around the customer's scale, sensors, software and documentation needs. What does help is explaining what drives the price and offering a short quote request form. That way the buyer knows what to prepare and your sales engineer gets the information needed to reply properly.

faqs.q: Which languages should an equipment manufacturer website be in?
faqs.a: If you sell outside your home market, English is essential, as it is the common language of buyers, technical publications and industry trade shows. Next come the languages of the markets where you have sales staff or distributors, such as German if Germany is a priority. A few well maintained languages beat many that were translated once and then forgotten.

faqs.q: Can we publish case studies if we work under NDAs?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as you explain the problem and the solution without naming the customer or sharing details of their process. Give the type of company, the scale, the application and what changed with the equipment. Before publishing, it is wise to get the customer's written approval, even if their name appears nowhere.

bio-web-multiidioma-europa.intro: Start with the languages of the markets where you already sell or can actually serve customers, give each language its own folder and connect the versions with hreflang. Fully localise the pages that sell, such as applications, products and contact, and keep in English only what your customers already read in English. Then make sure every enquiry reaches someone who can answer in that language.

seccions.titol: Which languages to add first
seccions.text:
A new language on your website is a promise. If an engineer in Germany writes to you in German, they expect someone to reply in German, whether that is your own team or a distributor. So your first languages should be those of markets where you already sell or have someone who can serve customers. English acts as the base for everything else.
Data helps too. Search Console shows which countries your impressions and clicks come from, Analytics shows visits by country and your CRM shows where quote requests originate. If a country keeps appearing and you already have someone to cover it, it is a strong candidate. If no data points to it, it may be too early.

seccions.titol: Folders, subdomains or one domain per country
seccions.text:
Google recommends a separate URL for each language version rather than switching the text with cookies or browser settings. There are three main structures. A country domain such as example.de, a subdomain such as de.example.com, or a folder such as example.com/de/. Google sets out the pros and cons of each in its guide to multi-regional sites.
For an equipment manufacturer selling from a single company, folders are usually the most practical choice. Google lists them as easy to set up and low maintenance, since everything sits on the same host. A country domain sends a clear geographic signal, but it is more expensive, needs more infrastructure and targets only one country. If you sell in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, a single /de/ folder can serve German speakers in all three.

seccions.titol: Hreflang rules you cannot skip
seccions.text: Hreflang tells Google which pages are the same content in another language, so each searcher gets the right one. You can declare it in the HTML, in HTTP headers or in your sitemap. To work out a page's language, Google looks at the visible content and does not use the lang attribute or the URL. So every page should be in a single language, navigation included.

seccions.titol: Make every enquiry reach someone who can answer it
seccions.text:
A site in five languages with a single form that goes to head office wastes the customer's time. The form should ask for the country and send the request to the right distributor or sales manager, in the customer's language. Each version can have a local contact page with real names, and the CRM should record the language and country of every contact.
Google advises against automatically redirecting users based on the language you think they speak, because it can stop people and search engines from seeing all versions. A visible language switcher on every page, linking to the same page in the other language, works better. And if you pass contacts to distributors, your privacy policy needs to say so.

seccions.titol: How to keep language versions from drifting apart
seccions.text:
The risk with a multilingual site is that a datasheet changes in English while the German version keeps the old figures. You need a reference language, a glossary of approved technical terms and an owner for each language, which can be the local distributor. When a specification changes, it changes in every version at the same time.
We set up the folder structure and hreflang from the start, because changing them later means moving URLs and putting existing rankings at risk. Then we use a crawler to check that every version points to the others and that no page mixes languages.

faqs.q: Do we need to translate the whole website into every language?
faqs.a: Not all at once. Start with the pages that sell and leave the news archive or older articles for later. What you do need is for every published page to be complete in one language. A page with German navigation and English body text confuses both the customer and the search engine.

faqs.q: Country domain or a /de/ folder?
faqs.a: If you are one company selling in several countries, a folder is usually more practical. Google describes it as easy to set up and low maintenance. A country domain sends a clear signal, but it costs more, needs more infrastructure and targets a single country. It makes sense when you have a local subsidiary with its own offer.

faqs.q: Can we use machine translation for the other versions?
faqs.a: As a first draft, yes, and it saves time. Before publishing, though, a native speaker who knows the field should review it, with your company glossary at hand. In bioprocessing, one badly translated term can change the meaning of a specification, and a local engineer will spot it straight away.

bio-web-startup-inversors.intro: Before the first call, an investor opens a biotech startup's website to check what you do, what stage you are at, who is on the team and whether the science and intellectual property hold up. Your website should explain the pipeline or platform, the team, patent status and milestones in plain words, and leave out unpublished data and promises you cannot keep.

seccions.titol: What an investor does with your website before the call
seccions.text:
Your website is the first filter. A fund analyst will often get your deck by email or meet you at a partnering session, then open the website to check what you do, your stage and your team. If the website says something different from the deck, or has not been updated in a year, the first impression is already one of doubt.
The capital reaching the sector is growing, and much of it comes from abroad. According to AseBio, Spanish biotech companies raised 408 million euros in 2025, more than double the 2024 figure, and 302 million came through deals with international investors. Biocat reports that 82% of 2025 deals in Catalan health startups and scaleups involved investors from abroad. An English version is essential.

seccions.titol: How to explain your pipeline or platform without jargon
seccions.text:
Investors want to see at a glance which candidates you have, for which indication, what modality they are and what stage they have reached, from discovery to preclinical or clinical development. A simple pipeline table or chart says this better than three paragraphs. If you are a platform company, explain what makes the technology different and which applications or partnerships it opens up.
Write each explanation on two levels. First, one sentence a non-specialist can follow. Then a more technical layer for the fund's scientific adviser. Diagrams of the mechanism and real photos from the lab help far more than generic illustrations.

seccions.titol: Team and advisers, with names and track records
seccions.text:
In a biotech startup, the team carries as much weight as the science. Every founder and key person should have a photo, a role, the experience that matters for the project and a link to their LinkedIn profile. The scientific advisory board belongs there too, with each member's institution.
If a key profile is still missing, such as a chief medical or business officer, the website should not paper over it. The investor will spot it in the meeting anyway. Logos of the university, accelerators or programmes that have funded you help, as long as you have permission to use them.

seccions.titol: Patents and milestones, explained clearly
seccions.text:
Describe your intellectual property as far as you can in public. For example, whether you have patent applications on file, whether they are your own or licensed from a university and which territories they cover. Technical details that have not been published yet belong in the meeting and the data room.
Milestones work the same way. Past ones come with dates, such as incorporation, the first round, preclinical proof of concept or a grant awarded. Future ones are goals, without promising dates you do not control, such as the start of a clinical trial, which needs approval from the regulator.

seccions.titol: What is better kept off your website
seccions.text: Article 54 of the European Patent Convention treats everything made public before the filing date as part of the state of the art. An overly detailed website can cost an invention its novelty. Article 87 of Directive 2001/83/EC also requires member states to ban advertising of medicines without a marketing authorisation. So your pipeline page should speak to investors and partners and never present a candidate as an available treatment.

seccions.titol: Your website and deck must describe the same company
seccions.text: The deck is shared privately and goes into more detail, while the website is the public summary. Both should use the same names, the same stage and the same figures. When something important changes, such as a new round, a key hire or newly published data, update the website first, because that is what investors check before they reply to your email.

faqs.q: Should we put our pitch deck on the website?
faqs.a: Better not to make it public. The deck changes often, contains information you do not want freely available and it pays to know who reads it. On the website, a clear summary plus a form or an address to request the deck is enough. That also tells you which funds are interested in you.

faqs.q: Does a biotech startup website need an investor section?
faqs.a: At an early stage, a short page is enough. It should say what kind of investors or partners you are looking for, what stage the company is at and how to reach the person who handles those conversations. Round figures and financial details are shared privately, in the meeting or the data room.

faqs.q: How often should a startup update its website?
faqs.a: Every time you hit a milestone. A funding round, a new team member, a scientific publication, a patent filing or a new partnership are all reasons to update the site. A news page that has not moved for months makes investors wonder whether the company has stalled too.

bio-webinar-tecnic-compradors.intro: A technical webinar attracts buyers when it answers a problem they have right now, such as scaling a process, running a tech transfer or meeting Annex 1, rather than walking through your catalogue. Pick the topic from real sales questions, bring in a customer or an outside expert, build a registration form that tells you who is who and reuse the recording for months.

seccions.titol: The topic comes from questions buyers already ask you
seccions.text:
A broad topic, such as an introduction to bioprocessing, fills the room with students and the merely curious. A specific problem draws people who need to solve it soon, for example how to move from a 2 litre bioreactor to a 200 litre one without losing performance, or what to prepare for a tech transfer to a CDMO.
You already have the best questions. They come from sales calls, the URS documents you receive, the applications lab and technical service. Annex 1 of the EU GMP guide, for instance, calls in point 2.3 for a contamination control strategy across the whole facility, and the European Commission lists it as fully applicable since 25 August 2024. That topic sits close to home for QA and production teams.

seccions.titol: A customer or expert alongside your specialist
seccions.text:
If only your product manager speaks, the webinar feels like a sales pitch. A customer explaining how they scaled their process, a GMP consultant or a process engineer from a CDMO adds credibility and shares the session with their own network. Your specialist handles the technical questions and someone from marketing moderates.
Agree in advance what can be shown. Customer data is often under a confidentiality agreement, and it is better to find out while building the slides than live on air. Rehearse with the platform, the audio and the questions you expect, and decide who answers which kind of question.

seccions.titol: A registration form that qualifies without scaring people off
seccions.text:
The registration form is your first filter. Ask for company, job title, the scale they work at, such as lab, pilot or production, and the project stage. Add one open question about what they want answered. That tells sales who to call afterwards and tells you which questions to prepare.
Do not ask for more than you will use. Article 5(1)(c) of the GDPR says data must be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the purpose, and Article 13 requires you to say who handles it and why. If you later want to email offers to registrants in Spain, Article 21 of Law 34/2002 requires their prior request or express permission, so make that a separate tick box.

seccions.titol: A format that respects an engineer's diary
seccions.text: Technical people join for an answer and tend to leave when the sales pitch starts. A running order that works for bioprocess webinars keeps company slides to a minimum and leaves plenty of time for data and questions.

seccions.titol: What to do during the webinar and right after
seccions.text:
During the session, note who asks what. A question about lead times, validation or a specific scale says far more than attendance alone. A short poll on scale and project timeline also helps prioritise follow-up.
Afterwards, send the recording to everyone who registered, including no-shows. Sales calls first the people who asked specific questions or work at pilot or production scale, and the rest receive related content automatically. Students are not a problem, but do not count them as opportunities.

seccions.titol: The recording as months of content
seccions.text:
An hour of webinar goes a long way. Cut the recording into clips that each answer one question, post them on LinkedIn and write an article with the questions and answers for your website. If you want Google to show the video, its guidance asks for it to be embedded on a page with a stable thumbnail and recommends a dedicated watch page for each video.
Decide what stays open and what sits behind a form. Clips and the summary stay open so they can be found on Google and in AI answers. The full recording gets a short form, because people who watch it to the end usually have real interest. After a few months, check which clips bring the most registrations to the next webinar.

faqs.q: How many attendees make a webinar worthwhile?
faqs.a: Ignore the total. Look at how many people with a buyer profile register, how many ask questions and how many sales conversations follow in the weeks after. A small webinar with three plants that are choosing a supplier can be worth more than a packed one full of students.

faqs.q: Live or pre-recorded?
faqs.a: Live gives you the Q&A, which is the most useful part for spotting buyers. You can pre-record the riskier parts, such as an equipment demo, and run the presentation and questions live. What does not work is a canned video with nobody there to answer, because technical audiences notice straight away.

faqs.q: Which language should we run it in?
faqs.a: English if you want to reach buyers abroad, which is the norm in this sector. Spanish or Catalan if the audience is local, for example plants and labs in Spain. Avoid mixing languages in a single session. If needed, run two sessions with the same content and different speakers.

faqs.q: How do we stop it filling up with students?
faqs.a: Use a title about a plant or project problem, a description that says who it is for, a time slot during working hours and a job title field on the form. Students will still sign up, and that is fine because they are future customers, but the form lets you keep them out of sales follow-up.

bio-white-paper-nota-aplicacio.intro: It depends on where the buyer is. An application note, with method and data, is what people evaluating equipment ask for, and it is best left open or nearly open. A white paper helps while the customer is still defining the problem, such as single-use versus stainless steel. A webinar starts a conversation with an expert and is where asking for contact details makes most sense.

seccions.titol: What each format is and what readers expect from it
seccions.text:
An application note shows how a specific application was solved with a piece of equipment. For example, a CHO cell culture in a 50 litre bioreactor or concentrating a protein with a TFF system. It covers method, conditions and results, and readers use it to check whether their own process fits.
A white paper argues a point about a broader problem, such as when switching to single-use pays off or what to prepare before scaling up to a pilot plant. A webinar is a live session with an expert and audience questions, recorded for later. Each format takes different work and attracts a different reader.

seccions.titol: Which format fits each stage of the purchase
seccions.text: Buying bioprocess equipment has three clear stages. First the customer defines the problem, then evaluates systems and suppliers, and finally has to convince quality, engineering and procurement. Each format works best at one of these stages, as the table shows.

seccions.titol: What scientists actually download
seccions.text:
A scientist or process engineer will not download a brochure with a new cover. They want data they can compare with their own. Growth curves, culture conditions, filtration performance, scale-up steps from lab to pilot plant and the protocol that was followed.
That data comes from your applications lab or from customer projects. If it belongs to a customer, you need their written permission and often have to anonymise it. Everything goes through engineering before publication, because an inflated figure in an application note gets found out at the first trial.

seccions.titol: What is worth putting behind a form
seccions.text:
Asking for details has a cost, because a scientist who only wanted to check a protocol may leave without reading it. A practical rule is to gate what is long and decision-grade, such as a white paper or webinar registration, and leave the application note open, or at least its summary with the key data.
Open content also helps people find you. Google recommends making important content available as text, and a PDF that only opens after a form does not help. A page with the summary, the key data and the full PDF one click away works for search engines, for AI answers and for the reader.

seccions.titol: How to tell which format brings real leads
seccions.text:
In Google Analytics 4, any event can be marked as a key event. Mark each document download, form submission and webinar registration, and you will see which channels drive those actions. But a download is not a sale. You need to match it against your CRM to see which contacts turn into real opportunities.
To put content in front of the right people, LinkedIn lets you target by job title, company or industry, run campaigns to a list of named accounts and retarget people who have already engaged with your brand. A webinar on bioreactor scale-up makes more sense in front of process leads at CDMOs and biotechs than the whole industry.

seccions.titol: Automated follow-up after the download
seccions.text: This is where automation saves time. When someone downloads a document, the system can later send a related application note or an invitation to the next webinar, and alert sales only when the contact fits your profile. We connect the form, the CRM and the email tool with simple rules your sales team understands and can change.

faqs.q: Should application notes be gated?
faqs.a: Not always. If the note is short and the data is what convinces, leave it open or gate only the full PDF, with the summary and key data on the page. More people read it, search engines can index it, and the form is saved for longer documents or the webinar.

faqs.q: Live or recorded webinar?
faqs.a: Live, the value is the conversation. Audience questions show what worries customers and give you ideas for the next application notes. The recording can go to people who could not attend and works as on-demand content. The practical choice is to run it live and publish the recording afterwards behind a registration form.

faqs.q: Can we use a customer's data?
faqs.a: Only with their written permission and after agreeing with them what can be shown. If the project is under NDA, the customer may not want their name, the molecule or the scale to appear. The alternative is to use data from your own applications lab or to anonymise the case with the customer's input.

calculadora-cost-fira.intro: Using the official ACHEMA 2027 fees, a 12 square metre stand with a basic build costs €7,627 excluding VAT, before travel, hotels and shipping. This calculator adds up the full cost of your show, from space and stand build to travel and shipping your demo equipment, and divides it by the qualified contacts and opportunities you expect. Everything is calculated in your browser and nothing is sent anywhere.

seccions.titol: Work out the full cost of your trade show
seccions.text:
Fill in the fields with the prices you have, from the stand quote to the hotel rate. If you are going to ACHEMA, pick one of the published space fees and the price per square metre fills itself in. Empty fields count as zero, so the total only includes what you have entered.
The result is only as good as your figures. The ACHEMA fees are the official 2027 rates, excluding VAT and excluding stand build, services and the charges the show adds on top. The calculator does not store or send anything, and your figures are gone when you close the page.

seccions.titol: What the space costs and what the fee leaves out
seccions.text:
Space is charged per square metre and the rate goes up with the open sides. At ACHEMA 2027, held in Frankfurt from 14 to 18 June, stands along hall walls or outer gangways cost €378 per square metre, other aisle stands with one open side €453.60, and stands with two or more open sides €529.20. Start-ups and academic research institutions pay €239.
These fees exclude VAT and do not cover stand build or services. The conditions of participation also add a mandatory media package of €495 per exhibitor and a mandatory visitor flat-rate charge by stand size, which is €220 for 12 square metres. Put these amounts under other costs.
According to ACHEMA’s exhibitor FAQ, space is paid in three instalments. The first, 94 euros per square metre, is due right after you apply. The second, 65 % of the balance, falls due no earlier than 15 September 2026, and the third, the remaining 35 %, no earlier than 15 February 2027. There is no application deadline, and space is allocated by availability.
If you cancel between 1 September 2026 and 14 March 2027, you pay 50 % of the agreed fees, and from 15 March, 100 % of the space. A co-exhibitor pays 1,060 euros plus the 90-euro visitor flat rate and the 495-euro media package, and the fee is not refunded on cancellation.

seccions.titol: Stand build, per square metre or as a lump sum
seccions.text:
Stand build can be quoted in two ways and the calculator takes both. ACHEMA sells all-in-one packages charged per square metre on top of the space fee, such as Compact at €198 for stands of 12 to 25 square metres. If you work with your own stand builder, enter the lump sum from their quote.
Before comparing quotes, check what each one includes. Electricity, cleaning, furniture, screens and graphics may be inside the price or billed separately. Add anything billed separately under other costs so the total does not come up short.

seccions.titol: People, travel, hotels and daily allowances
seccions.text:
Team costs multiply with every person who travels. The calculator works out travel per person, hotel per person and night, and allowance per person and day. Count the build-up and dismantling days too if someone from your team is there, because those nights and meals are paid as well.
Working hours are not part of this calculation. If you want the real cost to the company, add the days your sales and engineering people spend away from the office under other costs. Then the cost per opportunity can be compared fairly with a sales visit or a campaign.

seccions.titol: Shipping and insuring your demo equipment
seccions.text:
Taking a bioreactor or a filtration system to the stand has a cost of its own. It covers packing, shipping there and back, handling inside the venue and insurance while the equipment is away. Ask for a complete price with the return leg included, so the bill does not arrive in pieces.
If the equipment is too big or too delicate to move, showing it on screen with a 3D render or animation may work out better. Look at how much this item weighs in the cost split before deciding what you bring and what you explain on video.

seccions.titol: What a trade show costs, using published figures
seccions.text:
At the start, space is the biggest line, and each organiser publishes its price per square metre. At ACHEMA 2027 it ranges from €378 to €529.20 excluding VAT depending on the open sides, and at analytica 2028, the Munich laboratory show, from €295 to €375. Both set a minimum stand size of 12 square metres.
On top come mandatory charges that are not in the headline rate. At ACHEMA, a €495 media package and a visitor flat rate that runs from €220 for 12 square metres up to €6,990 for more than 500. At analytica, a €1,370 communications fee, €6 per square metre for waste disposal and €0.80 for the AUMA levy.
With those figures, a small ACHEMA 2027 stand works out as follows before travel, hotels, per diems and equipment shipping. We use the show's own Compact build package at €198 per square metre, with prices excluding VAT. A 12 square metre wall stand costs €7,627, and an 18 square metre stand with two open sides €13,944.60.
The rest is down to you. The guide from AUMA, the German trade fair industry association, groups the cost of exhibiting into four blocks. Basic costs such as space rental, stand build and fittings, staff and travel, and other spending such as communication, catering, transport and waste. If your budget only covers the first two, it is not the full cost yet.

faqs.q: Does the calculator store or send my figures?
faqs.a: No. Everything is calculated in your browser by a small script and nothing is sent to crida studio or anyone else. Your figures are not stored anywhere and disappear when you close or reload the page. If you want to keep the result, write it down or take a screenshot before you leave.

faqs.q: Do the ACHEMA fees include VAT and stand build?
faqs.a: No. According to the ACHEMA 2027 conditions of participation, all fees are net prices without VAT, and neither services nor stand construction are included. On top of that there is a mandatory €495 media package and a visitor flat-rate charge based on stand size. Add them under other costs.

faqs.q: Can I use the calculator for another show?
faqs.a: Yes. Leave the ACHEMA fee unselected and type in the price per square metre published by the organiser of your show. The other fields work the same for any event, from CPHI to BIO. Always check whether the published price includes VAT, stand build and mandatory charges.

faqs.q: How many contacts and opportunities should I enter?
faqs.a: The number you realistically expect, based on previous shows or meetings already booked. If you have no data, try several figures to see how many opportunities it takes for the show to pay off. After the show, come back with the real numbers from your CRM.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to exhibit at a trade show?
faqs.a: It depends on the show and the floor space. Using the official ACHEMA 2027 fees, a 12 square metre wall stand with a basic build costs €7,627 excluding VAT, and an 18 square metre stand with two open sides €13,944.60. On top of that come travel, hotels, per diems, equipment shipping and your team's time.

estudi-webs-fabricants-bioproces-europa.intro: Almost every European bioprocess equipment maker has an English website, but few invite buyers to ask for a quote from the home page. We analysed the home pages of 66 websites on 1 November 2026. 62 (93.9%) offer English, 38 (57.6%) two or more languages and only 10 (15.2%) a button to request a quote, an offer or a demo.

seccions.titol: What the numbers say about 66 bioprocess manufacturer websites
seccions.text:
European bioprocess equipment makers have the technical basics and English covered, and fall short when it comes to selling. 61 of 63 (96.8%) redirect to HTTPS on their own, 62 of 66 (93.9%) offer English and 52 (78.8%) have a meta description. By contrast, only 10 (15.2%) have a quote or demo button and none has all five sales elements we looked for.
The sample is 79 Europe-based makers of bioreactors, filtration, single-use systems, chromatography, sensors and process plants. We could read the home page of 66 (83.5%). 45 of the 79 are headquartered in Germany, Austria or Switzerland, which weighs on the overall figures.

seccions.titol: How we chose the companies and how we measured
seccions.text:
There is no census of European bioprocess equipment makers, so we cross-checked the public exhibitor lists of BioProcess International in Europe and the United States from 2023 to 2026, ACHEMA 2027 and analytica 2026, plus the bionity.com and AseBio directories. We kept own-brand manufacturers headquartered in Europe and left out distributors, CDMOs, software firms and subsidiaries of non-European groups.
Our own program read the home page, robots.txt and llms.txt of each site on 1 November 2026, without running JavaScript, one request at a time and with pauses. It identifies itself as crida studio and respects robots.txt. Of the 13 sites we could not read, 9 sit behind bot protection, which we did not try to get around.
This is neither a census nor an audit. Anything loaded with JavaScript is invisible to us, so the figures are minimums. The sales index is our own yardstick. We give no results by company size because no public source covers enough firms. The sample includes one crida studio client and the company where its founder used to work. Like the rest, they are not named.

seccions.titol: How many languages they offer and where the gaps are
seccions.text:
English is almost universal, but most sites stop there or shortly after. 62 of 66 (93.9%) offer English and 38 (57.6%) two or more languages. 28 (42.4%) show a single language, nearly always English, and 36 (54.5%) use hreflang, the tag that tells Google which version is meant for each language.
Companies headquartered in Germany, Austria and Switzerland offer more languages. 26 of 38 of their sites (68.4%) have two or more, against 5 of 10 (50.0%) in Spain and Portugal and 7 of 18 (38.9%) in the rest of Europe. For a maker selling across several countries, speaking the buyer’s language can still set it apart.

seccions.titol: How they invite quote requests and what buyers can download
seccions.text:
Nearly every home page has a contact link, 65 of 66 (98.5%), but few go further. Only 10 (15.2%) have a button or link in the HTML to request a quote, an offer or a demo, or to talk to an expert, and 20 (30.3%) have a form on the home page. For a buyer who knows what they need, a plain contact link is too generic.
49 of 66 (74.2%) link to LinkedIn and 31 (47.0%) to a PDF or to datasheets, a catalogue or downloads. Our sales index runs from 0 to 5 and gives one point each for English, a quote or demo button, LinkedIn, datasheets and company or product structured data. The average is 2.8, 19 sites score four and none scores five.

seccions.titol: What Google and AI assistants can read
seccions.text:
Structured data is there, but it often says little. 44 of 66 (66.7%) include JSON-LD, often what the content management system adds by default, and 33 (50.0%) state who they are with the Organization type. Only 1 (1.5%) describes a product with the Product type, which is what helps a search engine or an AI understand what the company makes.
11 sites (16.7%) already have an llms.txt, the file that summarises a website for language models. Only 4 (6.1%) block at least one of GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended or CCBot, and none blocks all five. However, 9 of the 79 sites (11.4%) would not let our clearly identified robot read their home page.

seccions.titol: What an equipment maker can check on its own website
seccions.text:
Use this list to go through your home page against the study criteria. Almost everything can be checked by opening the site and its source code, and fixed from the content management system. Our guide to bioprocess equipment manufacturer websites covers each element in more detail.
The aggregates by country group and segment can be downloaded as CSV files from the links below. They contain no data on individual companies and let you compare your own group or simply rerun the numbers.

faqs.q: Can I find out how my company’s website did?
faqs.a: Yes, if you work for the company. The page and the CSV files only contain aggregates by country group and segment, because the study is not meant to single out any manufacturer. Ask us through the contact form and we will explain what we saw on your home page, without publishing it anywhere.

faqs.q: Why is my company not in the study?
faqs.a: Because it only covers Europe-based manufacturers that appear in the exhibitor lists and directories we used, from BioProcess International, ACHEMA 2027, analytica 2026, bionity.com and AseBio. Distributors and the European subsidiaries of groups headquartered outside Europe are not included either.

faqs.q: What does the sales index mean?
faqs.a: It is our own yardstick, from 0 to 5. It gives one point for each element that helps an international buyer from the home page, an English version, a quote or demo button, a LinkedIn link, datasheets or a catalogue, and company or product structured data. It does not say whether a site sells well.

faqs.q: How was each website measured?
faqs.a: With a program that downloads the home page, robots.txt and llms.txt of each site and reads the HTML for a fixed set of indicators. It does not run JavaScript, identifies itself as crida studio, respects robots.txt and makes one request at a time, with pauses. If a site blocks it, we do not force our way in and report it as not analysed.

bio-assajos-terapies-avancades-espanya.intro: ClinicalTrials.gov lists 81 active cell and gene therapy trials with at least one site in Spain, based on our download of 1 November 2026. Industry sponsors 62 of them (76.5%), spread across 32 different sponsors. Barcelona and Madrid host the most trials. For a bioprocess supplier, the data points to two audiences with very different decision makers.

seccions.titol: Who sponsors advanced therapy trials in Spain
seccions.text:
Most cell and gene therapy trials active in Spain are sponsored by industry. Of the 81 we counted, 62 (76.5%) have a lead sponsor in the registry’s industry class. 18 are led by hospitals, research institutes and foundations or individual investigators, and 1 is in the network class. There are 32 different industry sponsors.
The count covers CAR-T, other cell therapies, mesenchymal cells and gene therapies using AAV or lentiviral vectors. Every trial has at least one Spanish site and is recruiting, not yet recruiting, active but not recruiting, or enrolling by invitation. We count trials, not patients or purchasing volume.

seccions.titol: Which phase the trials are in
seccions.text:
Almost half of the trials are in early phases. 36 of the 81 (44.4%) are early phase 1, phase 1 or phase 1/2, while 26 (32.1%) have already reached phase 3. The rest are 16 in phase 2, 2 in phase 2/3 and 1 in phase 4.
Phase 3 belongs almost entirely to industry, with 25 of the 26 trials. Non-industry sponsors cluster at the start. They hold both early phase 1 trials, 4 of the 10 phase 1 trials, 7 of the 24 phase 1/2 trials counting the one in the network class, and 5 of the 16 phase 2 trials.

seccions.titol: Which Spanish cities host the most trials
seccions.text:
Barcelona and Madrid host the most trials. Barcelona has a site in 62 of the 81 trials and Madrid in 46. Next come Salamanca with 23, Valencia with 21, and Pamplona and Seville with 19 each. Santander has 12, Córdoba 10, Badalona 8 and Málaga 7.
Each trial counts once per city, even if it uses more than one hospital there. Cities are taken as written in the registry, which is why Badalona appears separately from Barcelona. For a supplier based in Girona or elsewhere in Catalonia, a large share of this activity is close to home.

seccions.titol: Trials run by hospitals and foundations themselves
seccions.text:
Trials with sites only in Spain are mostly academic. There are 20 of them out of 81, and 17 have a non-industry sponsor. Put another way, 17 of the 19 non-industry trials run only in Spain, while just 3 of the 62 industry trials are Spain-only.
The registry shows clear examples. Fundació Clínic per a la Recerca Biomèdica is listed as lead sponsor of the CAR-T trials ARI0002h, in phase 2, and ARI0003, in early phase 1. Hospital Infantil Universitario Niño Jesús in Madrid sponsors AloCELYVIR, in phase 1/2. Here the sponsor is the hospital or foundation itself, which makes it a potential buyer or partner.

seccions.titol: How to use this data in your marketing
seccions.text:
Read from a marketing angle, the data points to two audiences. In an industry trial, the hospital is where the trial runs, but decisions on equipment and consumables may sit at the sponsor’s headquarters or its CDMO, which may be outside Spain. In an academic trial, the hospital or foundation may be the buyer or the partner.
So it pays to split your accounts. Most of the 32 industry sponsors are global accounts, reached at headquarters and often in English. Hospitals and foundations running their own trials, mainly in Barcelona and Madrid, are local accounts where direct contact and site visits make sense.

seccions.titol: How we counted and what the data does not say
seccions.text:
We used the ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, downloaded on 1 November 2026, with registry data up to 30 October. We filtered by site in Spain and by status (recruiting, not yet recruiting, active not recruiting or enrolling by invitation) and searched interventions for CAR-T, CAR T, chimeric antigen receptor, gene therapy, cell therapy, AAV, lentiviral and mesenchymal.
The query returned 147 records. We kept interventional studies where one of those terms, or certain product names ending in -leucel or -vec, appears in the intervention name, description or other names. That leaves 81. We have kept the list of NCT identifiers, and the count can be repeated with the same query.
There are limits. ClinicalTrials.gov does not cover every trial authorised in Spain, and the Spanish Clinical Studies Registry run by AEMPS is a separate registry. The term-based classification is ours and may miss or include a borderline case. The sponsor class is the registry’s own. These are trial counts, not market size, and a multinational trial counts the same as a Spain-only one.

faqs.q: How many cell and gene therapy trials are there in Spain?
faqs.a: Based on our ClinicalTrials.gov download of 1 November 2026, there are 81 active interventional cell and gene therapy trials with at least one site in Spain. It is not an exact total, because this registry does not cover every trial authorised in the country and the term-based classification is our own.

faqs.q: Why does it matter whether the sponsor is a company or a hospital?
faqs.a: Because it changes who buys. In an industry trial the hospital treats the patients, but decisions on production equipment and consumables may sit with the sponsor or its CDMO, outside Spain. In an academic trial the hospital or foundation may develop its own product and can become a customer or a partner.

faqs.q: How often is it worth repeating this count?
faqs.a: Trials open, change status and close all year round, so an account list built from this data soon goes stale. With the query and filters described in the method section, you can repeat the download before a trade show, a campaign or the annual sales plan, and see which sponsors have joined or dropped out.

bio-fabricacio-continua-ich-q13.intro: ICH Q13 is the international guideline on continuous manufacturing of medicines, adopted on 16 November 2022, and it covers therapeutic proteins. It describes what the drug manufacturer should consider and does not certify any equipment. A supplier of perfusion, chromatography, TFF, sensors or automation, or a CDMO, should explain it with data on what its equipment actually does and never present it as a requirement.

seccions.titol: What ICH Q13 covers and what it does not
seccions.text:
ICH Q13 deals with continuous manufacturing of drug substances and drug products, for both chemical entities and therapeutic proteins. Section 1.2 says it applies to new products, including generics and biosimilars, and to converting existing products from batch to continuous. It adds that its principles may also apply to other biological products.
The guideline focuses on systems where two or more unit operations are directly connected. As examples of a single unit operation it mentions process chromatography and perfusion cell culture. The FDA published it as guidance for industry in March 2023, and the EMA lists it as a scientific guideline with an effective date of 10 July 2023.

seccions.titol: What Annex III says about therapeutic proteins
seccions.text:
Annex III sketches an example continuous process for proteins. It has a bioreactor compatible with perfusion culture, continuous capture chromatography, virus inactivation, polishing chromatography, virus filtration and a TFF step for buffer exchange and concentration. The guideline itself says the example is illustrative and that other approaches can be used.
For equipment makers, the annex gives very concrete pointers. It asks for the integrity of single-use components to be ensured during use, since connections may run for long periods or be changed often. It covers changing filters and integrity testing them without interrupting the process, surge tanks and in-line sensors. It also notes that continuous bioreactors may run far longer than batch ones.

seccions.titol: How to talk about the guideline without selling it as a rule
seccions.text:
ICH Q13 is written for the company that makes the medicine and files the dossier. The customer decides how a batch is defined. Section 2.2 says the size of a continuous batch can be set by the quantity of output material, the quantity of input material or the run time at a defined mass flow rate. Your equipment does not make that call.
That is why claims that use the guideline like a seal of approval backfire. A quality lead knows no piece of equipment complies with ICH Q13 on its own. The table lists common claims and a more accurate way to put them.

seccions.titol: What to put on the datasheet of continuous process equipment
seccions.text:
The datasheet should say how the equipment behaves inside a continuous process. Section 3.1.4 lists design considerations such as components that hold up for the maximum run time, the physical connections and digital control interfaces between equipment, and where the sampling and material diversion points sit.
The same goes for “perfusion ready”. Say which cell retention device it was tested with, for how many consecutive days and what data you have. A CDMO can do the same on its website with the operating modes it runs and the campaigns it has already completed.

seccions.titol: Which evidence convinces a process development team
seccions.text:
The strongest evidence answers the risks the guideline itself lists. Section 3.2 says issues not seen in short runs may appear as run time increases. It names process drift, rising equipment temperatures, material build-up, exceeding resin cycle limits, membrane or sensor fouling and microbial contamination.
A test report with the real run time or an application note showing how drift is detected is worth more than any adjective. Section 3.1.5 says process analytical technology, PAT, is well suited to continuous manufacturing, and gives in-line UV flow cells for protein concentration as an example.

faqs.q: Is ICH Q13 mandatory for equipment manufacturers?
faqs.a: It is a harmonised guideline written for the company that makes the medicine and files the dossier. It looks at equipment from that company's point of view and sets no obligations for equipment manufacturers. The FDA published it as guidance for industry and the EMA as a scientific guideline. On your website, say what data your equipment provides for the customer's control strategy.

faqs.q: Can I say my equipment is ICH Q13 compliant?
faqs.a: Better not. The guideline does not certify equipment and has no list of approved systems. Describe what the equipment does in a continuous process instead, for example how long it was tested without stopping, which in-line sensors it carries, how it connects to the rest of the line and what documentation you supply for qualification.

faqs.q: If I make batch equipment, does continuous manufacturing leave me out?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Section 2.1 of the guideline describes processes where some unit operations run in batch mode and others continuously, as well as surge tanks to keep material flowing. If your equipment can work in a hybrid process, show it with a diagram and the conditions under which it was tested.

faqs.q: What should a CDMO explain about continuous manufacturing?
faqs.a: Which modes it runs, from single unit operations to integrated lines, which campaigns it has completed and how long they lasted, which in-line sensors it has and how it handles disturbances. Section 4.8 of the guideline describes a plan for managing disturbances and diverting material within the quality system. Explaining yours builds trust.

bio-comprador-b2b-sense-comercial.intro: Most B2B buyers would now rather buy without going through a sales rep. In Gartner's surveys, 61% of 632 buyers preferred a rep-free experience in 2024 and 67% of 646 buyers did in 2025. For a bioprocess equipment maker or consumables supplier, that means the website has to answer prices or price ranges, specifications, lead times, validation, compatibility, references and who to talk to before a rep gets involved.

seccions.titol: What the latest B2B buyer surveys say
seccions.text:
Two Gartner surveys in a row point the same way. In the first, run in August and September 2024, Gartner asked 632 B2B buyers and 61% said they preferred an overall rep-free buying experience. In the second, run in August and September 2025, it asked 646 buyers and the figure rose to 67%. Of that second group, 45% had already used AI during a recent purchase.
The 2024 survey also shows why the website carries so much weight. Of the 632 buyers, 69% report inconsistencies between what a supplier's website says and what its sellers tell them. And 73% actively avoid suppliers who send irrelevant outreach.

seccions.titol: When buyers still want a sales rep
seccions.text:
Buyers still want a rep, just later in the process. In the 2024 survey, Gartner found they favour online self-service for general information and for learning new things. They prefer seller input when a task needs context, such as working out whether a product fits their company's needs.
In bioprocess, the first half of the purchase usually happens on the website. An engineer comparing bioreactors or a TFF system wants working volumes, materials, documentation and lead times without having to ask. Once they can see the equipment might fit their process, they do want someone to talk through the URS, the FAT and scale-up. If the website does not cover the first half, it is hard to get to the second.

seccions.titol: Thought leadership also helps you onto the shortlist
seccions.text:
Expert content with a point of view counts when buyers decide who to invite to quote. Marketers call it thought leadership. The 2024 Edelman and LinkedIn report surveyed nearly 3,500 management-level professionals in seven countries. Among buyers, 86% say they are moderately or very likely to invite organisations that consistently publish it to take part in an RFP. Among the organisations producing it, only 38% expect that.
In the same survey, 73% see this kind of content as a more trustworthy basis for judging a company's competencies than its marketing materials. Yet only 15% rate what they read as very good or excellent. And 55% say the best content includes strong research and data. In bioprocess, that means application notes with real data, scale-up comparisons or test results.

seccions.titol: Seven answers the website must give before a rep gets involved
seccions.text:
If most buyers want to move forward on their own, the website has to do the job of the first sales visit. For a bioprocess equipment or consumables supplier, that comes down to seven answers a buyer expects to find without filling in a form.
Price and lead time are the two answers that scare suppliers most. Every system is configured to order and delivery dates move. Yet in Gartner's 2024 survey, 69% of the 632 buyers found the website and the rep inconsistent. The simplest fix is for both to give the same facts.

seccions.titol: New website or more trade shows. How to decide with this data
seccions.text:
Trade shows and the website do different jobs. A show puts you in front of buyers who did not know you. The website is where they check what you told them at the stand and where buyers who prefer to move without a rep end up. If the seven answers are missing, they have to write to a rep. That is the very step 67% of the 646 buyers Gartner surveyed in 2025 would rather avoid.
If you run marketing at a mid-size European equipment maker, check whether the website says what you say at the stand in every language you sell in. If you are the only marketer at a life science supplier in Catalonia or elsewhere in Spain, remember that a show lasts a few days while the website works all year. Either way, fill the gaps on the website first. Then measure how many requests for quotation each show brings in.

seccions.titol: How to check your website in an afternoon
seccions.text:
Take your last ten requests for quotation and note what each buyer asked in their first message. Then look for each answer on your website the way they would. Start from Google and use a phone. Whatever you cannot find in two clicks is what you are forcing buyers to ask a rep about.
Compare the web page with the sales deck as well. If the PDF gives one working-volume range and the website another, that is the inconsistency reported by 69% of the 632 buyers Gartner surveyed in 2024. Once that is fixed, it makes sense to bring buyers in with SEO and campaigns. They will land on pages that answer and the rep will join conversations that have already started.

faqs.q: Do we have to publish equipment prices on the website?
faqs.a: You do not need a fixed price. If it depends on the configuration, explain what drives it, what is included and, if you can, give a range. That saves the first call and filters out poor fits. It also means the website and the rep say the same thing. In Gartner's 2024 survey of 632 buyers, 69% found inconsistencies between the two.

faqs.q: Are these surveys about bioprocess?
faqs.a: No. The Gartner surveys cover B2B buyers in general and the 2024 Edelman and LinkedIn report covers decision-makers in seven countries. They show where B2B buying is heading. To see what is happening in your market, ask your latest buyers what they had looked up before sending you a request for quotation.

faqs.q: Can weak technical content actually hurt us?
faqs.a: Yes. In an Edelman and LinkedIn survey of 1,300 decision-makers and C-suite executives, run in October and November 2016, 45% of decision-makers and 53% of C-suite executives said poor thought leadership had sometimes made them lose respect for the company behind it. And 30% and 35% respectively said it could also affect how much business they awarded.

bio-fires-bioproces-cost-visitants.intro: Every organiser counts differently, and total attendance does not tell you how many bioprocess equipment buyers you will meet. According to DECHEMA's summary, ACHEMA 2024 had 106,001 participants and 32.0% worked in pharma and life sciences. This guide gathers the figures for ACHEMA, CPHI, BPI and BIO with their source documents and shows how to turn them into cost per useful contact before you book a 2027 stand.

seccions.titol: What each organiser publishes and how to compare it
seccions.text: Each organiser publishes different figures, and not all of them are dated. ACHEMA and CPHI issue a PDF with visitor origin, job level and interests. BPI shows undated counters on its website, and BIO published expectations on 22 June 2026. We read all of them on 1 November 2026.

seccions.titol: ACHEMA 2024. A huge crowd from many industries
seccions.text:
According to Insights ACHEMA 2024, DECHEMA's summary, the show had 106,001 participants from 141 countries and 2,842 exhibitors from 56 countries. The PDF carries no date, and its file metadata says October 2025. Of the participants, 48.9% came from outside Germany and 7.4% from Southern Europe. For 52% of visitors, ACHEMA is the only trade show they attend.
If you make bioprocess equipment, look at how many people come from your industry. The same summary says 32.0% of participants work in the pharmaceutical and life sciences industry and 40.4% in chemicals. The shares add up to more than 100, so one person can appear in more than one industry. By exhibition group, 28.0% are interested in pharmaceutical, packaging and storage techniques.

seccions.titol: CPHI Frankfurt 2025. The whole pharma supply chain
seccions.text:
CPHI presents itself as the show for the whole pharma supply chain. The organiser's Post Show Report 2025 is an undated PDF and reports 59,000+ attendees from 170 countries and 2,900+ exhibitors from 116 countries. Of the attendees, 56% came from Europe and 29% from Asia. Spain ranked ninth among attendee countries and fifth among exhibitor countries.
The same report says 23% of attendees listed pharmaceutical machinery and technology as an area of interest. Finished dosage forms reached 41% and APIs 40%. By department, business development made up 28% and purchasing 10%. The event app recorded 17,500+ confirmed meetings.

seccions.titol: BPI Europe and BPI Boston. Two shows built around bioprocessing
seccions.text:
The BPI Europe website, run by Informa Connect, shows a counter of 800+ participants from across all phases of bioprocessing. It gives no year, and we read it on 1 November 2026. The same site says 400+ meetings were arranged through the ConnectMe app in 2025. The 2026 edition took place in Vienna and the 2027 edition moves to Hamburg from 27 to 29 April.
BPI Boston, from the same series, runs as part of Biotech Week Boston. According to its website, 3,000+ bioprocessing professionals from 40+ countries attend. That counter is undated too, and we also read it on 1 November 2026. Of the attendees, 85% are scientists, engineers or director level and above. The exhibit hall features 250+ CDMOs, CROs and suppliers. The 2027 edition is set for 20 to 23 September.

seccions.titol: BIO, BIO-Europe and BIOSPAIN. Shows built around partnering meetings
seccions.text:
The BIO International Convention opened its 2026 edition in San Diego on 22 June. BIO's press release that day expected 20,000 registrants. Over 40% of them would be international. It also expected 70,000 partnering meetings among nearly 10,000 delegates and cited 68+ countries and 1,600+ exhibitors. These are opening-day figures and the final count may differ.
BIO-Europe and BIOSPAIN are also built on one-to-one meetings. Biotechs, pharma companies, investors and suppliers book them before the show. At these events, look at how many meetings you can lock in before you go. The BIOSPAIN 2025 and 2026 figures and the 2027 dates are in our BioSpain or Farmaforum guide.

seccions.titol: From total visitors to cost per useful contact
seccions.text:
Start from each organiser's figure and apply your buyer filter. At ACHEMA, use the 32.0% from pharma and life sciences in DECHEMA's summary. At CPHI, the 23% who listed machinery in its report. At BPI Boston, the 85% its website counts as scientists, engineers or director level and above. Each share measures something different and only works within its own show.
Next comes the crida studio trade show cost calculator. It adds up space, stand build, travel, hotels, daily allowances, equipment shipping and insurance, and other costs. Then it divides the total by the qualified contacts and opportunities you expect. Those two numbers are your own estimate. Empty fields count as zero, and the only preset prices are ACHEMA 2027 space fees excluding VAT and stand build. Staff time only counts if you add it under other costs.
To estimate contacts, count how many quality conversations each person on the stand can hold per day and how many meetings you arrive with. Then compare two or three shows under the same rules before signing anything.

faqs.q: Can you use organiser figures to compare shows?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as you compare like with like. ACHEMA counts participants, and its undated summary PDF notes that the daily total of 164,200 includes people counted more than once. BIO gave expected registrants on 22 June 2026, and BPI shows undated counters. Before you book, ask the organiser for the attendance report by industry and job level.

faqs.q: What counts as a useful contact at a bioprocess show?
faqs.a: In this guide, it is an identified person with a clear company and application who agrees to a next step. That could be a visit, a trial or a request for quotation. Badges scanned without a conversation do not count. Settle the definition before the show and use the same one in the calculator and your CRM.

faqs.q: Should we exhibit at BIO, BIO-Europe or BIOSPAIN if we sell equipment?
faqs.a: It depends on who buys from you. In its press release of 22 June 2026, BIO cited 1,600+ exhibitors and expected 70,000 partnering meetings. At BIO-Europe and BIOSPAIN the weight is on one-to-one meetings. If your customers are start-ups scaling up or CDMOs looking for partners, you can start as a visitor with meetings booked in advance and decide on a stand later.

obs-2026-01.intro: According to ClinicalTrials.gov, 17 industry-sponsored biologics trials with sites in Europe got under way in December 2025, 9 more than in November. This first edition of the Market Watch reads open data from the EMA, the FDA, Eurostat and other registries up to 31 December 2025. It is written for marketing and sales leads at European makers of bioprocess equipment, consumables and services.

seccions.titol: What the December 2025 data say
seccions.text:
In December 2025, 17 industry biologics trials started in Europe, 9 more than in November, and 62 worldwide. Spain had 13, more than any other European country we track. The EMA authorised 1 medicine and the FDA approved 10.
FDA CGMP warning letters came to 13, and imports of subheading 8419.89 stayed almost level with November. The table compares each indicator with the previous month, and its figures are counts of official records, not equipment demand.

seccions.titol: EMA authorisations and FDA approvals, July to December
seccions.text:
In December 2025 the EMA authorised 1 human medicine and the FDA approved 10, made up of 7 novel drugs from CDER and 3 biologics licenses from CBER. In November each agency had approved 14. From July to December, the EMA ranged between 1 and 14 authorisations a month and the FDA between 2 and 14.
The EMA authorises in batches, so a month with 1 authorisation does not mean the sector has stalled. In November, 9 of the 14 medicines authorised were biosimilars, and in December none. The EMA table flags biosimilars but does not single out other biologics. CBER approves vaccines, blood products, gene therapies and some diagnostic reagents.
Each authorisation is a product that can now be sold and will need manufacturing with qualified consumables, equipment and services. This edition only counts authorisations, and the individual products are listed in the EMA and FDA sources.

seccions.titol: Where biologics trials started in December
seccions.text:
In December 2025, 17 industry biologics trials started with sites in Europe, 31 in the United States, 32 in Asia and 9 in Latin America. Worldwide the figure was 62. The territories add up to more than the total because a trial with sites in several countries counts in each one.
Within Europe, Spain had 13, Italy 9 and Germany 8. France, the United Kingdom and Poland had 7 each, Belgium 6, the Netherlands 3 and Switzerland none. These are small numbers, and in November Spain had only 3. One month does not make a trend, and December may still rise because many studies are registered late.
A new trial means clinical batches that someone has to make, often a CDMO or a pilot plant. The site country tells you where patients are treated, not where the medicine is made. It shows where the activity is and which sponsors to follow.

seccions.titol: Imports under subheading 8419.89, which includes reactors and fermenters
seccions.text:
In December 2025, the latest month of the edition's period with data for all 27 states, EU member states imported goods under subheading 8419.89 worth 207,864 thousand euros, according to Eurostat. November stood at 207,414 thousand, 450 less, a change of 0.2%. Germany imported 41,479 thousand, the Netherlands 24,585, France 22,691 and Belgium 22,453.
Spain ranked sixth with 10,420 thousand euros, behind Austria with 12,451. Read this with care. The subheading includes other heat treatment apparatus that are neither reactors nor fermenters, and it counts purchases from any country, including within the EU.
The data files include the monthly 2025 series for the 27 states combined. The lowest month was August, at 152,702,945 euros, and the highest was December, at 207,864,244 euros. With such a broad subheading, there is no way to tell how much of it is bioreactors.

seccions.titol: What open data can tell you about Asia and Latin America
seccions.text:
In Asia, which here means Japan, China, India and South Korea, 32 industry biologics trials started in December 2025. China had 24, Japan 9, South Korea 7 and India 2. Latin America had 9, with 4 in Brazil, 4 in Chile, 3 in Argentina, 1 in Mexico and none in Colombia.
In Brazil, ANVISA completed 4 biologics registrations in December and none in November, by the date the process closed. In Japan, the PMDA gives 135 entries for fiscal year 2024, from April 2024 to March 2025. Fiscal year 2025 has 104 up to December and is still partial. These entries also include new indications and doses.
Many countries run their own trial registries, and not everything appears on ClinicalTrials.gov. ANVISA and the PMDA count different things from the EMA and the FDA and cannot be compared with each other. They show whether a country is moving.

seccions.titol: What this means for a European bioprocess supplier
seccions.text:
For the coming quarter, these data show where clinical and regulatory work is happening. Germany, Spain, France, Italy, Poland and the United Kingdom had industry biologics trials starting in every month of 2025. That makes a good list for checking whether your CRM covers the sponsors and CDMOs in those countries.
The message depends on who is buying. In November, 9 of the 14 medicines the EMA authorised were biosimilars, a field where cost per batch and capacity weigh heavily. Among the licenses CBER approves are gene therapies, made in small batches with tight traceability. English works across the sector, but buyers in Germany, Spain, Italy or France appreciate their own language.
Before the quarter starts, it pays to prepare a page for each type of customer, datasheets to download in English and in each country's language, a kit for distributors and a trade show calendar with the cost per contact. At crida studio we do marketing for bioprocess equipment makers and life science companies, and the studio's founder ran marketing at a European manufacturer for three and a half years.

seccions.titol: What changed since November and how to read the series
seccions.text:
As this is the first edition, the comparison is with the previous month, November 2025. Trial starts rose in every territory, up 9 in Europe, 18 in the United States, 14 in Asia and 7 in Latin America. Approvals fell, down 13 at the EMA and 4 at the FDA, and CGMP warning letters went from 8 to 13.
The chart shows trials started worldwide in each month of 2025, between 37 in January and 65 in June, with 62 in December. Each point is a count of records, and the latest months can rise with late registrations. A real change shows up when it repeats over several months.

seccions.titol: Method, sources and limits of this edition
seccions.text: Edition prepared in November 2026 with the data for its period. The data run to 31 December 2025 and were downloaded on 1 November 2026 from eight public sources. They are counts of official records, not equipment demand, and no figure is a market size. The latest month may still rise because some records arrive late. The list below sets out what each source counts, what it leaves out and the exact query.

faqs.q: How many biologics trials started in Spain in December 2025?
faqs.a: 13, according to ClinicalTrials.gov. These are industry-sponsored interventional trials with at least one biological intervention and at least one site in Spain. November had 3. A trial with sites in several countries counts in each one, and a single month is not a trend. The latest month may also still rise.

faqs.q: Are these counts a measure of equipment demand?
faqs.a: No. They are counts of official records, such as trials, authorisations or FDA letters, and they do not say how much equipment will be bought or for what value. They show where the activity is and which sponsors to follow. The Eurostat imports are in euros, but subheading 8419.89 includes plenty of apparatus that is not a bioreactor.

faqs.q: How was each figure calculated?
faqs.a: From public data published by the EMA, the FDA, ClinicalTrials.gov, Eurostat, ANVISA and the PMDA, downloaded on 1 November 2026. Every figure comes straight from its source, with no estimates. The method section gives the exact query and the limits of each source, and the data can be downloaded as CSV and JSON to repeat the calculations.

obs-2026-02.intro: In January 2026, 6 industry biologics trials with at least one site in Europe got under way, down from 17 in December. This edition reads open official data from February 2025 through 31 January 2026. It is written for European makers and suppliers of bioprocess equipment, consumables and services who want to see where the activity is.

seccions.titol: January 2026 in numbers
seccions.text:
Europe saw 6 new industry biologics trials in January 2026, 11 fewer than in December. Worldwide, 57 trials started, and Asia, with 27, had more than any other territory. The EMA authorised 11 medicines and the FDA approved 1, the reverse of December.
FDA CGMP warning letters fell from 13 to 5, and imports under subheading 8419.89 into the 27 EU member states went from 207,864 to 159,894 thousand euros. These are counts of official records and Eurostat trade statistics, and with counts this small a single month does not make a trend.

seccions.titol: The EMA authorised 11 medicines in January and the FDA approved 1
seccions.text:
The EMA authorised 11 human medicines through the centralised procedure in January 2026, 2 of them biosimilars. The FDA approved 1, a novel drug from CDER, and CBER approved no new biologics license. December had been the other way round, with 1 EMA authorisation and 10 FDA approvals, 7 from CDER and 3 from CBER.
EMA authorisations come in batches. A month with just 1, such as October or December 2025, does not mean anything has slowed down. The EMA table flags biosimilars but does not separate other biologics from small-molecule medicines, and it includes generics. CBER licenses vaccines, blood products, gene therapies and some diagnostic reagents. Neither count says where each product is made.

seccions.titol: How many biologics trials started in each territory
seccions.text:
In January 2026, 57 industry trials with at least one biological intervention started. Of these, 27 had a site in Asia, 18 in the United States, 6 in Europe and 6 in Latin America. A trial with sites in several territories counts in each one, and some countries fall outside the four territories, so these figures should not be added together.
In Europe, 5 of the 6 trials had a site in Spain, and 4 each in Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom. France and Poland had 3 each, the Netherlands and Belgium 1 each, and Switzerland none. Several trials run in more than one country, which is why the countries add up to more than the total.
The registry shows where patients are treated, not where the product is made or on what equipment. For a supplier of pilot plant or single-use equipment, it points to where clinical work is happening, which you then need to check with customers and distributors. Many antibodies are also registered as drugs rather than biologics, so the count falls short.

seccions.titol: Which EU member states imported most under subheading 8419.89
seccions.text:
January 2026 is the latest month with data for all 27 member states within this edition's period. That month, the 27 together imported 159,894 thousand euros under subheading 8419.89. Germany imported the most, at 33,924 thousand euros, followed by the Netherlands at 25,844 and France at 14,348. Spain came sixth, at 8,601.
