Read this with care. Subheading 8419.89 covers other equipment for treating materials through a change of temperature, and much of it is neither a bioreactor nor a fermenter. It also counts trade between EU states. In the twelve-month series for the 27 combined, December 2025 is the highest month and August the lowest. January is 23.1% below December, and Eurostat may still revise these figures.

seccions.titol: What open data can tell you about Asia and Latin America
seccions.text:
In Asia, 21 of the 27 trials started in January 2026 had a site in China, 5 in South Korea, 4 in Japan and 2 in India. China has been the Asian country with the most trials every month, between 13 and 25 over the twelve months of the series. This edition reads only ClinicalTrials.gov, not the national trial registries of each Asian country.
In Latin America, all 6 January trials had a site in Brazil, 3 in Argentina and 1 each in Mexico, Colombia and Chile. ANVISA registered 1 medicine in the biological category in January and 4 in December, going by the process completion date. Over the series, ANVISA ranges from 0 to 10 registrations a month.
In Japan, PMDA approvals are counted by fiscal year, April to March. Between FY2020 and FY2024 they ranged from 123 to 146 entries a year. FY2025 is still partial, with 104 entries from April 2025 to January 2026, so it cannot be compared with complete years. The list also counts new indications and doses, not only new active ingredients.

seccions.titol: What it means for a European bioprocess supplier
seccions.text:
For the coming quarter, one month is no reason to move budget, but it is a reason to check where you are looking. Germany had sites in 4 of the 6 European trials in January and was the top importer under subheading 8419.89, while Spain appeared in 5 of the 6. Before deciding, open your country's records on ClinicalTrials.gov and see which companies sponsor them.
In your messaging, English is the base, because several trials run in more than one country at once. For Germany, datasheets and pages in German are worth having, and for Brazil, in Portuguese. The message that fits these figures is the step from the lab to clinical manufacturing, backed by IQ, OQ and PQ qualification documents and local service.
It is worth preparing a website with downloadable datasheets in each language, a kit for distributors in Asia and Brazil, and a trade show plan built on numbers, for example with the trade show cost calculator. At crida studio we do marketing for bioprocess equipment makers and life science companies, and the studio's founder ran marketing at a European manufacturer for three and a half years.

seccions.titol: What has changed since the January edition
seccions.text:
Compared with the previous edition, which ran to December 2025, almost every January count is down. Europe goes from 17 to 6 trials, the United States from 31 to 18, Asia from 32 to 27 and Latin America from 9 to 6. Spain falls from 13 to 5. Worldwide the drop is smaller, from 62 to 57, down 8.1%.
EMA authorisations rise from 1 to 11, and authorised biosimilars from 0 to 2. FDA approvals fall from 10 to 1, CGMP warning letters from 13 to 5, ANVISA biologics registrations from 4 to 1, and imports under subheading 8419.89 from 207,864 to 159,894 thousand euros.
The line shows the worldwide total each month, from a low of 38 trials in February 2025 to a high of 65 in June, with January 2026 at 57. December 2025 was the busiest month for Europe in the whole series, with 17 trials, which is why the January drop looks so steep.

seccions.titol: How this edition was built and what its limits are
seccions.text: Edition prepared in November 2026 with the data for its period, February 2025 to 31 January 2026, downloaded on 1 November 2026 from eight open sources. These are counts of official records, not equipment demand or market figures. The latest month may still rise, because some records arrive late. The list below gives each exact query and its limits.

faqs.q: How many biologics trials started in Spain in January 2026?
faqs.a: According to ClinicalTrials.gov, 5 industry trials with at least one biological intervention started in January 2026 with a site in Spain, against 13 in December 2025. A trial with sites in several countries counts in each country. The figure may still rise as late registrations come in.

faqs.q: Are these counts equipment demand?
faqs.a: No. They are counts of official records, such as registered trials and authorised medicines, plus trade statistics for a customs subheading that also covers other equipment. They show where and when there is activity, but not how many units will be bought or for how much. To decide where to sell, combine them with what you know about your customers and distributors.

faqs.q: How was this edition calculated?

obs-2026-03.intro: In February 2026, 13 industry biologics trials started in Europe, according to ClinicalTrials.gov. seccions.titol: What the open data say for February 2026
seccions.text:
In February 2026, 55 industry biologics trials started worldwide, and 13 had at least one site in Europe. The United States also had 13, Asia 26 and Latin America 4. The EMA authorised 7 medicines, 2 of them biosimilars, while the FDA approved 4 and issued 6 CGMP warning letters.
According to Eurostat, the 27 EU member states imported 158,349 thousand euros under subheading 8419.89 that month, with Germany accounting for 38,846 thousand. Trials and approvals are small counts of official records, not equipment demand, and a single month does not make a trend.

seccions.titol: How many medicines did the EMA and the FDA approve?
seccions.text:
In February 2026 the EMA authorised 7 human medicines through the centralised procedure, 2 of them biosimilars. The FDA approved 4, all novel drugs from CDER, and CBER granted no new biologics license. The chart compares both agencies over the last six months.
The EMA authorises in batches. It authorised 1 medicine in October 2025 and 1 in December 2025, but 14 in November. So one weak month does not make a trend. For a supplier, each authorisation is a product that can now be sold in the EU and that someone will have to make. The EMA table flags biosimilars but does not single out other biologics.

seccions.titol: Where did February's biologics trials start?
seccions.text:
In February 2026, Europe and the United States had 13 trials each, Asia 26 and Latin America 4. These are interventional studies sponsored by companies, with at least one biological intervention, counted by start month on ClinicalTrials.gov. Each one needs clinical batches made under GMP.
By European country, France and Spain had 6 each, Italy 5 and the United Kingdom 3. Germany, Belgium and Poland had 2 each, the Netherlands 1 and Switzerland none. A study with sites in several countries counts in each one, which is why the countries add up to more than the European total.
This count does not tell you where manufacturing will happen. A trial's country is where the sites and patients are, and the clinical batch may be made elsewhere. For a supplier, the figure shows where there is clinical activity with biologics and where it makes sense to look for contacts, but not how much equipment will be bought.

seccions.titol: Which member states imported most under subheading 8419.89?
seccions.text:
February 2026 is the latest month with data for all 27 member states in Eurostat within this edition's period. That month the 27 imported 158,349 thousand euros under subheading 8419.89. Germany imported 38,846 thousand, followed by the Netherlands with 16,114, Sweden with 14,998 and France with 13,540. Spain imported 8,269 thousand.
Subheading 8419.89 covers other machinery, plant and laboratory equipment for treating materials through a change of temperature. It includes bioreactors and fermenters, but also plenty of equipment that is neither. It also counts goods arriving from other EU states. Over the last twelve months, the lowest month was August 2025, with 152,702,945 euros, and the highest was December 2025, with 207,864,244 euros.

seccions.titol: What can open data tell us about Asia and Latin America?
seccions.text:
In Asia, 26 biologics trials started in February 2026. Of these, 21 had a site in China, 4 in Japan, 4 in South Korea and none in India. China had more trials than each of the other three countries in every month of the series. Japan and South Korea see few trials a month, so a change from one month to the next says little.
In Latin America, 4 trials started in February 2026, 2 of them with sites in Brazil. That month the Brazilian agency ANVISA registered no biologics, after 1 in January. Over the last twelve months, the peak was 10 registrations, in March 2025. The ANVISA open file has no registration date, so the count uses the date the process was completed.
In Japan we count PMDA approvals by fiscal year, from April to March. Between FY2020 and FY2024 there were between 123 and 146 a year. FY2025 has 119 from April 2025 to February 2026, a partial figure. These entries include new indications and doses, not only new active ingredients, so they are context rather than a monthly gauge.

seccions.titol: What does this month mean for a European supplier?
seccions.text:
For the April to June 2026 quarter, February offers two leads in Europe. Of the European countries broken out here, France, Spain and Italy had the most trial starts. Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden imported the most under subheading 8419.89. France had both 6 trials and 13,540 thousand euros of imports. Before moving budget, check the twelve-month series in the CSV, because one month is not a trend.
If you sell to teams making clinical batches, talk about scale-up from lab to pilot plant, single-use and GMP documentation such as URS, FAT, SAT, IQ, OQ and PQ. Do it in English for the whole of Europe and add French, German, Italian or Spanish where you really want to win business. If you are looking at Asia, where China had 21 trials in February, prepare English material built for distributors.
Get your website ready with language versions and hreflang, downloadable datasheets and a kit for distributors in each country. If you are weighing up a trade show, work out the cost per contact first. At crida studio we do marketing for bioprocess equipment makers and life science companies, and the studio's founder ran marketing at a European manufacturer for three and a half years.

seccions.titol: What went up and what went down since the last edition?
seccions.text:
Compared with the February edition, which covered January 2026, trials in Europe went from 6 to 13 and in Spain from 5 to 6. FDA approvals rose from 1 to 4, all from CDER. CGMP warning letters went from 5 to 6. EMA biosimilars stayed at 2 and CBER licenses at 0.
In the United States, trials fell from 18 to 13, and in Latin America from 6 to 4. Worldwide they went from 57 to 55 and in Asia from 27 to 26. EMA authorisations went from 11 to 7 and ANVISA registrations from 1 to 0. Imports under subheading 8419.89 fell from 159,894 to 158,349 thousand euros, down 1.0%.
The chart shows biologics trials started worldwide each month from March 2025 to February 2026. The low was 42 in November 2025 and the high 65 in June 2025. February had 55. With numbers this small, no one-month move is a trend.

obs-2026-04.intro: In March 2026, 8 industry-sponsored biologics trials started in Europe, 5 fewer than in February, while 45 started in Asia. seccions.titol: What the open data say about March 2026
seccions.text:

The EMA authorised 6 medicines, none of them biosimilars, and the FDA approved 7 across CDER and CBER. The FDA also issued 9 CGMP warning letters, 3 more than in February, and the table below sets these figures against February's.

seccions.titol: How many medicines the EMA and the FDA approved in March 2026
seccions.text:
The EMA authorised 6 human medicines in March 2026 and the FDA approved 7, made up of 5 CDER novel drugs and 2 CBER biologics licenses. The two figures do not measure the same thing. The EMA count includes generics and biosimilars, while the FDA count only covers CDER novel drugs and new CBER licenses.
The chart shows that the EMA authorises in batches. It authorised 14 in November 2025, 1 in December and 11 in January 2026, so a month with a single authorisation means little on its own. The FDA also swings widely, from 14 approvals in November 2025 to 1 in January 2026.
For a supplier, each authorisation is a product that can now be sold and that someone has to make at commercial scale. The EMA table does not say which ones are biologics and only flags biosimilars, none in March and 2 in February. CBER covers vaccines, blood products and gene therapies, but also some diagnostic reagents.

seccions.titol: Where biologics trials started in March 2026
seccions.text:
Asia was the territory with the most industry biologics trials started in March 2026, with 45. The United States had 11, Europe 8 and Latin America 4. The world total of 74 also counts countries not broken out here.
Within Europe, Spain led the nine countries we break out, with 4. Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom had 3 each, France and Poland 2, Switzerland 1, and the Netherlands and Belgium none. A trial with sites in several countries counts in each one, which is why the countries add up to more than Europe's 8.
A new trial usually means clinical batches that someone has to make, often in a pilot plant or at a CDMO. The count does not say where they are made or on what equipment, though. Many antibodies are also registered as drugs rather than biologics, so the figure falls short.

seccions.titol: Which EU states imported the most under subheading 8419.89
seccions.text:
Germany was the member state that imported the most under subheading 8419.89 in March 2026, with 45,827 thousand euros. France followed with 17,787 and the Netherlands with 17,370, while Spain came seventh with 9,053. March 2026 is the latest month with data for all 27 states within this edition's period.
In total, the 27 states imported 182,468 thousand euros in March, 24,119 more than in February, a rise of 15.2%. Over the twelve-month series, the total ranges from a low of 152,702,945 euros in August 2025 to a high of 207,864,244 euros in December 2025.
Subheading 8419.89 includes bioreactors and fermenters, but also other apparatus for treating materials through a change of temperature. These are imports from any country, other EU states included, in current euros. The data show which countries import most of this kind of equipment, but not how many bioreactors are sold.

seccions.titol: What open data can tell you about Asia and Latin America
seccions.text:
In Asia, China had 45 trials started in March 2026, as many as the whole territory, up from 21 in February. Japan had 4, South Korea 3 and India none. This is a one-month jump, and ClinicalTrials.gov does not capture every trial in the region, so it is too early to call it a trend.
In Latin America, 4 trials started, the same number as in February. Brazil had 3, Chile 2, and Mexico, Argentina and Colombia 1 each. In Brazil, ANVISA has 6 biologic medicine registrations with the process completed in March and none in February. The file has no registration date, so we use the process completion date.
For Japan, we count PMDA approvals by fiscal year, which runs from April to March. There were 135 in FY2024 and 119 in FY2025, which is partial because the list runs to February 2026. These entries include new indications and doses, not only new drugs, and serve as context.

seccions.titol: What this means if you sell bioprocess equipment or services
seccions.text:
To decide where to put your sales effort next quarter, look at the twelve-month series rather than March alone. Asia has had more trials than Europe every month, and more than the United States every month since August 2025. If you already have a distributor there, it may be worth giving them more support. If not, take the time to study it before entering.
What to say depends on who buys. Trials point to clinical manufacturing, and authorisations to commercial production. If you sell pilot or single-use equipment, talk about scale-up and clinical batches. If you sell to plants already in production, talk about GMP, validation and service. Do it in English and in the language of each key country, such as German for Germany, which led imports this month.
Before the next trade show, check that your website has technical datasheets in English, that distributors have the same material and that trade show contacts reach your CRM. At crida studio we do marketing for bioprocess equipment manufacturers and life science companies, and the studio's founder ran marketing at a European manufacturer for three and a half years.

seccions.titol: What went up and what went down since the last edition
seccions.text:
Compared with the previous edition, which covered February 2026, trials rose worldwide, from 55 to 74 (+34.5%), and in Asia, from 26 to 45. FDA approvals also rose, from 4 to 7, as did CGMP warning letters, from 6 to 9, and ANVISA biologics registrations, from 0 to 6. EU27 imports rose by 15.2%.
Trials fell in Europe, from 13 to 8, in the United States, from 13 to 11, and in Spain, from 6 to 4. EMA authorisations went from 7 to 6 and biosimilars from 2 to 0. Latin America stayed at 4. These are small numbers, and none of these one-month moves makes a trend.
The line chart puts March in context. Over twelve months, trials started worldwide range from 42 in November 2025 to 74 in March 2026, and before this month the peak was 65, in June 2025. Bear in mind that the last month in the series can rise as late registrations come in.

seccions.titol: What this month means for a European bioprocess supplier

With these figures, sales effort for the following quarter makes more sense where trials keep coming month after month than where there is a one-off peak. On messaging, in April the EMA authorised 5 biosimilars and the FDA issued 12 CGMP warning letters. If you sell to biosimilar makers, talk about scale-up and cost per batch. The EMA goes from 4 to 7 authorisations and the FDA holds at 10, with CDER up from 7 to 9 and CBER down from 3 to 1. CGMP warning letters rise from 11 to 13 (+18.2%) and imports under subheading 8419.89 fall 9.9% from June to July. No one-month change is a trend, and in the chart worldwide trials range from 39 to 74 a month.

seccions.titol: Where the figures come from and what they cannot tell you
seccions.text: Edition prepared in November 2026 with the data for its period. All sources were downloaded on 1 November 2026 and the data run to 30 September 2026, except Eurostat, which runs to July, and the PMDA, to February. These are counts of official records, not equipment sales, and recent months may still rise. The list below gives the exact query, download date and limits for each source.

faqs.q: How many biologics trials started in Spain in September 2026?
faqs.a: According to ClinicalTrials.gov, 2 industry trials with at least one biological intervention, the same as in August. A study with sites in Spain and other countries counts in each country. September is the last month in this edition, so the figure may rise once studies that have already started are registered.

faqs.q: Do these counts measure demand for bioprocess equipment?
faqs.a: No. They are counts of official records, such as trials starting or medicines authorised, plus import values published by Eurostat. They show where there is activity and help decide where to look first, but they do not say how many bioreactors, filters or consumables will be bought, or by whom. That is why this watch gives no market size.

faqs.q: How was each figure calculated?
faqs.a: With scripts that download the official sources and always apply the same filters, without estimates. The eight sources are the EMA, the FDA's CDER and CBER, FDA warning letters, ClinicalTrials.gov, Eurostat, ANVISA and the PMDA. The exact query for each one is in the method section at the end of the page.

observatori-bioproces.intro: Bioprocess Market Watch is a monthly report by crida studio built on open data from the EMA, the FDA, ClinicalTrials.gov, Eurostat, ANVISA and the PMDA. It counts medicine approvals, clinical trials with biologics and equipment imports into the EU, and explains what they mean for anyone selling bioprocess equipment or services in Europe. Here are all the editions, newest first, with the data behind each one.

seccions.titol: What the Market Watch is and who it is for
seccions.text:
Each edition goes through the official records of the previous month. Which medicines the EMA authorised and which the FDA approved, how many industry trials with biologics started in Europe, the United States, Asia and Latin America, and how EU imports of equipment under heading 8419.89 are moving.
It is written for the people who run marketing or sales at a European supplier of bioprocess equipment or services. These are counts from public sources with the method in plain sight, not a demand forecast.

seccions.titol: All editions
seccions.text: The first in the list is the newest edition. Each one carries the key figure of the month, the charts, the method and the data as CSV and JSON.

seccions.titol: Where the data comes from
seccions.text: Every figure comes from public sources, queried the same way each month. Each edition gives the exact query, the download date and the limits of each source.

seccions.titol: How to use the data
seccions.text:
The data and the charts are under a CC BY 4.0 licence. You can use them in presentations, reports or articles if you credit crida studio and link to this page or to the edition they come from.
A new edition comes out every month, once the sources have published the data for the previous month. This address does not change and the list is always up to date.

faqs.q: How often does Bioprocess Market Watch come out?
faqs.a: Every month. Each edition gathers the public data for the previous month and comes out once the sources have published it.

faqs.q: Are the Market Watch counts demand for bioprocess equipment?
faqs.a: No. They are official records, such as trials that start or medicines that get authorised, and import values from Eurostat. They show where there is activity, but not how much equipment or how many consumables will be bought, or by whom.

faqs.q: Can I use the Market Watch data?
faqs.a: Yes. The data and the charts are under a CC BY 4.0 licence. Credit crida studio and link to this page or to the edition the figures come from.

infografia-3d-arquitectura.intro: In Spanish and Catalan property marketing, an infografía 3D and a render are the same thing. It is a computer-generated image made from a 3D model of the building. The useful question is which piece you need. A street view, an aerial view, an interior, a 3D floor plan, a 360 panorama or a video each answer a different buyer question.

seccions.titol: Are infografía 3D and render the same thing?
seccions.text:
Yes. In Spanish architecture and property sales, both words are used for the same image. Render means calculating the final image from the 3D model, with light and materials. Infografía is the word many Spanish studios and developers use. At crida studio we use both words for the same work.
The confusion comes from a second meaning. Infografía can also be a chart that explains data, like the English infographic. In 2022 TERMCAT, the Catalan terminology centre, published an infografia with the names of data chart types. If you brief a studio in Girona or Barcelona, render and infografía 3D will both be understood.

seccions.titol: What to call it on an English-language property site
seccions.text:
In English, an infographic is a data graphic. The Cambridge Dictionary defines it as a picture or diagram that shows or explains information. If the English page of a Costa Brava development says 3D infographics, a buyer from abroad may expect charts.
In English, write 3D render, architectural visualisation or CGI. The same applies to file names and alt text. Use the words a buyer from Germany, the UK or the Netherlands would actually type into Google in their own language.

seccions.titol: Which images a development can have and what each one is for
seccions.text: Each piece answers a different buyer question. Before asking for a number of images, write down what the development needs to explain. Then pick the pieces that explain it. Three nearly identical exterior views do not say more than one.

seccions.titol: When to commission renders for a development
seccions.text:
Order the final images once the architecture and materials are settled. If the facade or flooring changes after the image is done, it has to be redone, and buyers may already have seen a version that is no longer accurate.
If decisions are still open, start with an untextured massing model. It helps choose camera angles and brief the sales team. The finished images come later, with materials approved by the architect and the developer.
If you want to know what it might cost, the guide to how much a 3D render costs has starting prices and what they depend on.

seccions.titol: What Spanish rules say about property advertising
seccions.text:
Royal Decree 515/1989 governs information in the sale and rental of homes in Spain. Article 2 says advertising must match the real features, conditions and use of the home and always state whether it is under construction or finished. Article 3.2 says advertised details on construction, location, services and installations can be required even if they are not in the contract.
Article 4.2 requires a general site plan and the floor plan of the home to be available to the public. A 3D floor plan helps people read that plan. If an image is made or edited with AI, see our guide on renders, virtual staging and AI.
The second additional provision says the decree applies on a supplementary basis in regions whose statute gives them full powers over consumer protection, except articles 3.2 and 10, which apply across Spain. Before publishing, have the developer's adviser check the text that goes with the images and the regional rules, such as Catalonia's.

seccions.titol: How to publish renders so Google understands them
seccions.text:
Google uses the file name, alt text and page text to work out what an image shows. Its Google Images guidance says so, and recommends short, descriptive file names and placing images near the text about them.
A name like render-final-v3.jpg says nothing. One like penthouse-terrace-girona-new-build.jpg does. Alt text should describe what is visible, for example a penthouse terrace with mountain views. Google supports BMP, GIF, JPEG, PNG, WebP, SVG and AVIF.

faqs.q: Is an infografía 3D more expensive than a render?
faqs.a: No, because they are the same thing. What changes the quote is the number of pieces, whether the 3D model has to be built from scratch, how many finishes need to be shown and how many formats are delivered. When comparing quotes, check which views each one includes and how many rounds of changes.

faqs.q: Can renders be published before the building permit is granted?
faqs.a: This guide cannot answer that, because it depends on each development and the developer's adviser should look at it. What article 2 of Royal Decree 515/1989 does say is that advertising must always state whether the home is under construction or finished.

faqs.q: How many renders does a small development need?
faqs.a: It depends on what needs explaining. As a starting point, one exterior, a living room interior for each unit type and a 3D floor plan of each flat usually cover the essentials. Aerial views and video make more sense when there are shared areas or surroundings worth showing.

faqs.q: What does a 3D studio need to get started?
faqs.a: Floor plans in DWG or PDF with dimensions, elevations, the specification of finishes and approved material references. If the architect has a 3D model, it saves work. It also helps to know where the images will be used, because a website hero and a vertical ad need different framing.

google-ads-negoci-local.intro: Google Ads makes sense for a local business when people already search for what you do, someone can answer the phone and you have a clear page to send them to. If not, fix that first. The rest comes down to limiting ads to the area you serve, choosing who sees them and setting a daily budget you can sustain for the whole month.

seccions.titol: When Google Ads makes sense for a business that serves one area
seccions.text:
It makes sense when customers look for you on Google at the moment they need you. Think of a plumber in la Selva, a dental clinic in Girona or a car repair shop in Cassà. Someone types the service and the town, and wants to call today. Search ads can show up right then, before that person picks who to call.
It also helps when you open a new business and do not rank in organic results yet, or when your season is short and you cannot wait months. SEO and your Google Maps listing are still the foundation. Ads are a way to be visible while that foundation grows, or to push the services you most want to sell.

seccions.titol: When it is better to wait
seccions.text:
Hold off if nobody can pick up the phone or answer forms the same day. You pay for every click, even when the person never gets through to you. It is also a poor idea if the ad lands on the home page of a slow or confusing website, where the visitor cannot find the service they searched for.
Before spending anything, go through these points calmly. If one of them fails, fix it first and run the campaign afterwards. A campaign only sends more people to your website and your phone. If the site does not convince or nobody answers, those clicks are wasted.

seccions.titol: How to limit ads to the area you serve
seccions.text:
Google Ads lets you choose where your ads appear. You can pick a country, areas within a country or a radius around an address. Depending on the country, areas can be regions, cities or postcodes. Google lists the radius option as a fit for local businesses whose customers live near the premises.
The radius has to be at least one kilometre. Google warns that with a very small radius or area your ads may only show now and then, or not at all. So a shop in central Girona can start with a radius that covers the neighbourhoods and towns its customers actually come from, then adjust it once there is data.

seccions.titol: Presence or interest. Who sees your ads
seccions.text:
Google Ads gives you two main options. With presence or interest, the ad reaches people who are in the area and also people who have shown interest in it. Google recommends this for search campaigns. Someone in Barcelona looking for a restaurant in Palamós for the summer could see the ad.
If you only want to reach people who are physically in the area, choose the presence option. That fits a home repair service or an emergency call-out. Google says location is worked out from several signals and is not 100 per cent accurate. If you run ads in English for visitors from abroad, Google advises keeping language and location targeting consistent and writing the ads in English.

seccions.titol: Calls and your address inside the ad
seccions.text:
A local ad can carry your phone number. With call assets, mobile users see a button to call you straight away. You can schedule the number to show only when someone can answer. A tap on that button costs the same as a click on the headline. If you turn on call reporting, Google uses a forwarding number and can count calls as conversions. This only works on the Search Network.
With location assets, the ad can show your address, a map or the approximate distance to your premises. That data comes from Google Maps and your Google Business Profile, which you can link to your Google Ads account. If the profile has the wrong address or phone number, so will the ad. And if you mark the business as closed, those assets stop showing.

seccions.titol: How the daily budget works
seccions.text:
In Google Ads you set an average daily budget for each campaign, and you can change it at any time. On a given day the campaign may spend up to twice that amount when there are more searches. Over the month, though, it will not spend more than 30.4 times the daily budget. If you think in monthly terms, divide that figure by 30.4.
What nobody can tell you in advance is how many enquiries you will get. It depends on how many people search in your area and how many competitors advertise. That is why it pays to track calls and form submissions from the ads from day one, not just clicks.

faqs.q: How much do I need to spend to start with Google Ads?
faqs.a: You choose the average daily budget for each campaign and can change it at any time. Bear in mind that on a single day it can spend up to twice that amount, but over the month it will not exceed 30.4 times the daily budget. The right figure depends on local search volume and how many enquiries you need.

faqs.q: If I already rank well on Google Maps, do I need ads?
faqs.a: Not always. If your listing already brings in enough calls, you may not need them. Ads can help if you want to appear in searches where you do not show up yet, if you launch a new service or if your season is short. You can also link your Business Profile to Google Ads so the ad can show your address and distance.

faqs.q: Can I show ads only when the business is open?
faqs.a: Yes. You can schedule a campaign so ads only run on certain days and at certain hours. The call button can also be scheduled to appear only when someone is available to answer. Bear in mind that with a schedule the campaign still paces towards a monthly spend of 30.4 times the daily budget, however few days it runs.

bio-dades-estructurades-equips-sense-pre.intro: With no published price and no genuine reviews, an equipment page is not eligible for Google's product snippet with stars or price, or for merchant listings. You can still describe the product with its name, description, brand, images and part numbers. Anything that isn't visible on the page stays out of the markup. And never a made-up price, a zero price or ratings you wrote yourself.

seccions.titol: What Google can show for a page with no price
seccions.text:
Google has two kinds of product result. A product snippet is a text result that can add ratings, review details, price and availability. Merchant listings are for pages where the customer can buy the product, and they can show price, availability, shipping or returns. A bioreactor or a TFF system sold on quotation fits neither of them as it stands.
The page can still rank well as a standard result, with a title and a description. Google also points out that correct markup doesn't guarantee any rich result. In the end, what wins the buyer over is what they read once they land on the page.

seccions.titol: What Google requires for a product snippet
seccions.text:
For a product snippet, Google requires the product name (name) plus one of three things, a review (review), an aggregate rating (aggregateRating) or an offer with a price (offers). Without any of the three, Product markup is not eligible for this result. It also only works on pages that focus on a single product or its variants.
Merchant listings ask for more. Only pages where the shopper can buy the product qualify, not pages that link to another site that sells it. You need a name, an image and an offer, and the price must be greater than zero. Google may also try to verify this data before showing it.

seccions.titol: Made-up prices, zero prices and home-made stars
seccions.text: The temptation is to add an indicative price, a zero or a few stars to get the rich result. Google's general guidelines rule that out. Markup has to reflect what is visible on the page and must not mislead. If it doesn't, Google can apply a manual action and the page loses its rich results.

seccions.titol: Which markup fits each type of page
seccions.text: One website usually holds very different pages. Custom equipment is sold through a quotation, single-use consumables often have a price in the online shop and range pages group several models. The table sums up what you can mark up in each case and what not to expect from Google.

seccions.titol: Product ranges, variants and demo videos
seccions.text:
If a model comes in variants, say the same bioreactor in several working volumes, product markup still fits. Google supports pages about a single product or several variants of the same product, including when each variant has its own URL. For merchant listings there are properties that tie each variant to its group, such as isVariantOf and inProductGroupWithID.
On range pages, Google recommends adding markup to individual product pages rather than to pages that list products or categories. On the range page itself, what helps is clear links to each model. If the product page has a demo video, the general guidelines let you mark up the video alongside the product and connect them with @id, so Google knows the video is about that piece of equipment.

seccions.titol: How to check the markup is right
seccions.text: Before rolling it out across the catalogue, test it on a handful of pages. The steps Google suggests are the same for a site with twenty pieces of equipment or a consumables catalogue with hundreds of part numbers.

faqs.q: Can I mark up price on request in structured data?
faqs.a: There is no way to mark it up as a price. Google's Offer requires a price, and merchant listings need it to be greater than zero. If the page shows no price, leave the offer out of the markup and explain on the page how to request a quotation. A made-up price goes against Google's general guidelines.

faqs.q: Is it worth marking up an equipment page if no stars will show?
faqs.a: It depends on the effort. Without a review, rating or offer, Product markup isn't eligible for the product snippet, and Google asks for no special markup for AI answers. If your CMS already outputs it with correct, visible data, you can keep it. If it has to be done by hand, improve the page content first.

faqs.q: Can we show our customers' ratings on the product page?
faqs.a: Yes, if they are genuine and visible on the page with the review text and the score. Google asks you not to mark up fake reviews, incentivised reviews without disclosure or ratings copied from other sites. It recommends accepting only ratings with a comment and the author's name. Stars about the company itself on its own site aren't eligible.

bio-inversio-recerca-farma-europa.intro: According to EFPIA, the pharmaceutical industry invested €56,344 million in R&D in Europe in 2024, more than double the 2010 figure. If you sell lab and bioprocess equipment, or manufacturing capacity, the useful part is where that research happens and where medicines are made. Reading the two tables together helps you choose markets, languages, campaigns and trade shows.

seccions.titol: How much pharma invests in R&D in Europe, according to EFPIA
seccions.text:
Pharmaceutical R&D spending in Europe reached €56,344 million in 2024. These are official figures from EFPIA member associations, covering the EU, Norway, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and a few other countries. In 2010 the figure was €27,920 million, and in 2020 it was €38,736 million. In fourteen years it has more than doubled.
EFPIA puts 2025 at around €60,000 million, but that is its own estimate, so it is left out of the chart. For a supplier the message is simple. European pharma customers spend more on research every year, and part of that budget ends up in labs, pilot plants, clinical trials and outsourced services.
The European Commission report on the 2,000 companies that invest most in R&D worldwide points the same way. In 2024 the health sector worldwide, which covers pharma, biotech and medical technology, spent 13.4% of its sales on R&D, more than any other sector. The 57 EU-based health companies in the ranking invested €46.3 billion, 13% more than the year before.

seccions.titol: Where research happens and where medicines are made
seccions.text:
Research is concentrated in a handful of countries. In 2024 the United Kingdom spent €11,023 million and Germany €10,728 million, both official figures. Switzerland, Belgium and France follow, but with estimates or 2023 data. Production paints a different map. Ireland, Switzerland and Italy top the production table, all three with estimated figures.
That is why there is no country chart here. Many values are estimates or refer to another year, and bars would make them look comparable. The table gives the figures exactly as EFPIA publishes them, with the note for each case.
For the United Kingdom, government data shows the trend. Pharmaceutical R&D performed by businesses was equivalent to 0.33% of GDP in 2024, after 0.35% in 2022 and 0.32% in 2023. In the 2023 comparison of 16 countries with data, only Switzerland, at 1.08% in 2021, and Belgium, at 0.84%, spent a larger share of GDP.

seccions.titol: Research and production may buy different things
seccions.text:
A useful working hypothesis for marketing is that research-heavy countries mostly buy lab and pilot-scale equipment, while production-heavy countries buy GMP capacity. EFPIA does not measure equipment purchases. Treat it as a pointer for setting priorities and check it against your own sales.
Ireland has the highest production in the table, an estimated €87,713 million. Its R&D figure is a 2013 estimate and says little about research there today. If the hypothesis holds, Ireland would matter more to a CDMO or a seller of production systems than to someone selling benchtop bioreactors. Germany and the United Kingdom score high on both and could buy across the whole range.

seccions.titol: What the figures say about Spain
seccions.text:
Spain reported €1,647 million of pharmaceutical R&D in 2024, an official figure. Its production figure, €20,380 million, is from 2023 and is an estimate. With those caveats, production weighs far more than research in Spain, as it does in Italy, while research carries more weight in Germany and the United Kingdom.
For a Spanish or Catalan manufacturer, this may mean manufacturing weighs more than research in the home market. Lab sales may have more room to grow abroad. Check it against your own data before moving any budget.

seccions.titol: How to read these figures without getting them wrong
seccions.text:
The country tables mix official figures, estimates and different years. France and Poland report 2023 R&D, Ireland 2013, and production for the United Kingdom and Spain is from 2023. Use the figures to sort countries into broad groups, not to calculate market shares.
Do not confuse these figures with the equipment market either. R&D includes salaries, clinical trials and services, and production is the value of what is made. They are demand signals. If you need a market size for your product, you need your own analysis built on your sales data and other public sources.

seccions.titol: Where a pharma R&D budget actually goes
seccions.text:
The biggest share goes to clinical trials. EFPIA reproduces the 2025 survey by PhRMA, the association of US pharmaceutical companies, based on 2024 data. Its members spend 44.6% of their R&D on clinical trials, with Phase III alone at 27.4%. Pre-clinical research takes 15%, pharmacovigilance 7.7% and approval 2.7%.
These are US companies, but they give a sense of where the money goes. Our reading is that much of the spending flows through trials, CROs and clinical batch manufacturing, not just research labs. For a CDMO or a pilot-scale equipment supplier, that is a reason to talk about clinical batches and scale-up on your website.
The cycles are long. EFPIA says 12 to 13 years pass between the first synthesis of a substance and the medicine reaching the market, and puts the cost of a new medicine at €3,130 million. The AIHTA report behind that figure points out that published estimates range from $214 million to $6.16 billion depending on the method.

seccions.titol: Europe and China, where pharma research is growing fastest
seccions.text:
In Europe, R&D is growing in money more than in people. According to EFPIA, the industry employed 119,423 people in R&D in Europe in 2024, only slightly more than the 114,283 of 2010. In China, according to the national statistical yearbook cited in the same report, the figure was 202,008 in 2024, up from 55,234 in 2010 and 134,291 in 2020.
For equipment suppliers, that is a reason to keep a close eye on Asia without losing sight of Europe, where the investment in these tables sits. Our bioprocess market observatory counts the industry biologics trials started each month, and in its March 2026 edition Asia was ahead of Europe in every month of the series.

faqs.q: How much does the pharmaceutical industry invest in R&D in Europe?
faqs.a: According to EFPIA, €56,344 million in 2024, based on official figures from its member associations. For 2025, EFPIA estimates around €60,000 million. The series covers the EU, Norway, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and other European countries, and has more than doubled since 2010, when it stood at €27,920 million.

faqs.q: Which European country invests most in pharmaceutical R&D?
faqs.a: In the EFPIA 2024 table, the United Kingdom reports €11,023 million and Germany €10,728 million, both official figures. Switzerland reports €9,553 million, but that is an estimate. Belgium and France come next, also with estimates or 2023 data, so the exact order between them should be read with care.

faqs.q: Can this data be used to size the equipment market?
faqs.a: Not directly. It shows where research and production happen, which helps you rank countries. R&D spending includes salaries, clinical trials and services, and EFPIA does not measure equipment purchases. To size the market for a specific product you need to combine it with your own sales, your contacts and other public sources.

faqs.q: How much does the UK pharmaceutical industry spend on R&D?
faqs.a: According to EFPIA, €11,023 million in 2024, an official figure that puts the UK first in Europe, just ahead of Germany. UK government data shows business pharmaceutical R&D at 0.33% of GDP in 2024, and in 2023 only Switzerland and Belgium spent a larger share of GDP among the 16 countries compared.

faqs.q: What does a pharma company spend its R&D budget on?
faqs.a: Mostly clinical trials. In the PhRMA survey reproduced by EFPIA, US pharmaceutical companies spent 44.6% of their R&D on clinical trials in 2024, and 27.4% on Phase III alone. Pre-clinical research takes 15%, pharmacovigilance 7.7% and approval 2.7%, while 30% is uncategorised.

web-angles-clients-estrangers.intro: An English website for foreign customers has to answer what someone asks when they don't know you or speak your language. Prices, season, how to get there, how to book or get in touch and which languages your staff speak. Start with the pages that sell, have a person review the translation and give each language its own address so Google can find it.

seccions.titol: First, check where your customers come from
seccions.text:
Before translating anything, look at who actually visits you. According to the Costa Brava Girona Tourist Board, in 2025 visitors from Spain, Catalans included, accounted for 41.9% of the nights spent in Costa Brava accommodation. The rest, almost six in ten, were spent by visitors from abroad.
The largest foreign market is France, with 20.0% of nights. Next come the Dutch with 10.1%, Germans with 7.2% and the British with 5.8%. So for many businesses on the coast, French can matter as much as English. Check your bookings, enquiries and analytics before you decide.

seccions.titol: Which pages to translate first
seccions.text:
Translate the pages that lead to a booking or an enquiry first. That means the home page, the page for each service, room or product, prices and conditions, how to get there and contact. The blog and news can wait.
Three well-written pages in English do more than a whole site half translated. If a foreign customer lands on an English page and one click later everything is in Spanish or Catalan, they leave and look somewhere else.

seccions.titol: What a customer from abroad needs to read
seccions.text: A foreign customer doesn't know the town or how things work here. The English version has to answer what a local customer already knows. If they can't find it, they email you with questions or book somewhere else.

seccions.titol: Use machine translation as a first draft
seccions.text:
A machine translation tool or AI is fine to get started, but someone with good English should review the result. Google's spam policies say it doesn't want pages produced at scale through automated transformations such as translating, when they add little value for readers.
Check names of dishes, services and places in particular, because translation tools often change them. And don't mix languages on one page. Google says it works out a page's language from the visible text, not the code, and recommends one language per page, menus included.

seccions.titol: Give each language its own address
seccions.text:
Each language needs its own address, for example an /en/ folder on the same domain. Google recommends separate URLs for each version rather than switching the text with cookies or browser settings, because that way it can find and show every version.
The versions are linked with hreflang tags. Each page must list itself and every other version, and those versions must list it back. If the return link is missing, Google may ignore the tags or misread them.

seccions.titol: How to keep the versions in step
seccions.text:
The usual problem comes after the translation, when the versions drift apart. You change a price or opening hours in Catalan and the English page still shows last year's. Keep a list of the pages with details that change and update them all together whenever you touch one.
Before the season starts, go through the English site as if you were a customer. See whether you can book or send a message without switching language. In Search Console you can filter performance by country and see whether the English pages show up in searches from abroad.

faqs.q: If most of my customers are French, do I need English at all?
faqs.a: It depends on who visits you. On the Costa Brava in 2025, French visitors accounted for 20.0% of nights, while Dutch, German and British visitors together made up 23.1%. A single English version can serve many of them. If your customers are mostly French, it may make sense to start with French.

faqs.q: Can I just add a button that translates the site automatically?
faqs.a: It helps visitors who are already on your site, but it is unlikely to bring you new customers from Google. If the text changes without a separate address for each language, Google may not find those versions. An /en/ folder with reviewed text can appear in English-language searches.

faqs.q: Do I need a separate domain for English?
faqs.a: No. An /en/ folder on the same domain is easy to set up and maintain, according to Google, because everything stays on the same host. Google says country domains such as .fr or .de send a strong signal about which country a site targets, which suits a business that works for a single country.

bio-bioregio-catalunya-2025-proveidors.intro: Biocat's 2025 BioRegion of Catalonia Report, presented on 19 February 2026, counts 1,650 companies and 94 research institutions. Investment in health startups and scaleups hit a record €517 million in 2025. If you sell equipment, consumables or services, the useful reading is who buys, with what money and when, so you can adjust your messaging, website and calendar.

seccions.titol: Who makes up the BioRegion of Catalonia in 2025
seccions.text:
The BioRegion of Catalonia has 1,650 companies in 2025, up 8.3% on the previous year, plus 94 research institutions. 90% of the companies are SMEs and 93.4% are in Barcelona. More are setting up outside the metropolitan area, mainly in Girona. According to Biocat's company map of December 2025, Girona already hosts nearly 3% of them.
Biocat's ecosystem map splits the companies by subsector. There are 423 biotech companies, 259 in digital health, 238 in medtech and 130 in pharma. It also counts 279 professional services and consulting firms, 81 investors and 240 suppliers. Those 240 may be your competitors or your partners, so find out who they are before you enter.
What does this mean for marketing? If nine in ten companies are SMEs, many of your buyers will be small firms with few decision makers and a tight budget. With buyers like these, a demo or a good conversation at a trade show can count as much as a campaign.

seccions.titol: A record €517 million for health startups and scaleups
seccions.text:
Investment in Catalan health startups and scaleups reached €517 million in 2025, up 43% on 2024 and 7% above the previous peak in 2022. Biotech raised €347 million, 68% of the total. Medtech took €92 million and digital health €71 million.
Venture capital contributed €327.6 million across 38 deals, the lowest deal count in recent years. The top five rounds make up 47% of the total. So fewer companies have fresh money, but the rounds are bigger. Competitive public grants also hit a record, at €124.3 million.
A startup that closes a round may use it to move from the lab to a pilot plant. If it does, it will need bioreactors, purification systems, consumables or CDMO capacity. Follow funding news from Biocat and the investors. That way your message can land while the company is planning the purchase, before it picks a supplier.

seccions.titol: Research centres and clinical trials buy differently
seccions.text:
Catalonia has 5,768 active clinical trials in 2025, 92% of the activity in Spain, and Biocat ranks it fourth in Europe for active trials. The clinical pipeline holds 71 assets in development, 51 molecules and 20 advanced therapies, almost double the 2020 figure. That can mean work for CROs, CDMOs, testing labs and consumables suppliers.
A research centre does not buy the way a company does. It may pay from a project budget tied to a grant call, and the end user is the research group. So it pays to have complete technical datasheets, scientific references and paperwork ready to help them justify the purchase.

seccions.titol: A different message for each type of buyer
seccions.text:
With these figures, we suggest splitting your marketing plan into at least four groups. Each one has a different question in mind and needs its own page, its own emails and its own arguments. That way you stop talking to everyone the same way.
Catalonia also exported €9.165 billion worth of life sciences and healthcare products in 2024, 45.7% of Spain's total. The top destinations are Switzerland, Germany, France and the United States. If one of your customers exports to those markets, expect them to ask for supplier documentation that meets international standards.

seccions.titol: A website in three languages and a presence at events
seccions.text:
If you want to sell in Catalonia, a website in Catalan, Spanish and English helps. 82% of the venture capital raised in 2025 involved international investors, and English is the norm in many research and startup teams. With SMEs and plants, on the other hand, sales and service may work better in Catalan or Spanish.
Trade shows and sector events are where relationships are built. Biocat presented its 2025 report on 19 February 2026 to a record turnout. BioSpain and Farmaforum attract different audiences, as our guide to the two shows explains. Prepare a message for each segment before you go and follow up with your contacts the week after.

seccions.titol: What each figure in the report actually counts
seccions.text:
The report covers the whole life sciences and healthcare sector, not just biotech. The 1,650 companies include service firms, consultancies, investors and suppliers. Before you work out how many potential customers you have, filter for your subsector. Our market analysis guide compares this figure with AseBio's.
The €517 million includes venture capital, competitive grants, venture debt, stock market funding and crowdequity, raised by startups and scaleups. As for exports, 91% are pharmaceutical products, so the figure says little about lab equipment. Biocat notes that company creation figures for the last two years are provisional. Always quote each figure with its year and what it covers.

faqs.q: How many life sciences companies are there in Catalonia?
faqs.a: According to Biocat's 2025 BioRegion of Catalonia Report, 1,650 companies, up 8.3% on the previous year, plus 94 research institutions. 90% are SMEs and 93.4% are in Barcelona. The figure includes service firms, consultancies, investors and suppliers. 423 of them are biotech companies.

faqs.q: How much was invested in Catalan health startups in 2025?
faqs.a: Biocat counts €517 million in 2025 for health startups and scaleups, a record. Biotech raised €347 million, medtech €92 million and digital health €71 million. Venture capital put in €327.6 million across 38 deals, and the five largest rounds account for 47% of the total.

faqs.q: Do I need a Catalan-language website to sell to the sector in Catalonia?
faqs.a: It is not mandatory, but it helps. Research teams and startups work a lot in English, and 82% of the venture capital raised in 2025 involved international investors. With SMEs and plants, service and procurement may work better in Catalan or Spanish. A website in all three languages covers both cases.

bio-publicacions-que-citen-equip.intro: Search your brand and model names in Europe PMC, which searches the full text, then fill the gaps with PubMed and Google Scholar. For each paper, record the journal, year, DOI and what the equipment was used for. Then group them by application on a publications page, put two or three on each product page and link them by DOI, without presenting them as an endorsement.

seccions.titol: Where to find the papers that use your equipment
seccions.text:
Start with Europe PMC, because it searches inside the full text and not just the abstract. Its REST API gives access to 10.2 million full text articles and lets you search by field. One of those fields covers the methods section (METHODS), which is where authors say which bioreactor or TFF system they used.
PubMed works differently. Its Text Words field [tw] covers the title, abstract, MeSH terms and other record data, but not the full text. You will only find papers that name your brand in the title or abstract. Google Scholar indexes papers from most major publishers and repositories worldwide, free and paywalled, and helps you pick up what the others miss.

seccions.titol: What to record for each paper
seccions.text: Start a spreadsheet with the very first paper, and read the methods passage before you log it, because the name sometimes belongs to another company. Once you have fifty papers you will want to filter by application or scale. These columns help most.

seccions.titol: How to link a paper and what you may copy
seccions.text:
Link each paper by its DOI, not by the journal's URL. Crossref recommends this because, if the journal moves, the publisher updates the record and the link keeps working. Show the DOI as a full link with https and doi.org, without a doi prefix in front and without dx in the domain.
Title, journal, year and link is the safe option. Copying the PDF, a figure or a long passage depends on each article's licence, which you will find on the journal page. Under CC BY 4.0 you may reuse the material, commercially too, as long as you credit the author, link to the licence and say whether you changed anything.
The licence also says you may not suggest the rights holder endorses you. If the article carries another licence, or none is stated, link to it and describe it in your own words. Do not copy figures without permission.

seccions.titol: Two or three papers on each product page
seccions.text:
On each model's page, pick two or three papers that match what visitors are looking for. Recent ones in well known journals of the field, covering different applications, work best. Place them near the specifications, with title, journal, year and DOI link, and add a link to the full publications page.
If the model is new and has no papers yet, do not borrow another model's citations as if they were its own. You can link papers for the product range and say clearly which unit was used. Anyone who reads the paper can check.

seccions.titol: What you cannot claim from a paper that cites you
seccions.text: A research group naming your equipment in its methods means they used it. It does not mean they recommend it or that their university backs your brand. Say exactly that, with wording such as “used in” or “cited in”.

seccions.titol: How to keep the list up to date every month
seccions.text:
Save your searches and review them once a month. In PubMed you can create an email alert with the button under the search bar, if you have a My NCBI account, or set up an RSS feed. In Google Scholar, the envelope icon on the results page creates an alert that emails you new papers.
With the Europe PMC API, someone on your team can save one query per brand and model and sort it by publication date with the sort_date option. Results come back as JSON or XML. Always check each new paper by hand before you publish it.

faqs.q: Do I need the author's permission to list their paper on our site?
faqs.a: Citing it with title, journal, year and DOI link copies none of its content, it just points readers to it. Reusing figures, tables or the PDF depends on the licence. Under CC BY 4.0 you can, as long as you credit the author, link to the licence and note any changes. If there is no open licence, ask the journal.

faqs.q: PubMed does not find our equipment. Does that mean nobody uses it?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. In PubMed, the Text Words field covers the title, abstract and other record data, but not the methods section. Equipment is often named only in the methods. Run the same search in Europe PMC restricted to methods, and in Google Scholar, before drawing any conclusion.

faqs.q: Can we ask customers to cite us in their papers?
faqs.a: You can make it easy for them. Publish the exact company and model names the way you want them to appear, and include them in the documentation that ships with the equipment. Authors then spell them correctly and you find the papers faster. What makes no sense is asking a paper to say anything the authors have not tested.

n8n-make-zapier-pime.intro: If you want to automate a few steps between well known apps and nobody on your team writes code, Zapier is usually the easiest way to start. If your workflows branch and depend on conditions, Make tends to fit well. If volume grows or you want the data on your own server, n8n can pay off, as long as someone looks after it. The deciding factor is what each tool counts when it bills you.

seccions.titol: What each tool counts when it bills you
seccions.text:
All three charge by usage, but each one counts something different. Zapier counts tasks. Its help centre says that in Classic Zaps a task is any action that runs successfully, while triggers and filters do not count. A form that creates a CRM contact and emails you uses two tasks. From 1 December 2026, every successful run of a Next Gen Zap uses at least one task.
Make counts credits. Its help centre explains that by default one module operation equals one credit, and that only things triggered by a scenario run use credits. Some more complex modules use more than one credit per operation, two or ten for example. Many AI modules use credits based on the tokens they consume.
n8n counts executions. Its pricing page, as of November 2026, says an execution is one full run of the workflow, however many steps it has. The same form with a CRM entry and an email is a single execution. For long workflows that run many times a day, this way of counting changes the numbers a lot.

seccions.titol: Where your customers' data ends up
seccions.text:
If you automate quotes or customer records, personal data flows through the tool and you need to know where it is stored. n8n says on its pricing page that on its hosted plans data is stored in the EU, on servers in Frankfurt. If you install it on your own server, the data stays wherever you decide.
Make lets you pick the data centre when you create your organisation, either the United States or the European Union, and its help centre warns that you cannot change it later. Get it right on day one. For Zapier, the sources we cite do not say, so ask where data is stored before you send customer information through it.

seccions.titol: Who keeps the automations running
seccions.text:
Zapier and Make run in their own cloud, and the vendor looks after the servers and updates. You only maintain the workflows. With n8n you have two options. You can use n8n Cloud, which works the same way, or install the Community Edition on a server you own or rent.
The Community Edition is used under the Sustainable Use License. According to the n8n docs, it lets you use and modify the software for your own internal business purposes or for non commercial use. For a small business automating its own work, that fits. Reselling it to others as a service needs a separate agreement with n8n.
Self hosting does not mean free. You pay for the server, and someone has to install updates, run backups and check what happened when a workflow fails on a Saturday. If nobody in the company can do that, count those hours as a cost or hand the maintenance to someone who can.

seccions.titol: How each tool is built and what it connects to
seccions.text:
Zapier is built as a list of steps, one after another, and is usually the simplest to get started with. Make draws the workflow as a diagram with branches. That helps when there are conditions, such as sending a quote to one sales rep or another depending on the area. n8n is visual too, but if you host it yourself you need to know how to run a server.
Before you choose, check that your apps are supported. Look at your CRM, booking or appointment software, email, spreadsheets and WhatsApp Business. For n8n, the pricing page says every plan includes every integration. If an app has no connector but does have an API, you will need someone who can connect it.

seccions.titol: n8n, Make and Zapier side by side
seccions.text: The table sums up what each vendor's official documentation says as of November 2026. We leave prices out because they change often and depend on each company's volume. Open each pricing page with your own count of runs and steps in hand, and work out the numbers for your case.

seccions.titol: What to prepare before you choose
seccions.text: The decision almost makes itself once three things are clear. How often the process happens, which apps it touches and who will deal with it when it breaks. Run the count on one real process, such as quote requests at a clinic in Girona or bookings at a restaurant on the Costa Brava.

faqs.q: Is n8n free?
faqs.a: The n8n Community Edition has no licence fee if you install it on your own server and use it for your company's internal work. What you pay for is the server and the hours of whoever updates and monitors it. n8n Cloud is a paid service and bills by the number of workflow executions each month.

faqs.q: Which one is cheapest for a small business?
faqs.a: It depends on volume and number of steps. For a few short workflows, any of the three can work out fine. When a workflow has many steps and runs often, counting one execution per run, as n8n does, can work out cheaper. Count your own process and check each tool's current prices.

faqs.q: Can I move from Zapier or Make to n8n later?
faqs.a: Yes, but you will have to rebuild the workflows, because each tool stores them its own way. That is why it helps to write down what each workflow does, which apps it touches and what data it moves. With that list, switching is a configuration job and the process is already worked out.

faqs.q: Can these tools send WhatsApp notifications?
faqs.a: It depends on the connector and on how you use WhatsApp. Before you build anything, check whether the tool you pick has a WhatsApp Business connector and what it lets you do. The phone app and the API are not meant for the same things. Our guide on the WhatsApp Business app versus the API explains the differences and how to choose.

bio-biosimilars-autoritzats-ema.intro: The EMA's public medicines file lists 153 authorised biosimilars for human use, based on our download of 22 November 2026. They cover 27 molecules and 41 different holders. 44 of 153 were authorised in 2025, and 26 of those are denosumab. If you sell equipment, consumables or manufacturing services, this is a public list of potential customers and of the molecules where things are moving.

seccions.titol: How many biosimilars the EMA has authorised and who holds them
seccions.text:
The EMA's public medicines file shows 153 biosimilars for human use with the status authorised. They cover 27 different active substances and 41 marketing authorisation holders. In the EMA's words, a biosimilar is a biological medicine highly similar to another one already approved in the EU, known as the reference medicine.
The file also keeps the ones that left or never made it. There are 22 withdrawn biosimilars, 14 withdrawn applications, 2 refused and 1 lapsed. Another 6 have the status opinion, meaning the EMA's scientific committee has given an opinion but they are not yet listed as authorised.
For a supplier, every holder is a potential account. Behind each authorisation is a biological medicine made from living cells or organisms, in the holder's own plant or at a CDMO. The holder is not always the manufacturer, but it is the first name to look at.

seccions.titol: How many biosimilars were authorised each year
seccions.text:
2025 is the year with the most biosimilars still authorised today. There were 44, more than double the 17 from 2024. 2026 already has 14 up to 22 November. Adding up the three years, 75 of the 153 have an authorisation date from 2024 onwards.
Before that, the peak came in 2017 and 2018, with 11 and 14. Between 2019 and 2023 there are 4 to 8 a year. Only medicines that are authorised today count here. Withdrawn ones are left out, so the older years look smaller than what was actually approved.

seccions.titol: Which molecules have the most authorised biosimilars
seccions.text:
Denosumab is the molecule with the most authorised biosimilars, with 30. Next come aflibercept and pegfilgrastim with 12 each, ustekinumab with 11 and adalimumab with 10. Trastuzumab, bevacizumab and ranibizumab have 8 each. The other 19 molecules have 7 or fewer.
The 2025 jump has clear names behind it. Of the 44 biosimilars authorised that year, 26 are denosumab and 8 are aflibercept. For denosumab, 26 of its 30 authorised biosimilars date from 2025. In this molecule, most competitors arrived in the same year.
Of the 6 files with the status opinion, 2 are insulin aspart and there is 1 each for ranibizumab, filgrastim, omalizumab and pertuzumab. Omalizumab and pertuzumab have only 1 authorised biosimilar each today. For these two molecules, only a few companies have reached this stage.

seccions.titol: Why biosimilars arrive in waves
seccions.text:
Authorisations follow the timeline of the reference medicine. The EMA explains that a biosimilar can only be authorised once the data exclusivity period of the reference medicine has expired. In general, the reference medicine must have been authorised for at least eight years before another company can apply for approval of a biosimilar.
For marketing, that buys you time. Before authorisation, the EMA requires comparative quality, non-clinical and clinical studies. We have no data on when each company buys. But those studies need a working production process, so our reading is that much of the process buying happens earlier. If you wait for the approval news, you may be late.
So it pays to watch two things. Holders that already have authorised biosimilars know the route and can run it again with another molecule. Files with the status opinion show which biosimilars are about to arrive, and for which molecules.

seccions.titol: How to use this list in your marketing
seccions.text:
The EMA list is public, free and easy to filter in a spreadsheet. With the filters in this guide, your marketing team gets an account base sorted by molecule and date that it can share with sales.
This is where we work with suppliers in the sector. We help turn public data like this into account lists, messaging and web content for each type of buyer, without promising results that depend on each market.

seccions.titol: How we counted and what the data does not say
seccions.text:
We downloaded the file Medicines output, medicines report from the EMA's Download medicine data page. The EMA generated it on 22 November 2026 at 6 pm and we downloaded it the same day. We kept the rows with category Human and Biosimilar Yes. That gives 198 rows, and 153 have the status Authorised.
We counted holders without regard to upper or lower case. For the yearly count we used the marketing authorisation date. Two authorised medicines, Pavblu and Nylaspeg, have no such date in the file and are left out of the yearly count, which therefore adds up to 151.
There are limits. The EMA itself says it evaluates the majority of biosimilar applications in the EU, not all of them. We count authorisations, not sales or production volume. One molecule can have several brand names from the same holder.

faqs.q: What is a biosimilar according to the EMA?
faqs.a: For the EMA, a biosimilar is a biological medicine highly similar to another one already approved in the EU in structure, biological activity, efficacy, safety and immunogenicity. It is not treated as a generic, because the natural variability and more complex manufacturing of biologics do not allow an exact copy. The EU approved its first biosimilar in 2006.

faqs.q: When can a biosimilar of a given molecule be authorised?
faqs.a: According to the EMA, once the data exclusivity period of the reference medicine has expired. In general, the reference medicine must have been authorised for at least eight years before another company can apply. For a specific molecule you need to check its own documents, and patents are a separate question that this guide does not cover.

faqs.q: Can a biosimilar be used instead of the reference medicine?
faqs.a: The EMA and the Heads of Medicines Agencies (HMA) state that biosimilars approved in the EU are interchangeable from a scientific viewpoint, including between biosimilars of the same reference. Each member state decides whether pharmacies can substitute automatically. So one molecule can have the reference medicine and several biosimilars on the market side by side, as the counts in this guide show.

bio-escriure-web-per-a-cientifics.intro: Put the evidence right next to every claim, meaning the number with its unit, the test conditions and a link to the application note or protocol. Cut brochure words like revolutionary or market-leading, use the technical terms your readers search for and show who wrote the page. Scientists read fast and distrust anything they cannot check.

seccions.titol: Why scientists distrust supplier copy
seccions.text:
A scientist reads a supplier website the way they read a paper. They look for the data, check the conditions behind it and ask whether they could reproduce it. When they find adjectives instead of data, they assume there is none and stop reading.
They do not want harder text either. The GOV.UK style guidance asks for plain English for specialists too. It cites research on legal language where 80 % of people preferred sentences in clear English, and the more complex the issue, the stronger that preference. The more educated and specialist the reader, the more they preferred plain English. Specialists can follow complex language, but they would rather not read it if there is an alternative.

seccions.titol: Every claim with its evidence beside it
seccions.text:
Whenever the site says a system does something well, the data and where it comes from should sit right next to it. Seamless scale-up says nothing. A credible sentence says which working volume you moved from and to, with which cell line and which scale-up criterion you kept constant, such as kLa or power per volume.
Then add the link. If the figure comes from an application note, link to it. If it comes from a paper, give the DOI. If it is an internal test, say so and describe the method. For a CDMO, experience in monoclonal antibodies carries less weight than saying which steps you run, at what scale and on which equipment.

seccions.titol: How to write units and numbers
seccions.text:
A badly written unit stands out at once and suggests nobody from the lab checked the text. The NIST checklist, from the US national metrology institute, sets out the basic rules of the International System of Units. Leave a space between the number and the symbol, even when the value is used as an adjective. Symbols take no plural and no full stop, and abbreviations such as cc or sec are not used.
In a range, each value carries its unit, or both go in brackets with the unit at the end. English uses a decimal point, while Spanish and Catalan use a comma. Pick one format per language and use it the same way on the website and in the PDFs. The NIST checklist is meant for reviewing scientific manuscripts. If the label or an approved document already says 2-8 °C, copy it exactly on the website so everything matches.

seccions.titol: Who wrote it and how it was tested
seccions.text:
Google's guidance on helpful content suggests asking who created each page, how and why. It asks whether authorship is clear, whether pages carry a byline where readers would expect one and whether it leads to more about the author. On an equipment maker's site, that means signing application notes with the name and role of the application specialist or process engineer.
It also helps to explain how the test was run. Google uses product reviews as an example, where it helps to say how many products were tested, what the results were and how. And never invent authors. Google says fabricating creator profiles, with AI-generated headshots, made-up names or false credentials, is deception and makes a page untrustworthy.

seccions.titol: How to review a page before it goes live
seccions.text: Before publishing, have someone from the lab or the applications team read the text, not just marketing. Ask them to flag every sentence they could not defend if a customer asked for the data. Those sentences either get their evidence or get cut. GOV.UK also recommends splitting sentences over 25 words and using the active voice.

faqs.q: If I write more plainly, will scientists think it is not technical enough?
faqs.a: Not if the data is there. GOV.UK cites research on legal documents where the more educated and specialist the reader, the more they preferred plain English. Copy looks non-technical when it gives no figures and no test conditions, whatever the sentence length.

faqs.q: Can we publish data before we have an application note?
