faqs.a: Yes, as long as you say where it comes from. Explain that it is an internal test, the conditions and the result. If you do not have enough data yet, saying nothing beats a figure with no context. Once the application note exists, link to it from the same sentence.

faqs.q: Who should sign the technical content on our website?
faqs.a: The person who can answer questions about it, usually the application specialist, the process engineer or the product manager. Google recommends bylines where readers would expect them, leading to more information about the author, such as a page with their background and experience.

seo-allotjaments-turistics.intro: SEO for a hotel, campsite or holiday rental happens in two places. One is your Google Business Profile, which is what shows on Maps, and the other is your website, where people book. Check that the profile follows Google's rules, that every room, pitch or house type has its own page, that each language has its own URL and that your booking engine feeds Google's free booking links.

seccions.titol: Where guests look for you before they book
seccions.text:
People looking for somewhere to stay usually search by place and type, such as "campsite near L'Escala" or "holiday cottage in the Garrotxa". Others search for the name of a property they saw on a booking platform. In the first case local search and Google Maps matter most. In the second, you want your own website to show up and take the booking without detours.
So before you think about a blog, make sure Google understands what you are and where you are, that your website answers what guests ask, and that booking direct is easy to find and to finish on a phone.

seccions.titol: Your Google Business Profile and the rules for lodging
seccions.text:
Your Google Business Profile is what appears on Maps and next to the search results, and it is often the first thing a guest sees. Google's guidelines say the name must reflect your real-world name and do not allow unnecessary information. Use the name on your sign, without the town or "with pool" tacked on.
Two rules apply directly to lodging. Google says hotels and motels should not list opening hours. And if there is a restaurant or bar inside the hotel, it should have its own profile, and the hotel should not add "restaurant" as a category. Our Business Profile guide explains how to create and verify one.

seccions.titol: Google's free booking links
seccions.text:
When someone searches for a hotel, Google can show a link to your own booking site with your property's name and the rate for their dates. Google Hotel Center help says these links are unpaid and ranked by how useful they are to users. Hotel Ads, by contrast, are paid.
Google says that if you use a reservation system, you may already be connected through your provider, and they can set the links up for you. Ask the company behind your booking engine. Then check the page the click lands on, because landing page experience is one of the signals Google uses to rank the links. If it opens in the wrong language or without the dates guests picked, they have to start again.

seccions.titol: One page for each room, pitch or house type
seccions.text:
If everything you offer sits on a single Rooms page, Google has nowhere to send someone looking for something specific, like a dog-friendly bungalow or a family room. Each room type, pitch, bungalow or house needs its own page with photos, capacity, what is included and a button to book that option.
Put the answers to what guests ask before booking on the website too. How to get there without a car, where to park, whether dogs are allowed, check-in and check-out times and what is nearby. If you already answer these by email or WhatsApp, use the words your guests use.

seccions.titol: One URL per language, with the whole page in that language
seccions.text:
If you host guests from abroad, each language needs its own URL and text written in that language. Google recommends marking up the versions with hreflang so each user reaches the right one, and says each language version must list itself as well as all the others.
Google also points out that it does not use hreflang or the HTML lang attribute to detect a page's language. It relies on its own algorithms instead. So each version should be fully in its language, including the menu, buttons and booking engine. Our guide on English websites for foreign customers goes into more detail.

seccions.titol: What to tell Google with structured data
seccions.text:
Structured data is code guests never see that tells Google what a page is about. Google asks you to use the most specific local business type possible, and schema.org has lodging types such as Hotel, Campground, BedAndBreakfast, Hostel and VacationRental. In our study of 675 accommodation websites in the Girona area, only 103 had lodging structured data on their home page.
Before adding star ratings, check what Google says about aggregate ratings. It only recommends them for sites that collect reviews about other local businesses, not for marking up your own property's reviews. The reviews worth working on are those on your Business Profile, which our reviews guide covers.

seccions.titol: Where to start if you only have an afternoon
seccions.text: Run through this check in this order. You can do it yourself with a phone and a laptop, without paid tools, and it will show you where the biggest problem is, on the profile or on the website.

faqs.q: Can I put "hotel in Roses" in my Google Business Profile name?
faqs.a: Only if that is what your business is called on your sign and website. Google does not allow unnecessary information in the name, such as location or services. The town goes in the address, and the type of property and amenities go in the category and description.

faqs.q: Can a small holiday rental appear in Google's free booking links?
faqs.a: Google's help talks about hotels and booking partners, and points those without a Hotel Center account to a starter guide. The practical step is to ask your booking engine provider whether they offer a Google connection. If your website has no booking engine yet, that comes first.

faqs.q: What structured data should a campsite website have?
faqs.a: The schema.org Campground type, which is the most specific one for a campsite. Google lists name and address as required for a local business and recommends adding phone number, coordinates and website URL. Then check it with Google's Rich Results Test.

bio-annex-22-ia-gmp.intro: Annex 22 is a European Commission draft that proposes how AI models used in critical GMP applications should be tested and controlled. The consultation closed on 7 October 2025, and as of 11 November 2026 no final text has been published. If your equipment or software uses AI, our advice is that your website and datasheets explain what the model does, what it decides and who checks the result.

seccions.titol: What Annex 22 is and where it stands
seccions.text:
Annex 22 is a new annex to the EU GMP guidelines covering artificial intelligence. The European Commission put it out for consultation from 7 July to 7 October 2025, together with a revised Chapter 4 on documentation and a revised Annex 11 on computerised systems. It was drafted by the EMA GMDP Inspectors Working Group in cooperation with PIC/S.
On the EudraLex Volume 4 page, checked on 11 November 2026, the Annex 11 in force is still the January 2011 version and Annex 22 is not listed. It is a draft and may change. So our advice is not to describe your equipment as Annex 22 compliant or certified. There is no final text yet to measure it against.

seccions.titol: Which AI the draft covers and which it leaves out
seccions.text:
Under section 1, the annex applies to machine learning models used in critical applications, meaning those with a direct impact on patient safety, product quality or data integrity. It only covers static models, which do not change while in use, and deterministic ones, which always give the same output for the same input.
Models that keep learning during use, and models that can give different outputs for identical inputs, should not be used in critical GMP applications. Nor should generative AI or large language models. If they are used in non-critical GMP applications, qualified staff should always be responsible for making sure the output is suitable. The text calls this human-in-the-loop.
In 2023 the FDA published a discussion paper, explicitly not guidance, listing possible uses in drug manufacturing. They include process design and scale-up, advanced process control, process monitoring and fault detection, vision-based inspection of packaging, labels and vials, and trend monitoring of deviation reports.

seccions.titol: What your customer's QA team will ask
seccions.text: Section 2.2 says the regulated user should have access to the model documentation and review it, even when a supplier trained and tested the model. The list sums up what the draft asks for. Our reading is that your customer's QA team will raise these points, so your website and datasheet should already answer them.

seccions.titol: What to put on your website, datasheet and demo
seccions.text:
We suggest leading with the intended use in one plain sentence. For example, the vision system sorts vials into pass or review, or the model flags when a process parameter starts trending away from normal. Then say what the model decides and what the operator decides, and whether the model is static or gets updated.
State what documentation you hand over and how model updates are handled. Under section 10.1, any change to the model, the system or the process should be documented and assessed to decide whether the model needs retesting.
Keep R&D messaging apart from GMP production messaging. In a development lab, a model that suggests scale-up parameters can be sold on speed. In a GMP plant, the same claim needs the intended use, the limits and the human review alongside it.

seccions.titol: Phrases to avoid and what to say instead
seccions.text:
Some words that work well in a tech campaign make a pharma buyer wary. The table is our own suggestion and does not come from the annex. It lists the most common ones, with an alternative that makes the same point without promising more than your documents can back up.
The same goes for demos. Show a case where the model is unsure and how the operator sees it. That way the buyer sees the confidence threshold at work, which the draft covers in section 9.2.

seccions.titol: Where a generative AI assistant fits
seccions.text:
A generative AI chatbot should not be marketed as a GMP tool, because the draft says these models should not be used in critical applications. It can help with non-critical work, such as searching an instrument's technical documentation, as long as a person reviews the output.
If you offer one, say on your website what it is for and what it is not for. Our guide to AI assistants for technical documentation covers how to scope it. Also look at the draft revised Annex 11, which the consultation page says reinforces supplier oversight, data integrity, audit trails, electronic signatures and security.

seccions.titol: Annex 11 vs Annex 22, what is the difference
seccions.text:
Annex 11 applies to every computerised system used to manufacture medicinal products and active substances, while Annex 22 only covers AI models used in critical applications within those systems. Section 1 of Annex 22 says so plainly. It provides additional guidance to Annex 11 for systems with an embedded AI model, so AI-enabled equipment would fall under both.
The size of the texts differs too. The draft revised Annex 11 runs to 19 pages and 17 sections, from lifecycle and risk management to audit trails, electronic signatures, security, backup and archiving. The Annex 22 draft has 6 pages and 10 sections focused on testing the model, from intended use and test data to explainability and confidence.
Both share one idea. Annex 11 says that when a system replaces a manual operation or another system, the overall risk of the process should not increase. Annex 22 asks that the model performs at least as well as the process it replaces. For marketing the lesson is the same. You need to know how the old process performed and show it with data.

seccions.titol: What the revised Annex 11 changes for equipment and software suppliers
seccions.text:
The draft revised Annex 11 gives section 7 to suppliers and service providers. If a customer relies on the vendor’s qualification of a system, it should run an audit or a thorough assessment according to risk, and the documentation must be accessible and explainable from its own site. The customer stays fully responsible.
Section 7.5 lists what the contract should cover when a service provider qualifies or operates the system. Among other points, it includes support during inspections, how quality and security issues are reported, an exit strategy so the customer keeps control of its data, and how new versions are released and whether the customer can test them first.
On your website, that means concrete answers. Say whether you accept audits, what qualification documentation you hand over, how you announce new versions and how a customer gets its data back if it changes systems. Our guide on how to show GMP and Part 11 on your website covers how to say this without promising more than you can prove.

faqs.q: Is EU GMP Annex 22 mandatory yet?
faqs.a: No. It is a draft that went out for public consultation from 7 July to 7 October 2025. As of 11 November 2026, the EudraLex Volume 4 page still does not list it and keeps the 2011 Annex 11. The text may change, so no equipment can be presented as compliant.

faqs.q: Can ChatGPT or another LLM be used in a GMP plant?
faqs.a: According to the draft, generative AI and large language models should not be used in critical GMP applications, those with a direct impact on patient safety, product quality or data integrity. If they are used for non-critical tasks, qualified staff should always be responsible for making sure the output is suitable.

faqs.q: What should a supplier of AI-enabled equipment hand over?
faqs.a: Section 2.2 says the regulated user, your customer, should have and review the model documentation even if the supplier did the testing. The draft asks for documented intended use (3.1), acceptance criteria (4.2), a test plan (7.2) and change control (10.1). If you have this ready, say so on your website.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Annex 11 and Annex 22?
faqs.a: Annex 11 covers every computerised system used in GMP manufacturing, and the version in force dates from 2011. Annex 22 is a new draft that adds requirements only for AI models in critical applications, with a focus on testing them. AI-enabled equipment would need to consider both, and both revised texts are still drafts.

bio-youtube-fabricants-equips.intro: Buyers of lab and bioprocess equipment go to YouTube for videos that answer one specific technical question. How the equipment is set up, how it is cleaned, how it scales and which applications it suits. To get those videos found, give each one a title built on search terms, chapters, subtitles in your markets' languages and its own page on your website.

seccions.titol: Is a YouTube channel worth it for an equipment manufacturer?
seccions.text:
It is worth it if you treat it as a library of technical answers. Nobody buying bioprocess equipment subscribes for entertainment. They land on a video from a specific search, on YouTube or Google, when they want to see how a system is assembled or how a consumable is swapped. The channel stores those videos and keeps them in order.
YouTube hosts the video and you embed it on your site without dealing with servers or file formats. What it will not do on its own is bring in viewers. Views come from the title, the description and the page you give it on your website, and that is where the work goes.

seccions.titol: The videos technical buyers actually search for
seccions.text: The videos that work answer a question someone types into a search box before asking for a quote. You can find those questions in sales calls, service tickets and Search Console queries. These five formats cover much of what a process engineer or lab manager wants to know.

seccions.titol: Titles, descriptions and chapters in the words engineers use
seccions.text:
Put the words an engineer would type in the title, such as the equipment type, the task and the scale, rather than the internal model name. «How to change the bag on a 50 litre single-use bioreactor» gets found. «Introducing our new model» only interests people who already know you. Use the description to say in two or three sentences what the video shows, and link to the product page.
Chapters come from timestamps in the description. According to YouTube Help, the first one must start at zero, you need at least three in ascending order and each chapter must last at least ten seconds. Automatic chapters are switched on by default for new uploads, but not every video is eligible. If you add your own, they override the automatic ones.
Label each chapter with search terms, such as «connecting the permeate line» or «filter integrity test». Google's video guidance says that for YouTube videos it can show key moments based on the timestamps and labels in the description, and that it gives priority to key moments you set yourself.

seccions.titol: Subtitles in the languages of your markets
seccions.text:
If you sell into Germany, Scandinavia or Asia, your videos should carry subtitles in those languages. YouTube points out that subtitles and captions help you reach deaf or hard of hearing viewers and people who speak another language.
You add subtitles in YouTube Studio through the add language option. You can upload a file with or without timing, or use auto-sync, which lines a transcript up with the video. The transcript has to be in the spoken language, and YouTube does not recommend it for videos over an hour long or with poor audio. Automatic captions are only available in the video's default language.

seccions.titol: Playlists by product line and by application
seccions.text: Organise the channel into playlists that match the way buyers search. Create one playlist per product line, such as bioreactors, TFF systems or consumables, and another per application, such as cell therapy or fermentation. That way, someone who arrives through one clip finds the next without going back to search. Use the same product line and application names as on your website and in your catalogue.

seccions.titol: A dedicated watch page on your website for each video
seccions.text:
To get the video into Google's video results as well, embed it on a page of your site where the video is the main content. Google calls this a watch page and recommends a dedicated one for each video, where that makes sense for your business. A product page with a video next to the specs does not count, but the same video can sit on both pages.
When the video is on YouTube, Google may index it both on your page and on YouTube, and either can show up. Add VideoObject structured data with the name, thumbnail and upload date, which Google requires, plus a unique description. A written summary next to the video gives search engines and AI assistants text they can read.

faqs.q: How many videos do I need to start a channel?
faqs.a: Start with the five or six questions your sales and service teams hear most often and make one clip for each. A small channel whose videos answer real questions does more for you than a large one without structure. Then add new videos as fresh questions come up at trade shows, in demos or in Search Console.

faqs.q: Should I use YouTube or host videos on my own website?
faqs.a: The two work well together. YouTube stores the video and gives buyers a second place to find it, while your website holds a dedicated watch page for each video with the embed, supporting text and a link to the product. Google says that when you embed a YouTube video, it may index it both on your page and on YouTube.

faqs.q: Do I need a separate video for each language?
faqs.a: Usually not. If the video relies on visuals and on-screen text, one version with subtitles in several languages is enough. If it has a voice-over and one market matters a lot, such as Germany, a dubbed version can be worth it. Either way, have someone from the industry who speaks that language check the terminology.

renders-producte-botiga-online.intro: Google Merchant Center requires the main image to show the exact product you sell, with no added text or logos, and from 31 January 2027 at least 500 x 500 pixels. It also recommends one image per variant. The rules say nothing about renders, but a render built from the real product model and checked against a sample can meet them and produce every variant from a single scene.

seccions.titol: Does Google Shopping accept product renders?
seccions.text:
Google Merchant Center's rules do not mention renders or photography. They describe what the main image must show, which is the exact item being sold. They reject placeholders, logos used instead of the product, and mockups, line art or illustrations that do not depict the physical product.
So the useful question is whether the render is accurate. If it comes from the product's 3D model or drawings and the finishes have been checked against a sample, it shows what the customer will receive. A generic mockup where only the colour changes is closer to what Google rejects. Generic images and illustrations are only allowed in three categories, hardware, vehicles and parts, and software.

seccions.titol: What size should product images be?
seccions.text:
Google will require at least 500 x 500 pixels for all products from 31 January 2027. It recommends images of around 1500 x 1500 pixels or more so they perform well in every format. The upper limit is 64 megapixels and 16 MB per file.
It accepts JPEG, WebP, PNG, GIF, BMP and TIFF, and warns that the file extension must match the actual format. With a render, size is rarely a problem, because the same scene can be exported again at a larger size. Put it in the brief so you are not left with only the small web versions.

seccions.titol: What the main image cannot include
seccions.text: The main image has to show the product on its own, with nothing added in post-production. It is the first thing shoppers see across Google. If it contains any of the following, Google disapproves the product, does not show it and flags the issue in the Diagnostics section of Merchant Center.

seccions.titol: One image for every colour and finish
seccions.text:
If a product comes in several colours or finishes, Google recommends a dedicated image for each variant, showing the exact colour, material and finish, and only one variant per image. It advises against group shots with every colour together. Google also recommends that the product fills between 75% and 90% of the image.
This is where a render saves the most work. Once the model exists, each variant is a material change in the same scene, with the same lighting and framing. What you cannot skip is checking. Every colour needs comparing against the real sample before it goes live.

seccions.titol: Additional images and lifestyle scenes
seccions.text:
Besides the main image, each product can carry up to 10 additional images. Google suggests using them for other angles, the contents of the box or the product in use. There is also a separate attribute for lifestyle images, which show the product in a real-world setting, such as furniture staged in a room.
Lifestyle scenes are the other classic job for a render. A chair can be placed in a dining room without finding one or organising a shoot. Plan the whole set at once, with the clean main image, two or three angles, a close-up of the finish and a scene, so that they all come from the same model.

seccions.titol: If generative AI is involved, keep the metadata
seccions.text:
Google requires images created with generative AI to carry metadata that says so, such as the IPTC DigitalSourceType tag, and asks merchants not to remove it. That includes images made with Google's own tools, such as Product Studio, which can remove backgrounds or generate scenes.
Ask whoever produces your images whether any part of them, the background, the scene or a retouch, comes from a generative AI tool. If it does, check that the software compressing images for your site, or the plugin sending your catalogue to Google, does not strip that metadata.

seccions.titol: What to put in a product render brief
seccions.text:
With these requirements in hand, the brief can be written before any work starts. Take a chair maker in la Selva, near Girona, selling through its own online store and Google Shopping. It is a made-up example with no client data. The maker has four models, each in three finishes.
For your own website, Google Search Central recommends short, descriptive file names and alt text that explains the image. If you localise images for other languages, it also recommends translating the file names. Ask for the files to arrive already named that way.

faqs.q: Can I use renders instead of photos on Google Shopping?
faqs.a: Google Merchant Center's rules say nothing about photos or renders. They require the main image to show the exact product being sold and reject mockups and illustrations that do not depict the physical product. A render built from the product's model and checked against a sample shows what the customer will actually receive.

faqs.q: What is the minimum image size for Google Shopping?
faqs.a: From 31 January 2027, Google will require at least 500 x 500 pixels for every product. It recommends images of 1500 x 1500 pixels or more, with a maximum of 64 megapixels and 16 MB per file. If you are commissioning renders now, ask for them at the recommended size from the start.

faqs.q: Can I add my logo or a promotion to the main product image?
faqs.a: Not on the main image. Google disapproves store or manufacturer logos added in post-production, watermarks, and text about price, discounts or shipping. A logo can only appear if it is part of the physical product itself. Keep designs with text for social media or banners on your own site.

bio-assajos-anticossos-monoclonals-europ.intro: A search for monoclonal antibody on ClinicalTrials.gov returns 3,600 open clinical trials, based on our download of 4 November 2026. 809 have at least one site in Europe, and 432 of 809 have a site in Spain, more than any other European country. Most are phase 2 or phase 3. If you sell bioprocess equipment, consumables or services, this is a public list of sponsors and a pointer to where the activity is.

seccions.titol: How many monoclonal antibody trials are open in Europe
seccions.text:
There are 809 open monoclonal antibody trials with at least one site in Europe, out of 3,600 worldwide. 1,790 have a site in the United States and 1,077 in China. 411 of the 809 European trials also have US sites.
Open here means the trial is recruiting, not yet recruiting, active but not recruiting, or enrolling by invitation. In Europe, 417 are recruiting right now, 350 remain active without recruiting and 39 have not started yet.

seccions.titol: Which European countries host the most trials
seccions.text:
Spain hosts more open monoclonal antibody trials than any other European country, with 432. France follows with 406, then Italy with 343, the United Kingdom with 313 and Germany with 305. Poland has 221 and Belgium 220. Altogether, 28 European countries have at least one open trial. PMFarma reported it on 25 November 2026.
The total is higher than 809 because a trial counts in every country where it has a site. Only 346 of the 809 run sites in a single European country, and France leads that group with 90. Spain has 37.

seccions.titol: Which phase the European trials are in
seccions.text:
Phase 2 is the most common, with 267 of the 809 European trials, followed by phase 3 with 251. There are 110 phase 1 trials and 106 that combine phases 1 and 2. Phase 4, run once the medicine is approved, has 33.
Who sponsors each phase varies a lot. Industry sponsors 90 of the 110 phase 1 trials and 176 of the 251 phase 3 trials. In phase 2, though, 169 of 267 come from hospitals, universities, research groups or individual investigators, which the registry classes as other. Across Europe as a whole, industry sponsors 459 trials and these other sponsors 335.

seccions.titol: What the trials with sites in Spain show
seccions.text:
In Spain, industry carries more weight than in the rest of Europe. It sponsors 378 of the 432 trials with a Spanish site, through 109 different companies. Of the 377 European trials with no Spanish site, industry sponsors 81. In Spain, phase 3 leads with 168, followed by phase 2 with 113. Just 21 of the 432 have no site outside Spain.
The industry sponsors with the most trials in Spain are AstraZeneca with 33, Hoffmann-La Roche with 26, Bristol-Myers Squibb with 25, Merck Sharp & Dohme with 17, Regeneron with 15 and AbbVie with 14. We mention them only as registry data.
Spanish hospitals take part in many trials, but the product is made by the sponsor in its own plant or at a CDMO, often in another country. For a process supplier, a Spanish site is a sign of activity. The account is the sponsor and whoever manufactures for it.

seccions.titol: What each phase may signal to process equipment and service suppliers
seccions.text: A trial is not a purchase order, and we have no data on when each sponsor buys. In the United States, the FDA requires the application to start a trial to include manufacturing information. So by the time a trial shows up in the registry, there is usually a process that makes the product. Our working hypothesis is that each phase points to different needs.

seccions.titol: How to turn this data into a target account list
seccions.text:
The query is public and can be rerun through the ClinicalTrials.gov API. In a spreadsheet, the marketing team can rank industry sponsors by number of trials, phase and country, and hand it to sales ahead of each trade show or campaign.
At crida studio we do this as part of marketing strategy work. We turn public registries like this one into account lists, phase-specific messages and web content that a sales team can use. We do not promise results, because they depend on each market.

seccions.titol: How we counted and what the data cannot tell you
seccions.text:
We queried the ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 on 4 November 2026. We searched for monoclonal antibody in the intervention search area, which covers intervention names, titles, keywords and MeSH terms and adds synonyms. We kept interventional studies that are recruiting, not yet recruiting, active but not recruiting, or enrolling by invitation, with no date filter. That gives 3,600 trials.
Europe here means the EU 27 plus the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Norway and Iceland, and a trial counts if it has at least one site in one of those countries. Phase and sponsor type are as stated in each record.
There are limits. 3,087 of the 3,600 have an intervention with antibody in its name or a name ending in -mab. The rest come in through the registry search, and we have not checked them one by one. The EU also has its own public register, the EMA's CTIS, which we did not query. We count trials, not purchases or production volume.

faqs.q: What is the difference between phase 1, phase 2 and phase 3?
faqs.a: According to the FDA, phase 1 looks at safety and dosage in 20 to 100 people over several months. Phase 2 looks at efficacy and side effects in up to several hundred patients, over several months to two years. Phase 3 looks at efficacy and monitors adverse reactions in 300 to 3,000 participants over one to four years.

faqs.q: Does an open trial mean the sponsor will buy equipment or services?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. A trial tells you there is a medicine in development and a process that makes it, but not who manufactures it or when they buy. That is why we use it to prioritise accounts and tailor messages, not as a sales forecast. Actual purchases have to be confirmed by talking to each company.

faqs.q: How often should this count be repeated?
faqs.a: The registry changes often, as sponsors open trials, close them and move them to the next phase. Rerunning it every quarter or before a major trade show is usually enough. With the same query and the same filters, the figures can be compared from one download to the next.

bio-marqueting-consumibles-single-use.intro: If you make or distribute single-use consumables, you earn your money on repeat orders, and customers reorder when they trust your supply. Marketing has to make certificates and extractables and leachables data easy to find, flag changes before customers hear about them elsewhere and automate reorder reminders. A customer who has already validated your bag rarely switches because of an ad. A badly handled change notice is another story.

seccions.titol: With single-use consumables, the business is the reorder
seccions.text:
A single-use bag, filter or connector is used once and bought again. What matters is the same customer ordering the same part number year after year. The first sale gets you in the door, but the revenue comes from the orders that follow it.
A listed company in the sector shows it clearly. In its preliminary 2025 results, published on 3 February 2026, Sartorius reported 2,865 million euros in sales for its Bioprocess Solutions division. A large majority came from recurring business with consumables such as filters and single-use bags. Equipment sales fell as customers held back on investment.
For 2026, the same release expects the division's growth to come mainly from consumables. If you sell consumables, landing a customer is where the real work starts, which is serving them well enough that they never go looking for another supplier.

seccions.titol: Why switching suppliers is hard for the customer
seccions.text:
Customers validate a consumable inside their process, and once it is validated, replacing it means opening a change control. Annex 1 of the EU GMP guidelines, which covers the manufacture of sterile medicinal products, says in point 8.134 that assessing suppliers of single-use systems is critical to selecting and using them.
Point 8.136 asks for the extractable and leachable profiles to be evaluated, with an assessment for each component. Point 8.138 asks for the documents that come with each delivery, such as the certificate of conformance and proof of sterilisation, to be reviewed on receipt. All of that takes the customer time, so a happy customer would rather leave things alone.

seccions.titol: Change notification is marketing too
seccions.text:
A badly handled change notice is the moment a customer starts thinking about leaving. Change is part of life with single-use systems, and the customer has to decide whether to accept each one. BioPhorum, where biomanufacturers and suppliers work together, published a guide in 2020 on the information that should come with these notices.
The guide aims for all the information to arrive in one place at the right time, so the customer can make an informed decision. In 2022 BioPhorum released a template for these notices. The template page says notifications have risen sharply since the start of the pandemic, and that one member went from receiving two a week to 200 a month.
The same page names incomplete data and non-standard formats as problems. A notice that arrives complete, in the same format every time and with a named contact avoids both. Publish your change notification policy on your website and explain how people can sign up to receive notices.

seccions.titol: What documents customers should find on your website
seccions.text:
A customer validating a consumable looks for paperwork before prices. If they find it without emailing anyone, your website has saved them work. If it takes three emails to get a certificate, they will remember it the day someone offers them an alternative.
Public information belongs on each product page. Anything lot-specific or confidential goes in a customer area behind a login. Use exactly the same part number on the website, on the delivery note and on the certificate.

seccions.titol: How to automate reorders and customer notices
seccions.text:
Consumable reorders follow the customer's production schedule, and you can read that schedule in the order history. With that history in your CRM you know how often each customer orders each part number, so you can send a reorder email before they run short. The email shows the part number, the last quantity and a button to repeat the order.
The same data drives your notices. If you store the part numbers each customer buys, a change or delay notice reaches only the people it affects, with the documents attached. Customers who do not buy that part get no noise and keep opening your emails.

faqs.q: Do we need a customer portal, or is email enough?
faqs.a: It depends on how many customers and part numbers you have. With a small customer base, a well-built reorder email and a folder of certificates by lot may be enough. As part numbers and lots grow, a customer area with orders, certificates and repeat ordering saves work on both sides and cuts the emails asking for paperwork.

faqs.q: Can we publish extractables and leachables studies on our website?
faqs.a: You can publish a summary and explain how to request the full report. Many manufacturers share it inside a customer area or under a confidentiality agreement. EU GMP Annex 1 asks customers to evaluate these profiles for each component, so the easier you make access, the easier it is for them to validate your product.

faqs.q: Who should receive change notices at the customer?
faqs.a: Usually quality, purchasing and the process person who validated the consumable. Store who is who in your CRM for each customer and part number. The 2020 BioPhorum guide aims for all the information to arrive in one place and on time, and that only happens if you know who to send it to.

comprovar-nom-marca-registrada.intro: To run a Spain trademark search, check the name in the OEPM trademark locator, the free search tool of the Spanish Patent and Trademark Office, and then in TMview, which searches trademarks held by other offices worldwide. Search the classes for what you will sell, try similar variants and do it before you commission a logo. A company name approved by the Central Mercantile Registry sits in a separate register and does not tell you whether the trademark is free.

seccions.titol: Why the name comes before the logo
seccions.text:
Check the name before anyone draws anything. The OEPM, Spain's patent and trademark office, says the exclusive right to use a mark comes from registering it, and that the owner can stop others using an identical or similar sign for similar goods or services. It also says you cannot register signs identical or similar to marks already registered for identical or similar goods or services.
The OEPM adds that the law also protects a mark that is well known in Spain even if it is not registered. That is why searching the registers is the first step, but not the only one.
Picture a winery in the Empordà with labels, a website and printed boxes ready when it finds out another company has registered the same name for wine. A search before the design work would have flagged it in time. The example is made up, but the same applies to a shop, a clinic or a property development.

seccions.titol: Where to search for existing trade marks
seccions.text: Start on the OEPM website, which groups its tools on one trademark and trade name search page. The trademark locator is free, and you only need to type the name you want to use to see whether it is already registered.

seccions.titol: Search in the classes you will trade in
seccions.text:
Trademarks are registered for specific goods and services, grouped into 45 classes. The OEPM rules out identical or similar signs for identical or similar goods or services. If the earlier mark has a reputation, the bar also reaches different goods or activities when the new mark could take unfair advantage of it or harm it.
WIPO publishes the Nice Classification, and since 2013 a new version has come out every year. If you are unsure of your class, the OEPM has a table matching Spanish CNAE business activities to classes. One application can cover as many classes as you like, with a fee for each class.

seccions.titol: Searching the exact name is not enough
seccions.text: An exact-match search misses the cases that cause the most trouble. The OEPM talks about identical or similar signs, and the paid search it offers covers both identical and similar marks. So it is worth running variants like these through the locator too.

seccions.titol: A company name is not a trade mark
seccions.text:
When you set up a Spanish SL, the company name is issued by the Central Mercantile Registry, the body in charge of names for incorporating companies. A trademark, on the other hand, is registered at the OEPM, and that registration is what gives the exclusive right to use it.
An SL can carry the founders' names and trade under a different brand. If customers will see another name, that is the one to search at the OEPM. Also search Google for the name in quotes and check whether the domain and social handles are free. None of these is a trademark register, but they warn you if someone already uses the name.

seccions.titol: What happens once you pick the name
seccions.text:
With two or three names that pass the search, the visual identity work can start. If you file the mark, the OEPM publishes the application in its official bulletin, the BOPI. For the next two months, anyone with standing under Article 19 of the Spanish Trademark Act can oppose it. With or without oppositions, the OEPM then examines the grounds for refusal in Articles 5.1 and 9.1.b of the Act and grants or refuses the mark.
A granted mark lasts ten years from filing and can be renewed for further ten-year periods. To keep it you have to use it in trade and renew it. If the search leaves doubts, a Spanish industrial property agent (agente de la propiedad industrial) can do a full analysis. This guide shows where to look, but it does not replace that advice.

seccions.titol: How to use the OEPM trademark search, step by step
seccions.text:
The OEPM trademark locator is free and has three searches on the same page. One for Spanish national marks and trade names, one for international marks with effect in Spain and a link to the EUIPO service for European Union trade marks. The OEPM says you should search all three, because each one holds registrations that are valid in Spain.
The OEPM's own examples show the difference. Search Cola with the option that contains it and you get marks such as Coca Cola or Colacao. Search Coca with the option that matches the exact name and you get Coca but not Coca Cola. The locator finds live applications and registrations, as well as refusals with an appeal still pending.

seccions.titol: Trademark class search. How to filter by Nice class
seccions.text:
The OEPM locator does not let you search by class. The OEPM says so itself and offers a paid search for identical or similar marks in the Nice classes you choose. The locator also warns that it is not built to find names that sound alike, and points to that paid service for this purpose.
The free route is TMview. Its advanced search has a goods and services field where you can type one or more class numbers separated by commas. In the offices field you can pick ES for the OEPM, EM for the EUIPO and WO for WIPO. The fuzzy search option helps catch similar names.
Bear in mind that TMview is a search tool. The EUIPO states that it is not an official register and that the information in it has no legal effect. If you find a similar mark in your class, check it with the office that registered it before you decide anything.

seccions.titol: Trademark watch in Spain and the EU. Where new filings appear and the deadlines to oppose
seccions.text:
Trademark watching means keeping an eye on the applications other people file after yours and opposing in time if one clashes with your mark. You have to do it yourself or have someone do it for you. The OEPM and the EUIPO notify owners about some applications, but only the ones their own searches turn up.
In Spain, applications are published in the BOPI, the official bulletin the OEPM issues every day, and from publication there are two months to file an opposition. European Union trade marks, which also cover Spain, are published in the EUIPO's EU Trade Marks Bulletin, and there the deadline is three months. In both cases an opposition only counts as filed once the fee has been paid.
In practice, set a fixed check, for example once a month, because the shortest deadline is two months. Search your name and its variants in the OEPM locator, which also finds pending applications, and in TMview, in your classes. If a similar application turns up, note the publication date and count the deadline. A Spanish industrial property agent can help you file the opposition.

faqs.q: If the company name is free at the Mercantile Registry, can I use it as a brand?
faqs.a: They are two separate registers. The Central Mercantile Registry issues names for incorporating companies, while trademarks are registered at the OEPM, which is where the exclusive right to use a mark comes from. To find out whether identical or similar trademarks exist, you still need to search the OEPM locator and TMview.

faqs.q: How long does a trademark registration last in Spain?
faqs.a: Ten years from the filing date, renewable for successive ten-year periods. The OEPM sends a reminder well before it expires. According to the OEPM, keeping a mark takes two things, using it in trade and renewing it every ten years. Put the renewal date in the company calendar from day one.

faqs.q: Can I register a word that describes what I sell?
faqs.a: The OEPM lists generic names and signs that describe the goods or services, or are commonly used for them, among the absolute grounds for refusal. It also points out that a mark must distinguish one company's goods or services from those of its competitors. If you are unsure about your case, check with an industrial property agent before any design work.

faqs.q: How do I register a trademark outside Spain?
faqs.a: The OEPM describes three routes. You can file in each country separately. An EU trademark is filed with the EUIPO in Alicante in a single application and has the same effect across the whole EU. An international mark is filed through the OEPM, which passes it to WIPO, and can cover more than 100 countries, though each country can grant or refuse it.

faqs.q: What is trademark watching once the mark is registered?
faqs.a: It means keeping an eye on later applications that clash with your mark. According to the OEPM, if you have a mark applied for or registered, it notifies you, for information only, of later applications its search detects that could affect you, about seven days before they are published in the BOPI. From publication you have two months to file an opposition. The OEPM points out that this notice does not remove your own duty to watch.

faqs.q: Is the OEPM trademark search free?
faqs.a: Yes. The OEPM trademark locator is free, and you only need the name to see whether it is already registered. TMview, linked from the OEPM, is free too and covers trademarks held by other offices.

bio-canvi-marca-adquisicio.intro: After an acquisition or merger, the brand has four routes. You can keep the acquired brand, keep it with an endorsement from the group, fold it into your own or create a new name. Choose based on what each name is worth to customers with validated equipment and in Google. Then make the change in order, customers and documents first, and the website with 301 redirects last.

seccions.titol: Four brand options after an acquisition
seccions.text:
When one company in the sector buys another, the first decision is what happens to the name. There are four common options. Keep the acquired brand as it is, keep it with an endorsement such as “a … company”, fold it into your own brand or create a new name for the whole business.
Danaher offers a public example from the sector. On 31 March 2020 it announced that it had completed the acquisition of the Biopharma business of General Electric's Life Sciences division. The same release said that, as part of Danaher, the business would be called Cytiva and would be a standalone operating company.
The same case shows the timeline. Danaher announced the agreement on 25 February 2019 and expected to close in the fourth quarter of that year. It closed on 31 March 2020, thirteen months later, and the new name appeared in the closing release itself. The gap between signing and closing gives you time to prepare the brand without going public.

seccions.titol: What should weigh most in the decision
seccions.text:
Customer trust should weigh more than the logo. In this sector many customers have the bioreactor, TFF system or consumable validated in their process, with IQ, OQ and PQ completed. For them, the brand is the name printed on documents they have already approved.
Look at where each name gets searched, too. If people know the acquired name on Google, on LinkedIn or at trade shows, dropping it overnight closes a door that brings in leads. If the real problem is two product ranges competing with each other, that is a brand architecture question and the fix is to organise the range.
David Monje, founder of crida studio, ran marketing at a European bioprocess equipment manufacturer for three and a half years. There he repositioned the brand to compete with the large corporations and acted as the bridge between engineering, product and sales. When an equipment maker changes its brand, getting those three teams aligned matters as much as the design.

seccions.titol: How to tell customers who run validated equipment
seccions.text:
Customers working under GMP should know what changes and what stays the same before a delivery note arrives with a new name on it. A different name on the label, the certificate of conformance or the manual can trigger a change control on the customer side. If they know in advance that the product, the site and the process are unchanged, the review will be easier for them.
Send a formal change notification to quality and procurement, not just to your sales contact. It should say when the name changes, which documents change and how lots made before and after can be told apart. Check with your quality team and your supply agreements whether notice periods have been agreed with individual customers.

seccions.titol: Distributors, LinkedIn, YouTube and trade shows
seccions.text:
Distributors should hear about the change before end customers do, because they will be the first ones asked. Give them a kit with the new logo, updated datasheets, a short text explaining the deal and answers to the questions that will come up. If you sell in several countries, produce it in the languages your partners sell in.
On LinkedIn and YouTube, decide whether to merge or keep the pages. A page with followers and a channel with demo videos watched over several years are assets worth keeping and renaming where it makes sense. At trade shows, the first booth under the new brand is a good moment to explain the change face to face.

seccions.titol: How to migrate the website and domain without losing rankings
seccions.text:
If the acquired brand goes away, its website has to be redirected page by page. Google's guide to site moves recommends mapping every old URL to its new equivalent and using server-side permanent redirects such as 301. It also states that 301 redirects do not cause a loss in PageRank.
Google warns against redirecting many old URLs to a single unrelated page such as the home page, because it may be treated as a soft 404. It recommends changing one thing at a time, the domain first and the design later, and keeping redirects for as long as possible, generally at least a year. Remember the PDFs and images as well.
When the domain changes, the Change of Address tool in Search Console tells Google about the move. Its help page requires you to own both properties and advises against combining several moves into one location. It suggests moving them one by one, waiting for traffic to settle, and paying for the old domain for at least a year.

seccions.titol: In what order to roll out the rebrand
seccions.text:
Decision and name first, then customers, and the public side last. If the name is new, check whether it is registered in the countries where you sell. Then build the inventory, notify customers and distributors and, once they know, launch the new website with the redirects and the change of address.
Google explains that rankings can fluctuate for a while during a move as it recrawls the site, and that for a medium-sized site it can take a few weeks or more to show the new URLs. Warn the sales team and watch the Search Console data for both sites.

seccions.titol: How long a rebrand after an acquisition takes
seccions.text:
There is no single timeline, but other parties set some of the deadlines. The deal itself can take months to close, as Danaher's thirteen show. Customers with validated equipment need time to review the new documents. And Google says a medium-sized site can take a few weeks or more to show the new URLs after a move.
While the deal is still open, prepare the work nobody sees. The document inventory, the notice for quality and procurement, the distributor kit and the list of old URLs mapped to their new equivalents. If the name is new, search WIPO's Global Brand Database and the registers in the countries where you sell before any design work starts.
If the company you bought is a startup or spin-off with a young brand and a small installed base, folding the name in usually costs less. Even so, check first what that name is worth to investors, partners and in Google. The criteria behind a startup or spin-off brand help you judge whether it is worth keeping.

seccions.titol: What the studio running the rebrand should deliver and what it costs
seccions.text:
The studio should do more than draw a logo. In a rebrand after an acquisition it also has to deliver the materials sales, quality and distributors use every day, and work alongside whoever handles the website. These are the items worth asking for in the quote.
At crida studio, a rebrand starts at €4,000 and a new brand at €3,500, excluding VAT, with prices updated in November 2026. That covers logo, colours, typography, a short brand guide and basic applications. Positioning, full guidelines and the roll-out to the website and materials are added separately. You get a fixed quote in writing within five working days.

faqs.q: What should the name change notice to customers include?
faqs.a: It should say when the name changes, which documents change and how lots made before and after can be told apart. If the product, the site and the process are unchanged, say so plainly. Send it to quality and procurement as well as your sales contact, and have the new documents ready so they can review them before they arrive.

faqs.q: How long should redirects from the old website stay in place?
faqs.a: Google's site move guide says at least a year and, from the user's point of view, indefinitely if you can. The Change of Address help page mentions a minimum of 180 days, or longer if Google Search is still sending traffic, and advises paying for the old domain for at least a year.

faqs.q: Can I keep both websites live for a while?
faqs.a: Yes, if both brands carry on and each has its own audience. If one is going away, two websites covering the same equipment confuse customers and leave two pages competing for the same searches. In that case it is better to move the site with 301 redirects and add a page that explains the deal.

faqs.q: How do we update email signatures and templates after the acquisition?
faqs.a: Create one new signature template for everyone and switch it on the same day the new website goes live, so email and web say the same thing. If you keep the brand with a group endorsement, add the group line to the signature. Check quotes, invoices and presentations as well, since those are what customers actually see.

faqs.q: How much does a rebrand after an acquisition cost?
faqs.a: It depends on how much changes. At crida studio, a rebrand starts at €4,000 excluding VAT, covering logo, colours, typography, a short brand guide and basic applications. The roll-out to the website, documents and distributor materials is quoted separately, and the website move with redirects depends on how many pages the site has.

bio-comerc-farmaceutic-ue-2025.intro: The EU exported €365.8 billion of medicinal and pharmaceutical products outside the Union in 2025, according to Eurostat, 16% more than in 2024. Ireland is the largest exporter with €93.1 billion, followed by Germany with €67.9 billion, and the top five countries account for 72% of the total. If you sell bioprocess or lab equipment, this is a map of where to look first.

seccions.titol: Which EU countries export the most pharmaceuticals outside the EU
seccions.text:
Ireland is the EU's largest pharmaceutical exporter to non-EU markets, with €93,122 million in 2025. Germany follows with €67,911 million, then Belgium with €38,759 million, Italy with €36,166 million and Slovenia with €28,961 million. Spain ranks ninth, with €10,742 million.
Exports are highly concentrated. Ireland and Germany together account for 44% of the EU total, the top five for 72% and the top ten for 95%. Eurostat also notes that Denmark, Ireland and Slovenia sell less than 40% of their pharmaceutical exports to other EU countries, against an EU average of 44%. The rest goes outside the EU.
The table ranks the top ten countries and compares them with 2024. Ireland went from €56,214 million to €93,122 million, up 66% in a single year. Italy and Slovenia grew by close to 30%, Germany stayed flat, and Belgium and Austria fell by 12% and 19%. A jump that large in one year should be read with caution.

seccions.titol: How fast EU pharmaceutical trade is growing
seccions.text:
EU pharmaceutical exports have grown every year since 2015 except 2023, according to Eurostat. In 2025 they rose 16% on 2024, an increase of about €50 billion, while imports rose 21%. The trade surplus went from €195 billion to a record €221 billion. In 2015 it stood at €69 billion.
Between 2015 and 2025, exports grew 151% and imports 88%. Part of that growth is price. The unit value index for exports climbed from 91.2 in 2015 to 130.8 in 2025, and Eurostat says this suggests the increase was partly driven by higher prices.
For marketing, read this with care. More export value does not mean the same rise in litres produced or in equipment orders. What it does show is an industry exporting more value, which may leave room to invest in capacity. Check that against your own sales before acting on it.

seccions.titol: The United States is the main market for EU medicines
seccions.text:
The United States is the top destination for EU pharmaceutical exports. Its share rose from 26% in 2015 to 44% in 2025. Switzerland, at 16%, is the only other partner with a double-digit share. On the import side the United States also leads, with 41%, followed by Switzerland with 28% and China with 9%.
For a supplier, it is likely that many European customers also produce with the US market in mind. If your equipment helps them with the documentation those markets ask for, show it on your website with concrete examples, without claiming more than it does.
Ireland is the clearest case. According to Comext, €81,910 million of the €93,122 million it exported outside the EU in 2025 went to the United States, almost 88%. Ireland's Central Statistics Office says the country exported €138.6 billion of medical and pharmaceutical products worldwide that year, 39% more than in 2024.

seccions.titol: Where the plants that buy equipment and consumables are
seccions.text:
Our working hypothesis is that where exports are concentrated, there are many production plants buying bioreactors, filtration systems, single-use consumables and services. Eurostat does not measure equipment purchases. Even so, Ireland, Germany, Belgium, Italy and Slovenia account for 72% of exports, which makes them a sensible starting point when ranking markets.
Read the figures carefully. Eurostat warns that trade with non-EU countries is reported by the Member State where the customs declaration is lodged, usually where the goods cross the EU border, which is not always the real buyer or seller. It mainly affects countries with large ports such as Antwerp and Rotterdam, hence the name Rotterdam effect. Belgium and the Netherlands may rank higher than their actual production.

seccions.titol: What a supplier should change in the marketing plan
seccions.text:
These figures help you decide which languages and markets deserve budget and time. Before you move money, cross them with your sales, your Search Console traffic by country and your trade show contacts. These are the areas where the data matters most.
At crida studio we help suppliers in the sector turn public data like this into an international marketing plan, with languages, websites, campaigns and trade shows ranked by priority. We do not promise results, because they depend on each market and each product.

seccions.titol: Where the data comes from and what it does not tell you
seccions.text:
The country figures come from Eurostat's Comext dataset DS-059331, downloaded on 4 November 2026 and last updated on 16 October. We filtered for 2025, SITC Rev. 4 division 54, which covers medicinal and pharmaceutical products, the export flow and extra-EU partners. We used the value in euros.
These are extra-EU exports reported by the country where the goods leave the EU. They are not each country's production and they leave out sales within the EU. Growth, destinations and intra-EU shares come from the Statistics Explained article, with data from March 2026, and may shift slightly if Eurostat revises its figures.
The country table, the comparison with 2024 and the destinations for Ireland and Spain come from new queries on the same dataset, run on 11 November 2026. The CSO figures are from its release of 17 February 2026 and cover all destinations, including those inside the EU.

seccions.titol: How much Spain exports in pharmaceuticals, and where to
seccions.text:
Spain exported €21,188 million of medicinal and pharmaceutical products in 2025, according to Comext. Almost half, €10,446 million, went to other EU countries, and €10,742 million left the Union, 20% more than in 2024. Outside the EU it is the ninth largest exporter, with 2.9% of the total.
Its destinations are not those of the EU as a whole. Outside the Union, the United Kingdom comes first with €2,247 million, followed by Switzerland with €1,972 million, China with €1,312 million and the United States with €1,306 million. Inside the EU, Germany at €2,660 million and France at €1,480 million lead. If you sell to plants in Spain, the US matters far less than the EU average suggests.

seccions.titol: How to pull these figures for your own country or product
seccions.text: The data is free and you can run the same query yourself. Comext, Eurostat's foreign trade database, holds dataset DS-059331 with trade by product under the SITC classification. We used division 54 here, but the same method works for another product, another country or another year.

faqs.q: Which EU country exports the most pharmaceuticals?
faqs.a: Ireland, with €93,122 million of exports outside the EU in 2025 according to Eurostat, or 25% of the EU total. Germany is second with €67,911 million. These are exports reported by the country where the goods leave the EU, so they are not exactly each country's production, but they clearly show where exports are concentrated.

faqs.q: How much have European pharmaceutical exports grown?
faqs.a: According to Eurostat, EU exports of medicinal and pharmaceutical products grew 16% in 2025 compared with 2024, and 151% between 2015 and 2025. They have risen every year since 2015 except 2023. Part of the growth comes from higher prices, as the export unit value index went from 91.2 to 130.8 over those ten years.

faqs.q: Can I use this data to choose which country to sell in?
faqs.a: Use it to rank where to look first, not to decide on its own. It shows where export manufacturing is concentrated, not who buys equipment or when. Cross it with your sales, your traffic by country and your trade show contacts. We have a separate guide on choosing your next export market step by step.

faqs.q: How much does Spain export in pharmaceuticals?
faqs.a: According to Eurostat, Spain exported €21,188 million of medicinal and pharmaceutical products in 2025. Of that, €10,742 million went outside the EU, 20% more than in 2024, and the rest to other EU countries. Outside the EU, its main destinations are the United Kingdom, Switzerland, China and the United States.

faqs.q: Where can I find EU pharmaceutical export data?
faqs.a: In Comext, Eurostat's foreign trade database, which is free to use. Dataset DS-059331 gives trade by product, country and partner, and medicines are SITC division 54. Eurostat also publishes a Statistics Explained article on this trade each year, covering growth and the main destinations.

videos-web-google.intro: To get a video on your website to show up on Google, put it on a page built around that one video, make sure it loads without a click and give it a thumbnail at a stable URL. Describe it with structured data or a video sitemap, then check Search Console to see whether Google indexed it.

seccions.titol: Where your website videos can appear on Google
seccions.text:
A video on your website can appear in several places on Google. Google's documentation names four, the main results page, Video mode, Google Images and Discover. So a product video can bring in visits beyond YouTube.
Google warns that structured data doesn't guarantee a video result. First, the page hosting the video has to be indexed and performing well in search before the video is even considered. Even then, an indexed page doesn't mean the video is indexed too.

seccions.titol: Every important video needs its own watch page
seccions.text:
Google only indexes videos that sit on a watch page, a page whose main purpose is to show one video. Its examples include a video landing page and an event clip page. Each watch page needs a title and description unique to that video.
A blog post reviewing an embedded video, or a product page with a 360 video, doesn't count as a watch page. You can still use the same video on the product page and on its own watch page. The product page can then appear as a text result, or in Google Images with a video badge. Here's how that could look for businesses around Girona.

seccions.titol: YouTube, Vimeo or your own server
seccions.text:
You can host on YouTube or Vimeo and embed the video on your site. Google says it may then index the video both on your page and on the platform's page, and both can appear if they meet the requirements. For your own page, it still recommends adding structured data and, if you like, listing it in a video sitemap.
Some features, like video previews and key moments, need Google to be able to fetch the video file itself. If you host the file on your server or a CDN, keep it at a stable URL. If you use a platform, Google suggests checking with them that they let Google fetch the file.

seccions.titol: Make sure the video loads without a click
seccions.text:
Google finds videos placed with the usual HTML elements, such as video, embed, iframe or object. Nobody should have to click, swipe or type for the video to load. If you inject the video with JavaScript, use the URL Inspection tool in Search Console to check that it appears in the rendered HTML.
A common mistake is showing a screenshot of the player that has to be clicked before the real video loads. Search Console flags this as being unable to determine the video's position and size. The fix is to load the player at its real size and position as soon as the page opens.

seccions.titol: Thumbnail and video structured data
seccions.text: Without a valid thumbnail, a video can't appear in video features. Google tries to generate one if it can fetch the file, but you can choose your own with the poster attribute, a video sitemap or structured data. Use the same thumbnail URL everywhere. VideoObject structured data has three required properties, the name, the thumbnail URL and the upload date.

seccions.titol: Key moments and video previews
seccions.text:
Key moments let people jump to a specific part of the video straight from Google, like chapters in a book. Google tries to detect them on its own, but gives priority to the ones you mark. On YouTube you add them as timestamps in the description. On your own site you use Clip or SeekToAction structured data.
In a three-minute video about an industrial product, marking segments like setup, operation and maintenance helps people who only need one part. For a site in Catalan, use Clip, which works in every language Google Search supports, because SeekToAction doesn't support Catalan. Google picks the moving preview itself, and to be eligible it needs to be able to fetch the video file.

seccions.titol: How to check in Search Console whether a video is indexed
seccions.text: The Video indexing report in Search Console shows how many pages have an indexed video and why others don't. Because it only counts indexed pages, a high number of pages with no video indexed points to a problem with the videos themselves. The URL Inspection tool lets you check a single page and see whether Google found the video on it. These are some of the reasons the report lists.

faqs.q: If the video is already on YouTube, do I need to do anything on my website?
faqs.a: Yes, if you want your own page to appear too. Google recommends adding video structured data to your page, and you can list the page in a video sitemap. If the video is only a small part of the page, the page can show as a text result, but not as a video.

faqs.q: Will the video on my homepage show up on Google as a video?
faqs.a: Usually not. Google indexes videos that are the main content of a page. A homepage with a background video, or a video among lots of other content, doesn't meet that condition. If the video matters to your business, give it its own page with a unique title and description, and link to it from the homepage.

faqs.q: How long does Google take to index a new video?
faqs.a: Google doesn't give a timeframe. At first the Search Console report may show that the video is still being processed, and Google suggests checking back in a few days. A video sitemap helps Google discover new videos. And if the thumbnail URL changes too often, Google may not manage to index the video.

bio-projectes-horizon-europe-bioproces.intro: We counted 158 Horizon Europe projects that mention bioprocessing or bioreactors, using CORDIS data downloaded on 5 November 2026. Germany takes part in 67 and Spain in 61, but Spain coordinates more than any other country, 29 of 158. Private companies account for 397 of the 962 participations. If you make or sell bioprocess equipment, this is a public map of accounts, applications and partners.

seccions.titol: How many Horizon Europe projects work on bioprocessing
seccions.text:
158 Horizon Europe projects mention bioprocessing or bioreactors in their title, summary or keywords. CORDIS lists 135 as signed, 13 as closed and 10 as ended early. 89 mention bioreactors and 78 mention bioprocessing, with some overlap. Only 24 have the term in the title.
By signature year there are 42 from 2022, 31 from 2023, 30 from 2024, 25 from 2025 and 30 from 2026 up to 5 October. The maximum EU contribution adds up to 407.0 million euros. That money pays for research and does not say what will be bought. It does show where groups are working with bioreactors.

seccions.titol: Which countries have the most bioprocess projects
seccions.text:
Germany appears in the most projects, 67 of 158, followed by Spain with 61. Next come the Netherlands with 54, Italy with 46, France with 42 and the United Kingdom with 39. A project counts in every country where it has a participant, so the total is higher than 158.
Spain coordinates more projects than any other country, 29 of 158, ahead of Germany with 27 and the Netherlands with 17. It also has the most participations, 135 against 123 for Germany. In funding terms, German participants are allocated 66.6 million euros of EU funding and Spanish participants 55.8 million.

seccions.titol: What kind of organisations take part
seccions.text:
Private companies are the largest group, with 397 of the 962 participations. Universities account for 350 and research centres for 170. 291 participations are SMEs, and 101 of the 158 projects include at least one private company. Each participation is one organisation in one project, associated partners included.
Coordination usually sits with a university. Universities coordinate 92 projects, companies 35 and research centres 28. Our reading is that an equipment supplier should usually start with the group running the project, even when companies are in the consortium.

seccions.titol: Which applications go beyond pharma
seccions.text:
Bioprocessing in these projects reaches well beyond medicines. We did not count by category, but reading the titles shows five broad application areas. In our view, each area needs its own vocabulary, messages and trade shows.
A few example titles are PAT4CGT, on automated monitoring and control in cell and gene therapy, MultiSpek, a multi-sensing platform for single-use applications, ComfyCell, a bioreactor for stem and immune cell manufacturing, and AIR2FOOD, a European hub for gas precision fermentation.

seccions.titol: What equipment marketing teams can take from this
seccions.text:
The count does not tell you who will buy. It does give you a public list of groups, companies and applications already working with bioreactors. With that list, the marketing team of a bioprocess equipment maker or supplier can work on four concrete things.
Spain and Catalonia are a nearby market for a supplier based here. There are 135 Spanish participations in 61 projects, 54 from companies, 39 from universities and 37 from research centres. Catalonia has 29 in 21 projects and the Madrid region 42. These are accounts you can visit without long trips.

seccions.titol: How to repeat the count and turn it into an account list
seccions.text:
You can repeat the count without writing code. In the CORDIS project search, filter by the Horizon Europe programme and search for bioreactor or bioprocess. The CSV download lets you go further and join projects and organisations in a spreadsheet by country, organisation type and application.
At crida studio we do this work as part of strategy and market research for the biotech sector. We turn public data like this into a list of accounts, segments and messages your sales team can use. We do not promise results, because they depend on each product and each market.

seccions.titol: How we counted and where the limits are
seccions.text:
We downloaded the CORDIS CSV file of Horizon Europe projects on 5 November 2026, with files dated 5 October 2026. Using python3, we counted projects with a word starting with bioprocess or bioreactor in the title, summary or keywords. A project that uses bioreactors without naming them is missed, and some that only mention them in passing are included. The United Kingdom takes part as an associated country, and 2026 is not complete.
Each participation is one row in the organisations file, meaning one organisation in one project, including associated partners and third parties. The country is the one in each organisation's address. Amounts are the EU contribution recorded in CORDIS, which does not mean it has already been paid.

faqs.q: What is CORDIS and who can use it?
faqs.a: CORDIS is the European Commission service that publishes EU-funded research projects, with each project's summary, participants and funding. Anyone can search it online or download the data as CSV files. That is why this count can be repeated and compared a few months from now using the same filter.

faqs.q: Does a Horizon Europe project buy bioprocess equipment?
faqs.a: Not always, and the data does not say. The EU contribution covers research costs, which can include equipment, staff or services. What a project does tell you is that a team will be working with bioreactors or bioprocessing for a few years. So we use it to prioritise accounts and plan content, not to forecast sales.

faqs.q: How can an equipment maker join a European consortium?
faqs.a: Usually by talking to groups already preparing proposals, which are often universities or research centres. A company can bring equipment, scale-up or industrial validation. CORDIS shows who coordinates projects in each application and country. A web page that explains what your company brings to a consortium also helps.

bio-resultats-sartorius-2026-bioproces.intro: Bioprocess demand is growing in every region in 2026, according to Sartorius's nine-month results published on 22 October. Sartorius Stedim Biotech sold €2,289 million, up 6.5% in constant currencies. Consumables still drive the business, equipment is growing again and Asia/Pacific is the fastest-growing region. For a mid-sized equipment maker or supplier, that has a direct bearing on repeat orders, product messaging, pricing and next year's marketing budget.

seccions.titol: What Sartorius results say about bioprocess demand
seccions.text:
Bioprocess demand is in good shape, according to the two Sartorius releases of 22 October 2026. Sartorius Stedim Biotech booked €2,289 million in sales over nine months, up 6.5% in constant currencies. Excluding tariff compensation paid to customers, operational growth came to 7.8%.
The group's Bioprocess Solutions division posted €2,213 million in sales, with operational growth of 8.1%. The company describes end markets as fundamentally healthy and customer activity as robust. If you sell to the same customers, that is a reason to plan 2027 with a little more confidence.

seccions.titol: Consumables are still the engine of the business
seccions.text:
The recurring consumables business was the main growth driver at Sartorius Stedim Biotech, and its CEO calls it the backbone of the business. A single-use consumable is used once, so a customer who has validated it in their process keeps ordering it.
For marketing, that means putting as much effort into keeping customers as into winning new ones. Clear pages for every part number help, along with easy reordering through your website or distributor, well-explained product change notices and quality documents such as lot certificates that buyers can find in seconds.

seccions.titol: Bioprocess equipment is growing again
seccions.text:
Sartorius Stedim Biotech's bioprocess equipment business grew year on year, and the group says demand for equipment and instruments continued to recover.
