Conjugates are also growing. They join an antibody to a drug or a toxin, and their names carry a second word such as vedotin or deruxtecan. We counted 8 new ones from 2021 to 2025, against 4 from 2016 to 2020. Each one needs an antibody, a payload and a conjugation step.

seccions.titol: Why the newest antibodies no longer end in -mab
seccions.text:
In October 2021 the WHO expert group on international non-proprietary names decided to stop using the -mab ending. It replaced it with four new endings, published in May 2022. -tug is for unmodified full antibodies, -bart for antibodies with an engineered constant region, -ment for fragments and -mig for bispecific and multispecific antibodies.
The first one is already authorised in the EU. Kavigale, with sipavibart, an antibody against COVID-19, got its authorisation on 20 January 2025. Frehemgo, with denecimig, a bispecific for haemophilia, has a positive opinion and is waiting for the Commission decision. Older names keep -mab, so both systems will live side by side, and a team that searches registers for -mab only will miss the new ones.

seccions.titol: What the trend means for bioprocess suppliers
seccions.text:
More authorised antibodies mean more commercial processes to supply, but the figures do not say who buys what or when. Our reading is that each biosimilar wave brings many holders at once and that each new substance brings one company that is still scaling up. Equipment and consumables makers can plan campaigns around both. Open clinical trials with antibodies show what may come next.
Sartorius describes its end markets as fundamentally healthy. In the Sartorius results for the first nine months of 2026, recurring consumables were the main driver, and the CEO said demand for bioprocess equipment and instruments continued to recover.
This is part of our marketing for biotech and bioprocess suppliers. We turn public registers like this one into account lists, messages for each type of buyer and web content that sales can use. We do not promise results, because they depend on each market.

seccions.titol: How to rerun and use this count tomorrow
seccions.text: The EMA updates its data tables overnight, so you can repeat the count whenever you need it. A spreadsheet is enough. At the end you will have your own list of holders, sorted by molecule and by date.

seccions.titol: How we counted and what the data does not say
seccions.text:
We downloaded the Medicines output file from the EMA on 10 November 2026. The EMA generated it that day at 6 pm. We kept 2,357 human medicines and looked for an antibody name in the international non-proprietary name or the active substance. That gave 311 rows, and 271 have a marketing authorisation date.
The count includes withdrawn medicines, so older years are complete. It includes four imaging antibodies from the 1990s. It leaves out fusion proteins such as etanercept and aflibercept, which are not antibodies. The Biosimilar column is the EMA's own, and a product marked as not biosimilar is not always a new molecule.
We count authorisations, not sales, doses or production volume. Each brand counts once, and some holders register two brands of the same molecule. 2026 is partial. The download on this page has the figures of the charts. We also keep the list of 271 medicines with their EMA number.

faqs.q: How many monoclonal antibodies are authorised in the EU?
faqs.a: In the EMA file of 10 November 2026 we found 271 monoclonal antibodies authorised since 1996, and 231 are still authorised. They are brand names, so one molecule can appear several times. Biosimilars share the name of their reference medicine, and counting each name once leaves 151 different antibody substances, with combinations counted as one.

faqs.q: Does every monoclonal antibody in the EU go through the EMA?
faqs.a: Medicines made with biotechnology, such as genetic engineering, must use the EU centralised procedure, which goes through the EMA. That covers monoclonal antibodies. So the EMA file is the most complete public list of antibodies authorised in the EU. It also keeps withdrawn medicines, with the authorisation date and status of each.

faqs.q: Is aflibercept a monoclonal antibody?
faqs.a: No. Aflibercept and etanercept are fusion proteins, a receptor joined to part of an antibody. Their names do not end in -mab and we left them out of the count. Many of their biosimilars appear in the same years, so mixing them in would inflate the 2025 figure for antibodies.

faqs.q: How often can I update the count?
faqs.a: The EMA says it updates the download tables on its website overnight. The European Commission grants the authorisation within 67 days of the EMA recommendation, and until then the file shows the status Opinion. Running the count before each campaign or trade show is usually enough to catch the new holders and the files with a positive opinion.

preu-render-3d.intro: At crida studio, a 3D product render on a neutral background starts at €250 per image and an interior of one room at €350, excluding VAT. The final price mostly depends on whether the model has to be built from scratch, how many materials and variants need showing, whether the image is a full scene and how it will be used.

seccions.titol: How much does a 3D render cost in 2026?
seccions.text:
At crida studio, a product render on a neutral background with a single view starts at €250 per image. An interior of one room starts at €350, and a pack of 3 to 5 images at €2,000. These are November 2026 prices, excluding VAT, and the starting price includes two rounds of revisions.
Lifestyle scenes, variants of the same product and development exteriors with their surroundings can be added, but they have no published starting price. Each one is looked at case by case, because the work varies a lot from one job to the next. Our pricing page lists the starting prices for every other service too.
Each image takes one to two weeks. You get a fixed quote in writing within five working days, after a thirty-minute call. The table below sums up each starting price and what tends to push it up.

seccions.titol: What drives the price of a render?
seccions.text:
The price of a render comes from the work done before the image is calculated. The computer does the calculation. The hours go into building the model, setting up materials, lighting and the scene, and reviewing everything with someone who knows the product. These are the things that move the figure.
That is why two quotes for a render can look nothing alike. Before comparing figures, check that both count the same number of images, views, variants and revision rounds, and that both say whether the 3D model is included.

seccions.titol: A worked example with a 12-product catalogue
seccions.text:
Take a chair manufacturer selling 12 models in its online shop, each in 3 finishes, a made-up example with no client data. That makes 36 distinct products. For one neutral-background view of each model, the starting point at our prices is 12 times €250, which comes to €3,000 excluding VAT.
The other two finishes of each chair add 24 more images. If the company sells through Google Shopping, it will need them, because Merchant Center asks for a separate image for every variant and SKU, showing the exact colour, finish and material. Variants have no published starting price. They reuse the model and lighting, and only the material changes.
With photography, all 36 combinations would have to exist and be in the studio on the day of the shoot. With a product render, the model and a sample of each finish are enough, and a chair that has not been manufactured yet can be shown just the same. If the chairs already exist and there are few variants, a photo shoot may well work out cheaper.

seccions.titol: Why do interiors and developments cost more?
seccions.text:
An interior costs more than a product because a whole room has to be built instead of one object. Walls, floor, joinery, furniture, lamps and the daylight coming through the window all have to match the design. That is why an interior of one room starts at €350 and a product on a neutral background at €250.
A development exterior adds the surroundings, with neighbouring buildings, the street, planting and the sky. It has no published starting price, and a detached house and an apartment block on a narrow street are very different jobs. In Spain, architectural renders are often called infografías 3D, but it is the same image at the same price.
For homes sold in Spain, the images also have to be accurate. Article 2 of Royal Decree 515/1989 says advertising for the sale or rental of homes must match their real features, and article 3.2 says those details can be required even if they are not in the contract. Order the final images once the specification is settled, because what they show has to match what will be handed over.

seccions.titol: What to send to get a fixed quote
seccions.text:
A fixed quote depends on knowing what will be drawn, how many times and what for. With this list, any studio can give you a figure that will not change halfway through, and you can compare two proposals with the same scope.
Ask for the quote to state the uses as well. Article 43 of Spain's Intellectual Property Act says an assignment of rights is limited to the forms of exploitation expressly provided for and to the term and territory that are set. If no term is stated, it is five years, and if no territory is stated, it is the country where the assignment is made.
So write down every planned use, for example website, online shop, ads, printed catalogue and trade fairs, and say if you need them outside Spain. Ask too how many revision rounds are included and what happens if you need a third. Our starting price includes two.

seccions.titol: What about making the images with AI?
seccions.text:
Generative AI is useful for exploring mood and camera angles before you commission anything. For the image that sells a specific product, it has two limits. If the product has not been made yet, there is no photo to start from, and Google asks for AI-made images to say so in their metadata.
Google Merchant Center says all images created with generative AI must contain metadata indicating it, such as the IPTC TrainedAlgorithmicMedia tag, and asks you not to remove it. The same page says not to submit line art, mockups or illustrations that do not depict the physical product. The image on a product listing has to show the product as it is sold.
IPTC, which maintains those codes, separates media created by a human using non-generative tools, digitalCreation, from media created with generative AI, trainedAlgorithmicMedia. An image edited with generative AI has its own code, compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia. If you are weighing a render, virtual staging or an AI image for a property, we have a guide on what you should disclose.

seccions.titol: What to do tomorrow if you need renders
seccions.text: In half an hour you can gather what you need to ask for a quote that can be compared with others. These steps work just as well for a product catalogue, a housing development or a shop refit.

faqs.q: Is 3D modelling charged separately from each image?
faqs.a: It depends on the studio. What matters is that the quote says whether the model is included and whether it can be reused for other views or variants. If the manufacturer has a CAD file with dimensions, modelling is quicker. If there are only photos, it takes more work. Ask for it on its own line so quotes are easier to compare.

faqs.q: How much does an architectural render cost?
faqs.a: At crida studio, an interior of one room starts at €350 excluding VAT, and a pack of 3 to 5 images at €2,000. A development exterior with its surroundings has no published starting price and depends on the building and what is around it. In Spain these images are often called infografías 3D, and they cost the same as a render.

faqs.q: How many revisions are included and how long does it take?
faqs.a: Our starting price includes two rounds of revisions, and each image takes one to two weeks. It helps to review the framing and shape first on an untextured view, then the finishes, because a change of shape at the end means redoing far more work than a change of colour.

faqs.q: Is a render cheaper than a photo shoot?
faqs.a: It depends on how many variants you have and whether the product already exists. With many colours or finishes, a render reuses the model and you do not need every combination made. With a few products already in the warehouse, a photo shoot may work out cheaper. Do the maths on final images, not on products.

bio-triar-agencia-marqueting-life-scienc.intro: To choose a life science marketing agency, write a brief that defines success as qualified quote requests, send the same RFP questions to three or four agencies and score every proposal with the same weighted rubric. Then check that the team understands your buyers and the rules of your sector, and compare prices line by line.

seccions.titol: Specialist life science agency or generalist B2B agency?
seccions.text:
The specialist label matters less than whether the team can talk to your buyers. A bioreactor, a TFF system or a CDMO service is bought by a committee where process engineering, quality and procurement each read your website looking for something different. An agency that has never written for that committee will need months to learn it, and you pay for those months.
A generalist B2B agency can work well if someone in your company checks every technical claim and knows the buyers. A specialist pays off when nobody on your side has time to brief, review and correct. Decide which of the two situations you are in before you shortlist anyone.
A word on who is writing this. crida studio is itself an agency that offers marketing for biotech and bioprocess companies, so we have an interest in the answer. That is why this guide ranks no agencies and why our own prices appear only as one reference, clearly marked as ours.

seccions.titol: What to put in the brief before you ask for proposals
seccions.text:
Proposals can only be compared if every agency answers the same brief. Without one, each agency sells what it does best, one a new website and another a LinkedIn campaign, and you end up comparing different projects.
An agency that plans to measure marketing by quote requests will ask early for access to your CRM and your sales team, which is a good sign. A brief of one or two pages is enough if it covers these points.

seccions.titol: RFP questions that show whether an agency knows the sector
seccions.text:
Send the same questions to every agency and ask for written answers before any presentation. Written answers show what each agency proposes, without the effect of a polished pitch. Google suggests something similar before hiring an SEO, asking for examples of previous work, experience in your industry and how success will be measured.
The Google Ads question works as a quick filter. Google's healthcare and medicines policy restricts prescription drug terms in ads, landing pages and keywords, and pharmaceutical manufacturers must be certified by Google to advertise prescription drugs where that is allowed. An agency that has worked in the sector will bring this up without being asked.

seccions.titol: A weighted rubric to score agency proposals
seccions.text:
Score every proposal against the same criteria, from 1 to 5, before you discuss price with anyone. Multiply each score by its weight and divide by 5, so the maximum is 100. The weights below are our proposal for a mid-sized equipment maker or CDMO. Adjust them to your situation, but fix them before you read the proposals.
Ask two people to score separately, for example the managing director and the sales director, and compare the results before meeting the agencies. Where the two scores differ by two points or more, you have found the question to ask that agency. The rubric also shows what a more expensive proposal gives you for the extra money.

seccions.titol: How much a life science marketing agency costs in Europe
seccions.text:
There is no open, dated survey of life science agency fees in Europe. ISBA's agency hourly rate benchmarks are only available to members who contribute data, and most price lists that rank in search come from US agencies. The most honest reference is the prices agencies publish themselves, compared line by line.
As one example, these are crida studio's own starting prices, published in November 2026 and excluding VAT. A marketing diagnosis with a twelve-month plan starts at €2,500. A fractional marketing director, two days a month, starts at €2,100 a month. An outsourced marketing department of forty hours a month starts at €5,000 a month. Both monthly services have a six-month minimum term.
Trade shows can be the largest line in the budget, and the agency fee is only part of it. For ACHEMA 2027, from 14 to 18 June, the exhibition fee runs from €378 per square metre for a stand along a hall wall to €529.20 for a stand with at least two open sides, plus VAT. Start-ups and academic institutions pay €239.
The minimum stand at ACHEMA is 12 square metres, so the space alone costs €4,536 along a wall and €6,350.40 with two open sides, before stand construction, travel or any agency work. When an agency quotes for preparing ACHEMA or CPHI, ask it to show these lines separately from its own fee.

seccions.titol: What to put in writing before you sign
seccions.text:
If the agency will work with your CRM, forms or email lists, it processes personal data on your behalf. Article 28 of the GDPR says that processing by a processor must be governed by a contract or another legal act. Among other points, it must say that the agency acts only on your documented instructions and deletes or returns the data when the service ends.
Accounts need the same clarity. Ask for the Google Ads account, Google Analytics, Search Console, the domain and the website to be registered to your company, with the agency added as a user. If an SEO offers an audit, Google advises granting read access to Search Console only, not write access.
Finally, agree in writing who keeps the source files, such as 3D models, video projects and design files, and what is handed over if the relationship ends. Add the minimum term, the notice period and how fees change when the scope changes.

seccions.titol: Red flags in a life science agency proposal
seccions.text:
Some warning signs show up in the proposal itself. Google states that no one can guarantee a number one ranking and advises finding someone else if an SEO promises first place. It also says it never accepts money to include or rank sites in its search results.
Treat lists of the best life science marketing agencies with care. On 12 November 2026, the lists that came up for these searches were published by agencies or software vendors, not by independent bodies. They help you find names, but they are not a neutral ranking.

seccions.titol: What to do tomorrow
seccions.text: Work the timeline back from your next big trade show. Leave enough time between the brief and the signature for the agency to start well before it, because a stand prepared in a rush rarely brings qualified contacts.

faqs.q: Should I ask agencies for free creative work in the pitch?
faqs.a: You can, but it costs them a lot. The 2025 annual report of the EACA, the European association of communications agencies, cites a survey of 412 agencies that spend an average of €650,937 a year each pitching for new business. A written approach to your brief, or a short paid diagnosis, tells you more than speculative designs.

faqs.q: Should I pay the agency a percentage of ad spend or a fixed fee?
faqs.a: Either can work, but put it in writing. A percentage of spend gives the agency a reason to recommend spending more, while a fixed fee does not move with the budget. In both cases, pay for ads directly to Google from an account in your company's name, so ad spend and agency fees stay as separate lines.

faqs.q: Does a Google Partner badge mean an agency knows life science?
faqs.a: No. Google checks three things for the badge, an optimisation score of at least 70%, $10,000 of ad spend over 90 days across managed accounts and at least half of the account strategists certified in Google Ads. It shows that the agency runs Google Ads at some scale, not that it understands your buyers.

faqs.q: How long before I can judge an agency's work?
faqs.a: Agree it in the brief, not afterwards. Google's own advice before hiring an SEO is to ask what results to expect and in what timeframe, and how success will be measured. A sensible review point is the end of the first phase, measured against the quote request figure you defined at the start.

faqs.q: Should I use a freelancer or hire someone in-house?
faqs.a: If you need one skill, such as Google Ads, a specialist freelancer can be enough. If you need direction and several skills, from the website to trade shows, an agency or a fractional marketing director covers more with less management time. An in-house hire makes sense once the workload is steady and someone senior can direct that person.

visites-chatgpt-ga4.intro: Open Google Analytics 4 and go to the Traffic acquisition report. Since 13 May 2026, GA4 has had its own AI Assistant channel for visits from ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and other AI chat tools. It shows how many visits there are and, once you add the source, which chat tool sent them. What it misses is traffic that arrives with no trace, which GA4 counts as direct.

seccions.titol: Where does ChatGPT traffic show up in GA4?
seccions.text:
In the AI Assistant channel of the default channel group. Google launched it on 13 May 2026 and there is nothing to set up. When a visit comes from an AI chat tool Google recognises, GA4 sets the medium to ai-assistant and the campaign to (ai-assistant), and files it under that channel.
To see it, go to Reports, Acquisition and Traffic acquisition. AI Assistant appears as one row in the table. Add session source as a secondary dimension to tell chatgpt.com from gemini.google.com and the rest. Add landing page to see where people arrive.
Google's help pages give ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek, Copilot and Grok as examples, but Google does not publish the full list of tools it recognises. AI Overviews and Google's AI Mode are left out too. Those visits stay in organic search, because they come from Google.

seccions.titol: How to build an AI channel group with a regex
seccions.text:
A custom channel group lets you decide which sources count as AI. It is worth having for two reasons. You can add sources that may be missing from Google's list, such as Perplexity or Meta AI, and Google's help says custom groups can also be applied to past data.
Google's help offers a sample, but its regex starts with ^.*ai, a part that can also catch sources ending in ai that are not chat tools. The one in the list below only matches specific chat tools, and you can add new ones as they appear.
A standard property allows two custom groups on top of the default one, with up to 50 channels each. You need the Editor role or higher to create one. Order matters, because GA4 puts each visit in the first channel it matches. Google asks you to put the AI channel above Referral, because otherwise those visits stay in Referral.

seccions.titol: Why ChatGPT traffic shows up as direct in GA4
seccions.text:
GA4 only knows where a visit came from if the browser tells it. Google explains that when that information is missing, the visit is recorded as (direct) / (none). That includes typed addresses and links in documents such as PDFs. If someone copies the address ChatGPT gave them and pastes it into the browser, GA4 treats it as typed.
Another gap never shows up anywhere. If your site only loads GA4 once people accept analytics in your cookie banner, anyone who declines is invisible, whether they came from ChatGPT or Google. On a small site, that means the AI visits you see are fewer than the ones you get.
There is a clue, though it proves nothing. Look at direct visits that land on a guide or a product page rather than the home page. Few people type a long address from memory, so some of those visits may come from a link copied out of a chat or an email.

seccions.titol: What Search Console tells you about AI answers, and what it doesn't
seccions.text:
Search Console tells you nothing about ChatGPT. It tells you how often your pages appeared in Google's own AI answers. The generative AI performance report has been open to every site since 31 August 2026 and counts impressions in AI Overviews and AI Mode, by page, country, device and date.
There are no clicks and no queries. Clicks from those answers sit inside the normal Performance report, under the Web search type, mixed in with everything else. In GA4 they arrive as Google organic search. To find out whether you appear in Google's AI Mode, a manual test each month is still the most direct way.
For Copilot, Bing Webmaster Tools has offered a report called AI Performance, in public preview, since 10 February 2026. It shows how often Copilot and Bing's AI-generated summaries cite you, and which pages. It also gives a sample of the phrases the AI used to look things up. It counts citations and does not tell you how many people then visit your site.

seccions.titol: Which pages AI tools read, and what each tool measures
seccions.text:
When someone asks ChatGPT a question, it may open a page to read it and answer. OpenAI says it does this with the ChatGPT-User agent, which visits because a person asked and is not used to crawl the web on its own. Don't expect to find these reads in GA4, which counts visits from people. You see them in your server logs.
If your site runs behind Cloudflare, its AI Crawl Control tool shows which AI services visit, on every plan. In Cloudflare's data for crida.studio, for example, ChatGPT-User, Claude-User and Perplexity-User all show up with the pages they open. It tells you which topics bring you questions, even when the person never clicks through. The table sums up what each tool shows.

seccions.titol: How much AI traffic is normal for a small business?
seccions.text:
Not much. According to SE Ranking's study published on 17 June 2026, AI platforms sent an average of 0.30% of website traffic in Spain between January and April 2026. Organic search sent 40.70%. Within AI traffic, ChatGPT accounts for 70.49%.
crida.studio gets far more. In one month, GA4 on the site counted 564 visits from chatgpt.com. And our site only loads GA4 when visitors accept analytics, so some are still left out.
AI services come in even more often. From 19 October to 16 November 2026, Cloudflare counted about 1,590 requests from ChatGPT-User, the agent ChatGPT uses when it reads a page to answer someone, about 1,280 from Claude-User and about 4,580 from Perplexity. Counting OpenAI's crawlers that read sites for its search and for training too, OpenAI alone made about 7,000. Cloudflare works from samples, so these figures are approximate. That is more than the visits GA4 sees, because many answers stay inside the chat and the person never clicks.
At the study's 0.30% average, a site with 1,000 visits a month would get about 3 from AI tools. So a handful of AI visits a month is normal for a small business, even if some sites, like ours, get far more. What counts is whether they turn into a call or a form, and you see that in GA4 key events.

seccions.titol: What to do tomorrow, especially if you see no AI traffic yet
seccions.text:
If no AI visits show up at all, first check that you are not blocking the bots these tools use for search. OpenAI says sites that block OAI-SearchBot are not shown in ChatGPT search answers. Blocking GPTBot is a different matter, because it only asks that your content is not used to train models.
Then measure the same way every month and write it down. The numbers will stay small for a while, and what matters is the trend and which pages get the visits. If none of your service pages shows up anywhere, it may be time to check whether your site can be found and understood first.
At crida studio, our SEO work comes with a monthly report. Whoever prepares yours, it is worth putting these AI figures next to the calls and form submissions that come in. That way you can see whether visits from chat tools turn into work.

faqs.q: Can I see what the person asked ChatGPT before they clicked?
faqs.a: No. GA4 tells you where the visit came from and which page it landed on, but not what the person typed into the chat. Search Console's generative AI report has no queries either. The closest thing is the sample of phrases the AI used to look things up in Bing's AI Performance report, which only covers Copilot and Bing.

faqs.q: Does the AI Assistant channel cover months before May 2026?
faqs.a: Google does not say it applies to the months before 13 May 2026. If you want to compare with older data, use a custom channel group. Google's help says custom channel groups can be applied to your reports retroactively, so you can see your earlier ChatGPT visits that way.

faqs.q: Do visits from Google's AI Overviews count as AI traffic in GA4?
faqs.a: No. Google says the AI Assistant channel excludes AI Overviews and AI Mode. Those visits show up as Google organic search, mixed in with the rest. You will find impressions in those answers in Search Console's generative AI report, but without clicks.

faqs.q: If I block AI bots, will I stop getting visits from ChatGPT?
faqs.a: It depends on the bot. OpenAI says that if you block OAI-SearchBot your site will not appear in ChatGPT search answers, although it can still show up as a navigational link. Blocking GPTBot only asks that your content is not used for training. To keep getting visits, OAI-SearchBot is the one not to block.

pressupost-marqueting-digital-pime-2027.intro: Using crida studio's starting prices, a small business that wants a simple website, a Google Business Profile and six months of SEO should budget €4,450 to €4,680 for the first year, excluding VAT. Adding managed Google Ads raises the bar to €20,280 a year for Google Ads alone, because management and ad spend are paid separately. A percentage of revenue does little to settle the question.

seccions.titol: What percentage of revenue goes on marketing
seccions.text:
The figure you see most often comes from Gartner. Its 2026 survey puts the average marketing budget at 7.8% of company revenue, almost unchanged from 7.7% in 2025. The 401 respondents were marketing leaders in North America, the UK and Europe, most of them at companies with more than $1 billion in annual revenue.
For a small business that percentage is misleading. A company turning over €400,000 that applied 7.8% would have €31,200 a year for marketing. A shop on tight margins cannot get there, and a new business may need more than its percentage just to become visible.
It works better the other way round. Start with what you cannot do without. Then price each piece and check how long it takes to pay off. Compare the total with your revenue to see whether you can afford it.

seccions.titol: What the bare minimum costs
seccions.text:
The minimum has three parts. A Google Business Profile, which Google says you can manage at no cost and which puts you on Maps and Search. A website of your own, where crida studio's simple template-based site of 3 to 5 pages starts at €1,200 excluding VAT. And the running costs every website has, whoever builds it.
A domain costs €10 to €40 a year, hosting €100 to €300 a year and maintenance, with updates, backups and monitoring, €40 to €120 a month depending on the website. A simple website with domain and hosting comes to between €1,310 and €1,540 up front, plus monthly maintenance if you take it.
Many small firms in Spain still lack that minimum. According to Spain's National Statistics Institute (INE), in the first quarter of 2026 only 36.2% of companies with fewer than 10 employees and an internet connection had a website, against 82.9% of those with 10 or more. Social media shows the same gap, at 32.1% and 65.4%.

seccions.titol: What comes first, the website, SEO or Google Ads
seccions.text:
The order depends on where the business is now more than on its sector. Don't pay to send people to a website that fails to convince them, and don't expect SEO to deliver if you need calls this month. With that in mind, most businesses fit one of these four cases.
If you can't tell which one is yours, the marketing diagnosis starts at €2,500 excluding VAT and ends in a twelve-month plan with a budget and the measures that show whether it works. Google suggests asking any SEO specialist what results they expect and by when, and warns that no one can guarantee a number one ranking.

seccions.titol: How much to put into ads on top of management
seccions.text:
Google Ads means two budget lines. Google Ads management, which starts at €790 a month at crida studio, and the ad spend itself, which you pay straight to Google from your own account. Management covers search campaigns, lead tracking and a monthly report, and makes sense from €900 a month in ads, because below that there is not enough data to improve the campaigns.
Over a year that is €9,480 for management and at least €10,800 in ads, or €20,280 excluding VAT. Keep that figure in mind before putting Google Ads into a €6,000 or €15,000 budget. Running the campaigns yourself saves the management fee, but the ad spend stays the same.
In Google Ads you set an average daily budget. Google explains that a campaign can spend up to twice that on a given day, but by the end of the month it will not have spent more than 30.4 times the daily figure. To reach about €900 a month, set €30 a day, which caps the month at €912.

seccions.titol: How to split €6,000, €15,000 or €30,000 a year
seccions.text:
These three splits come from the starting prices crida studio publishes, excluding VAT, plus the running costs of any website. Each line is the minimum, with no extras. The first month of maintenance after launch is included, and after that maintenance is optional.
With €6,000, a new business or one without a website can get a simple site, a Google profile and six months of SEO. With €15,000, a company with an outdated website can start with the diagnosis, then build a custom site and run ten months of SEO once it is live. That still leaves €3,310 to €4,350 for website extras such as more pages, a second language or copywriting.
With €30,000, a company whose website already works can run a year of Google Ads at the minimum spend and a year of SEO side by side. The ads bring enquiries from the first month while SEO builds up. The €2,180 to €3,490 left over can go into extra ad spend in the busy months.

seccions.titol: What changes in 2027 with AI Mode and ChatGPT ads
seccions.text:
Google's AI Mode is already live in Spain and supports Spanish and Catalan, according to Google's help centre. Google says there are no additional requirements to appear in it and that the usual SEO best practice still applies, such as keeping your Business Profile up to date. So it does not need its own line in the budget.
ChatGPT has shown ads in Spain since 24 August 2026, on the free and Go plans. At first, access ran through OpenAI's sales team and partner agencies, and OpenAI says advertising does not influence its answers. For a small business it is something to watch in 2027 rather than a line to fund from day one.
AI is also part of daily work now. According to the INE, 21.4% of Spanish companies with fewer than 10 employees and an internet connection were already using some form of AI in the first quarter of 2026. If you want a voice assistant on your website, crida studio’s Ona costs €149 a month with a 12-month commitment, plus a €750 setup. Maintenance is included, and AI usage is billed separately based on use.

seccions.titol: How to tell whether the budget works, and what to do tomorrow
seccions.text:
A budget works if it brings enquiries that turn into paid work. Divide what you spent in a quarter by the enquiries you received and you have the cost of each one. Do it per channel, the Google profile, SEO and ads, and compare it with what a customer is worth to you.
To get those numbers, count calls and form submissions from day one, not just visits. Review the split every three months and move money to the channel that brings the cheapest enquiries. Give SEO time, because a single quarter is not enough to judge it. To start tomorrow, take these five steps.

faqs.q: Can I start with just social media and a Google Business Profile?
faqs.a: You can, and Google says the profile costs nothing to manage. But social media and the profile are other people's platforms, and anyone who wants to know more about you ends up looking for a website. If money is very tight, start with a well-built profile and add a simple website, from €1,200 excluding VAT, as soon as you can.

faqs.q: Can I run Google Ads myself to save the management fee?
faqs.a: Yes. The account is yours and you can create and run campaigns without a middleman. You save the management fee, which starts at €790 a month at crida studio, but the ad spend is the same. Allow for the hours it takes to set up and review campaigns every week, and track calls and form submissions from day one.

faqs.q: Do these budgets include VAT?
faqs.a: No. Every figure excludes VAT, just like crida studio's pricing page. Ad spend is paid to Google from your own account. If you want to see the total with tax, the website budget calculator adds Spanish VAT on a separate line for each service you pick.

faqs.q: How often should I review my marketing budget?
faqs.a: Every three months, using the enquiries that came in and what each channel cost. Ads can be adjusted more often, because you can change the daily budget whenever you like. SEO, on the other hand, needs three to six months at least before you judge it. Once a year, look at everything together and set the next year's budget.

faqs.q: What if no enquiries come in by mid-year?
faqs.a: First work out whether people can't find you, or find you and don't get in touch. If there are visits but no enquiries, the website or the offer is the problem, and more ad spend won't fix it. If there are no visits, check your Google profile, your SEO and your ad spend. A diagnosis helps you tell the two apart.

obs-2026-11.intro: So far, ClinicalTrials.gov counts 4 industry biologics trials started in Europe in October 2026. The count is provisional, because many studies are registered weeks after they start. This edition covers open data up to 31 October 2026, or the latest month published, on trials, medicine approvals, equipment imports into the EU and registrations in Brazil, for anyone running marketing or sales at a European bioprocess supplier.

seccions.titol: What the official records say about October 2026
seccions.text:
In October 2026, 64 industry biologics trials started worldwide, 24 in the United States, 20 in Asia and 4 in Europe. In the last twelve months, only March had more worldwide, with 74. The EMA authorised 1 medicine and the FDA approved 2. The FDA also issued 14 CGMP warning letters. EU import data run to August 2026.
Europe's 4 is provisional and the lowest figure of the twelve months. Many studies reach ClinicalTrials.gov weeks after they start, so the latest month usually rises. That is what happened to September. In the October edition, with data downloaded on 1 November 2026, September had 10 trials in Europe, and the 15 November download gives it 13.

seccions.titol: EMA authorisations and FDA approvals from May to October 2026
seccions.text:
In October 2026, the EMA authorised 1 human medicine through the centralised procedure, and it was not a biosimilar. The FDA approved 2, both novel drugs from CDER, while CBER approved no new licenses. Over the six months in the chart, the EMA peaks in July with 8, and the FDA in August and September with 10.
A month with 1 or 2 approvals does not signal a change of direction. The EMA authorises in batches, and the series has 14 medicines in November 2025 and only 1 in December. Recent CBER licenses may not be on the FDA page yet. And the EMA table only flags biosimilars, so it does not say whether October's medicine is a biologic.

seccions.titol: Where industry biologics trials started in October 2026
seccions.text:
By territory, the United States had 24 new trials in October 2026, Asia 20, Europe 4 and Latin America 1. The count covers industry-sponsored interventional studies with at least one biological intervention, by the start month recorded on ClinicalTrials.gov. A study with sites in several countries counts in each country and once in each territory.
In the country breakdown, Switzerland has 2, and Germany and Spain 1 each. France, Italy, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Belgium and Poland have none yet. The European total also includes countries outside the breakdown, and one study can count in more than one country, so the 4 do not necessarily come from those three.
For a supplier, behind each new trial is a sponsor that needs clinical trial material, often made in its own pilot plant or at a CDMO. The count understates the total, because many monoclonal antibody trials are registered as DRUG rather than BIOLOGICAL. For Europe, look at all twelve months, which range from 6 to 17 outside October.

seccions.titol: Imports under 8419.89 into the 27 EU member states in August 2026
seccions.text:
Eurostat publishes with a lag, and August 2026 is the latest month with data for all 27 member states, updated on 13 November. That month, the 27 imported 162,202 thousand euros under subheading 8419.89, against 194,616 in July (-16.7%). Germany imported 41,098 thousand euros, the Netherlands 15,541, France 13,476 and Spain 11,070, fourth on the list.
Subheading 8419.89 covers many machines for treating materials through a change of temperature, and bioreactors and fermenters are only part of it. It counts what enters each state from anywhere, other EU states included, in current euros. Eurostat may still revise August, and one month is not a trend.

seccions.titol: What the data show for Asia and Latin America in October 2026
seccions.text:
In Asia, 20 biologics trials started in October 2026, and 15 of them have a site in China. South Korea has 3, Japan 2 and India 1. Latin America had 1, with a site in Colombia, while Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Chile have none yet.
In Brazil, ANVISA registered 7 biological medicines in October and 6 in September, and the highest month in the series is April 2026, with 20. In Japan, the PMDA list has 135 new drug entries for FY2024, from April 2024 to March 2025. FY2025, still partial, has 119 entries up to February 2026.
Asia here means only Japan, China, India and South Korea, and Latin America means Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia and Chile. Studies that appear only in a national registry are left out. The ANVISA file of 13 November has no registration date, so the process completion date is used. PMDA entries include new indications and doses and serve only as context.

seccions.titol: What a European bioprocess supplier can do with the October figures
seccions.text:
For the coming quarter, these figures do not call for big changes. The United States, with 24 new trials, and Asia, with 20, stay within their range of the past year, so if you already sell there, keep up the effort. In Europe, check each country's twelve months in this edition's CSV file before cutting back, because the 4 is provisional. In Spain, with 1 trial in October and 3 in September, one month says little.
With trial sponsors, talk about clinical trial material, scale-up and GMP documentation. For the United States, make sure your English content answers technical questions so buyers do not need to call. For Asia, decide the language with your distributor in each country. Germany was the largest importer under subheading 8419.89 in August, but the subheading covers far more than bioreactors. If you want to sell there, it helps to have your key pages in German.
Make sure your website and datasheets state the scale each system works at and the GMP documentation that comes with it, and share them with your distributors. If you are going to a trade show before the next edition, bring these figures with their download date. crida studio does marketing for bioprocess equipment makers and life science companies, and its founder ran marketing at a European manufacturer for three and a half years.

seccions.titol: What changed compared with September 2026
seccions.text:
Compared with September, trials rise from 62 to 64 worldwide (+3.2%), from 22 to 24 in the United States (+9.1%) and from 18 to 20 in Asia (+11.1%). Europe goes from 13 to 4, and Latin America and Spain from 3 to 1, with October still incomplete. The September figures come from the 15 November download, and some no longer match those in the October edition.
The EMA goes from 7 authorisations to 1 and the FDA from 10 approvals to 2. CGMP warning letters rise from 13 to 14 (+7.7%), and October may still add more. Imports under subheading 8419.89 fall 16.7% from July to August. In the chart, worldwide trials range from a low of 39 in July to a high of 74 in March, and October, at 64, is the second-highest month.

seccions.titol: Sources, queries and limits of this edition
seccions.text: All sources were downloaded on 15 November 2026. The data run to 31 October 2026, except Eurostat, which runs to August, and the PMDA list, which runs to February 2026. These are counts of official records and, for Eurostat, import values, with no estimates of our own. They do not measure orders or sales of bioprocess equipment. The latest month of each series can still move. Below are the exact query and limits for each source.

faqs.q: How many biologics trials started in Spain in October 2026?
faqs.a: ClinicalTrials.gov counts 1 industry trial with at least one biological intervention and a site in Spain, against 3 in September. The figure is provisional, from the database as of 13 November 2026, and may rise once studies that have already started are registered. A study with sites in Spain and other countries counts in each country.

faqs.q: Why does Europe show only 4 trials in October 2026?
faqs.a: Because the count is still incomplete. October is the last month in this edition and many studies are registered weeks after they start. September shows how this works, with 10 trials in Europe in the 1 November 2026 download and 13 in the 15 November one. The 4 is the lowest figure of the twelve months, but it does not yet point to a decline.

faqs.q: Do these counts measure demand for bioprocess equipment?
faqs.a: No. The figures are counts of official records, such as a study starting, a medicine being authorised or an FDA letter, plus the value imported under a subheading that covers far more than bioreactors. They show where the sector is moving, but they do not say how much bioprocess equipment is bought, in units or in euros. That is why there are no market sizes or forecasts here.

faqs.q: Where can I download the data and how were they counted?
faqs.a: The figures can be downloaded as CSV and JSON from this page, with the source and download date of each value. Scripts read the eight official sources with the same filters every month, without estimates. The method section at the end of the page gives the exact query and the limits of each source.

bio-pla-llancament-equip-laboratori.intro: To launch new lab or bioprocess equipment in 90 days, fix the launch date first, ideally the opening day of a trade show your buyers attend, and count back 13 weeks. Weeks 1 to 4 lock the message, the price list and the evidence. Weeks 5 to 9 produce the renders, video, datasheet and product page. Weeks 10 to 13 train sales and distributors and fill the diary with meetings.

seccions.titol: What has to be decided before the 90 days start
seccions.text:
The 90 days only work if the product is ready to sell when they start. Engineering has frozen the specification, the list price and lead time are agreed, and the conformity route is clear. If any of these is still moving, the plan turns into a countdown to a date you will have to move.
In 2027 there is one more reason to check conformity early. The EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 applies from 14 January 2027 (Article 54) and repeals Directive 2006/42/EC from that same day (Article 51). Ask whoever handles CE marking which framework applies to your instrument, because it changes the documents you publish at launch.
Whether the market wants the product is a separate question, and it comes first. If you have not answered it yet, run the market analysis, get a go decision from management and then come back to this plan.

seccions.titol: Which 2027 trade show to time the launch to
seccions.text:
Tie the launch date to a show where your buyers already are. Launching on the opening day gives the press release a reason and sales a place to meet buyers, and it sets a date nobody can push back. The table counts 13 weeks back from each opening day, using the dates the organisers publish, checked on 17 November 2026.
If you start this week, the 90 days end in mid-February, too late for SLAS2027 in San Diego. Analytica, the Munich lab show, does not run in 2027, and its next edition is from 25 to 28 April 2028. For most European instrument makers, the realistic windows in the first half of the year are BPI Europe and ACHEMA.
ACHEMA has a date worth marking. From 15 March 2027, the Monday the 13 weeks would start, cancelling your stand costs 100% of the exhibition fee. Take the go or no-go decision before then. The full calendar of 2027 trade shows also covers BIO, Farmaforum and BioSpain.

seccions.titol: The 13-week launch plan, block by block
seccions.text:
Each block ends with something you can check, such as a signed claim sheet or a page ready to publish. If a block slips, cut scope in the next one rather than moving the launch date, because the show will not move.
The order matters more than the speed. Writing the product page before engineering has approved the claims means rewriting it twice, and filming before the figures are fixed means a reshoot when one of them changes.

seccions.titol: Which launch assets come first and who owns them
seccions.text:
Start with the assets everything else is cut from. Approved claims feed the datasheet, the datasheet feeds the product page, and the renders and video feed the page, the booth and sales. The table shows a workable order for a mid-sized maker.
Buyers in GMP plants check the documentation early. EU GMP Annex 15 says equipment should be confirmed against the URS at the vendor site before installation, where applicable, and that FAT may be supplemented by a SAT on site (points 3.5 and 3.7). An outline of how you run both, published with the product, answers that question before it comes up.
If your instructions for use will be digital, treat them as a launch asset. Article 10(7) of Regulation 2023/1230 allows it, but they must be printable and downloadable, stay online for the expected lifetime of the machine and for at least ten years after it is placed on the market, and be sent on paper free of charge within one month if the user asks at purchase.
Plan the video shoot for three uses, the website, the silent booth loop and short clips for sales follow-up. Our guide to filming one equipment demo lists the shots a bioreactor or TFF demo needs and what should stay out of shot.

seccions.titol: How to get early-user evidence when customers are under NDA
seccions.text:
Launch evidence does not have to name a customer. Data from your own applications lab, run with a protocol you publish, is evidence you control. Show the method, the cell line or process, the scale and the result, and say it was run in-house.
With early users, ask in week 3 what they can share and in what form. Some will accept a quote without their name, a description such as a European CDMO, or a joint poster once their own team has approved it. Get that permission in writing before you design anything around it.
If none of this is ready by week 9, launch with your own data and add the case study without the customer's name later. The wording and the approvals are the same, only the date changes.

seccions.titol: Launch week at the show and the numbers that matter
seccions.text:
Put the launch on the opening morning and the key demos midweek. At ACHEMA 2024, the opening Monday drew 29,010 visitors and Wednesday 43,137, according to the organiser. The press release and the page go live on Monday, and demos with target accounts go on Tuesday and Wednesday. The figures for each day and how to staff the booth are in our guide to preparing for ACHEMA or CPHI.
Count what shows buying intent, not visits. Demo requests, quote requests, meetings with target accounts and opportunities opened by distributors in the first 30 days tell you whether the launch works. Page views and badge scans only tell you that people noticed.
Set the targets in week 1, together with sales, and review them 30, 60 and 90 days after launch. If the page gets visits but no demo requests, look first at the message and the form, and fix them while the show contacts are still warm.

seccions.titol: What to do tomorrow
seccions.text:
You can start this week with a handful of decisions and a calendar on one wall. None of the five steps below needs a budget, and together they tell you within a few days whether the show you have in mind is still realistic or whether the next window fits better.
If nobody in the company has the time to run the launch, a fractional marketing director can hold the calendar, chase the weekly deadlines and coordinate engineering, sales, distributors and outside suppliers, so the people who know the product can stay focused on it.
We plan launches like this one, with renders, demo video, the product page and Google Ads, as part of our marketing for biotech and bioprocess companies. The first step is always the same, a calendar with the show date and the thirteen weeks before it.

faqs.q: How long before a trade show should a product launch start?
faqs.a: Thirteen weeks is a tight minimum for a mid-sized maker that already has a working unit. It leaves four weeks for message and evidence, five for assets and four for training and meetings. Book the stand much earlier, because ACHEMA lets space on availability and charges 50% of the fees for cancellations between 1 September 2026 and 14 March 2027.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to launch a lab instrument?
faqs.a: There is no public benchmark for a whole launch. Our prices start at €2,000 for 3 to 5 product renders, €2,500 for a 60 to 90 second explainer video with script, 2D animation and voice-over, and €3,000 for a custom website. At ACHEMA 2027 the minimum 12 m² along a hall wall costs €4,536 for space alone. All prices exclude VAT.

faqs.q: Should we launch at a trade show or online?
faqs.a: Both, on the same day. The show gives sales meetings and press attention, while the product page, the video and an email to your contacts reach the buyers who are not there. An online-only launch can work too, but without a fixed date it tends to slip, so set one anyway.

faqs.q: What if the product is not ready on time?
faqs.a: Cut scope, not the date, if the product itself is ready. Launch with the renders, the datasheet and the page, and add the video or the case study later. If the unit is not ready to sell, cancel the show launch early and choose the next window in the table, rather than showing a product nobody can order.

faqs.q: Do distributors need a demo unit before launch?
faqs.a: They need training and a demo plan before launch, and ideally a demo unit in their main market within the first weeks after it. Without one, they will send every interested lab to you, and the distance slows the sale. Agree in writing who pays for demo units and how long they stay with the distributor.

etiquetar-contingut-ia-2-desembre.intro: Not everything you make with AI needs a label. Since 2 August 2026, the EU AI Act has required anyone publishing a deepfake (an image, audio or video that looks real but isn't) or AI-written text on matters of public interest that nobody has reviewed to disclose it. 2 December 2026 is only the deadline for AI tools already on the market to mark what they generate.

seccions.titol: What Article 50 of the AI Act says about content
seccions.text:
Article 50 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 splits the work between two roles. The provider develops the AI tool and places it on the market under its own name. The deployer uses it under its own authority, outside purely personal, non-professional use (Article 3(4)). A small business creating images with AI for its website is a deployer.
Paragraph 2 requires providers to make sure the text, images, audio or video their tool generates are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificial. Paragraph 4 requires the people publishing to disclose two things, deepfakes and text that informs the public on matters of public interest.
Article 113 makes all of this apply from 2 August 2026. The European Commission guidelines of 5 November 2026 say any activity through which someone earns money on a regular basis counts as professional (point 19). A freelancer creating AI images for their business is covered too.

seccions.titol: What needs a label, content type by content type
seccions.text: It depends on the type of content and on whether it could make someone believe it is real. The table sums up Article 50 and the examples in the Commission guidelines, which explain how the Commission reads it. Use it as a first filter. If your case isn't listed, compare it with the closest example.

seccions.titol: What actually changes on 2 December 2026
seccions.text:
2 December 2026 only affects providers. Article 111(4), added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, gives systems that generate audio, images, video or text and were placed on the market before 2 August 2026 until that day to comply with Article 50(2), the machine-readable marking rule.
There is no such extension for visible labels on deepfakes and public-interest text. The guidelines say Article 50 has applied to all systems since 2 August 2026, and tools that both chat and generate content only get extra time for marking (point 153). Telling people they are talking to an AI was already mandatory in August.
Nor do you need to label what was made earlier. According to the guidelines, content and deepfakes generated before 2 August 2026 don't need retroactive marking or labelling (point 154). Public-interest text generated before that date but published after it does need a label.
For a small business, 2 December is mostly a reminder to ask your tools whether they already mark what they generate. Google, for example, says it embeds invisible SynthID watermarks and C2PA metadata in images and videos generated with Google Ads tools.

seccions.titol: Do AI images on your website or social media need a label?
seccions.text:
Only if they are deepfakes. Article 3(60) defines a deep fake as AI-generated or manipulated image, audio or video content that resembles existing persons, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear to a person to be authentic or truthful. The guidelines add that no intent to deceive is needed (point 114).
The guidelines give marketing examples (section 6.1.1). An AI-generated product image that makes the product look different or better than it is counts as a deepfake, as does a synthetic influencer testing a product or a realistic avatar of the CEO thanking staff. A real car shown against a generated background doesn't, as long as it doesn't mislead about the car.
Everyday edits usually don't count. According to the guidelines, colour correction, removing a passer-by or swapping a background for aesthetic reasons tend to have little effect on how people perceive the content, though it depends on context (point 116). An empty flat furnished with AI, by contrast, is the example the EU uses for its partially modified content icon.
If the product has to look exactly right, the safest route is to start from the real thing, with photos or product renders built from its true dimensions and materials. If you're unsure whether an image could pass as real, add the label.

seccions.titol: What about AI-written text that a person reviews?
seccions.text:
If a person genuinely reviews it and someone is accountable for it, no label is needed. Article 50(4) only requires disclosure for AI-generated or manipulated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest. It makes an exception where the text has undergone human review or editorial control and a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility.
Most business text falls outside it. The guidelines say ad copy and product descriptions are not covered, provided they make no claims about health, consumer safety or sustainability. Covered examples (section 6.2.1) include an article on a lifestyle website about diets and disease, or investor information published by a listed company.
The review has to be substantive and done by someone who knows the subject. The guidelines say fact-checking is the minimum, while a spell-check, an editorial policy nobody applies or a quick sign-off don't count (points 134 and 135). If AI changes the text again after the review, the exception no longer applies (point 136).
A clinic blogging about a medical condition or a town council publishing notices with AI is much closer to the line. They should decide who reviews each text, put that in writing and, where there is no review, put the label at the start of the text.

seccions.titol: What Google Ads asks for with AI-made ads
seccions.text:
Since July 2026, Google has allowed text or visual labels inside image and video creatives generated or modified with AI, and doesn't treat them as banned text overlays or watermarks. It has also been rolling out an AI label setting across Google Ads, Merchant Center, Ads Editor, Display & Video 360 and Campaign Manager 360.
With the setting, you mark each asset as created or edited with AI. The ad then explains this in the section on how it was made, under the three-dot menu, and in campaigns targeting the European Union the label also appears on the ad itself. If you use Google's fully automated features, Google may apply the label itself and it can't be removed.
Google warns that using the setting doesn't guarantee compliance with any regulation. If you add your own label, it recommends keeping it away from the corners and edges of the image and turning off automatic image enhancements, which can crop it. In Google Ads campaigns with generated images, check every asset before it goes live.

seccions.titol: What a label should look like and the EU icons
seccions.text:
The label must be clear and distinguishable and reach people at the latest the first time they see the content (Article 50(5)). The guidelines say it isn't enough to put it in the terms of use, in a manual or deep in a menu, or to rely on the invisible mark in the file (points 117 and 142).
In a video, the label goes at the start, and again later if some viewers are likely to miss the beginning (point 143). On social media you can use the labelling tool that large platforms offer, but the guidelines say the responsibility stays with you (point 126).
The EU has published free icons for labelling content, in three versions (basic, fully AI-generated and partially AI-modified) and four colour variants. They are optional, work better with a short text label next to them and, according to the Commission, should be embedded in the content so they stay visible when it is shared or downloaded. Where you can, add alt text saying it was made with AI.
Fines for breaching Article 50 can reach EUR 15 million or 3% of total worldwide annual turnover for the previous financial year, whichever is higher (Article 99(4)). For SMEs, including start-ups, the lower of the two applies (Article 99(6)). If you also run a chatbot, the chatbot notice is a separate obligation under Article 50(1).

seccions.titol: What to check this week on your website, social media and ads
seccions.text: You can do this check in an afternoon and be ready before 2 December. If your team uses AI applied to marketing every week, keep the list and run it again whenever you change tools.

faqs.q: If I write my blog with ChatGPT, do I have to say it's AI?
faqs.a: Only if the text informs the public on a matter of public interest, such as health, politics or a public service, and nobody has properly reviewed it. If a person checks the facts, edits it substantively and someone in the business is accountable for it, Article 50(4) doesn't require a label. Ad copy and product text are outside its scope, according to the guidelines.

faqs.q: Do AI-generated stock images need a label?
faqs.a: It depends on what they show. If they look like real photos of people, places or events and someone could take them as authentic, they fit the Article 3(60) definition of a deep fake and whoever publishes them must disclose it. If they are clearly illustrations or impossible scenes, the guidelines give similar examples that are not deepfakes.

faqs.q: Does a humorous ad made with AI need a label too?
faqs.a: If it is a deepfake, yes, but the requirement is lighter. When it is part of an evidently artistic, creative, satirical or fictional work, disclosure in a way that doesn't spoil the work is enough (Article 50(4)). The guidelines say ads only qualify in specific cases (point 122), and a video of synthetic consumers trying out a product to sell it does not.

faqs.q: If a studio makes the images for me, who adds the label?
faqs.a: It depends on who decides how AI is used. The guidelines say a company that simply commissions an ad, without deciding or controlling whether or how AI is used to make it, is not a deployer (point 14). If you decide and control how AI is used, you are. Either way, put in writing who adds the label.

faqs.q: Is the Commission's code of practice mandatory?
faqs.a: No. The Commission published it on 10 June 2026 and it is voluntary, but Article 50 itself is binding. Signatories can rely on it to show they comply. Non-signatories have to show compliance by other means, and the guidelines say they may face more requests for information (point 148). By the end of July about 190 organisations had signed it.

informe-google-ads-looker-studio.intro: A good Google Ads report in Looker Studio, which Google has renamed back to Data Studio, tells a B2B company how many real leads came in, what they cost, which searches brought them and whether the budget is on pace. You build it from Google Ads, Google Analytics 4, Search Console and a sheet that logs every lead, and you check it every week.

seccions.titol: What a B2B Google Ads report needs to tell you
seccions.text:
When you sell to other businesses, leads are few and each one can turn into a large order. That is why the report cannot stop at clicks and impressions. It has to show how many good leads came in, what each one cost and which searches they came from. Every other number is there to explain why those go up or down.
Before you build anything, write down what management will ask when they open the report. Usually they want to know how many leads we had, whether they were any good, whether spend is on track and what we will change next month. Each page of the report should answer one of those questions. If a chart answers none, take it out.

seccions.titol: The four data sources and what each one adds
seccions.text:
A useful report brings four sources together, and each one answers a different question. Google Ads tells you what you paid and for which searches. Google Analytics 4 tells you what people do once they reach the site. Search Console tells you how people find you on Google without ads. And the lead sheet tells you who actually got in touch.
The lead sheet is the source that counts. Google Ads and GA4 count submitted forms, but they cannot tell whether the person writing was a buyer, a student or someone trying to sell you something. In the sheet, someone on the team marks each lead as good or not, and the report only counts the good ones.
GA4 also misses some forms. Since the site added its cookie banner, some people decline measurement and GA4 loses part of them, while every lead still reaches the sheet. So when it comes to counting leads, the sheet always wins, and GA4 tells you where they came from.

seccions.titol: The five pages your report should have
seccions.text:
The Looker Studio report we built for a pharmaceutical equipment manufacturer has five pages, and that order works for almost any B2B company. Each page answers a single question, and the summary comes first because it is what management reads.
The tracking page is the one people open most. In B2B, leads trickle in and a month can bring very few, but clicks and cost per click move every day. If one product line gets more expensive or stops getting clicks, you see it within days rather than at the end of the month. Here are the five pages, in order.

seccions.titol: How to connect the sources in Looker Studio
seccions.text:
You can start from scratch or from a template. The Data Studio gallery has Google’s own templates for Google Ads and Google Analytics. Open one, click “Edit and share” to make your own copy and use “Use my own data” to connect your account. Then cut it down to the five pages and remove what you do not need.
Think carefully about which account connects the sources. With owner’s credentials, anyone who opens the report sees the data without needing access to Google Ads. If the person who connected them leaves, or an agency used one of its own accounts, the report can lose its data. Use a company account.
Before connecting anything, put the product line at the start of every campaign name, always written the same way. A calculated field can then pull the line out of the name and split clicks and cost without any manual work. In the lead sheet, write each line with exactly the same name so you can join the two sources. Then connect the four sources like this.

seccions.titol: What not to count as a conversion
seccions.text:
In Google Ads, your primary conversion should be the lead you received, and nothing else. Primary conversion actions appear in the “Conversions” column and Google uses them for automated bidding. Secondary ones only appear under “All conversions” and play no part in bidding. If you mark something that is not a lead as primary, Google will go looking for more people who do that.
Also switch the count to one conversion per click. For website conversions, Google Ads counts every conversion after a click by default, so someone who sends the form twice adds two leads. With the “One” option, each click counts at most one conversion, which is what you want when the lead is what matters. And none of the following should ever be a primary conversion.

seccions.titol: How to read your budget pace
seccions.text:
Google Ads does not spend the same amount every day. According to its help centre, on any given day a campaign can spend up to twice its average daily budget, but by the end of the month it will not have spent more than 30.4 times that budget. That is why the budget page compares what you have spent so far with what you would expect at that point in the month.
Take an average daily budget of €30. The monthly maximum is €912, and a single day can spend up to €60. Halfway through the month, a normal pace would be around €450. If you have spent €600, you are ahead and spending will have to slow down. If you have spent €300, there is budget left and it is worth checking whether search volume allows for more.

seccions.titol: How often to review the report and what to look at
seccions.text:
Every week, a short review so you can correct course in time. Check the tracking page, read the new searches that brought clicks and block the ones that are not from buyers with negative keywords. Check the pace of spend and go through the week’s leads one by one, marking in the sheet whether they were good.
Every month, a longer review to discuss with management. Compare the month with the previous one, look at the cost per good lead for each product line and decide where you put more budget and where less. Write down what you changed and why, because three months from now nobody will remember.
Every quarter, match the leads against what happened next. Look at how many turned into a quote and how many into an order. In B2B, sales take months to close, and a month with few leads can bring the biggest sale of the year. That is why big decisions need several months of data.

seccions.titol: What you can do this week
seccions.text: You do not need everything on day one. With these steps you get a report that already answers the important questions, and you can improve it with whatever the team asks for. When we take on Google Ads management for a company, we follow this same order.

faqs.q: Are Looker Studio and Data Studio the same tool?
faqs.a: Yes. On 16 April 2026 Google renamed Looker Studio back to Data Studio. It is the same tool for building reports and dashboards from your own data. Many people still search for it as Looker Studio, which is why this guide uses both names.

faqs.q: Do you have to pay for Looker Studio?
faqs.a: Not for a report like this one. The Google Ads, Google Analytics, Search Console and Google Sheets connectors are made by Google and work in the standard version. There is a paid version, Data Studio Pro, which adds team workspaces and makes reports belong to the company rather than to whoever created them.

faqs.q: How often does the report data refresh?
faqs.a: It depends on the source. Google Ads and Search Console data refresh every 12 hours, and that cannot be changed. A Google Sheet refreshes every 15 minutes by default, and you can set it to every hour, every 4 hours or every 12 hours. That is why a lead from today can show up in the sheet before it appears in Google Ads.

faqs.q: Why does Google Ads show fewer leads than my sheet?
faqs.a: Because Google Ads only counts leads that come after a click on an ad and that it was able to measure. The sheet also includes people who phone, send an email or arrive from unpaid search. If the gap is very large, check that the conversion tag is on the thank-you page or fires when the form is sent.

bio-respondre-rfi-farma-proveidor.intro: To answer a pharma RFI well, reply to every block the buyer asks about with a short answer and the document that proves it. That means company and capacity, quality system and certificates, supply chain, specifications, regulatory statements and your willingness to accept audits and a quality agreement. Buyers then pass your package to their quality department, so the answers have to be ready, consistent and signed off before the RFI arrives.

seccions.titol: RFI, RFP, RFQ and the qualification questionnaire are different steps
seccions.text:
An RFI is the first filter, and qualification comes later. The APIC best practices guide for managing suppliers, version 2 of 18 March 2024, groups the request for information, proposal and quotation into one stage it calls RfX. At that stage buyers ask for standard documentation packages, plus commercial terms such as price, payment terms and minimum order quantity.
Then the buyer's team, quality included, reviews the package. According to the same guide, that review decides whether there are risks, which extra questions to ask and whether a site visit is needed. Only after that does formal qualification start, with questionnaires, statements, audits and, for critical materials and services, a quality agreement.
Pharma companies ask because GMP guidance asks them to. Section 2.7 of ICH Q10, dated 4 June 2008, says the company should assess the suitability and competence of a supplier before choosing it, for example through audits, material evaluations or qualification. Point 5.27 of chapter 5 of the EU GMP guidelines asks for the selection and approval of starting material suppliers to be documented, with supervision in proportion to the risk.

seccions.titol: What a pharma RFI usually asks
seccions.text: Most RFIs follow the same blocks, even when the form changes from one buyer to the next. The APIC guide lists what the RfX stage typically requests, besides the commercial terms. It was written for suppliers of API manufacturers, but the same blocks work for sorting what equipment and single-use buyers ask.

seccions.titol: Which document answers each block
seccions.text:
Every block in an RFI can be answered with a document or page you already have, or should have. The table links each block to its proof and to the person in your company who should own it. The owner keeps the document current and signs off each answer before it goes out.
For equipment makers there is an extra block. Point 3.5 of Annex 15 of the EU GMP guidelines says equipment should be confirmed against the URS at the vendor site before installation, where applicable, and point 3.7 says FAT may be supplemented by a SAT. Buyers will ask how you support that.

seccions.titol: The RFI kit to have ready before the request arrives
seccions.text:
The kit is a folder of approved answers and documents, each with a version, a date and an owner. With it, answering an RFI means picking and adapting answers you already have. Without it, someone spends a week chasing engineering and quality.
If you sell single-use products, look at the Rx-360 Supplier Assessment Questionnaire. It has six modules, from company and site information to a pre-audit questionnaire and a module for single-use bioprocessing products such as bags, tubing, filters and connectors. Rx-360 says suppliers can complete their response proactively and keep it current, and the tool returns a PDF and a JSON file to share with each customer.

seccions.titol: How to show references when everything is under NDA
seccions.text:
References are the block suppliers find hardest, because most pharma projects sit under confidentiality agreements. The answer is to prepare them before you need them, not to leave the field empty or to name a client without permission.
An anonymised case with the type of client, the process, the scale, the problem and an outcome the client has approved answers most of what a reference question is after. If a client agrees to take a call, note it in the kit and ask again each time, since people and policies change.
Be precise about anything the buyer can check. The APIC guide notes that regulatory track record can be verified, for example through warning letters. A modest, exact answer earns more trust than a broad claim that quality then has to take apart.

seccions.titol: How your website gets you onto the RFI list
seccions.text:
You can only answer an RFI that reaches you. Buyers send RfX requests once they have defined their requirements, so the shortlist is built before the first email. Part of it comes from what buyers find on websites and sometimes from AI assistants that buyers ask for a list of suppliers.
Publish the non-confidential part of your kit. A quality page with dated certificates, a clear statement of what you make and where, a supply chain summary and the line “SAQ response available on request” all answer questions a buyer would otherwise send in writing.
